beagle._note: Added 2026-10-10 (M5-R10-06, unattended run). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-10; spot-check before import (sources.md S111–S117, reused S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45). Pages were partly returned as paraphrase — only passages the tool returned in quotation marks are used as quotes. McMillan 2024 does not name the Beagle in its text or corrected Fig. 3 legend (S54 checked 2026-10-10), the Dogs Trust summary (S15) has no Beagle value in its text (the breed table is a separate PDF, not read) and the 2012 VetCompass poster (S71) has no Beagle row — so the lifespan is the VetCompass breed paper median (S116) per the runbook rule. Neither the FCI nor the RKC standard gives a weight; the only standard-type weight is PDSA (S115, tier B). Woodgreen and the AKC page were not found / not attempted.

identity.value: FCI No. 161, Group 6 Section 1.3 (Small-sized Hounds), Great Britain
identity.quote: Group: n°6 - Chiens courants, Chiens de recherche au sang et Races apparentées; Section: Chiens courants; Subsection: Chiens courant de petite taille; Country of origin: GRANDE-BRETAGNE
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S112, French-language fields as returned): standard number 161; definitive acceptance '26/04/1955'; 'Soumise à épreuve de travail' (with working trial). Valid-standard date returned as '08/09/2026' (the EN row '06/10/2026') — differs from the PDF (S111: 'DATE OF PUBLICATION OF THE OFFICIAL VALID STANDARD: 13.10.2010.'), verify. FCI standard PDF (S111): 'Group 6 Scent hounds and related breeds.' and 'Section 1.3 Small-sized Hounds. With working trial.' Quote assembled from the nomenclature fields.

size_class.notes: PDSA (S115) says 'Size: Medium' (key-facts box as returned) — conflict; RKC breed page preferred (runbook §2.2). FCI / RKC height 33–40 cm (S111, S114); PDSA weight 9–11 kg (S115) = PetMD small class upper edge (S10).

fci.quote: Desirable minimum height at the withers 33 cms.
fci.notes: FCI (S111): 'Desirable maximum height at the withers 40 cms.' One range for both sexes.

rkc.quote: Desirable minimum height at withers: 33 cms (13 ins).
rkc.notes: RKC standard (S114, last updated 1 April 2025): 'Desirable maximum height at withers: 40 cms (16 ins).'

pdsa_average.notes: PDSA key-facts box (label wording as returned).

pdsa.notes: PDSA key-facts box (label wording as returned), one range for both sexes. The FCI (S111) and RKC (S114) standards give no weight (height only); AKC standard not attempted. Tier B — the only weight range found.

uk_measured_median.unit: kg (median adult bodyweight, UK primary care 2019)
uk_measured_median.quote: The median adult bodyweight was 18.19 kg (IQR 15.68–21.07).
uk_measured_median.notes: O'Neill et al. 2025 (S116), VetCompass UK 2019. Results: 'Males (19.70 kg, IQR 17.26–22.44, range 8.11–46.25) were heavier than females' (sentence continues, females 16.59 kg as returned). Far above the PDSA range — measured pet dogs; the authors: 'High levels of obesity could offer another explanation for the heavier bodyweights in the wider population of Beagles'. Research only; not exported (would read as the breed's target weight).

salt_category.notes: Category assignment by weight is ours: 9–11 kg sits at the Salt 2017 band III / IV boundary (general_by_size.size_classes.salt_2017_bands_kg, S8). Salt 2017 breed list not checked.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. PDSA 9–11 kg (S115) = 19.8–24.3 lb → the 'Small (12–24 pounds)' class (the upper edge touches 'Medium (24–59 pounds): 12–15 months').

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no pet-Beagle growth curve found (the S9 laboratory-Beagle logistic parameters are used only for the medium-size general curve, general_by_size).

median_uk.quote: The median age at death was 11.28 years (IQR 9.32–13.08) for 322 deaths recorded during the study period.
median_uk.notes: O'Neill et al. 2025 (S116), VetCompass UK 2019, 19,906 Beagles. The abstract Conclusions say 'Their median age at death of 11.70 years suggests reasonable overall health' — a discrepancy inside the paper; the Results value (with n and IQR, repeated in the full text S116 and RVC Clinical Connections S117) is used. McMillan 2024 (S54) and the Dogs Trust summary (S15) have no Beagle value reachable (see _note) — runbook rule: else a VetCompass median. Conflicts with the breed-page band 'Over 12 years' (S113, S115). Medium until McMillan 2024 Supplementary Table is checked.

rkc.notes: PDSA (S115): 'Average lifespan: Over 12 years' (key-facts label as returned). Generic band; conflicts with the VetCompass median 11.28 y (S116).

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × 11.28 y (S116) → 0.75 × 11.28 = 8.46 y = 101.52 → 102 months. With the Conclusions value 11.70 y: 105.3 → 105 months. With the breed-page 'over 12 years' (S113): 0.75 × 12 = 9 y = 108 months. Dogs Trust rule of thumb > 7 y = 84 months (S14).

adult.quote: Exercise: Up to 1 hour per day
adult.notes: PDSA conflicts: key-facts 'Minimum exercise (per day): 1 hour' but text 'Your Beagle will need at least an hour and a half of exercise a day.' (S115). Runbook rule: RKC preferred → 60; PDSA 90 recorded as alternative in proposed_game_parameters.

energy.value: quite high energy; bold, with great activity and stamina
energy.quote: Beagles tend to be quite high energy and you'll find they enjoy being part of everything their owners do.
energy.notes: FCI (S111) / RKC (S114): 'Bold, with great activity, stamina and determination.'

temperament.value: merry scent hound; amiable and alert, no aggression or timidity; sociable
temperament.quote: Amiable and alert, showing no aggression or timidity.
temperament.notes: FCI (S111) / RKC (S114): 'A merry hound whose essential function is to hunt, primarily hare, by following a scent.' RKC breed page (S113): 'Historically developed to work in packs, the Beagle is sociable and generally good-tempered, thriving on companionship.' PDSA (S115): 'Beagles are loving and sociable dogs who enjoy nothing more than being involved in whatever is going on in the house.'; scent games 'Beagles are scent hounds, so they'll really enjoy playing scent games with you and getting the chance to use their keen sense of smell.'

family.value: suits family life when socialised young; popular family companion; supervise with children
family.quote: Due to their loving and tolerant nature, if socialised correctly from a young age Beagles suit family life really well.
family.notes: RKC breed page (S113): 'Its friendly, affectionate nature and manageable size have made it a popular family companion in modern times.' PDSA (S115): 'You should always supervise your Beagle with children in case playtime gets too boisterous.' No explicit 'good with children' statement → family_pet only, not children / small_children.

time_alone.value: should not be left alone; distressed and bored when alone — barks, may chew
time_alone.quote: We wouldn't recommend leaving your Beagle alone if you can avoid it.
time_alone.notes: PDSA (S115): 'Try to avoid leaving them alone and if you have to make sure there is plenty to keep them occupied.'; 'Beagles can be a little more vocal than other dogs when left alone so you may not realise they bark a lot.' → no often_alone tag.

other_pets.value: fine with other pets if socialised early; not alone with smaller pets
other_pets.quote: If your Beagle has been socialised with other pets from an early age, they will be fine with other pets in the home although we don't advise leaving them alone with smaller pets.
other_pets.notes: Conditional → no other_pets tag. Cats not mentioned.

chewing.value: may chew things when left alone and bored
chewing.quote: When left alone, Beagles can become distressed and bored which means they tend to bark a lot and may even chew things they shouldn't.
chewing.notes: PDSA (S115). Basis of the chews_when_bored tag.

food_motivation.notes: No Beagle-specific food-motivation statement found. Obesity is the most common disorder in UK primary care and the authors advise 'special emphasis on care related to bodyweight control' (S116; health.obesity) — but the food_motivated_weight chip says 'loves food', which no source states → no tag. PDSA (S115): 'Treats shouldn't make up more than 10% of their calories or they can unbalance their diet.'

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; percentages stay here and are never shown in the app, the register export or audience docs. Not a welfare-concern breed: RKC Breed Watch Category 1, 'Currently no points of concern specific to this breed have been identified for special attention by judges' (S113); Colour Watch Category 0. Main UK primary-care topics: bodyweight and teeth (S116).

obesity.value: obesity is the most common recorded disorder — weight control and dental care are priorities
obesity.quote: should put special emphasis on care related to bodyweight control and dental hygiene in Beagles.
obesity.notes: O'Neill et al. 2025 (S116) Conclusions (sentence as returned, starts mid-sentence). Results: obesity 24.27 %, periodontal disease 17.78 % (research only). RVC Clinical Connections (S117) repeats it. PDSA (S115): 'You'll need to feed them a complete, balanced dog food to keep them slim and healthy.'

epilepsy.quote: Epilepsy – a brain disorder which can lead to seizures.

back_ivdd.quote: Intervertebral disc disease – abnormality of the discs that provide cushioning between the vertebrae (back bones).

ears.value: ear infections (otitis externa)
ears.quote: Otitis Externa - where the ear canal becomes inflamed/infected, causing pain and irritation.
ears.notes: PDSA (S115). O'Neill 2025 (S116): otitis externa among the five most common disorders (11.18 %, research only).

other_conditions.value: meningitis, hypothyroidism, certain cancers, eye conditions incl. cherry eye
other_conditions.quote: Some eye conditions, including cherry eye.
other_conditions.notes: PDSA health list headings (S115): 'Meningitis', 'Hypothyroidism', 'Certain cancers.', eye conditions. O'Neill 2025 (S116): most common cause of death at group level neoplasia (research only).

dna_tests.value: DNA tests before breeding: Lafora's, NCCD (good practice); FVIID, IGS-2, MLS (best practice)
dna_tests.quote: We strongly recommend that breeders, at a minimum, conduct these tests before breeding
dna_tests.notes: RKC breed page (S113) health section (test names as returned).

common_disorders_2025.value: obesity, periodontal disease, overgrown nails, otitis externa, anal sac impaction
common_disorders_2025.notes: O'Neill et al. 2025 (S116): obesity 24.27 %, periodontal disease 17.78 %, overgrown nails 11.61 %, otitis externa 11.18 %, anal sac impaction 10.59 % (as summarised by the tool). Research only — never shown in the app or register.

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table (S35, tier C): rank 72, tied with the Mastiff, under 'Lowest Degree of Working/Obedience Intelligence'. Coren's own article (S34) could not be fetched in this run (not reachable through the fetch tool) — runbook: rank from S35. Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

coren_tier.notes: Tier 'Lowest Degree of Working/Obedience Intelligence' = ranks 70–79. Tier definitions from Wikipedia; verify in book. Coren ranks obedience to commands — a scent hound that follows its nose ranks low; not a measure of 'cleverness'.

training_notes.quote: Beagles can be mischievous characters so it's important to start positive, reward-based training as soon as possible.
training_notes.notes: PDSA (S115). FCI / RKC (S111, S114): 'Alert, intelligent and of even temperament.'

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value — see proposed_game_parameters.beagle.learning_multiplier (0.5, runbook rule).

general.value: sturdy, compactly built hound, quality without coarseness
general.quote: A sturdy, compactly built hound, conveying the impression of quality without coarseness.
general.notes: FCI (S111): 'A sturdy, compactly-built hound, conveying the impression of quality without coarseness.'

colours.quote: No other colours are permissible. Tip of stern white.
colours.notes: RKC standard (S114) and FCI (S111): 'Tricolour (black, tan and white); blue, white and tan; badger pied; hare pied; lemon pied; lemon and white;' / 'red and white; tan and white; black and white; all white.' / 'With the exception of all white, all the above mentioned colours can be found as mottle.' RKC breed page (S113): Colour Watch 'Category 0: Breeds with no NBS colour registration options.' Frequencies: not sourced.

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). No colour frequencies. Draw over a subset of the standard colours with tricolour highest (portrait default), then tan and white, lemon and white, red and white; all with the white tail tip (S114); never a non-standard colour.

coat.value: short, dense and weatherproof
coat.quote: Short, dense and weatherproof.
coat.notes: FCI (S111): 'Hair: Short, dense and weatherproof.' RKC breed page (S113): 'Coat length: Short'.

ears.value: long, rounded tip, set low, hanging close to the cheeks
ears.quote: Long, with rounded tip, reaching nearly to end of nose when drawn out.
ears.notes: RKC / FCI: 'Set on low, fine in texture and hanging gracefully close to cheeks.'

eyes.value: dark brown or hazel, fairly large, mild appealing expression
eyes.quote: Dark brown or hazel, fairly large, not deep set or prominent, set well apart with mild, appealing expression.

standard_poodle._note: Added 2026-10-10 (M5-R10-07, unattended run). Pages were partly returned as paraphrase — only passages the tool returned in quotation marks are used as quotes. The FCI standard covers four Poodle varieties; this entry is the Standard (large) variety only, which the RKC lists as its own breed 'Poodle (Standard)'. Lifespan: McMillan 2024 (S54) does not name any Poodle in its text / corrected Fig. 3 legend; the Dogs Trust life-expectancy table of the same study (S123) has a single 'Poodle' row (14.0 y) that pools all varieties — not variety-specific, so not used for the Standard (size drives longevity); no VetCompass Standard Poodle median found → runbook rule: RKC lower bound 'Over 12 years' (S120). Weight: neither the FCI (S118) nor the RKC (S121) standard gives a weight; PDSA (S122, tier B, 'Poodle' page, size Large) is the only weight range. Woodgreen and AKC pages not found / not attempted.

dachshund._note: Added 2026-10-10 (M5-R10-08, unattended run). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-10; spot-check before import (sources.md S124–S130, reused S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45). This entry is the STANDARD-size Dachshund (FCI variety a 'Standard'; RKC 'Dachshund (Smooth Haired)', one of six UK varieties that 'all share the same breed standard, divided by size and coat', S125); the portrait and the app use the smooth coat. Miniature values are recorded as alternatives only. The FCI standard PDF (148g04-en) could not be read (redirect loop https↔http, 2026-10-10) → identity from the FCI nomenclature page (S124), appearance and weight from the RKC standard (S126). Lifespan: McMillan 2024 names only the 'Miniature Dachshund' (14.0 y, via press S130); no standard-size McMillan / VetCompass median found → runbook rule: RKC lower bound 'Over 12 years' (S125). Welfare-concern breed (runbook §3): long-backed, short-legged conformation → intervertebral disc disease (BVA S128, RKC IVDD screening scheme S125, PDSA S127 / S129) → new consider tag `back_spine`. No advice against showing dachshunds in advertising found (BVA S128, excerpts; UFAW not fetchable) → stays in marketing; spot-check S128 before a campaign.

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; never shown in the app as a statistic. Colour Watch 'Category 2: Breeds with >2 to 10% registered NBS colours' (S125); the RKC refuses registrations from certain dapple matings because of vision / hearing risks (S125) → the app and portraits never draw dapple.

colours.quote: Nose and nails black in all colours except chocolate/tan and chocolate dapple where they are brown.
colours.notes: RKC standard colour section (S126, list paraphrased as returned): red (may have black hairs), black or chocolate with tan markings, dapple; brindle and cream only in certain varieties; 'In all colours no white permissible, save for a small patch on chest which is permitted but not desirable.'; double dapple, Isabella, blue, piebald and tricolour unacceptable. Game: red, black and tan, chocolate and tan only — never dapple (RKC dapple-gene registration restriction, S125), never white, piebald or tricolour. Frequencies: not sourced.

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). Red highest (portrait default), then black and tan, then chocolate and tan; never dapple.

coat.value: smooth: dense, short and smooth; skin loose and supple, little or no wrinkle
coat.quote: Smooth Haired: Dense, short and smooth.
coat.notes: RKC standard (S126): 'Skin loose and supple, but fitting closely all over without dewlap and little or no wrinkle.' Long- and wire-haired varieties exist (S125) — not used in the game (smooth only).

ears.value: set high, broad, moderate length, well rounded, mobile
ears.quote: Set high, and not too far forward. Broad, of moderate length, and well rounded (not pointed or folded).
ears.notes: RKC standard (S126).

eyes.value: medium size, almond-shaped, set obliquely; dark (lighter in chocolates)
eyes.quote: Medium size, almond-shaped, set obliquely. Dark except in chocolates, where they can be lighter.
eyes.notes: RKC standard (S126). Dapple 'wall' eyes not used (no dapple).

nose.value: long head, conical from above, tapering to the nose; black nose (brown in chocolate)
nose.quote: Long, appearing conical when seen from above; viewed from the side, tapering uniformly to tip of nose.
nose.notes: RKC standard head and skull (S126); nose colour: 'Nose and nails black in all colours except chocolate/tan and chocolate dapple where they are brown.'

tail.value: continues the line of the spine, slightly curved, not carried above the topline
tail.quote: Continues line of spine, but slightly curved, without kink or twist,
tail.notes: RKC standard (S126); not carried above the topline nor touching the ground at rest (paraphrase as returned).

body.value: moderately long and full muscled, back reasonably level
body.notes: RKC standard (S126): 'Sloping shoulders, back reasonably level, blending harmoniously between withers and slightly arched loin.' Game portrait: moderate length with ground clearance — no exaggerated length.

suitability._note: Source = RKC breed-page fields (S125, Dachshund (Smooth Haired)), RKC standard (S126) and PDSA (S127). Woodgreen page not looked up; AKC trait ratings not attempted (same as the earlier breeds).

australian_shepherd._note: Added 2026-10-10 (M5-R10-09, unattended run). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-10; spot-check before import (sources.md S131–S135, reused S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45). The RKC breed standard page (royalkennelclub.com/breed-standards/pastoral/australian-shepherd/) could not be fetched in this run (fetch-tool provenance refusal) → appearance from the FCI standard (S131), suitability from the RKC breed page (S133) and PDSA (S134). Neither the FCI standard nor the RKC breed page gives a weight → adult weight from PDSA (S134, tier B) only. Lifespan: McMillan 2024 (S135) names the Australian Shepherd only as a tip label in the Fig. 5 phylogeny, with no value; the Dogs Trust breed table (S123) was not reachable this run; no VetCompass Australian Shepherd median found (Teng et al. 2022 life tables cover 18 other breeds) → runbook rule: RKC lower bound 'Over 10 years' (S133; PDSA S134 the same). Not a welfare-concern breed: RKC Breed Watch Category 1 (S133). Merle is a standard colour (FCI S131); the RKC does not register puppies from a merle-to-merle mating because of 'impaired vision and hearing' (S133) — recorded under health, no tag.

identity.value: FCI No. 342, Group 1 Section 1 (Sheepdogs), USA
identity.quote: Group: n°1 - Chiens de berger et de bouvier (sauf chiens de bouvier suisses); Section: Chiens de berger; Country of origin: ETATS-UNIS
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S132, French-language fields as returned): standard number 342; 'Non soumise à épreuve de travail' (no working trial); definitive acceptance '21/05/2007'; valid standard '26/03/2009'. FCI standard PDF (S131): 'CLASSIFICATION F.C.I.: Group 1 Sheepdogs and Cattle dogs (except Swiss Cattle dogs)', 'Section 1 Sheepdogs', 'Without working trial.', 'ORIGIN: U.S.A.' Quote assembled from the nomenclature fields.

size_class.notes: PDSA (S134) key facts: body size 'Medium' — sources agree. FCI height 46–58 cm (S131); PDSA weight 18–29 kg (S134).

fci.quote: The preferred height for males is 20-23 inches (51-58 cm), females 18-21 inches (46-53 cm).
fci.notes: FCI (S131): 'Quality is not to be sacrificed in favour of size.'

pdsa_average.notes: PDSA key-facts box (value as returned; label wording not returned verbatim). One range for both sexes.

pdsa.notes: PDSA key-facts box (value as returned; label wording not returned verbatim), one range for both sexes. The FCI standard (S131) gives no weight ('The standard gives no weight figures for either sex', tool summary); the RKC breed page (S133) gives none; RKC and AKC standards not read. Tier B — the only weight range found.

salt_category.notes: Category assignment by weight is ours (general_by_size.size_classes.salt_2017_bands_kg, S8): 18–29 kg spans the medium-large bands. Salt 2017 breed list not checked.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. PDSA 18–29 kg (S134) = 39.7–63.9 lb → mostly the 'Medium' class (the top of the range touches 'Large (59–99 pounds): 15–18 months'); RKC / PDSA size 'Medium' (S133, S134) → 12–15 months, as for the Border Collie.

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Australian Shepherd growth curve found.

rkc.notes: RKC breed page (S133). PDSA key facts (S134): 'Over 10 years' — same.

mcmillan_2024.notes: McMillan et al. 2024 (S135, published version) names the 'Australian Shepherd' only as a tip label of the Fig. 5 phylogeny; no median in the text or legends (checked 2026-10-10). Supplementary Table / Dogs Trust breed table (S123) not reachable this run. UNSOURCED value — verify before replacing the RKC lower bound.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × RKC lower bound 10 y (S133; PDSA 'Over 10 years' agrees, S134) → 0.75 × 10 = 7.5 y = 90 months. Runbook order: McMillan 2024 (no value, S135) → VetCompass median (none found) → RKC lower bound. Dogs Trust rule of thumb > 7 y = 84 months (S14). Provisional until a McMillan / VetCompass median is checked.

adult.quote: Exercise: More than 2 hours per day
adult.notes: PDSA (S134): 'Your Australian Shepherd will need a minimum of two hours exercise every day' (key facts: minimum daily exercise '2 hours') — sources agree on 120.

energy.value: energy to spare; for owners who are on the go
energy.quote: Aussies have energy to spare which is why we’d only recommend having one if you’re on the go just as much as they are.
energy.notes: FCI (S131): 'He is attentive and animated, lithe and agile, solid and muscular without cloddiness.'

temperament.value: intelligent working dog with strong herding and guarding instincts; even disposition, good natured; may be reserved at first
temperament.quote: The Australian Shepherd is an intelligent working dog of strong herding and guarding instincts.
temperament.notes: FCI (S131): 'With an even disposition, he is good natured, seldom quarrelsome.' 'He may be somewhat reserved in initial meetings.' Disqualifying: 'Aggressive or overly shy'.

family.value: can be a really good family pet in the right household; not recommended with smaller children (herding — may knock them over)
family.quote: Aussies can make really good family pets in the right household.
family.notes: PDSA (S134): 'we wouldn't recommend an Australian Shepherd if you have smaller children' because 'they may accidentally knock them over.'; 'Always supervise your dog with children and vulnerable adults.' → family_pet + may_herd_children; never children / small_children.

herding_children.quote: because of their strong herding instinct, they can get the urge to herd children in the home
herding_children.notes: PDSA (S134); the page adds that this may involve gently bumping into them (paraphrase). 'The herding instinct is strong with Aussies, so you'll need to keep them on the lead when walking out in the countryside.'

mental_stimulation.value: needs plenty of exercise and mental stimulation; puzzle games and training sessions
mental_stimulation.quote: The best way to prevent your dog from barking for no reason is to make sure they're getting plenty of exercise and mental stimulation throughout the day.
mental_stimulation.notes: PDSA (S134): 'Puzzle games and interesting training sessions are a great way to keep them occupied!'

time_alone.value: should not be left alone; ideally someone at home all day; may suffer separation anxiety
time_alone.quote: Ideally, Aussies need someone at home with them all day because they need to be kept active.
time_alone.notes: PDSA (S134): 'Because Australian Shepherds form close ties with their owners, they can suffer with separation anxiety if left alone.' → no often_alone tag.

other_pets.value: fine with dogs, cats and other pets they grew up with; may try to herd them
other_pets.quote: Aussies are known to get on well with any cats or other pets they have grown up with, however they may be tempted to herd them at times.
other_pets.notes: PDSA (S134): 'As long as your Australian Shepherd has been socialised with other dogs from a young age they should be fine with other dogs.' Conditional → no other_pets tag.

boredom_chewing.value: chews when bored or left alone
boredom_chewing.quote: An Aussie left to their own devices could develop bad habits like barking or chewing things around the home.
boredom_chewing.notes: PDSA (S134): 'If they get bored, they can get into all kinds of mischief around the home (which usually involves a lot of chewing!).' Basis of the chews_when_bored tag.

food_motivation.notes: No breed-specific food-motivation statement found. PDSA (S134): 'Treats shouldn’t make up more than 10% of their daily calorie intake as this can unbalance their diet.' → no food_motivated_weight tag.

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages for this breed were collected. Not a welfare-concern breed: RKC Breed Watch Category 1, 'Currently no points of concern specific to this breed have been identified for special attention by judges' (S133); Colour Watch Category 0. Main topics: hips and elbows, inherited eye disease, MDR1 drug sensitivity, merle-to-merle breeding (S133, S134).

hip_elbow_dysplasia.value: hip and elbow dysplasia — choose puppies from hip- and elbow-scored parents
hip_elbow_dysplasia.quote: Hip testing (for hip dysplasia) using the BVA/KC Hip Dysplasia Scheme
hip_elbow_dysplasia.notes: RKC best practice (S133): 'Hip testing (for hip dysplasia) using the BVA/KC Hip Dysplasia Scheme', 'Elbow testing (for elbow dysplasia) using the BVA/KC Elbow Dysplasia Scheme'. PDSA health list (S134) 'Hip dysplasia': 'where the hip joint doesn’t fit together perfectly, which will eventually lead to arthritis.' and 'Elbow dysplasia' ('where the elbow joint doesn’t fit together perfectly, which will eventually lead to arthritis.'). Not a Breed Watch point → no hips_hind_legs tag (that chip is for a recognised conformation concern).

eyes.value: inherited eye disease: collie eye anomaly, hereditary cataracts, progressive retinal atrophy
eyes.quote: an abnormality in the back of the eye.
eyes.notes: PDSA (S134) 'Collie eye anomaly' (quote) and 'Certain eye conditions': 'such as inherited eye conditions (including cataracts and progressive retinal atrophy) which can lead to blindness.' RKC (S133): 'DNA test for Collie eye anomaly/ choroidal hypoplasia (CEA/CH)', 'DNA test for Hereditary cataracts (HC-HSF4)', 'DNA test for Progressive retinal atrophy (prcd-PRA)', 'Eye testing using the BVA/KC/ISDS Eye Scheme'.

mdr1.value: multi-drug sensitivity (MDR1) — some medicines need care; tell the vet
mdr1.quote: an inherited condition that makes affected dogs particularly sensitive to certain drugs.
mdr1.notes: PDSA (S134) 'Multi drug sensitivity'. RKC best practice (S133): 'DNA test for Multi-drug resistance (MDR1)'.

cobalamin_malabsorption.quote: a genetic condition where vitamin B12 cannot be absorbed in the gut, leading to poor growth, weakness and blood problems.

merle_to_merle.value: no merle-to-merle breeding — impaired vision and hearing
merle_to_merle.quote: This is due to associated health risks of impaired vision and hearing associated with the merle gene in this breed.
merle_to_merle.notes: RKC breed page (S133): 'With effect from 1st January 2013, The Kennel Club will not register puppies whelped from a merle to merle mating'. Merle itself is a standard colour (FCI S131). The game draws one merle or solid adult; nothing about breeding is simulated.

dna_tests.value: DNA tests before breeding: CEA/CH (good practice); HC-HSF4, MDR1, prcd-PRA + hip, elbow and eye schemes (best practice)
dna_tests.quote: We strongly recommend that breeders, at a minimum, conduct these tests before breeding
dna_tests.notes: RKC breed page (S133) health section (test names as returned).

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table (S35, tier C): rank 42, tied with the Kuvasz, under 'Average Working/Obedience Intelligence' (quote reassembled from the row as returned). Coren's own article (S34) lists only the top / bottom 10 — runbook: rank from S35. Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

coren_tier.quote: Understanding of new commands: 25 to 40 repetitions.; Obey first command: 50% of the time or better.
coren_tier.notes: Tier 'Average' = ranks 40–54. Tier definitions from Wikipedia; verify in book. Coren ranks obedience to commands, not 'cleverness'.

training_notes.value: clever; needs positive, reward-based training from a young age; easy to train for experienced owners
training_notes.quote: Australian Shepherds are clever dogs who need positive, reward-based training from a young age.
training_notes.notes: PDSA (S134): 'Aussies are really clever dogs and so can be easy to train for owners with a lot of experience.'; 'If you are a first-time owner or need some extra help with training, we'd recommend taking them to accredited training classes.' FCI (S131): 'an intelligent working dog'.

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value — see proposed_game_parameters.australian_shepherd.learning_multiplier (1.0, runbook rule).

general.value: well balanced, slightly longer than tall, medium size and bone; attentive, lithe and agile
general.quote: The Australian Shepherd is well balanced, slightly longer than tall, of medium size and bone,
general.notes: FCI (S131): 'with colouring that offers variety and individuality.' 'He is attentive and animated, lithe and agile, solid and muscular without cloddiness.'

colours.unit: list (each with or without white and/or tan markings)
colours.quote: Blue merle, black, red merle, red – all with or without white markings and/or tan markings,
colours.notes: FCI (S131): 'with no order of preference.' White limits: 'The hairline of a white collar does not exceed the point of the withers at the skin.' 'White on the head should not predominate, and the eyes must be fully surrounded by colour and pigment.' Disqualifying: 'White body splashes in all colours'. Merle is standard here (runbook §3 colour rule).

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). The FCI standard ranks no colour ('no order of preference', S131); blue merle with white and tan markings is drawn highest (portrait default), then black, red merle and red, each with white and tan markings; never white body splashes, white around the eyes or a predominantly white head.

coat.value: medium length, straight to wavy, weather resistant; moderate mane and frill
coat.quote: Of medium texture, straight to wavy, weather resistant and of medium length.
coat.notes: FCI (S131): 'Hair is short and smooth on the head, ears, front of forelegs and below the hocks.' 'There is a moderate mane and frill, more pronounced in dogs than in bitches.' RKC breed page (S133): 'Coat length: Medium'.

ears.value: triangular, moderate size, set high, breaking forward and over (or to the side as a rose ear)
ears.quote: Triangular, of moderate size and leather, set high on the head.
ears.notes: FCI (S131): 'At full attention they break forward and over, or to the side as a rose ear.'

eyes.value: brown, blue, amber or any combination incl. flecks and marbling; almond shaped
eyes.quote: Brown, blue, amber or any variation or combination thereof, including flecks and marbling.
eyes.notes: FCI (S131): 'Almond shaped, not protruding nor sunken.' Black eye rims in blue merles / blacks, liver in red merles / reds.

nose.value: black nose in blue merles and blacks, liver in red merles and reds; moderate, well-defined stop; muzzle equal to or slightly shorter than the back skull
nose.quote: Blue merles and blacks have black pigmentation on the nose (and lips).
nose.notes: FCI (S131): 'Red merles and reds have liver (brown) pigmentation on the nose (and lips).'; stop 'Moderate, well-defined.'; muzzle 'Equal in length or slightly shorter than the back skull.'

tail.value: straight, naturally long or naturally short
tail.quote: Straight, naturally long or naturally short.
tail.notes: FCI (S131): 'When docked (in countries where this practice is not forbidden), or naturally short, not to exceed 10 cm.' The game draws a natural long tail (no docking).

rkc_grooming.notes: PDSA (S134): 'a brush a few times a week' → frequent_grooming.

havanese._note: Added 2026-10-10 (M5-R10-10, unattended run). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-10; spot-check before import (sources.md S136–S141, reused S10, S11, S14, S35, S45). identity.value: FCI No. 250, Group 9 Section 1 (Bichons and related breeds), Cuba

Neither the FCI nor the RKC standard gives a weight → adult weight from PDSA (S147, tier B) only. Lifespan: McMillan 2024 / the Dogs Trust breed table (S123) were not reachable this run → runbook rule: VetCompass median 13.4 y (O'Neill et al. 2019, S148; RVC summary S149). Welfare-concern breed under the runbook rule: RKC Breed Watch 'Category 2' with 'Signs of dermatitis irritation and/or hair loss or scarring from previous dermatitis' (S146) → new consider tag sensitive_skin (PDSA S147 'Westies are known to suffer from skin allergies'). McMillan 2024 (S54) and the Dogs Trust breed table (S123) not reachable this run — runbook rule: else a VetCompass median. health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; percentages from O'Neill et al. 2019 (S148) stay here only and are never shown in the app, the export or audience docs. Welfare-concern breed (runbook §3): RKC Breed Watch 'Category 2' (S144) with the points 'Misplaced canine teeth' and 'Signs of dermatitis irritation and/or hair loss or scarring from previous dermatitis' (S146); the RKC breed page notes 'This breed can be affected by conformational concerns' (S144, as returned). The RKC page lists no breed-specific pre-breeding screening and no DNA package (S144, paraphrase). Main topics: skin allergies (PDSA S147, RKC S146, VetCompass S148), Westie lung (PDSA S147; lower respiratory tract disease as a common cause of death, S148 / S149), jaw bone disorder, kneecaps, dry eye, Legg-Perthes (PDSA S147).

sensitive_skin.value: skin allergies / dermatitis — a recognised point of concern in the breed
sensitive_skin.quote: Westies are known to suffer from skin allergies, so speak to your vet before buying a shampoo.
sensitive_skin.notes: PDSA health list (S147): 'Skin allergies'. RKC Breed Watch (S146): 'Signs of dermatitis irritation and/or hair loss or scarring from previous dermatitis'. RKC breed standard (S145) coat: 'Free from obvious skin problems.' VetCompass (S148): allergic skin disorder among the most prevalent specific disorders (percentage research only); RVC summary (S149): 'Skin problems are often considered common in Westies. However the prevalence in this study was lower than might be expected.'

westie_lung.value: Westie lung (idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis); lower respiratory tract disease in older dogs
westie_lung.quote: Breathing problems known as Westie Lung (Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis)
westie_lung.notes: RVC summary (S149): 'Westies appear predisposed to lower respiratory tract disease, which owners should be aware of as their Westie ages.' O'Neill 2019 (S148): lower respiratory tract among the most common grouped causes of death (statistic research only).

jaw_bone.notes: PDSA health list (S147). (Known in the literature as craniomandibular osteopathy — our note, not from the source.)

bernese_mountain_dog._note: Added 2026-10-10 (M5-R10-12, unattended run). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-10; spot-check before import (sources.md S150–S157, reused S8, S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45). Appearance from the FCI standard (S150, valid standard 25.03.2003) and the RKC breed standard (S153); suitability from the RKC breed page (S152), PDSA (S154) and Woodgreen (S155). Neither the FCI nor the RKC standard gives a weight → adult weight from PDSA (S154, tier B). Lifespan: McMillan 2024 has a Bernese value only in its supplementary table (not reachable: the published text S135 names the breed only as a Fig. 5 tip label; the Author Correction S54 does not list it; the Dogs Trust table PDFs returned a fetch error), there is no VetCompass Bernese paper and the RKC band 'Under 10 years' (S152) has no lower bound → the senior boundary uses the peer-reviewed breed median of Klopfenstein et al. 2016 (8.4 y, Switzerland, S156), the closest equivalent of the runbook's 'VetCompass median' row; Claude's suggestion, seeded verified=false — waiting for David (proposed_game_parameters.bernese_mountain_dog.senior_boundary_months). Wikipedia (S157, tier C) quotes McMillan 2024 as 10.1 y — recorded as an alternative only. Not a conformation welfare breed (RKC Breed Watch 'Category 1', S152). Coren rank 22 (S35, 'Excellent') → learning 1.5. Only colour: tricolour (FCI / RKC).

Fields as returned (assembled here, paraphrase): breed 'BERNER SENNENHUND' (45); group 'n°2 - Chiens de type Pinscher et Schnauzer - Molossoïdes et chiens de montagne et de bouvier suisses'; country of origin 'SUISSE'; 'Non soumise à épreuve de travail selon la Nomenclature des races de la FCI' (no working trial); definitive acceptance 26/07/1954; valid standard 25/03/2003. FCI standard PDF (S150): 'ORIGIN: Switzerland.' Section 3 per the FCI group structure (the section number was not returned verbatim — paraphrase).

median_ch.quote: The median life expectancy of all dogs was 8.4 years (IQR, 6.9–9.7).
median_ch.notes: Klopfenstein M., Howard J., Rossetti M., Geissbühler U. (2016), BMC Veterinary Research 12:153 (S156): Swiss population, 389 dogs (table: 'All dogs | All | 389 | … | 8.40 |'); males 7.73 y (n 162), females 8.78 y (n 227) as returned from Table 1; 'the most frequent causes of death were neoplasia (222/381, 58.3 %)' (research only). Not a UK population — used because McMillan 2024 (S54 / S135) and a VetCompass median were not reachable and the RKC band has no lower bound. Consistent with the breed-page bands 'Under 10 years' (S152), 'Up to 10 years' (S154) and '7-10 years' (S155).

mcmillan_2024.notes: McMillan et al. 2024 (UK) as quoted by Wikipedia (S157, tier C): 'A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 10.1 years compared to 12 years for crossbreeds and 12.7 years for purebreds.' The paper's own text (S135) and the Author Correction (S54) give no Bernese value; the Dogs Trust table PDF returned a fetch error. Tier C → alternative only, not used. Verify in McMillan 2024 Supplementary Table.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × 8.4 y (S156) → 0.75 × 8.4 = 6.3 y = 75.6 → 76 months. With McMillan 2024 via Wikipedia (10.1 y, S157, tier C): 0.75 × 10.1 = 7.575 y = 90.9 → 91 months. With the Woodgreen lower bound 7 y (S155): 63 months. Dogs Trust rule of thumb > 7 y = 84 months (S14). Provisional until McMillan 2024 is checked.

Main topics: a short life (RKC 'Under 10 years' S152, PDSA S154, Woodgreen S155, S156), cancers (PDSA 'Certain cancers.', neoplasia the most frequent cause of death in S156), hip and elbow dysplasia (RKC good-practice BVA/KC schemes S152, PDSA S154), GDV, degenerative myelopathy, PRA, cruciate disease, hot spots (PDSA S154).

siberian_husky._note: Added 2026-10-10 (M5-R10-13, unattended run). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-10; spot-check before import (sources.md S158–S165, reused S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45). The PDSA page (S162) was returned partly as paraphrase with quotes capped at ~120 characters — only passages the tool returned in quotation marks are used as quotes; longer sentences are cut where the tool cut them. Every S162 quote used (energy, children, exercise, escaping, chewing, shedding, grooming, hip dysplasia) was re-checked character for character on a second fetch (2026-10-10, review of PR #161) — all present verbatim, including the page's own typo 'The have heaps of energy'. McMillan et al. 2024 (S54 / S135) names no Siberian Husky in its text or legends; its Supplementary Table 3, the Dogs Trust breed table (S123) and the 'shortest and longest' PDF were not reachable (fetch error 2026-10-10); Teng et al. 2022 (UK life tables) mentions the 'Husky' only in its sample list and probability-of-death sentences, the Husky life table itself (Table 3) was not reachable; no VetCompass Siberian Husky median found — so the lifespan is the RKC lower bound 'Over 10 years' (S160) per the runbook rule. Woodgreen and the AKC breed page were not found / not attempted.

identity.quote: Group: n°5 - Spitz and primitive types; Section: Nordic Sledge Dogs; Country of origin: UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S159): standard number 270; definitive acceptance '9/8/1966'; valid standard '11/14/2022'; 'Not subject to a working trial'. FCI standard PDF (S158): 'Group 5 Spitz and primitive types.', Section 1 'Nordic Sledge Dogs.', origin 'U.S.A.', valid standard '14.11.2022.' Quote assembled from the nomenclature fields as returned.

size_class.notes: PDSA (S162) key facts: 'Size: Large' — conflict; RKC breed page preferred (runbook §2.2). FCI (S158): 'a medium-sized working dog'. FCI height 50.5–60 cm, weight 15.5–28 kg (S158) → the game treats it as a medium dog for the growth class (S10).

fci.notes: FCI (S158): 'Females: 50,5 - 56 cm.' Disqualification: 'Dogs over 60 cm and bitches over 56 cm.'

rkc.quote: Height: dogs: 53-60 cms (21-23½ ins) at withers; bitches: 51-56 cms (20-22 ins) at withers.
rkc.notes: RKC breed standard (S161, last updated 1 April 2025).

akc.quote: Height - Dogs, 21 to 23½ inches at the withers. Bitches, 20 to 22 inches at the withers.
akc.notes: AKC standard (S163, approved February 9, 2021); inches converted to cm (× 2.54) by us.

pdsa_average.notes: PDSA key-facts box (label wording as returned).

fci.quote: Dogs: 20,5 - 28 kg.
fci.notes: FCI (S158): 'Females: 15,5 - 23 kg.' Fault: 'Any appearance of excessive bone or weight should be penalized.' Game range 15.5–28 kg (both sexes).

rkc.quote: Weight: dogs: 20.-27 kgs (45-60 lbs); bitches: 16-23 kgs (35-50 lbs).
rkc.notes: RKC breed standard (S161); the dog value is returned as '20.-27' (typo on the page; 45 lb = 20.4 kg).

akc.quote: Weight - Dogs, 45 to 60 pounds. Bitches, 35 to 50 pounds.
akc.notes: AKC standard (S163); pounds converted to kg (× 0.4536) by us.

pdsa.notes: PDSA key-facts box, one range for both sexes.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. FCI 15.5–28 kg (S158) = 34–62 lb → mostly the 'Medium' class (the top of the male range touches 'Large (59–99 pounds): 15–18 months'); FCI 'a medium-sized working dog' (S158) → 12–15 months, as for the Border Collie and the Australian Shepherd. Edge: the FCI male maximum 28 kg ≈ 62 lb sits in the 'Large (59–99 pounds): 15–18 months' class; the game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 120 min is reached at 12 months either way).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Siberian Husky growth curve found.

rkc.notes: RKC breed page (S160). PDSA key facts (S162): 'Average lifespan: Over 10 years' — same.

mcmillan_2024.notes: McMillan et al. 2024 (S135 / S54) names no Siberian Husky in its text or legends (checked via the nature.com article 2026-10-10: 'neither Siberian Husky nor Husky appears'); Supplementary Table 3 and the Dogs Trust breed table (S123) not reachable this run. UNSOURCED value — verify before replacing the RKC lower bound.

finland_average.unit: years (average life expectancy, Finnish Kennel Club data 2012–2021)
finland_average.quote: The average life expectancy according to the Finnish statistics is 9 years 9 months.
finland_average.notes: IPFD / DogWellNet 'Get a GRIHP!' (S165) citing Finnish Kennel Club mortality data; also 'Dogs that die because of old age usually reach the age of 13 years.' A Finnish average, not a UK median — recorded as an alternative only (0.75 × 9.75 y × 12 = 87.75 → 88 months); not used by the runbook rule.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × RKC lower bound 10 y (S160; PDSA 'Over 10 years' agrees, S162) → 0.75 × 10 = 7.5 y = 90 months. Runbook order: McMillan 2024 (no value reachable) → VetCompass median (none found) → RKC lower bound. Alternatives: 88 (Finnish average 9.75 y, S165), 84 (Dogs Trust > 7 y, S14). Provisional until a McMillan / VetCompass median is checked.

adult.quote: Exercise: More than 2 hours per day
adult.notes: PDSA (S162): 'Your Husky will need a minimum of two hours of exercise every day.' (key facts: minimum exercise '2 hours') — sources agree on 120.

energy.quote: The have heaps of energy and are the perfect pet for active, adventure-loving owners.
energy.notes: Quote as returned (the page's own typo 'The'). FCI (S158): 'quick and light on his feet and free and graceful in action'; RKC breed page (S160): 'The lightest and fastest of the sled dogs.'

spread_and_vary.value: spread exercise across the day, vary routes; early mornings / evenings in warm weather
spread_and_vary.quote: We’d recommend spreading this across the day and vary your walking routes so they don’t get bored.
spread_and_vary.notes: PDSA (S162): 'Early mornings and evenings are probably the best times to go for long walks and runs.'

temperament.quote: The characteristic temperament of the Siberian Husky is friendly and gentle, but also alert and outgoing.
temperament.notes: AKC (S163) the same sentence; RKC standard (S161): 'Friendly and gentle, alert and outgoing.' PDSA (S162): 'While they are very intelligent, they’re also independent thinkers'; 'Huskies really thrive off company because they are so social.'; 'they do have a reputation for howling and singing to their owners whenever the mood takes them.'

family.value: suits adult-only households or households with teenagers; not recommended with smaller children (may knock them over)
family.quote: They suit adult-only households or households with teenagers.
family.notes: PDSA (S162): 'we wouldn’t recommend getting a Husky if you have smaller children as they could knock them over accidentally.' → no family_pet / children / small_children tag.

time_alone.value: does not cope well alone; known for separation anxiety
time_alone.quote: Huskies really don’t cope well on their own
time_alone.notes: PDSA (S162): 'The breed is known for suffering from separation anxiety' → no often_alone tag.

other_pets.value: fine with other dogs if socialised young; not with smaller pets (high prey drive)
other_pets.quote: Huskies have such a high prey drive that we wouldn’t recommend keeping them with smaller pets
other_pets.notes: PDSA (S162): '…even if they have been introduced from a young age.'; 'Huskies love company so as long as they have been socialised from a young age, they should get along fine with other dogs.' Conditional → no other_pets tag. Cats not mentioned. → chases_small_pets (David 2026-10-12).

chewing.quote: so you may find they chew furniture to let you know.
chewing.notes: PDSA (S162): 'They are known for being destructive, especially when they get stressed from being alone,' — the chewing sentence ('so you may find they chew furniture to let you know.') follows it on the page. Like the West Highland White Terrier, the trigger is stress / boredom when left alone. Basis of the chews_when_bored tag.

escaping.value: escape artists — dig under and get over fences; need a very secure garden with high fences
escaping.quote: Owners need a very secure garden with high fences as Huskies are known for getting up to mischief

food_motivation.notes: No Siberian Husky food-motivation statement found. PDSA (S162): 'You should feed them a good quality, commercially available, complete dog food.' RKC Breed Watch points 'Too fat' / 'Too thin' (S164) concern show condition, not appetite → no food_motivated_weight tag.

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages for this breed are stored for the app (the Finnish / Swedish screening shares in S165 stay out of the app, the export and audience docs). Not a conformation welfare-concern breed: RKC Breed Watch 'Category 2' (S164) lists only 'Too fat' and 'Too thin' — body condition at shows, not an exaggerated conformation; the FCI standard asks for a moderate dog ('Any appearance of excessive bone or weight should be penalized.', S158).

breed_watch.notes: RKC Breed Watch (S164) heading 'Siberian Husky - Category 2'; points 'Too fat', 'Too thin'. Explanatory text: 'Particular points of concern for individual breeds may include features not specifically highlighted in the breed standard'. RKC breed page (S160): 'Breed Watch: Category 2'. Not conformation-related → the welfare-concern rule does not apply.

hip_dysplasia.value: hip dysplasia — hip screening of breeding dogs

hip_dysplasia.notes: PDSA health list (S162, wording as returned). RKC breed page (S160): Best Practice 'Hip testing (for hip dysplasia) using the BVA/RKC Hip Dysplasia Scheme'. Not the hips_hind_legs chip: no RKC / vet association names hind conformation as a concern for this breed.

rottweiler._note: Added 2026-10-11 (M5-R10-19, unattended run — first breed appended after the 20: AKC 2024 No. 8, S174). health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; percentages, hazard ratios and 'x times' figures stay here and are never shown in the app, the register export or audience docs. Flat-faced (brachycephalic) welfare breed: PDSA (S180) 'Bulldogs are a severely brachycephalic (flat-faced) breed.'; RKC Breed Watch Category 3 (S182) → brachycephalic_breathing chip (as the French Bulldog) and sensitive_skin chip (Breed Watch skin-fold dermatitis, as the West Highland White Terrier); BVA advises against brachycephalic imagery in advertising (S92) → in the app yes, in marketing no.

RKC breed page (S177): 'The soft tissue in the nose and throat of some brachycephalic dogs may be excessive for the airways'. Standards: RKC (S178) 'Dogs showing respiratory distress or making excessive respiratory noise highly undesirable.'; FCI (S175) 'Dogs showing respiratory distress highly undesirable.' UFAW (S183): flat-faced dogs have a strong chance of 'breathing difficulties, skin fold infections, eye disease, difficulty giving birth and spinal disease.' UK Brachycephalic Working Group (S93) and UFAW (S183): 'Stop and think before buying a flat-faced dog.'

breed_watch.value: RKC Breed Watch Category 3 — points of concern include respiratory difficulty, tail problems, heavy overnose wrinkle, pinched nostrils, too fat, unsound movement, skin-fold dermatitis, eyelid and eye problems

german_shorthaired_pointer._note: Added 2026-10-11 (M5-R10-21, unattended run — appended after the Bulldog: AKC 2024 No. 10, S174 'German Shorthaired Pointers remain at No. 10 from 2023 to 2024.'). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-11; spot-check before import (sources.md S184–S189, reused S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45, S123). The fetch tool capped quotes at ~125 characters on the AKC standard (GSPCA, S186); only passages it returned in quotation marks are used as quotes, condensed passages are marked '(paraphrase)'. The RKC breed page (older address, S187) was returned with several key-fact labels without values (minimum garden size, length of coat, sheds, town or country) and a lifespan value 'Over 10 Years' whose placement was ambiguous — only the fields returned with a clear value are used (Exercise, Size of home, Grooming). The RKC page returned no health-testing section. The PDSA page (S188) is titled 'German Pointer' and covers the shorthaired and wirehaired varieties together; its key facts are used for the breed as a whole. FCI (S184) gives no weight → weight from the AKC standard (S186). Lifespan: McMillan et al. 2024 via the Dogs Trust breed table (S123) — 13.4 years. Woodgreen and AKC trait ratings not attempted.

yorkshire_terrier._note: Added 2026-10-12 (M5-R10-22, unattended run — appended after the German Shorthaired Pointer: AKC 2024 No. 11, S174 table row '11 | Yorkshire Terrier'). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-12; spot-check before import (sources.md S190–S196, reused S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45, S174). The RKC breed page (older address, S192) returned the key-fact labels and values on separate lines; they are quoted as 'Label: value' like the earlier breeds. FCI (S190) and the RKC breed standard (S193) give only an upper weight ('Up to 3,2 kgs') and no height → height from PDSA (S194, average 20 cm). The VetCompass study (S195) describes the UK pet population, which is heavier than the pedigree standard (median 5.06 kg, S196) — background only, never the game weight. Lifespan: McMillan 2024 / the Dogs Trust breed table (S123) not reachable this run → runbook rule: VetCompass median 13.56 y (O'Neill et al. 2025, S195). Not a welfare-concern breed: RKC Breed Watch Category 1 (S192). Woodgreen and AKC trait ratings not attempted.

RVC summary (S196): 'The average lifespan of Yorkshire Terriers was an amazing 13.56 years.' 'Average lifespan did not differ significantly between females and males'. McMillan 2024 (S54) and the Dogs Trust breed table (S123) not reachable this run — runbook rule: else a VetCompass median. Consistent with the breed-page band 'Over 12 years' (S192, S194).

rkc.notes: RKC breed page (S192). PDSA key facts (S194): 'Average lifespan | Over 12 years' — same.

mcmillan_2024.notes: McMillan et al. 2024: the Dogs Trust breed table (S123) is not in this run's reachable set (fetch refused) and the 'shortest and longest' PDF returned a fetch error; the LJMU news page names no Yorkshire Terrier value. UNSOURCED value — verify in McMillan 2024 Supplementary Table before replacing the VetCompass median.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × 13.56 y (S195) → 0.75 × 13.56 = 10.17 y = 122.04 → 122 months. With the breed-page 'over 12 years' (S192): 0.75 × 12 = 9 y = 108 months. Dogs Trust rule of thumb > 7 y = 84 months (S14). Provisional until McMillan 2024 is checked.

adult.quote: Exercise: Up to 30 minutes per day
adult.notes: PDSA (S194): 'Yorkies need around 30 or 40 minutes exercise per day.' (key facts: 'Minimum exercise (per day) | 30 minutes') — RKC preferred (runbook rule), PDSA's lower number agrees; 40 recorded as an alternative in proposed_game_parameters.

energy.value: small but likes to run, fetch and play
energy.quote: Don’t be fooled by their small size – they enjoy running, fetching and playing games just as much as the next dog!
energy.notes: PDSA (S194). Covered by the game's walk and play (M5-R05) — nothing new to build.

temperament.value: alert, intelligent toy terrier; spirited with even disposition
temperament.quote: Alert, intelligent toy terrier. Spirited with even disposition.
temperament.notes: FCI (S190) 'BEHAVIOUR/TEMPERAMENT'; RKC breed standard (S193) the same wording. RKC breed page (S192): 'he still retains some of the features of his terrier background and can account for any domestic rodent'. Disqualifying (FCI): 'Aggressive or overly shy dogs'.

family.value: fine if brought up with children from a young age; better suited to families with older children (fragile bones)
family.quote: They are better suited to families with older children as they have very fragile bones
family.notes: PDSA (S194): 'Yorkshire Terriers should be fine if brought up with children from a young age.' The same paragraph limits it to older children → no `children` / `small_children` tag; new consider tag `fragile_older_children` (runbook new-tag rule). No PDSA 'family pet' sentence → no `family_pet` tag.

time_alone.notes: No breed-specific statement found (RKC S192 and PDSA S194 checked) → no often_alone tag.

other_pets.notes: No statement about other pets (PDSA S194 checked). RKC (S192): can catch 'any domestic rodent' (terrier background) — not a suitability statement → no other_pets tag.

chewing.notes: No breed-specific statement found (PDSA S194 checked) → no chews_when_bored tag.

food_motivation.notes: No breed-specific statement found → no food_motivated_weight tag.

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages are shown anywhere (the VetCompass percentages of S195 / S196 stay in the paper). Not a welfare-concern breed: RKC Breed Watch Category 1, 'Currently no points of concern specific to this breed have been identified for special attention by judges' (S192). Main topics: teeth (S194, S195, S196), kneecaps (S194, S196), windpipe (S194), eyes (S194), liver shunt (S194).

dental.value: dental (periodontal) disease and retained puppy teeth; daily tooth brushing advised
dental.quote: Yorkshire Terriers appear predisposed to dental (periodontal) disease and persistent deciduous teeth.
dental.notes: RVC VetCompass summary (S196) of O'Neill et al. 2025 (S195): 'Dental disease was by far the most common disorder diagnosed in Yorkshire Terriers'; advice: 'Owners are encouraged to undertake daily preventative home care to improve dental health e.g tooth brushing' (as returned, split by the fetch tool). PDSA (S194) health list: 'Dental problems'. Sourced need (daily tooth brushing) → proposed_game_parameters.yorkshire_terrier.tooth_brushing (no tooth-brushing mechanic yet → ROADMAP M5-R15).

luxating_patella.value: luxating patellas — kneecaps slipping out of place
luxating_patella.quote: Luxating patellas - the kneecaps slipping temporarily out of place.
luxating_patella.notes: PDSA health list (S194). RVC summary (S196) lists 'Slipping kneecap' among the most common disorders (chart label, no number used).

tracheal_collapse.value: tracheal collapse — the windpipe loses rigidity
tracheal_collapse.quote: Tracheal collapse – loss of rigidity of the windpipe, causing weakness and collapse.

eyes.value: progressive retinal atrophy, lens luxation, dry eye, distichiasis
eyes.quote: Progressive retinal atrophy – gradual deterioration of the retina of the eye.
eyes.notes: PDSA (S194): 'Lens luxation – dislocation of the lens of the eye.'; dry eye: 'decreased tear production, leading to dry eye and damage to the cornea (surface of the eye).'; distichiasis (paraphrase: extra eyelashes on the eyelid edge irritate the eye).

portosystemic_shunt.quote: abnormal blood circulation, with the blood effectively bypassing the liver and entering general circulation.
portosystemic_shunt.notes: PDSA (S194) health list, 'Portosystemic shunt' (partial line as returned).

legg_perthes.quote: blood supply to the femoral head is depleted, causing destruction of the femoral head.
legg_perthes.notes: PDSA (S194), partial line as returned. Not a Breed Watch point → no hips_hind_legs chip (research only).

other_pdsa.value: bladder stones, atopy, diabetes mellitus, hydrocephalus, Chiari malformation / syringomyelia

other_pdsa.notes: PDSA (S194): 'Atopy – hypersensitivity to certain allergens, causing itching and skin trauma.'; CM/SM 'a painful neurological condition in which fluid-filled cavities develop within the spinal cord near the brain.' (partial line); diabetes mellitus, hydrocephalus (paraphrase). Research only — not exported.

Coren's own top / bottom-10 article (S34) does not list the breed.

Ears 'colour very deep, rich tan'; tail 'darker blue in colour than rest of body'. RKC breed standard (S193) the same. RKC breed page (S192): puppies are born black and tan and become steel blue and tan (paraphrase) — adult portrait only. No other colour (never parti-colour, chocolate, gold or merle).

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). One standard colour → dark steel blue and tan, weight 100 (portrait default).

coat.quote: On body moderately long, perfectly straight (not wavy), glossy;
coat.notes: FCI (S190): 'fine silky texture, not woolly, must never impede movement.' RKC (S193): 'Hair on body moderately long, perfectly straight (not wavy), glossy; fine silky texture, not woolly.' The game draws a natural pet-length coat (not a floor-length show coat).

ears.value: small, V-shaped, carried erect, rich tan
ears.quote: Small, V-shaped, carried erect, not too far apart, covered with short hair, colour very deep, rich tan.
ears.notes: RKC (S193) the same.

eyes.notes: FCI (S190): 'Not prominent. Edge of eyelids dark.'

nose.notes: FCI (S190): skull 'Rather small and flat, not too prominent or round.'; muzzle 'Not too long.' RKC (S193): 'Rather small and flat, not too prominent or round in skull, nor too long in muzzle; black nose.' Not flat-faced.

cane_corso._note: Added 2026-10-12 (M5-R10-23, unattended run — fifth breed appended after the 20: AKC 2024 No. 14 in the full-list table, S174; No. 12 Australian Shepherd and No. 13 Cavalier King Charles Spaniel are already in the app). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-12; spot-check before import (sources.md S197–S201, reused S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45, S174). The breed is not recognised by The Royal Kennel Club (no RKC breed page, no RKC standard, no Breed Watch entry) and is 'a relatively uncommon breed in the UK' (PDSA S199): there is no VetCompass breed paper and no McMillan 2024 value was reachable (the Dogs Trust 'shortest and longest' PDF returned a fetch error; the Dogs Trust breed table S123 was not in the reachable set). Exercise, size, grooming and family advice therefore come from PDSA (S199, tier B — runbook: 'RKC breed page preferred … else PDSA'); weight, height and appearance from the FCI standard (S197, valid 25.09.2023) and the AKC standard (S200); lifespan from the one peer-reviewed breed study found (Korec et al. 2017, S201). The fetch tool split PDSA sentences longer than ~125 characters: only passages it returned in quotation marks are used as quotes; condensed passages are marked '(paraphrase)'. Woodgreen, Dogs Trust breed page and AKC trait ratings not attempted.

identity.value: FCI No. 343, Group 2 Section 2.1 (Molossian type, Mastiff type), Italy
identity.quote: Group: n°2 - Pinscher and Schnauzer - Molossoid and Swiss Mountain and Cattledogs; Section: Molossian type; Country of origin: ITALY
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S198): breed name 'CANE CORSO ITALIANO (343)'; subsection 'Mastiff type'; provisional acceptance '11/12/1996'; definitive acceptance '5/21/2007'; valid standard '9/25/2023'; 'Subject to a working trial according to the FCI Breeds Nomenclature'. FCI standard PDF (S197): 'ORIGIN: Italy.' and 'Section 2.1 Molossian, Mastiff type.' Quote assembled from the nomenclature fields as returned.

size_class.notes: PDSA key-facts box (S199). FCI (S197): 'Medium to large sized. Robust and sturdy dog, nevertheless with some elegance.' FCI weights males 45–50 kg / females 40–45 kg (S197) → the game treats it as a large dog; the growth class follows the weight (S10, below).

fci.quote: Males: 64 cm – 68 cm.
fci.notes: FCI (S197): 'Females: 60 cm – 64 cm.' and 'With a tolerance of 2 cm, more or less taller.' Over- or under-size is a severe fault (S197).

akc.quote: Height - Dogs 25 to 27½ inches; bitches 23½ to 26 inches.
akc.notes: AKC standard (S200, approved 2009, effective 2010). Inches converted to cm (× 2.54) by us.

pdsa_average.notes: PDSA key-facts box (label wording as returned).

fci.quote: Males: 45 – 50 kg.
fci.notes: FCI (S197): 'Females: 40 – 45 kg.' Game range 40–50 kg (both sexes). The AKC standard (S200) gives no number: 'Weight - Proportionate to height.'

pdsa.notes: PDSA key-facts box, one range for both sexes — agrees with FCI.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. FCI males 45–50 kg (≈ 99–110 lb) reach the 'Giant (over 100 pounds)' class; females 40–45 kg (≈ 88–99 lb) are 'Large (59–99 pounds): 15–18 months' — the same split as the Rottweiler and the Bernese Mountain Dog, so the same 18–24 months. The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 120 min is reached at 12 months either way).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Cane Corso growth curve found.

median_international.quote: The median lifespan of the whole examined group is 9.29 years (IQR 6.98-11.12, IQR = Interquartile Range).
median_international.notes: Korec E., Chalupa O., Hančl M., Korcová J., Bydžovská M. (2017), Open Veterinary Journal 7(2):170–173, doi:10.4314/ovj.v7i2.15 (S201): 'data of 232 dogs of the Cane Corso Italiano breed collected from kennels and individual owners from 25 countries.'; males 9.25 y (IQR 6.97-11.00), females 9.33 y (IQR 7.00-11.31), no significant sex difference. Not a UK primary-care population and the first author runs a Cane Corso kennel (koreccorso.cz) — used because McMillan 2024 (S54 / S135 / S123) has no reachable Cane Corso value, there is no VetCompass Cane Corso paper and there is no RKC breed page (the breed is not RKC-recognised). Consistent with the PDSA band 'Under 10 years' (S199).

pdsa.notes: PDSA key-facts box (S199). Basis of the shorter_lifespan chip together with S201 (runbook criterion: an A/B source gives an upper bound of 10 years or less).

rkc.notes: UNSOURCED — no RKC breed page — the Cane Corso is not recognised by The Royal Kennel Club (a UK parliament petition asks for recognition; no RKC page in the search results 2026-10-12).

mcmillan_2024.notes: UNSOURCED — McMillan et al. 2024 Cane Corso median not reachable: the Dogs Trust 'shortest and longest' PDF returned a fetch error and the Dogs Trust breed table (S123) was not in the reachable set (2026-10-12); the paper text (S135) and Author Correction (S54) carry no per-breed table. The breed may not be in the UK dataset at all (PDSA S199: 'The Cane Corso is a relatively uncommon breed in the UK.'). Verify in McMillan 2024 Supplementary Table 3 before replacing the S201 median.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × 9.29 y (S201) → 0.75 × 9.29 = 6.9675 y = 83.61 → 84 months. The runbook rule (McMillan 2024, else a VetCompass median, else the RKC lower bound) yields no value: no McMillan value reachable, no VetCompass paper, no RKC page (PDSA 'Under 10 years' has no lower bound). Closest rule row = a peer-reviewed breed median (as the Bernese Mountain Dog, M5-R10-12) → seeded verified=false. Alternative: Dogs Trust > 7 y = 84 months (S14) — the same number.

adult.quote: Your Cane Corso will need around two hours’ exercise every day.
adult.notes: PDSA (S199) 'around two hours’' → 120 (register qualifier 'about'); key facts 'Minimum exercise (per day): 2 hours'. No RKC breed page exists (breed not RKC-recognised) → runbook: else PDSA. 'This should include a couple of longer, brisk walks (or even a jog) with time to play off-lead somewhere secure.' (S199).

energy.value: active, likes tasks and being kept occupied; hates being bored
energy.quote: Cane Corsos love to be kept occupied and hate being bored.
energy.notes: PDSA (S199): 'Cane Corsos like being given specific tasks to make them feel useful.' and 'Puzzle games are perfect for Cane Corsos because they enjoy having something to focus on.' FCI (S197): 'extremely agile and responsive.'

off_lead_secure.quote: This should include a couple of longer, brisk walks (or even a jog) with time to play off-lead somewhere secure.
off_lead_secure.notes: PDSA (S199). No fence / escape advice → no secure_fencing tag.

temperament.value: guardian of property, family and livestock; agile and responsive; sociable and loving with its owners
temperament.quote: Guardian of property, family and livestock; extremely agile and responsive.
temperament.notes: PDSA (S199): 'Cane Corsos are sociable and loving dogs who enjoy the company of their owners and being out exploring.' AKC (S200): 'The Cane Corso as a protector of his property and owners is unequaled.' FCI disqualifying fault (S197): 'Aggressive or overly shy dogs.'

family.quote: We really wouldn’t recommend having a Cane Corso if you have small children
family.notes: PDSA (S199), sentence continues 'as they could get hurt if they are accidentally knocked over.'; 'They suit adult-only homes best, or families with older children or teenagers who understand the breed.' Basis of the new consider tag not_for_small_children; never children / small_children / family_pet.

experienced_owner.value: better suited to experienced dog owners
experienced_owner.quote: due to their size they’re better suited to experienced dog owners.
experienced_owner.notes: PDSA (S199) (clause as returned). Training: 'It’s really important they are trained using positive, reward-based training from a young age' (S199). Basis of experienced_owner (as the Rottweiler).

socialisation.value: socialise with many people and experiences from a young age
socialisation.quote: You’ll need to socialise your Cane Corso with lots of different people and experiences from a young age.
socialisation.notes: PDSA (S199). A sourced need (runbook §3, David 2026-10-11): the game's school (M5-R03) trains commands, not socialisation with people and new experiences → new ROADMAP M5-R17 (needs-david); see proposed_game_parameters.cane_corso.socialisation.

time_alone.value: general PDSA advice — never alone for longer than four hours
time_alone.quote: As with any dog, you should never leave your Cane Corso alone for longer than four hours.
time_alone.notes: PDSA (S199) general advice ('As with any dog') → no often_alone tag.

other_pets.quote: you should always supervise them with other pets.
other_pets.notes: PDSA (S199): 'If they’ve grown up with another pet in the home, your Cane Corso is likely to be OK with them' → conditional, no other_pets tag.

drooling.value: known to drool — keep a drool cloth at hand
drooling.quote: Despite not needing much attention for their fur, Cane Corsos are known to drool.
drooling.notes: PDSA (S199): keep a drool cloth with you at all times (paraphrase; the fragment 'it's a good idea to keep a drool cloth with you at all times' was returned). Basis of the new consider tag drools. Wiping drool is an owner habit, not a care routine of the dog with a sourced frequency → no game mechanic.

chewing.notes: No breed-specific chewing statement found (S199).

food_motivation.notes: No breed-specific appetite statement. PDSA (S199) feeding advice: 'it’s usually recommended to split their daily allowance into two meals.' (= the game's two adult meals) and 'Remember to leave a gap after eating and before exercising.' (GDV, see health.gdv and proposed_game_parameters.cane_corso.meal_exercise_gap) → no food_motivated_weight tag.

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages exist for this breed in the sources used. PDSA (S199): 'The Cane Corso is a relatively uncommon breed in the UK.' 'Because of this, we can’t be sure which health conditions will be more common with the breed.' Not a conformation welfare breed in the sources: no RKC Breed Watch entry (breed not RKC-recognised), no BVA / UFAW / VetCompass statement; not flat-faced (FCI muzzle : skull ≈ 1 : 2, 'noticeably shorter than the skull', S197) → no brachycephalic chip and no veterinary advice against advertising the breed type. Ear cropping and tail docking are illegal in the UK (PDSA S199) and the FCI 2023 standard requires natural ears and tail (S197).

hip_elbow_dysplasia.value: hip and elbow dysplasia — x-ray screening of the parents before breeding
hip_elbow_dysplasia.quote: Hip dysplasia – where the hip joint doesn’t fit together perfectly, which will eventually lead to arthritis.
hip_elbow_dysplasia.notes: PDSA (S199): 'Before breeding, dogs should be screened by x-rays through the BVA/Kennel Club Hip Dysplasia Scheme.'; 'Elbow dysplasia – where the elbow joint doesn’t fit together perfectly, which will eventually lead to arthritis.'; 'Before breeding, dogs should be screened by x-rays through the BVA/KC Elbow Dysplasia Scheme.' Basis of the breeder checklist (S199). No Breed Watch point → no hips_hind_legs chip.

The game draws only the two colours both standards share (black, brown with rust); blue and fawn are RKC-only. Never white markings, never merle or solid colours.

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). Black and rust first with the highest weight (portrait default), then brown and rust.

coat.value: short, hard and dense, lying tight and smooth; no undercoat
coat.quote: The hair is short, hard and dense. It lies tight and smooth and is equally distributed over the whole surface.
coat.notes: RKC (S210): 'Smooth, short, hard, thick and close-lying. Imperceptible undercoat on neck permissible.' RKC breed page (S209): 'Coat length: Short'.

ears.value: natural (uncropped), set high, lying close to the cheeks
ears.quote: The ears, are left natural and of an appropriate size;
ears.notes: FCI (S207, paraphrase of the rest): set on the highest point of the skull, ideally lying close to the cheeks. RKC standard (S210): 'Small, neat, set high on head, dropped and lying close to the cheeks.' Natural drop ears in the portrait (never cropped).

eyes.value: medium sized, oval, dark
eyes.quote: Medium sized, oval and dark in colour. Lighter shades are permitted for brown dogs.
eyes.notes: RKC (S210): 'Almond-shaped, not round, moderately deep set, not prominent, with lively, alert expression.'

nose.value: black in black dogs, lighter in brown dogs; long head like a blunt wedge
nose.quote: Black – in black dogs; in brown dogs, corresponding lighter shades.
nose.notes: RKC (S210): 'Seen from above and side, resembles an elongated blunt wedge. Upper part of head flat and free from wrinkle.' Not flat-faced.

tail.value: natural (undocked), carried high in a slight curve
tail.quote: The tail is left natural and is ideally carried high in a slight curve.
tail.notes: FCI 2015 (S207). RKC standard (S210) has both: 'Previously customarily docked.' and the undocked wording 'Appears to be a continuation of spine without material drop, kink or deformity.' Natural tail in the portrait (a standard option).
