boxer._note: Added 2026-10-12 (M5-R10-26, unattended run — appended after the Dobermann: AKC 2024 No. 17, S174 table row '17 | Boxer'). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-12; spot-check before import (sources.md S213–S220, reused S8, S10, S11, S14, S35, S45, S92, S123, S174). The English FCI standard PDF redirected in a loop; the French FCI standard (S213, valid 01.04.2008) was read instead — French quotes, English in notes. FCI and the RKC standard (S217) agree on heights; the RKC standard gives weights, FCI only 'over 30 kg' / 'about 25 kg'. Colours fawn or brindle with a black mask (all three standards). FCI ears and tail natural; the AKC standard (S218) still describes cropped ears and a docked tail — never drawn. Lifespan: McMillan 2024 median 11.3 y via the Dogs Trust breed table (S123). Welfare: RKC Breed Watch Category 2 — pinched nostrils, excessively short muzzle (S216); VetCompass 2023 (S220): 'a moderately brachycephalic skull shape'; PDSA (S219) lists BOAS 'in some Boxers with shorter faces' → new short_muzzle_breathing chip (not the flat-face chip) and no marketing (BVA S92). Slovenian name »boksar« (common name; KZS page not opened). Woodgreen and AKC trait ratings not attempted.

identity.value: FCI No. 144, Group 2 Section 2.1 (Molossoid, Mastiff type), Germany
identity.quote: Boxer (Deutscher Boxer) | 144 | Section 2, Molossian type | Subsection 2.1, Mastiff type | Germany
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature, Group 2 list (S214), fields as returned (quote assembled from the row fields). FCI standard (S213): Group 2, section 2.1, 'Avec épreuve de travail.' (with working trial); valid standard 01.04.2008. RKC group: Working (S215). AKC name: Boxer (S174).

size_class.notes: PDSA (S219) key facts: 'Size | Large' — sources agree. Standards: 'medium-sized' (RKC S217, AKC S218) — a proportion word, not a size class.

rkc.quote: Height: dogs: 57-63 cms (22½-25 ins); bitches: 53-59 cms (21-23 ins).
rkc.notes: FCI (S213, French): males 57–63 cm, females 53–59 cm — same. AKC (S218): 'Adult males 23 to 25 inches; females 21½ to 23½ inches at the withers.' PDSA (S219): 'Average height | 53-63 cm'.

rkc.quote: Weight: dogs: approximately 30-32 kgs (66-70 lbs); bitches: approximately 25-27 kgs (55-60 lbs).
rkc.notes: RKC breed standard (S217). FCI (S213, French, as summarised by the tool): males over 30 kg (at about 60 cm), females about 25 kg (at about 56 cm). The AKC standard (S218) gives no weight. Game range 25–32 kg (both sexes).

pdsa.notes: PDSA key facts (S219) — same as the RKC standard.

vetcompass_mean.quote: The mean adult bodyweight of males (32.99 kg, SD 5.42 kg) was heavier than for females (27.56 kg, SD 4.57 kg)
vetcompass_mean.notes: O'Neill et al. 2023 (S220), UK primary-care population — background only.

salt_category.value: IV (20–<30 kg) for females; males (30–32 kg) in V
salt_category.notes: Category assignment by weight is ours (general_by_size.size_classes.salt_2017_bands_kg, S8). The Salt 2017 Category IV list names the Boxer (general_by_size note).

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. RKC 25–32 kg (S217) = 55–70.5 lb: males 66–70 lb are 'Large'; bitches 55–60 lb straddle 'Medium (24–59 pounds): 12–15 months' and Large (as the Labrador). PDSA (S219): 'Boxers mature a lot slower than other breeds' (truncated by the tool). The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 120 min is reached at 12 months).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Boxer growth curve found.

median_uk.notes: McMillan et al. 2024 (Sci Rep) data as tabled by Dogs Trust (S123, columns Breed | Median Life Expectancy (Years) | Lower and Upper 95% CI | Total Number Individuals (Alive and Deceased) | Number Deceased Individuals). Runbook first choice (McMillan 2024). VetCompass 2023 (S220): 'The median longevity of 346 Boxers that died during the study was 10.46 years' (alternative). RKC (S215) and PDSA (S219): 'Over 10 years' — consistent.

vetcompass_2023.quote: The median longevity of 346 Boxers that died during the study was 10.46 years
vetcompass_2023.notes: O'Neill et al. 2023 (S220). Alternative only (runbook prefers McMillan 2024).

rkc.notes: RKC breed page (S215). PDSA key facts (S219): 'Average lifespan | Over 10 years' — same. Not 'Under 10 years' → no shorter_lifespan chip.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × 11.3 y (McMillan 2024 via S123) → 0.75 × 11.3 = 8.475 y = 101.7 → 102 months. Not chosen: 94 (0.75 × 10.46 y VetCompass 2023, S220), 84 (Dogs Trust > 7 y, S14).

adult.quote: Exercise: More than 2 hours per day
adult.notes: PDSA (S219): 'Your Boxer will need a minimum of two hours exercise every day.' (key facts 'Minimum exercise (per day) | 2 hours') — sources agree; RKC preferred (runbook rule).

energy.value: very high energy, playful; keeps a puppy attitude for long
energy.quote: Boxers are very high energy, active dogs who love playing and being involved in everything going on.
energy.notes: PDSA (S219): 'They keep their puppy attitude longer than most dogs so you might find your Boxer rarely has a calm moment at home!' / 'On top of this, your Boxer will also need regular, short training sessions.' Covered by the game's walk, play and school.

walk_structure.value: split into a few walks with sniffing and exploring, plus secure off-lead running and garden play
walk_structure.quote: This should be split into a few walks with plenty of opportunities for sniffing around and exploring.
walk_structure.notes: PDSA (S219): 'You should also give your Boxer plenty of time to exercise off lead somewhere secure so they can have a good run around.' / 'A large secure garden is a must if you have a Boxer so they have plenty of space to blow off steam.' The game's walks already count several walks per day; no new mechanic.

after_meals.value: leave a gap between eating and exercising
after_meals.quote: Remember to leave a gap between eating and exercising.
after_meals.notes: PDSA (S219), feeding section ('We usually recommend splitting their daily allowance into two meals.'). The page does not name bloat. → proposed_game_parameters.boxer.meal_exercise_gap (built, M5-R16).

temperament.value: equable, biddable, fearless, self-assured; kind and clownish, eager to please, very loyal
temperament.quote: Equable, biddable, fearless, self-assured.
temperament.notes: RKC standard (S217). FCI (S213, French, summarised by the tool): strong nerves, self-assured, calm and balanced; very attached to the family, wary of strangers. PDSA (S219): 'They are eager to please and very loyal dogs.'; 'Boxers are friendly dogs but do have a natural guarding instinct and can be protective' (truncated by the tool).

family.value: a much-loved family companion; not recommended with younger children (size, boisterous) — an adult-only home or one with teenagers is better
family.quote: much loved as a family companion for his intelligence and character
family.notes: RKC breed page (S215), clause as returned. PDSA (S219): 'Now they're known for their kind and clownish natures which has made them popular family pets.' / 'Generally speaking, Boxers are good around children of all ages given the right training.' but '...we wouldn't recommend a Boxer if you have younger children as they could accidentally knock them over.' and 'An adult only home or one with teenagers is better for a Boxer.' AKC standard (S218): 'With family and friends, his temperament is fundamentally playful, yet patient and stoical with children.' → family_pet and not_for_small_children; never children / small_children (conflicting statements).

experienced_owner.value: not recommended for first-time owners; does better with an experienced, patient owner
experienced_owner.quote: For this reason, we wouldn't recommend a Boxer if you are a first time owner.
experienced_owner.notes: PDSA (S219): 'Boxers can be very boisterous so do better with an experienced (and patient!) owner.' Basis of experienced_owner (as the Rottweiler, the Cane Corso and the Dobermann); never first_time_owner.

socialisation.value: socialise with other dogs from a young age (strong guarding instinct)
socialisation.quote: Boxers have a strong guarding instinct so it's important to socialise your Boxer with other dogs from a young age.
socialisation.notes: PDSA (S219): 'Puppy socialisation classes are a great way to get your pup used to new dogs.' Built: M5-R17 puppy socialisation (proposed_game_parameters.boxer.socialisation).

time_alone.value: loves company — can develop separation anxiety; best with someone at home all day
time_alone.quote: Boxers love human company so can develop separation anxiety if left alone.
time_alone.notes: PDSA (S219): 'It's best to have a Boxer if someone is going to be around the house with them all day.' / 'As they get so attached to their owners, it's best to have someone around all day with your dog.' Breed-specific (not only the general four-hour advice) → new consider tag needs_company (runbook 'new tag' rule); never often_alone.

other_pets.value: very high prey drive — not recommended with smaller pets; may accept a cat it grew up with, always supervise
other_pets.quote: Boxers do have a very high prey drive, so we wouldn't recommend keeping them with smaller pets.
other_pets.notes: PDSA (S219): 'They may get along OK with a cat they have grown up with, but you should always supervise your Boxer with smaller pets.' → no other_pets tag; → chases_small_pets (David 2026-10-12 rule).

chewing.quote: If they are alone or bored, they like to chew which means your furniture and belongings will be at risk!
chewing.notes: PDSA (S219) → chews_when_bored.

food_motivation.notes: No breed-specific statement found → no food_motivated_weight tag. PDSA (S219) general feeding advice: two meals a day, at similar times.

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages are shown anywhere. Conformation welfare: RKC Breed Watch Category 2 — 'Pinched nostrils', 'Excessively short muzzle' (S216); VetCompass 2023 (S220): 'a moderately brachycephalic skull shape'. PDSA (S219) introduces its list with 'Some of the conditions Boxers may develop include:'.

brachycephaly_boas.value: moderately short-faced (brachycephalic) skull; BOAS — severe breathing problems in some Boxers with shorter faces
brachycephaly_boas.quote: Brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome (BOAS) – this can cause severe breathing problems in some Boxers with shorter faces
brachycephaly_boas.notes: PDSA (S219), the sentence as returned (the tool cut it at 125 characters). VetCompass (S220): 'The Boxer is a medium-large sized, active dog with a short coat and a moderately brachycephalic skull shape'; 'Brachycephalic airway obstructive syndrome (BOAS) is widely considered as a common disorder in dogs with extreme brachycephaly'. Basis of short_muzzle_breathing (welfare rule) and of the marketing exclusion (BVA S92).

skull_shape.quote: The Boxer is a medium-large sized, active dog with a short coat and a moderately brachycephalic skull shape
skull_shape.notes: O'Neill et al. 2023 (S220, VetCompass / RVC). Also: 'The breed standard calls for a muzzle one-third the total length of the head'. FCI (S213): muzzle to skull '1 :2'.

breed_watch.value: RKC Breed Watch Category 2 — pinched nostrils, excessively short muzzle
breed_watch.notes: RKC Breed Watch page (S216), title 'Boxer - Category 2 | Breed Watch | Royal Kennel Club'; points of concern 'Pinched nostrils' and 'Excessively short muzzle'. RKC breed page (S215): 'Category 2'.

eyes_corneal_ulcers.value: eye problems such as corneal ulcers (skull shape, prominent eyes)
eyes_corneal_ulcers.quote: Eye problems – such as corneal ulcers due to the shape of their skulls and prominence of the eyes.
eyes_corneal_ulcers.notes: PDSA (S219). VetCompass (S220): 'Conformational predisposition to corneal ulceration among dogs with brachycephaly has been recognised for over a century'. RKC Best Practice eye scheme (S215).

skin_folds.value: skin problems — warts, skin tags, skin allergies and skin fold dermatitis; keep face folds clean and dry
skin_folds.quote: Due to the excess skin around their faces, Boxers are at risk of developing a condition called skin fold dermatitis.
skin_folds.notes: PDSA (S219): 'It's important to make sure the folds of skin are kept clean and dry so they don't get infected.'; health list 'Skin problems - such as warts, skin tags, skin allergies and soreness in skin folds around the face (skin fold dermatitis).' VetCompass (S220): skin disorders the most prevalent group (figures stay here). RKC breed page (S215): skin conditions among the breed's health priorities (paraphrase). A sourced need (face-fold care) → ROADMAP M5-R14 (not built, needs David). Not a Breed Watch point → no sensitive_skin chip.

heart.value: heart problems such as cardiomyopathy or aortic stenosis
heart.quote: Heart problems – such as cardiomyopathy or aortic stenosis.
heart.notes: PDSA (S219); the page adds that parents should be screened before breeding (paraphrase). RKC breed page (S215): heart conditions (aortic stenosis, ARVC) among the breed's health priorities (paraphrase). Research only — no chip (Dobermann precedent).

hip_dysplasia.value: hip dysplasia; parents hip-scored (BVA/KC scheme, RKC Best Practice)
hip_dysplasia.quote: Hip dysplasia – where the hip joint doesn't fit together perfectly, which will eventually lead to arthritis.
hip_dysplasia.notes: PDSA (S219). RKC breed page (S215) Best Practice: 'BVA/KC Hip Dysplasia Scheme'. Not a Breed Watch point → no hips_hind_legs chip.

epilepsy.quote: Epilepsy – a brain disorder causing seizures.

cancer.notes: PDSA health list (S219); RKC breed page (S215): cancers among the health priorities (paraphrase); VetCompass (S220): neoplasia the second most prevalent disorder group.

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table of Coren's ranking (S35): row '48 | Boxer' under 'Average Working/Obedience Intelligence' (ranks 40–54). Coren's own top/bottom-10 article (S34) does not list the breed. Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

coren_tier.quote: Understanding of new commands: 25 to 40 repetitions.
coren_tier.notes: S35 tier 'Average Working/Obedience Intelligence' (40–54): 'Obey first command: 50% of the time or better.'

training_notes.value: clever but boisterous; positive, reward-based training from a young age; matures slowly
training_notes.quote: Boxers are clever dogs but can be boisterous, so positive, reward-based training from a young age is really important.
training_notes.notes: PDSA (S219); FCI (S213, summarised): easy to train. The game's school (M5-R03) covers training.

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value — see proposed_game_parameters.boxer.learning_multiplier (1.0, runbook rule: Average tier, rank 48).

general.value: medium-sized, square build, strong bone and well developed muscles, smooth-coated
general.quote: Great nobility, smooth-coated, medium-sized, square build, strong bone and evident, well developed muscles.
general.notes: AKC (S218): 'The ideal Boxer is a medium-sized, square-built dog of good substance'. FCI (S213, French, summarised): medium size, short-haired, stocky and square, strong bone, dry well-marked muscles.

colours.unit: list (black mask; white markings up to one third)
colours.quote: Fawn or brindle.
colours.notes: RKC (S217): 'White markings acceptable not exceeding one-third of ground colour.' / 'Fawn: Various shades from dark deer red to light fawn.' / 'Brindle: Black stripes on previously described fawn shades, running parallel to ribs all over body.' FCI (S213, summarised): fawn (light yellow to dark deer red; red fawn most desired) or brindle, black mask, white markings allowed up to one third. AKC (S218): 'The colors are fawn and brindle.'; disqualification 'Boxers that are any color other than fawn or brindle.' Never all-white, black, merle or more than one third white.

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). Fawn with a black mask first with the highest weight (portrait default), then brindle.

coat.value: short, glossy, smooth and tight to the body
coat.quote: Short, glossy, smooth and tight to body.
coat.notes: FCI (S213, French): 'Ras, dur, brillant et serré.' RKC breed page (S215): 'Coat length: Short'.

ears.value: natural (uncropped), moderate, lying flat and close to the cheek, falling forward when alert
ears.quote: Moderate size, thin, set wide apart on highest part of skull lying flat and close to cheek in repose,
ears.notes: RKC (S217): 'but falling forward with definite crease when alert.' FCI (S213, summarised): natural. The AKC standard (S218) describes cropped ears ('...the ears are customarily cropped') — never drawn; natural ears in the portrait.

eyes.value: dark brown, forward looking, not protruding
eyes.quote: Dark brown, forward looking, not too small, protruding or deeply set.
eyes.notes: RKC (S217): 'Dark rims with good pigmentation showing no haw.' FCI (S213, summarised): dark, medium size, neither bulging nor deep set.

nose.value: broad, black, slightly turned up, wide open nostrils; broad, deep muzzle that is never short
nose.quote: Nose broad, black, slightly turned up, wide nostrils with well-defined line between.
nose.notes: RKC (S217): 'Muzzle broad, deep and powerful, never narrow, pointed, short or shallow.' / 'Balance of skull and muzzle essential, with muzzle never appearing small, viewed from any angle.' FCI (S213, French): truffe 'Large, noire, très légèrement remouchée'; muzzle to skull '1 :2'. Breed Watch (S216): pinched nostrils and an excessively short muzzle are concerns → PetPrep art: a moderate muzzle with wide open nostrils (welfare rule).

tail.value: natural (undocked), set high, carried gaily
tail.quote: Undocked: Set on high and carried gaily, of moderate thickness.
tail.notes: RKC (S217): 'Previously customarily docked.' FCI (S213, summarised): set rather high, normal natural length; a naturally short tail disqualifies. AKC (S218) describes a docked tail — never drawn; natural tail in the portrait.

miniature_schnauzer._note: Added 2026-10-13 (M5-R10-27, unattended run — appended after the Boxer: AKC 2024 No. 18, S174 table row '18 | Miniature Schnauzer'). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-13; spot-check before import (sources.md S221–S228, reused S10, S11, S14, S35, S45, S174). FCI standard N° 183 (S221, valid 06.03.2007): height 30–35 cm, weight approximately 4–8 kg (dogs and bitches), colours pure black, pepper and salt, black/silver, pure white; ears and tail natural. RKC standard (S224, KUSA copy, effective 01/07/2026) lists the same four colours (white included); the AKC standard (S225, AMSC copy) allows only salt and pepper, black and silver and solid black (white disqualifies) → the game draws pepper and salt (default), black and silver or black — never white (conservative reading of the 'never a disqualifying colour' rule; open for David). Lifespan: VetCompass 2019 median 11.6 y (S227) — McMillan 2024 / Dogs Trust table (S123) not reachable this run (fetch refused). RKC Breed Watch Category 1 (S223) → not a welfare breed, in marketing. Slovenian name »pritlikavi šnavcer« (common name; KZS page not opened). Woodgreen and AKC trait ratings not attempted.

FCI standard (S221): 'Section 1 Pinscher and Schnauzer type.', 'Without working trial.', ORIGIN 'Germany.', UTILIZATION 'House and Companion Dog'. RKC group: Utility (S223). great_dane._note: Added 2026-10-13 (M5-R10-29, unattended run — appended after the Shih Tzu: AKC 2024 No. 21, S174 table row '21 | Great Dane'). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-13; spot-check before import (sources.md S239–S244, reused S8, S10, S11, S14, S35, S45, S174, S212). Names: FCI 'DEUTSCHE DOGGE' / 'GREAT DANE' (S240), The Royal Kennel Club and the AKC 'Great Dane' (S241, S174); Slovenian »nemška doga«. FCI standard valid 21.08.2024 (S239); RKC standard (S242). Colours: the game draws only the colours both standards share (fawn, brindle, harlequin, black, blue — FCI merle and RKC mantle are each in one standard only; Dobermann precedent). Lifespan: McMillan 2024 not reachable (Dogs Trust table refused, 'shortest and longest' PDF fetch error, Science News and LJMU news name no Great Dane value) → runbook rule: a VetCompass median — O'Neill et al. 2013 (S212), 6.0 y from 23 deaths (small sample) → provisional. Welfare: RKC Breed Watch Category 2 (S244) — eyelids, hind conformation / movement, unsound movement, nervous temperament. Woodgreen and AKC trait ratings not attempted.

identity.value: FCI No. 235, Group 2 Section 2.1 (Molossoid breeds, Mastiff type), Germany
identity.quote: Group 2 Pinscher and Schnauzer – Molossoid breeds – Swiss Mountain and Cattle Dogs.
identity.notes: FCI standard N° 235 (S239): 'Section 2.1 Molossoid breeds, Mastiff type.'; utilization 'Companion, watch- and guard dog.'; valid standard '21.08.2024'. FCI nomenclature (S240, labels returned in French): 'DEUTSCHE DOGGE' (English 'GREAT DANE'), '235', country of origin 'ALLEMAGNE', 'Non soumise à épreuve de travail selon la Nomenclature des races de la FCI', definitive acceptance '18/11/1961'. RKC group: Working (S241). AKC name: Great Dane (S174).

size_class.notes: RKC breed page (S241) — the RKC's largest class ('Extra large') = the register's 'giant'. PDSA (S243) key facts: 'Size | Large'. PDSA: 'As the largest breed of dog, they need a lot of space both inside the house and outside' (truncated by the tool).

fci.quote: Males: at least 80 cm, should not exceed 90 cm.
fci.notes: FCI standard (S239): 'Females: at least 72 cm, should not exceed 84 cm.' RKC standard (S242): minimum height over 18 months 'dogs' '76 cms (30 ins)', bitches '71 cms (28 ins)'. PDSA (S243): 'Average height | 71-76 cm'.

pdsa.notes: PDSA key facts (S243), one range for both sexes (stored per sex) — the game range. RKC standard (S242): minimum weight over 18 months '54 kgs (120 lbs)' for dogs, '46 kgs (100 lbs)' for bitches (adult_weight.rkc_minimum) — the same numbers as minimums. FCI (S239) gives no weight.

rkc_minimum.notes: RKC standard (S242), Size: minimum weight over 18 months for dogs '54 kgs (120 lbs)'; bitches '46 kgs (100 lbs)'. A minimum, not a range — background for the PDSA range.

salt_category.notes: Category assignment by weight is ours (general_by_size.size_classes.salt_2017_bands_kg, S8): 46–54 kg = the band '>40 (no curve)'. Salt 2017 breed list not checked.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. PDSA 46–54 kg (S243) = 101–119 lb → 'Giant'. RKC standard (S242) gives the minimum height and weight 'over 18 months'. Same 18–24 months as the Bernese Mountain Dog. The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 120 min is reached at 12 months).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Great Dane growth curve found.

puppy_exercise.value: not too much exercise too soon (bones and joints)
puppy_exercise.notes: PDSA (S243, paraphrase as returned): too much exercise too soon could harm a puppy's bone and joint development. The game's puppy rule (10 min × age in months, capped) already limits puppy walks — no new mechanic.

median_uk.notes: O'Neill et al. 2013 (S212), VetCompass England, Table 1 row as returned (columns: breed, median years, IQR, range, number of dogs) — 23 deaths, a small sample. Results: 'the Great Dane (n=23; 6.0 years; IQR 4.0-9.0 years; Table 1)'; abstract: 'the shortest-lived were the Dogue de Bordeaux and Great Dane'. The same paper cites earlier estimates (paraphrase): 8.4 y (Michell 1999) and 6.5 y (Adams et al. 2010). McMillan 2024 not reachable this run — runbook rule: else a VetCompass median. Provisional.

rkc.notes: RKC breed page (S241). PDSA (S243): 'Average lifespan | Under 10 years' — same. Basis of shorter_lifespan.

mcmillan_2024.notes: McMillan et al. 2024: the Dogs Trust breed table (S123) was refused by the fetch tool (provenance), the 'shortest and longest' PDF returned a fetch error, the Science News article and the LJMU news page name no Great Dane value (2026-10-13). UNSOURCED value — verify in McMillan 2024 Supplementary Table / S123 before replacing the VetCompass median.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × 6.0 y (S212) → 0.75 × 6.0 = 4.5 y = 54 months. The RKC band 'Under 10 years' (S241) has no lower bound. Dogs Trust rule of thumb > 7 y = 84 months (S14). Provisional until McMillan 2024 is checked (small VetCompass sample — open for David).

adult.quote: Exercise: More than 2 hours per day
adult.notes: PDSA (S243): 'Great Danes need a minimum of two hours of exercise every day to burn off their excess energy and help keep them in' (truncated by the tool; key facts 'Minimum exercise (per day) | 2 hours') — sources agree; RKC preferred (runbook rule).

temperament.quote: Friendly, loving and devoted to his owners.
temperament.notes: FCI (S239): 'Might be reserved towards strangers.' RKC standard (S242): 'Kindly without nervousness, friendly and outgoing.' RKC breed page (S241): 'kind and loyal to his family.'

family.value: a wonderful family dog (RKC); not recommended with younger children because of size and strength (PDSA)

family.notes: RKC breed page (S241), clause as returned. PDSA (S243): 'While they can make great family pets, we wouldn’t recommend a Great Dane if you have younger children due to their' (truncated by the tool); 'You should always supervise your Great Dane with children and vulnerable adults as they often don't know their own stren' (truncated). → family_pet and not_for_small_children; never children / small_children.

experienced_owner.value: first-time owners may want the help of an accredited trainer
experienced_owner.quote: If you don't have much experience with Great Danes, or are a first time owner, you might want to ask for the help of an
experienced_owner.notes: PDSA (S243), truncated by the tool ('… an accredited trainer', paraphrase of the end). Advice to get help, not advice against first-time owners → neither experienced_owner nor first_time_owner.

socialisation.value: socialise with different experiences, people and dogs from a young age (can be sensitive to new situations)
socialisation.quote: This is why it's really important to socialise your Great Dane with different experiences, people and dogs from a young age.
socialisation.notes: PDSA (S243). → proposed_game_parameters.great_dane.socialisation (DOG_SOCIALISATION row, M5-R17).

time_alone.value: loves the family's company and will get upset if left alone; general PDSA four-hour advice
time_alone.quote: Great Danes love to have their family around for company and like most dogs will get upset if they are left alone.
time_alone.notes: PDSA (S243). 'like most dogs' — a general statement, not the Boxer's separation-anxiety warning → no needs_company chip, no often_alone tag.

other_pets.value: fairly strong prey drive — careful introductions, never unsupervised with smaller pets
other_pets.quote: Great Danes do have a fairly strong prey drive, though, so all introductions need to be done very carefully.
other_pets.notes: PDSA (S243); also 'Never leave your Great Dane unsupervised with smaller pets.' → chases_small_pets (a quote naming the prey drive, runbook §3); no other_pets tag.

chewing.value: may chew furniture and possessions when bored or left alone
chewing.quote: You might find that they chew your furniture and possessions when they're bored or left alone
chewing.notes: PDSA (S243), clause as returned (the sentence continues 'so it's best to have someo…', truncated). Basis of chews_when_bored.

drooling.quote: Great Danes are, however, known for drooling!
drooling.notes: PDSA (S243). Basis of drools (as the Cane Corso).

food_motivation.notes: No breed-specific statement found → no food_motivated_weight tag. PDSA (S243): feed two meals a day ('We usually recommend splitting their daily allowance into two meals.') = the game's adult meals.

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages are shown anywhere. Conformation welfare topic: RKC Breed Watch Category 2 (S244) — 'Eyelids not in normal contact with the eyeball, they are turned inwards or outwards', 'Unsound movement', 'Incorrect hind conformation and/or poor rear movement', 'Nervous temperamant' (sic) → hips_hind_legs (as the German Shepherd Dog and the Rottweiler) and the new eyelid_problems chip (welfare rule, 'a new one per the row above'). Not flat-faced → no brachycephalic chip, and no veterinary advice against advertising the breed type. PDSA (S243) introduces its list with 'Some of the conditions Great Danes may develop include:'.

breed_watch.value: RKC Breed Watch Category 2 — eyelids turned in or out; unsound movement; incorrect hind conformation / poor rear movement; nervous temperament
breed_watch.quote: Eyelids not in normal contact with the eyeball, they are turned inwards or outwards
breed_watch.notes: RKC Breed Watch page (S244), title 'Great Dane - Category 2'; further points 'Unsound movement', 'Incorrect hind conformation and/or poor rear movement', 'Nervous temperamant' (sic). The RKC Breed Watch tally sheet lists the first three. RKC breed page (S241): 'Category 2' and 'This breed can be affected by conformational concerns, more information can be found here.'

hind_conformation.value: incorrect hind conformation and/or poor rear movement (Breed Watch); hip and elbow dysplasia — parents X-rayed (BVA/KC schemes)
hind_conformation.quote: Incorrect hind conformation and/or poor rear movement
hind_conformation.notes: RKC Breed Watch (S244). PDSA (S243): 'Hip dysplasia – where the hip joint doesn't fit together perfectly, which will eventually lead to arthritis.'; 'Elbow dysplasia – where the elbow joint doesn’t fit together perfectly, which will eventually lead to arthritis.' RKC breed page (S241) Best Practice: hip and elbow schemes. Basis of hips_hind_legs.

hip_elbow_dysplasia.value: hip and elbow dysplasia — joints that don't fit together perfectly, leading to arthritis; parents X-rayed (BVA/KC schemes, RKC Best Practice)
hip_elbow_dysplasia.quote: Hip dysplasia – where the hip joint doesn't fit together perfectly, which will eventually lead to arthritis.
hip_elbow_dysplasia.notes: PDSA (S243): 'Elbow dysplasia – where the elbow joint doesn’t fit together perfectly, which will eventually lead to arthritis.' RKC breed page (S241) Best Practice: BVA/KC Hip Dysplasia Scheme and BVA/KC Elbow Dysplasia Scheme.

eyelids.value: eyelids turned inwards or outwards (entropion / ectropion) and other eye problems — eye-tested parents
eyelids.quote: Eye problems – a range of eye conditions including in-turning or out-turning (entropion/ectropion) of the eyelids,
eyelids.notes: PDSA (S243), truncated by the tool (the list goes on — paraphrase as returned: glaucoma, cherry eye, medial canthus pocketing; some have BVA/KC screening). RKC Breed Watch (S244): 'Eyelids not in normal contact with the eyeball, they are turned inwards or outwards'. RKC breed page (S241) Best Practice: eye testing (BVA/KC/ISDS Eye Scheme). Basis of eyelid_problems.

gdv.quote: Gastric Dilatation Volvulus (GDV) – this is where the stomach twists. It is an emergency and requires urgent veterinary
gdv.notes: PDSA (S243), truncated by the tool. Feeding section: leave a gap after eating and before exercising (exercise.after_meals) → meal_exercise_gap (M5-R16).

heart_dcm.quote: Dilated Cardiomyopathy (DCM) – a type of heart disease which means their heart is bigger than it should be and
heart_dcm.notes: PDSA (S243), truncated by the tool. Not a Breed Watch point → no heart chip (research only, Dobermann precedent).

wobbler.quote: Wobbler Syndrome – where the bones in the neck are unstable and causing their back legs to be weak.

imgd.quote: Inherited myopathy of Great Danes (IMGD) – a DNA test to screen breeding dogs for this muscle wasting disease.
imgd.notes: PDSA (S243). RKC breed page (S241) Best Practice: 'DNA test for inherited myopathy of Great Danes (IMGD)'.

shorter_lifespan.value: a shorter life than most breeds — usually under ten years
shorter_lifespan.notes: PDSA (S243): 'Average lifespan | Under 10 years'. VetCompass 2013 median 6.0 y (S212, 23 deaths) — research only. Basis of the consider tag shorter_lifespan — a calm chip, no number.

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table of Coren's ranking (S35): rank 48 shared by the Boxer and the Great Dane (the Great Dane on the continuation line under the Boxer, as returned), tier 'Average Working/Obedience Intelligence' (ranks 40–54). Coren's own article (S34) lists only the top and bottom 10. Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

coren_tier.quote: Understanding of new commands: 25 to 40 repetitions.
coren_tier.notes: S35 tier 'Average Working/Obedience Intelligence': 'Obey first command: 50% of the time or better.'

training_notes.value: very intelligent and eager to learn; can be strong-willed — early, consistent reward-based training
training_notes.quote: Great Danes are very intelligent and eager to learn which makes them easy to train for people already familiar with the
training_notes.notes: PDSA (S243), truncated by the tool; paraphrase of the rest: they can be strong-willed, so start reward-based training early and keep it consistent.

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value — see proposed_game_parameters.great_dane.learning_multiplier (1.0, runbook rule: Average tier, rank 48).

general.value: very large, powerful and well built, combining pride, strength and elegance; noble appearance
general.quote: The Great Dane in his noble appearance combines a large, powerful well constructed body with pride, strength and elegance.
general.notes: RKC standard (S242): 'Very muscular, strongly though elegantly built, with look of dash and daring.' / 'Alert expression, powerful, majestic action displaying dignity.'

colours.quote: Fawn: Light gold fawn to deep gold fawn, evenly shaded throughout the body.
colours.notes: FCI (S239) fawn and brindle: 'Black mask desired. Small white markings on the chest are permitted.' Colour varieties: 1 fawn and brindle, 2 harlequin, merle and black, 3 blue; brindle 'with black stripes running with the direction of the ribs.'; harlequin 'Harlequin (white with black splashed patches): Basic colour pure white, preferably with no ticking.' / 'Pure black patches well distributed all over the body, having the appearance of being torn.'; black 'Jet black, white markings on chest and feet permitted.'; blue 'Pure steel blue, white markings on chest and feet permitted.'; merle 'Basic colour grey, preferably with no ticking.' Disqualifying (summarised): fawn / brindle with white blaze, collar, paws or tail tip; albino harlequins. RKC standard (S242): brindles, fawns ('lightest buff to deepest orange'), blues, blacks ('Black is black.'), mantle, harlequins; white only on chest and feet and 'it is not desirable even there.' The game draws only the five colours both standards share (merle FCI-only, mantle RKC-only). Never white blazes or collars, never albino.

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). Fawn first with the highest weight (portrait default), then brindle, harlequin, black, blue.

coat.value: very short, dense, smooth and close lying, glossy
coat.quote: Very short, dense, smooth and close lying, glossy.
coat.notes: FCI (S239): 'Must never be coarse, dull or a double coat.' RKC (S242): 'Short dense and sleek-looking, never inclined to roughness.' RKC breed page (S241): 'Coat length: Short'.

ears.value: natural (uncropped), pendant, set on high
ears.quote: Naturally pendant set on high, but not lifted above skull or hanging low.
ears.notes: RKC standard (S242): 'Triangular, medium size, set high on skull and folded forward, not pendulous.' Natural folded / pendant ears in the portrait (never cropped).

eyes.value: medium size, lively and friendly expression, preferably dark
eyes.quote: Of medium size with lively friendly intelligent expression.
eyes.notes: RKC (S242): 'Fairly deep set, not giving the appearance of being round, of medium size and preferably dark.' Breed Watch (S244): eyelids in normal contact with the eyeball → tight eyelids in the portrait (welfare).

nose.value: black (except harlequins), broad with large nostrils; long, narrow head
nose.quote: Long, narrow, distinct and expressive. Never wedge shaped.
nose.notes: FCI (S239) nose: 'Well developed, more broad than round with large nostrils.' / 'Must be black with the exception of harlequins.' RKC (S242): 'Muzzle broad, skull proportionately narrow.'

tail.value: natural, reaching to the hocks, never curled over the back
tail.quote: Reaching to the hocks, must not be too long or too short.
tail.notes: RKC (S242): 'Thick at the root, tapering towards end, reaching to or just below hocks.'

pomeranian._note: Added 2026-10-13 (M5-R10-30, unattended run — appended after the Great Dane: AKC 2024 No. 22, S174 table row '22 | Pomeranian'). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-13 (the tool limits quotes to ~125 characters — long sentences are quoted in pieces); spot-check before import (sources.md S245–S252, reused S8, S10, S11, S14, S35, S45, S54, S123, S174). FCI keeps the Pomeranian as variety e) of the German Spitz (standard N° 97, S245 / S246); the FCI standard gives a height (21 cm ± 3 cm) but no weight ('should have a weight corresponding to its size') → game weight = the RKC breed standard (S249, per sex). Lifespan: McMillan 2024 (S54) / the Dogs Trust breed table (S123) not reachable this run (PMC browser check, 'shortest and longest' PDF fetch error); no VetCompass Pomeranian paper found → runbook rule: the RKC lower bound 'Over 12 years' (S247). Wikipedia (S252, tier C) cites McMillan 2024 = 12.2 years — alternative only, never alone. RKC Breed Watch Category 2 (S248) but the breed's points of concern were not returned (royalkennelclub.com page fetch error) → no welfare chip; open for David. Woodgreen and AKC trait ratings not attempted.

identity.value: FCI No. 97, Group 5 Section 4 (European Spitz), Germany
identity.quote: FCI-CLASSIFICATION: Group 5 Spitz and primitive types.
identity.notes: FCI standard N° 97 (S246, EN PDF): 'Section 4 European Spitz.'; 'ORIGIN: Germany'; 'UTILIZATION: Watch and Companion dog.'; date of publication as returned '04/09/2019' (the nomenclature, S245, lists a newer valid standard 9/3/2024 — re-check). FCI nomenclature (S245): 'DEUTSCHER SPITZ (97)', English 'GERMAN SPITZ', varieties a)–e) with 'e) Pomeranian'; not subject to a working trial; definitive acceptance 1/1/1957. The FCI breed is the German Spitz; the Pomeranian is its toy variety ('German Toy Spitz/Pomeranian'). RKC group: Toy (S249 'TOY GROUP: Pomeranian'). AKC name: Pomeranian (S174).

size_class.notes: PDSA (S250) key facts: 'Size | Small' — sources agree. RKC group: Toy (S249). RKC weight 1.8–2.5 kg (S249) = the smallest weight band (S8).

fci.quote: German Toy Spitz/Pomeranian: 21 cm ± 3 cm.
fci.notes: FCI standard (S246), height at withers, one value for both sexes → 18–24 cm (stored per sex). PDSA (S250): 'Average height | 25-27 cm' (taller than the FCI range — background only). The RKC standard (S249) gives no height.

rkc.notes: RKC breed standard (S249, KC standard hosted by KUSA, effective 01/07/2025): 'Females: 2kg – 2.5kg.' The RKC page of the standard (as summarised by the tool) calls these ideal weights and the standard a guide. FCI (S246) gives no weight: 'The German Toy Spitz/Pomeranian should have a weight corresponding to its size.' The game range (adult_weight_kg).

pdsa.notes: PDSA key facts (S250), one range for both sexes (stored per sex) — slightly heavier than the RKC standard (S249). Background only; the register shows the standard.

salt_category.notes: Category assignment by weight is ours (general_by_size.size_classes.salt_2017_bands_kg, S8): 1.8–2.5 kg = the smallest band. Salt 2017 breed list not checked.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. The RKC weight 1.8–2.5 kg (S249) ≈ 4–5.5 lb is a little below the 'Toy (5–12 pounds)' band — the smallest class PetMD gives, used as the nearest. The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 30 min is reached at 3 months).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Pomeranian growth curve found.

rkc.notes: RKC breed page (S247; older address S248 the same). PDSA (S250): 'Average lifespan | Over 12 years' — same. The basis of the senior boundary (runbook: RKC lower bound when no McMillan 2024 / VetCompass value is reachable).

mcmillan_2024.notes: McMillan et al. 2024: PMC (PMC10834484) returned a browser check, the Dogs Trust 'shortest and longest' PDF returned a fetch error and the DOAJ record names no breed values (2026-10-13). Wikipedia (S252, tier C) quotes McMillan 2024 as 12.2 years — UNSOURCED as an A/B value; verify in McMillan 2024 Supplementary Table / S123 before replacing the RKC lower bound.

alternatives.notes: Wikipedia (tier C) citing McMillan et al. 2024 (paraphrase as returned: 'A UK study found a life expectancy of 12.2 years'); never shown alone. With it the senior boundary would be round(0.75 × 12.2 × 12) = 110 months.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × 12 y (RKC lower bound 'Over 12 years', S247) → 0.75 × 12 = 9 y = 108 months. With McMillan 12.2 y (via S252, tier C): 110 months. Dogs Trust rule of thumb > 7 y = 84 months (S14). Provisional until McMillan 2024 is checked.

adult.quote: Exercise: Up to 30 minutes per day
adult.notes: PDSA (S250): 'Pomeranians need around half an hour of exercise per day.' (key facts 'Minimum exercise (per day) | 30 minutes'); 'They don’t require a large amount of exercise.' — sources agree; RKC preferred (runbook rule).

energy.value: lively, curious and very playful
energy.quote: Pomeranians are lively, curious and very playful, always interested in a game if there’s one on offer!
energy.notes: PDSA (S250). AKC (S251): 'Poms enjoy short walks, runs, and outdoor playtime.' Covered by the game's walk and play (M5-R05) — nothing new to build.

temperament.quote: Extrovert, lively, and intelligent.
temperament.notes: RKC breed standard (S249) 'Temperament'. RKC breed page (S248): 'aided by its dainty appearance and extrovert character.'

time_alone.notes: No breed-specific statement found (RKC S247 / S248, PDSA S250 and AKC S251 checked) → no often_alone / needs_company tag.

housetraining.notes: AKC (S251). The game's potty training (M1) already models accidents and training — nothing new to build; no tag in the vocabulary.

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages anywhere. RKC Breed Watch Category 2 (S248) — the breed's points of concern were not returned (royalkennelclub.com Breed Watch page fetch error 2026-10-13), so no welfare chip is given; the RKC breed page (S248): 'This breed can be affected by conformational concerns' — open for David. Main topics (PDSA S250): kneecaps, windpipe, eyes, elbows, CM/SM, thyroid.

luxating_patella.value: luxating patellas — kneecaps slipping out of place
luxating_patella.quote: Luxating patellas – the kneecaps slipping temporarily out of place.

tracheal_collapse.value: tracheal collapse — the windpipe rings collapse, making breathing difficult

eyes.value: progressive retinal atrophy, cataracts, entropion (eyelids turning inwards); eye testing available
eyes.quote: Progressive retinal atrophy – gradual deterioration of the retina of the eye.
eyes.notes: PDSA (S250): 'Symptoms can start with night blindness and progress to total blindness.'; cataracts 'opacity of the lens of the eye – giving a ‘cloudy’ appearance.'; entropion 'inward turning eyelids.' RKC best-practice eye testing (S247): 'Eye testing using the BVA/KC/ISDS Eye Scheme'.

elbow_dysplasia.quote: Elbow dysplasia - elbow joint laxity as a result of poor development, which will eventually lead to arthritis.
elbow_dysplasia.notes: PDSA health list (S250). Not a Breed Watch point → no hips_hind_legs chip (that chip is about hind legs / hips).

syringomyelia.value: Chiari-like malformation / syringomyelia (CM/SM); a BVA/KC screening scheme exists
syringomyelia.quote: CM/SM screening using the KC/ BVA Chiari-like malformation/ syringomyelia (CM/SM) screening scheme
syringomyelia.notes: RKC breed page best-practice test (S247). PDSA (S250, paraphrase as returned): a painful neurological condition in which fluid-filled cavities form in the spinal cord near the brain; a BVA/Kennel Club scheme can test for it. Not a conformation chip (no Breed Watch point returned; the Cavalier's heart_and_spine chip is for heart disease + CM/SM).

hypothyroidism.quote: a condition in which there’s a decrease in thyroid hormone production.

other_pdsa.quote: Hydrocephalus – increased accumulation of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) in the ventricles of the brain.
other_pdsa.notes: PDSA (S250): Cushing's syndrome (Hyperadrenocorticism) 'hormonal disorder which results in the production off too much cortisol.' (sic). Research only — not exported.

Coren's own top / bottom-10 article (S34) does not list the breed. Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

training_notes.notes: AKC (S251). PDSA (S250): 'Training will require patience, but can be achieved using reward-based techniques.' Not a first-time-owner statement → no first_time_owner / experienced_owner tag.

colours.quote: All whole colours permissible, but free from black or white shadings.
colours.notes: RKC (S249): 'Whole colours are: white, black, brown, light or dark, blue as pale as possible.' 'Orange, which should be self-coloured and bright as possible.' 'Beaver.' 'Cream dogs have black noses and black eye-rims.' 'Merles not permissible.' Parti-colours and shaded sables are allowed by the RKC. FCI (S246): 'White, black, brown, orange, grey-shaded, other colours.'; disqualifying 'Definite white markings or spots in all non-white Toy Spitz dogs/Pomeranians.' The game draws only RKC whole colours (S249) the FCI also allows (orange, white, black, brown by name; cream under FCI 'other colours') — never merle, never white markings on a coloured dog, no parti-colour (FCI disqualifies white markings).

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). Orange first with the highest weight (portrait default), then cream, white, black, brown.

coat.value: double coat: soft fluffy undercoat, long straight harsh outer coat; abundant frill round neck and shoulders
coat.quote: Two coats, an undercoat and an outercoat.
coat.notes: RKC (S249): 'Former soft, fluffy; the latter long, perfectly straight, harsh in texture and covering whole of body;' 'very abundant round neck and fore part of shoulders and chest; forming frill, extending over shoulders.' FCI (S246): 'Hair must not look like being modelled.' The game draws a natural, untrimmed coat (not a sculpted show trim).

ears.value: small, set high, carried perfectly erect
ears.quote: Relatively small, not set too wide apart or too low down, but carried perfectly erect.
ears.notes: FCI (S246): 'The small ears are set high and relatively close to each other'.

eyes.value: medium size, slightly oval, dark and bright
eyes.quote: Medium size, slightly oval, not full or set too wide apart; bright, dark, and showing great intelligence.
eyes.notes: FCI (S246): 'The eyes are of medium size, almond-shaped, slightly slanting and dark.'

nose.value: black in orange, cream, white and shaded sable dogs; brown in brown dogs; fox-like head with a fine muzzle
nose.quote: Nose black in white, orange, and shaded sable dogs;
nose.notes: RKC (S249): 'brown in chocolate-tipped sable dogs, but in other colours may be self-coloured, never parti-coloured or flesh.'; 'Cream dogs have black noses and black eye-rims.'; 'Head and nose foxy in outline, skull slightly flat, large in proportion to muzzle,' (truncated). Not flat-faced.

tail.value: set high, turned over the back, carried flat and straight, profusely covered with long harsh hair
tail.quote: High-set, turned over back and carried flat and straight, profusely covered with long, harsh, spreading hair.
tail.notes: FCI (S246): 'The tail is set on high and of medium length.'

boston_terrier._note: Added 2026-10-13 (M5-R10-31, unattended run — appended after the Pomeranian: AKC 2024 No. 23, S174 table row '| **23** | Boston Terrier |'). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-13 (the tool limits quotes to ~125 characters — long sentences are quoted in pieces; curly apostrophes as returned); spot-check before import (sources.md S253–S263, reused S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45, S54, S92, S93, S135, S174). Lifespan: McMillan et al. 2024 names no Boston Terrier median in the published text or the corrected Fig. 3 legend (S54 checked 2026-10-13; S135 and the Dogs Trust breed table S123 refused by the fetch tool — provenance; the Dogs Trust 'shortest and longest' PDF a fetch error); no VetCompass Boston Terrier longevity paper found → runbook rule: the RKC lower bound 'Over 10 years' (S255). Wikipedia (S262, tier C) cites McMillan 2024 = 11.8 years — alternative only, never alone. Weight: the FCI (S254) and RKC (S257) standards give weight classes up to 25 lb / 11.35–11.5 kg (lightest class 'under 15 pounds' without a lower bound) → game range 7–11 kg = PDSA (S259), inside the standards' maximum. No standard gives a height → PDSA 38–43 cm (S259). RKC Breed Watch Category 2 (S255, S256) — points of concern not returned (no Breed Watch page found). This is a flat-faced (brachycephalic) welfare breed (PDSA S259, RKC breed page S255, RKC / University of Cambridge BOAS research S261): the French Bulldog rules apply (welfare chip, no marketing — BVA S92). Woodgreen and AKC trait ratings not attempted (the AKC breed page returned navigation only).

identity.value: FCI No. 140, Group 9 Section 11 (Small Molossian type), USA
identity.quote: FCI-CLASSIFICATION: Group 9 Companion and Toy Dogs.
identity.notes: FCI standard N° 140 (S254, EN PDF): 'Section 11 Small Molossian Dogs.'; 'Without working trial.'; 'ORIGIN: U.S.A.'; 'UTILIZATION: Companion.'; 'DATE OF PUBLICATION OF THE OFFICIAL VALID STANDARD: 28.01.2013'. FCI nomenclature (S253): 'BOSTON TERRIER', standard 140, 'n°9 - Companion and Toy Dogs', section 'Small Molossian type Dogs', country of origin 'UNITED STATES OF AMERICA', definitive acceptance '1/29/1955', valid standard '1/28/2013', 'Not subject to a working trial according to the FCI breeds nomenclature'. RKC group: Utility (S255 'The Utility breed group'). English name: Boston Terrier (RKC, AKC); nickname 'the American Gentleman' (Wikipedia S262, tier C).

size_class.notes: PDSA (S259) key facts: 'Small' — sources agree. Weight up to 11.5 kg (S257).

pdsa_average.notes: PDSA key-facts box 'Average height' (label as returned by the tool; value verbatim). The FCI (S254) and RKC (S257) standards give no height. Wikipedia (S262, tier C) infobox '9–15 in (23–38 cm)' — lower; not used. Spot-check the PDSA value.

fci.quote: 20 pounds and not to exceed 25 pounds (9 to 11,35 kg).
fci.notes: FCI (S254) weight classes, not per sex: 'Weight is divided by classes as follows:' / 'under 15 pounds (6,8 kg),' / '15 pounds and under 20 pounds (6,8 to 9 kg),' / '20 pounds and not to exceed 25 pounds (9 to 11,35 kg).' The lightest class has no lower bound → stored as 6.8–11.35 kg (middle + heavy classes); maximum 11.35 kg.

rkc.notes: RKC breed standard (S257, 'Last updated November 2025'): lightweight under 6.8 kg, middleweight 6.8 to under 9.1 kg, heavyweight 9.1 to under 11.4 kg (paraphrase as returned); the KC standard as hosted by KUSA (S258): 'Lightweight: under 6.8kg.' / 'Middleweight: 6.8kg and under 9.1kg.' / 'Heavyweight: 9.1kg and under 11.4kg.' Stored as 6.8–11.5 kg (lightest class without a lower bound). AKC (S260): 'Boston Terriers are short-tailed little dogs that weigh no more than 25 pounds.'

pdsa.notes: PDSA key-facts box 'Average weight' (label as returned), one range for both sexes (stored per sex). Inside the FCI / RKC maximum. The game range (adult_weight_kg 7–11).

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. PDSA 7–11 kg (S259) ≈ 15.4–24.3 lb → the 'Small (12–24 pounds)' class (the top touches 'Medium'). The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 60 min is reached at 6 months).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Boston Terrier growth curve found.

rkc.notes: RKC breed page (S255; older address S256 the same). PDSA (S259) key facts 'Average lifespan': 'Over 10 years' — sources agree. The basis of the senior boundary (runbook: RKC lower bound when no McMillan 2024 / VetCompass value is reachable).

pdsa.notes: PDSA key-facts box 'Average lifespan' (label as returned).

mcmillan_2024.notes: McMillan et al. 2024: the corrected Fig. 3 legend (S54, read 2026-10-13) names eight breeds, not the Boston Terrier; the published text (S135) and the Dogs Trust breed table (S123) were refused by the fetch tool (provenance), the 'shortest and longest' PDF returned a fetch error, the LJMU news, Dogs Trust research page and Science News article name no Boston Terrier value. Wikipedia (S262, tier C) quotes McMillan 2024 as 11.8 years — UNSOURCED as an A/B value; verify in the McMillan 2024 supplementary table / S123 before replacing the RKC lower bound.

time_alone.quote: This breed doesn’t fare well when left alone for extended periods of time.
time_alone.notes: AKC (S260) — breed-specific ('This breed …'), not the general four-hour advice → consider tag needs_company (Boxer precedent); never often_alone. PDSA (S259) has no time-alone statement.

other_pets.quote: They form strong connections with family members and can get along well with other dogs.
other_pets.notes: AKC (S260): also 'They’re highly sociable and tend to be open with children, unfamiliar faces, and other dogs.' (as returned). Other dogs only — no statement about cats or small household pets → no other_pets tag. No prey-drive statement → no chases_small_pets.

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; percentages stay here and are never shown in the app, the register export or audience docs. Flat-faced (brachycephalic) welfare breed: PDSA (S259) 'Boston Terriers are a brachycephalic (flat-faced) breed.'; RKC / University of Cambridge BOAS research (S261) 'Boston Terriers are brachycephalic, which is why they were included in our research alongside other breeds.' → brachycephalic_breathing chip (flat face + heat, PDSA S259; as the French Bulldog and the Bulldog); BVA advises against brachycephalic imagery in advertising (S92) → in the app yes, in marketing no. RKC Breed Watch Category 2 (S255) — points of concern not returned.

brachycephaly_boas.value: flat-faced (brachycephalic) breed; brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome (BOAS) — narrowed nostrils, elongated soft palate, noisy or difficult breathing
brachycephaly_boas.quote: Boston Terriers are a brachycephalic (flat-faced) breed.
brachycephaly_boas.notes: PDSA (S259): 'Boston Terriers are likely to suffer from serious health and welfare issues due to their physical conformation,' / 'including severe breathing difficulties and eye problems.'; health list: brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome (upper-airway abnormalities incl. narrowed nostrils and an elongated soft palate — paraphrase). RKC breed page (S255): 'Dogs with a flat, wide-shaped head, are said to be brachycephalic' / 'The soft tissue in the nose and throat of some brachycephalic dogs may be excessive for the airways,' / 'making it difficult for them to breathe normally (causing heavy panting or noisy breathing).' RKC / University of Cambridge BOAS Research Group (S261): 'Boston Terriers are brachycephalic, which is why they were included in our research alongside other breeds.'; 'the findings confirm that Boston Terriers are affected by BOAS'; 'they are less severely impacted than some of the more popular flat-faced breeds'; key risk factors 'stenotic nostrils, facial foreshortening' (as returned; the share of unaffected dogs is research only). The RKC plans to expand the Respiratory Function Grading scheme to the breed (S261, paraphrase) — not yet a listed scheme. Standards: FCI fault 'Pinched nostrils.' (S254); RKC 'Nostrils open.' (S257). UK Brachycephalic Working Group (S93): 'Stop and think before buying a flat-faced dog.'

breed_watch.value: RKC Breed Watch Category 2 — points of concern not returned
breed_watch.notes: RKC breed page (S255) key fact 'Breed Watch category' (label as returned); older address (S256): 'This breed can be affected by conformational concerns'. No Breed Watch page / tally sheet for the breed found (2026-10-13) → no Breed-Watch-based chip (eyelid_problems, sensitive_skin); the welfare chip comes from the flat face.

eyes.value: prominent eyes at risk of trauma, ulcers and dryness; dry eye (KCS), cherry eye
eyes.quote: Some brachycephalic dogs may have shallow eye sockets, causing their eyes to become more prominent
eyes.notes: RKC breed page (S255): 'at a higher risk of trauma, ulcers and increasing the chance of them becoming dry and painful'. PDSA (S259) health list: dry eye (KCS), cherry eye (paraphrase); 'including severe breathing difficulties and eye problems.' RKC standard (S257): overly prominent eyes 'highly undesirable' (as returned). FCI fault 'Eyes showing too much white or haw.' No eye-care frequency found → no routine.

spine_hemivertebrae.notes: PDSA (S259) health list (paraphrase as returned: spinal bone deformities press on the spinal cord, causing weakness, loss of hind-limb function and incontinence). No verbatim quote → no chip (back_spine needs a quoted source).

luxating_patella.value: luxating patellas (kneecaps slip out of place)

skin_atopy.notes: PDSA (S259) health list (paraphrase). RKC breed page (S255): 'Some brachycephalic dogs may have an excess of skin, which creates folds, especially around the front of the face.' — general brachycephalic text; the breed standards ask for a skull and muzzle 'free from wrinkles' (FCI S254) → no face-fold routine, no sensitive_skin chip (no Breed Watch point returned).

teeth.value: shortened jaw with the same number of teeth — crowding
teeth.quote: Dogs with a shortened skull will often have a shortened jaw, but the number and size of teeth will stay the same.
teeth.notes: RKC breed page (S255), general brachycephalic text (dental / gum problems — paraphrase). No tooth-brushing frequency for the breed → no routine (ROADMAP M5-R15 covers tooth brushing in general).

birth.value: difficult births; caesarean sections often needed
birth.notes: PDSA (S259) health list (paraphrase). Background for parents only — the game has no breeding.

heat.value: prone to overheating — never exercise in the heat of the day
heat.quote: but it’s important to remember that they should never be exercised in the heat of the day as they are prone to overheating.
heat.notes: PDSA (S259). Wikipedia (S262, tier C): hyperthermia through 'an inability to effectively reduce body temperature via panting.' → exercise.heat_and_walk_timing (ROADMAP M5-R14).

welfare_advice_to_buyers.value: PDSA strongly recommends considering a healthier breed, crossbreed or mongrel; UK vets: stop and think before buying a flat-faced dog

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table of Coren's ranking (S35, read 2026-10-13): rank 54, shared with the Akita, under 'Average Working/Obedience Intelligence' (ranks 40–54). Coren's own top / bottom-10 article (S34) does not list the breed (runbook: rank from S35). Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

coren_tier.notes: Tier 'Average Working/Obedience Intelligence' = ranks 40–54 (S35, as returned). Tier definitions from Wikipedia; verify in book.

training_notes.value: responds well to training; eager to please; sensitive — no harsh methods
training_notes.quote: They respond well to training and enjoy the extra mental stimulation.
training_notes.notes: PDSA (S259): reward-based techniques. AKC (S260): 'Bostons are eager to please their owners, making them generally easier to train.' / 'Being a more sensitive breed, Bostons don’t respond well to harsh training methods.' Not a first-time-owner statement → no first_time_owner tag.

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value — see proposed_game_parameters.boston_terrier.learning_multiplier (1.0, runbook rule: Average tier, rank 54).

general.value: lively, smooth-coated, short-headed, compactly built, short-tailed, well balanced; brindle, seal or black, evenly marked with white
general.quote: The Boston Terrier is a lively, highly intelligent, smooth coated, short-headed, compactly built,
general.notes: FCI (S254): 'shorttailed, well balanced dog, brindle, seal or black in colour and evenly marked with white.' RKC (S257): 'A small, smooth-coated, square-headed, compactly built, short-tailed and wellbalanced dog.'

colours.quote: Colour: Brindle, seal or black with white markings. Brindle is preferred only if all other qualities are equal.
colours.notes: FCI (S254): '(Note : Seal defined : Seal appears black except it has a red cast when viewed in the sun or bright light).'; 'Required markings: White muzzle band, white blaze between the eyes, white forechest.'; disqualifying 'Solid black, solid brindle, or solid seal without required white markings.' and 'Grey or liver colours.' RKC (S257): 'Brindle: being a mixture of any shade of brown and black with white markings;' / 'Any other colour or combination of colours unacceptable'; brindle with white preferred (paraphrase; KUSA copy S258: 'Black with white markings but brindles with white markings preferred.'). Never solid colours without white, grey (blue), liver, fawn / red, merle; FCI disqualifies blue eyes and a Dudley nose.

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). No colour frequencies. Draw over the three standard colours, always with the required white markings; brindle and white weighted highest so the register portrait is brindle and white — the colour both the FCI (S254) and the RKC (S257 / S258) name as preferred. Proposal: brindle and white 0.45, black and white 0.30, seal and white 0.25.

coat.value: short, smooth, bright and fine
coat.quote: Hair: Short, smooth, bright and fine in texture.
coat.notes: RKC standard (S257): 'Short, smooth, lustrous and fine in texture.' RKC breed page (S255): 'Coat length: Short'.

ears.value: small, erect, set near the corners of the skull — natural (never cropped)
ears.quote: Small, carried erect, either natural or cropped to conform to the shape of the head
ears.notes: FCI (S254): 'and situated as near to the corners of the skull as possible.' RKC (S257): 'Small, thin, triangular in shape with height slightly greater than width, tapering to tip.' The AI portrait shows natural ears only (ear cropping is not shown).

eyes.value: wide apart, large, round, dark; not overly prominent
eyes.quote: Wide apart, large, round and dark in colour.
eyes.notes: RKC (S257): 'Set wide apart, relatively large, round, dark in colour.'; overly prominent eyes 'highly undesirable' (as returned). FCI fault: 'Eyes showing too much white or haw.'; disqualifying 'Eyes blue in colour or any trace of blue.'

nose.value: black, wide nose with open nostrils; muzzle short, square, wide and deep, free from wrinkles, about one-third of the skull length
nose.quote: Black and wide, with a well defined line between the nostrils.
nose.notes: FCI (S254) muzzle: 'Short, square, wide and deep and in proportion to the skull.' / 'It is free from wrinkles, shorter in length than in width or depth;' / 'not exceeding in length approximately one-third of the length of the skull.'; fault 'Pinched nostrils.'. RKC (S257): 'Muzzle relatively short, square, wide, and deep;' / 'Nostrils open.' BOAS risk factors stenotic nostrils and facial foreshortening (S261) → the AI appearance keeps a moderate, not extremely short muzzle with open nostrils and no wrinkles (welfare rule, as for the French Bulldog).

tail.value: set low, short, fine and tapering, straight or screw, never above the horizontal; natural (never docked)
tail.quote: Set-on low, short, fine and tapering, straight or screw and must not be carried above the horizontal.
tail.notes: FCI disqualifying fault 'Docked tail.' RKC (S257): 'Set on low; short, fine, tapering, straight or curled; devoid of fringes or coarse hair, never carried above horizontal.' The portrait shows a short natural straight tail.

rkc_shedding.notes: AKC (S260): 'Bostons’ coats are fine and sleek, and shed minimally.' — conflicting sources (sheds yes vs minimally) → neither sheds nor low_shedding (runbook §3).

akc_children.quote: They do well with children who know how to be gentle with animals.
akc_children.notes: AKC (S260) — caveat for the children tag.

akc_time_alone.quote: This breed doesn’t fare well when left alone for extended periods of time.

akc_grooming.quote: Bostons only require occasional bathing, and their nails should be trimmed regularly.
