miniature_american_shepherd._note: Added 2026-10-13 (M5-R10-32, unattended run — appended after the Boston Terrier: AKC 2024 No. 24, S174 full-list table 'ranks 20–30: … Boston Terrier, Miniature American Shepherd, Havanese …'). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-13 (the tool limits quotes to ~125 characters — long sentences are quoted in pieces; apostrophes as returned); spot-check before import (sources.md S264–S271, reused S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45, S123, S174). The breed is provisionally recognised by the FCI (No. 367, 2019, S264) and was recognised by The Royal Kennel Club in April 2026 (imported register — the RKC breed page and news item were found by search but every fetch of royalkennelclub.com returned an error, so no RKC key facts). No PDSA, Woodgreen or Dogs Trust breed page; no McMillan 2024 row (Dogs Trust table S123: no row); no VetCompass paper. Required fields therefore come from tier B: adult weight = AKC breed weight chart (S268, 'Is it a good fit' S267 agrees), exercise = PetMD (S269, DVM-written and DVM-reviewed, the S10 / S37 precedent for PetMD as tier B), lifespan = PetMD 12–13 years (S269) → senior boundary seeded verified=false (Claude's suggestion, open for David — runbook §3 closest row, Bernese / Cane Corso precedent). Not a welfare-concern breed (no conformation concern in any source) → in marketing.

identity.value: FCI No. 367, Group 1 Section 1 (Sheepdogs), USA
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S264): standard 367, group 'n°1 - Sheepdogs and Cattledogs (except Swiss Cattledogs)', section 'Sheepdogs', country of origin 'UNITED STATES OF AMERICA', provisional acceptance '9/4/2019', 'Not subject to a working trial according to the FCI breeds nomenclature'. FCI standard (S265): 'FCI-CLASSIFICATION: Group 1 Sheepdogs and Cattledogs (except Swiss Cattledogs)', 'Section 1 Sheepdogs', 'ORIGIN: United States of America.', 'UTILIZATION: Farm and ranch shepherd dog.', 'DATE OF PUBLICATION OF THE OFFICIAL VALID STANDARD: 04/09/2019.' AKC: Herding group, recognised 2015 (Wikipedia S271, tier C: 'was recognised by the American Kennel Club (AKC) in 2015 and is the club's 186th breed.'). Former name (AKC S270): 'Initially, the breed's name was Miniature Australian Shepherds'. English name: Miniature American Shepherd (AKC, FCI); nicknames 'Mini American', 'MAS' (S271, tier C).

size_class.quote: The Miniature American Shepherd is a small size herding dog that originated in the United States.
size_class.notes: FCI standard (S265, tier A). Alternative: PetMD (S269) uses 'medium-sized dogs' in its nutrition section ('high-quality puppy food for medium-sized dogs'); the AKC weight chart 20–40 lb (S268) ≈ 9.1–18.1 kg spans the top of the S10 'Small (12–24 pounds)' and the 'Medium (24–59 pounds)' weight classes — growth end uses the Medium weight class (S10). No RKC / PDSA size field reachable. Tier A preferred → small (QA review 2026-10-13).

alternatives.notes: PetMD nutrition wording

fci.quote: Males: 35.5 cm up to 46 cm at the top of the withers
fci.notes: FCI (S265): 'Females: 33 cm up to and including 43.5 cm at the top of the withers.'; disqualification outside these limits (dogs under 35.5 or over 46 cm, bitches under 33 or over 43.5 cm — paraphrase; not applied under six months). AKC standard (S266): 'Height for dogs is 14 inches up to and including 18 inches at the top of the withers.' / 'Height for bitches is 13 inches up to and including 17 inches at top of withers.'

akc.quote: Miniature American Shepherd | 20-40 pounds | 20-40 pounds
akc.notes: AKC breed weight chart (S268), row as returned (male | female): 20–40 lb for both sexes = 9.07–18.14 kg → stored as 9.1–18.1 kg. AKC (S267): 'Mini Americans stand between 13 and 18 inches at the shoulder, and weigh between 20 and 40 pounds.' PetMD (S269): 'A full-grown Miniature American Shepherd stands 13–18 inches tall and weighs 20–40 pounds.' — sources agree. Neither standard gives a weight (FCI S265: 'Healthy weight will vary based on individual size, sex and substance.'; AKC standard S266 has no weight statement). The game range (adult_weight_kg 9.1–18.1).

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. 20–40 lb (S268) → mostly the 'Medium' class (the bottom touches 'Small (12–24 pounds): 9–12 months'). The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 60 min is reached at 6 months).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Miniature American Shepherd growth curve found.

petmd.quote: The average Miniature American Shepherd lifespan is 12–13 years, and they're considered a generally healthy breed.
petmd.notes: PetMD (S269, Michelle Diener DVM, reviewed by Sarah Wooten DVM, updated 2026-09-29). The only A/B lifespan value found. Wikipedia (S271, tier C): 'The MAS has an expected lifespan of 13–15 years.' (citing Vetstreet) — alternative only, never alone. The lower bound 12 is the basis of the senior suggestion (verified=false).

rkc.notes: UNSOURCED — the RKC breed page (imported register, recognised April 2026) was found by search (royalkennelclub.com/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/pastoral/miniature-american-shepherd-imp/) but every fetch returned an error (2026-10-13); no lifespan field read.

mcmillan_2024.notes: UNSOURCED — no Miniature American Shepherd row in the Dogs Trust table of McMillan et al. 2024 (S123, checked 2026-10-13: 'NO ROW'; Australian Shepherd row present). No VetCompass Miniature American Shepherd longevity paper found.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × 12 y (PetMD lower bound '12–13 years', S269) → 0.75 × 12 = 9 y = 108 months. The runbook rule (McMillan 2024, else a VetCompass median, else the RKC lower bound) yields no value for this breed → closest row (Bernese Mountain Dog / Cane Corso precedent): a tier-B breed range from a vet-reviewed page, seeded verified=false (Claude's suggestion, open for David). Alternatives: Wikipedia 13–15 y (S271, tier C) → 0.75 × 13 × 12 = 117; Dogs Trust > 7 y (S14) = 84.

adult.quote: This breed has a lot of energy and needs at least one hour (ideally two) of exercise every day.
adult.notes: PetMD (S269). Runbook rule: 'at least N' → N = 60 ('ideally two' hours = 120 recorded as an alternative). AKC (S267): 'Mini Americans are an active, athletic breed and require a moderate amount of exercise.' / 'neglecting to give them regular exercise will cause them to misbehave.' (no number); AKC (S270): 'This breed requires more than average exercise but can still be adaptable to their family's way of life.' No RKC / PDSA exercise field reachable.

alternatives.notes: PetMD 'ideally two' hours — not the rule's number (at least N → N).

energy.value: athletic and energetic; strength and stamina for an active lifestyle
energy.quote: They are athletic and have a lot of energy
energy.notes: PetMD (S269). AKC (S270): 'Despite its smaller size, this breed has enough strength and stamina to keep pace with any active lifestyle.'

temperament.value: intelligent working dog of strong herding and guardian instincts; protective, good natured, devoted and loyal with the family; reserved with strangers
temperament.quote: The Miniature American Shepherd is intelligent, primarily a working dog of strong herding and guardian instincts.
temperament.notes: AKC standard (S266): 'With his family he is protective, good natured, devoted and loyal.' FCI (S265) the same first sentence. AKC (S270): 'With family members, Miniature American Shepherds are affectionate, loving, and sometimes cuddly'; 'Miniature American Shepherds have strong guardian instincts.' AKC (S267): 'They can be weary of new faces, but early, consistent socialization will build up a Mini American's confidence in new situations.'

family.value: can make great family dogs (with obedience training and early socialisation); good with children but may try to herd them
family.quote: Mini Americans can make for great family dogs, especially with proper obedience training and early socialization.
family.notes: AKC (S267): 'They tend to be good with children, but may try to herd them.' / 'Kids who understand the nature of dogs and the responsibility of owning a pet will likely be better suited for this breed.' PetMD (S269): 'Miniature American Shepherds make great family dogs due to their affection, intellect' and 'They are good with children and other pets but should be supervised initially when they are getting to know a new family member.' → family_pet, children (caveats kept: supervision at first, kids who understand dogs) and may_herd_children; no small-children rating → never small_children.

herding_children.quote: They tend to be good with children, but may try to herd them.
herding_children.notes: AKC (S267). Herding with nipping at heels (AKC S270): 'With some nipping at heels, this breed herds small flocks of goats, sheep, and ducks.' → may_herd_children (Australian Shepherd / Pembroke Welsh Corgi precedent).

socialisation.value: early, consistent socialisation builds confidence (can be wary of new faces)
socialisation.quote: They can be weary of new faces, but early, consistent socialization will build up a Mini American's confidence in new situations.
socialisation.notes: AKC (S267, 'weary' as returned). AKC (S267): 'Early socialization and puppy training courses are recommended for all breeds.' PetMD (S269): 'Enrolling your pup into a socialization class and/or puppy obedience class can help them grow up to be a well-behaved dog.' → proposed_game_parameters.miniature_american_shepherd.socialisation (DOG_SOCIALISATION row, M5-R17).

mental_stimulation.value: needs jobs to stay active and prevent boredom; happiest when the mind is engaged
mental_stimulation.quote: Miniature American Shepherds need to be given jobs to stay active and prevent boredom.
mental_stimulation.notes: PetMD (S269): 'Along with physical activity, Miniature American Shepherds are happiest when their minds are engaged' → needs_mental_stimulation (a need, not just enjoyment).

time_alone.value: devotion to family can lead to separation anxiety when left alone
time_alone.quote: Their devotion to family can lead to separation anxiety when they're left alone.
time_alone.notes: PetMD (S269), breed-specific ('Their devotion to family …'); the article recommends crate training puppies and interactive toys (paraphrase) → consider tag needs_company (Boxer / Boston Terrier precedent); never often_alone.

other_pets.value: affectionate and friendly with other pets; good with other pets (supervise at first)
other_pets.quote: They’re extremely affectionate and friendly with their families and other pets.
other_pets.notes: AKC (S267). PetMD (S269): 'They are good with children and other pets but should be supervised initially when they are getting to know a new family member.' → other_pets (with the caveat). No prey-drive statement → no chases_small_pets.

chewing.notes: No breed-specific statement found (AKC S267 / S270, PetMD S269 checked) → no chews_when_bored tag.

food_motivation.notes: No breed-specific appetite statement → no food_motivated_weight tag. PetMD (S269): two meals a day, 'Always measure the food for each meal.' (general feeding advice).

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages exist in these sources and none are ever shown in the app, the register export or audience docs. PetMD (S269): 'considered a generally healthy breed'. Not a conformation welfare-concern breed (no BVA / RKC Breed Watch / VetCompass concern found) → no welfare chip; in marketing.

eyes.value: collie eye anomaly, progressive retinal atrophy, cataracts — eye examination / DNA testing of the parents
eyes.quote: Reputable breeders will have their dogs’ eyes examined and/or be genetically tested for this condition.
eyes.notes: PetMD (S269) on collie eye anomaly; PRA: 'This condition is usually diagnosed in Miniature American Shepherds when they are 3–9 years old.'; cataracts: 'Cataracts are usually hereditary, so ask breeders about eye screening for the parents.'

hip_dysplasia.quote: Reputable Miniature American Shepherd breeders make sure their dogs are screened for this genetic condition.
hip_dysplasia.notes: PetMD (S269), hip dysplasia section.

luxating_patella.quote: Miniature American Shepherds should be evaluated for patellar luxation before breeding or if they have rear leg lameness.

mdr1.value: MDR1 gene mutation (sensitivity to some medicines) — every dog should be tested
mdr1.quote: All Miniature American Shepherds should be tested for this genetic mutation.
mdr1.notes: PetMD (S269), MDR1 section (as for the Australian Shepherd, the breed it was developed from).

merle.quote: With no order of preference, the recognized colors are black, blue merle, red, liver and red or liver merle.
merle.notes: FCI (S265). The game draws standard colours only; the register never advises merle-to-merle breeding (no source read for it here — background only).

coren_rank.notes: Not ranked: the Wikipedia table of Coren's ranking (S35) does not list the Miniature American Shepherd — the ranking (1994) predates the breed's AKC recognition (2015, S271). Runbook rule: unranked → 1.0.

coren_tier.notes: Unranked (S35).

training_notes.value: intelligent and eager to please — easy to train
training_notes.quote: Miniature American Shepherds are intelligent and eager-to-please dogs, which makes them easy to train.
training_notes.notes: PetMD (S269). AKC (S267): 'Miniature American Shepherds are bright by nature, and eager to please their owners.'; AKC (S270): 'They catch on quickly to new ideas, and accompanying you on a walk is a real treat for this breed.' Not a first-time-owner statement → no first_time_owner tag.

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value — see proposed_game_parameters.miniature_american_shepherd.learning_multiplier (1.0, runbook rule: unranked).

general.value: small, athletic herding dog, slightly longer than tall, moderate bone; medium-length straight-to-wavy coat; black, blue merle, red / liver or red / liver merle, with or without white and tan markings
general.quote: The Miniature American Shepherd is a small size herding dog that originated in the United States.
general.notes: FCI (S265): slightly longer than tall, moderate bone, smooth balanced movement, athletic and intelligent (paraphrase as returned).

colours.quote: With no order of preference, the recognized colors are black, blue merle, red, liver and red or liver merle.
colours.notes: AKC standard (S266): 'With no order of preference, the recognized colors are black, blue merle, red (liver) and red merle.' White and tan markings are permitted within limits (paraphrase); FCI (S265): 'The hairline of a white collar does not exceed the withers at the skin.'; 'White on the head does not predominate, and the eyes are fully surrounded by color and pigment.'; disqualifying 'White body splashes, which means any conspicuous, isolated spot or patch of white' and colours other than the recognised ones. Merle is a standard colour for this breed (runbook §3, as the Australian Shepherd).

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). No colour frequencies; both standards rank no colour ('no order of preference'). Proposal (Australian Shepherd precedent): blue merle with white and tan markings 0.35 (the register portrait), black 0.25, red merle 0.20, red 0.20, each with or without white and tan markings within the limits.

coat.value: medium texture, straight to wavy, weather resistant, medium length; moderate
coat.quote: Hair is of medium texture, straight to wavy, weather resistant, and of medium length.
coat.notes: AKC standard (S266): 'Moderation is the overall impression of the coat.' AKC (S270): 'Their weather-resistant double coat is medium-length.'

ears.value: triangular, moderate size, set high — folding (never prick)
ears.quote: Are triangular, of moderate size, set high on the head.
ears.notes: FCI (S265): 'Severe Fault - Prick ears and ears that hang with no lift.'

eyes.value: brown, blue, hazel, amber or any combination; eyes fully surrounded by colour
eyes.quote: Acceptable in all coat colors, one or both eyes may be brown, blue, hazel, amber or any color combination thereof
eyes.notes: FCI (S265); oval-set, almond-shaped (paraphrase); eye rims match the nose pigmentation (paraphrase).

tail.value: docked or natural bobtail preferred; the undocked tail may hang in a slight curve — drawn natural, undocked
tail.quote: The undocked tail when at rest may hang in a slight curve.
tail.notes: FCI (S265): 'A docked or natural bobtail is preferred.' (AKC S266 the same). The game draws a natural, undocked tail (no docking — Australian Shepherd precedent).

suitability._note: Source = AKC (S267, S270) and PetMD (S269). The RKC breed page could not be fetched (error), the breed has no PDSA / Woodgreen page → no RKC fields (size of home, garden, town or country). Not `apartment` (RKC only); PetMD (S269): 'apartments are not ideal for them unless they participate in daily exercise' / 'The perfect home for this breed has a large, fenced yard where they can run around with other dogs.' — no tag (large_home is RKC only; a 'perfect home' is not a secure-fencing need).

akc_family.quote: Mini Americans can make for great family dogs, especially with proper obedience training and early socialization.

petmd_family.quote: Miniature American Shepherds make great family dogs due to their affection, intellect
petmd_family.notes: PetMD (S269), caring section (sentence continues '… and good temperament around children and other pets.' as returned in paraphrase).

akc_children.value: tend to be good with children, but may try to herd them
akc_children.quote: They tend to be good with children, but may try to herd them.
akc_children.notes: Basis of children (caveat: herding; AKC 'Kids who understand the nature of dogs and the responsibility of owning a pet will likely be better suited for this breed.') and may_herd_children. No small-children rating → never small_children.

petmd_children_pets.value: good with children and other pets; supervise at first
petmd_children_pets.quote: They are good with children and other pets but should be supervised initially when they are getting to know a new family member.
petmd_children_pets.notes: Caveat kept: supervised initially with a new family member.

akc_other_pets.value: affectionate and friendly with other pets
akc_other_pets.quote: They’re extremely affectionate and friendly with their families and other pets.

akc_grooming.value: weekly brushing most of the year, daily during shedding season; mats and tangles
akc_grooming.quote: Weekly brushing is sufficient during most of the year, with daily brushing during shedding season.
akc_grooming.notes: AKC (S267): 'Be mindful of mats and tangles.' AKC (S270): monthly bath and weekly brushing, daily brushing during shedding (paraphrase). The out-of-season number 1 is the alternative to PetMD's 'a couple times a week' (2).

petmd_grooming.value: brushed a couple times a week
petmd_grooming.quote: The Miniature American Shepherd needs to be brushed a couple times a week to control shedding and minimize matting.
petmd_grooming.notes: PetMD (S269); during the heavy shedding seasons 'their coat should be brushed every day.' Basis of the brushing goal 2× a week (M5-R13). Not frequent_grooming: AKC (S267) says weekly brushing is sufficient most of the year — conflicting sources → no chip (runbook §3, as the Boston Terrier's shedding).

akc_shedding.value: sheds a fair amount, heavier once or twice a year
akc_shedding.quote: The breed sheds a fair amount, with heavier seasons of shedding once or twice a year.

petmd_shedding.value: sheds year-round with one or two heavy seasons
petmd_shedding.quote: This breed sheds year-round, with one or two heavy shedding seasons (in the spring and/or fall) every year.

akc_nails.quote: Like with all breeds, you should trim a Miniature American Shepherd's nails regularly to prevent discomfort.
akc_nails.notes: AKC (S267) — a sourced need without a game mechanic → proposed_game_parameters.miniature_american_shepherd.nail_trimming → ROADMAP M5-R19 (needs-david).

akc_home.quote: Miniature American Shepherds are an adaptable breed, and would be happy in the city, suburbs, or more rural areas.
akc_home.notes: No apartment / large_home tag (both are RKC-only criteria).

rkc_page.notes: UNSOURCED — the RKC breed page (imported register) returned a fetch error on every attempt (2026-10-13); no RKC fields recorded.

chihuahua._note: Added 2026-10-13 (M5-R10-33, unattended run — appended after the Miniature American Shepherd: AKC 2024 No. 27, S174 full-list table 'ranks 24–30: Miniature American Shepherd, Havanese, Siberian Husky, Chihuahua, …' — Havanese and Siberian Husky are already in). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-13 (the tool limits quotes to ~125 characters — long sentences are quoted in pieces; apostrophes as returned); spot-check before import (sources.md S272–S280, reused S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45, S92, S174). The game builds the **Smooth Coat** variety: The Royal Kennel Club lists Chihuahua (Smooth Coat) and Chihuahua (Long Coat) as two breeds (S275), the FCI keeps one breed with two varieties (S272); grooming, coat and the portrait follow the smooth coat (Dachshund 'smooth coat' precedent). Lifespan: no McMillan 2024 value reachable (Dogs Trust tables S123 and 'shortest and longest' returned a provenance block / fetch error, PMC a browser check); the VetCompass breed paper (S279) gives a median age at death of 8.2 years but its authors call the population 'young expanding' and say this biases age at death downwards — so the senior boundary uses the RKC / PDSA lower bound 'Over 12 years' (108 months) as Claude's suggestion, seeded verified=false (open for David; the strict rule order would give 74). Not a flat-faced breed (KC S274 'muzzle moderately short, slightly pointed'; no BVA / VetCompass source calls it brachycephalic) → in marketing; RKC Breed Watch Category 2 (S276) without returned points → no welfare chip (Pomeranian precedent, open for David).

identity.value: FCI No. 218, Group 9 Section 6 (Chihuahueño), Mexico
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S272): group 'n°9 - Chiens d'agrément et de compagnie', section 'Chihuahueno', country 'MEXIQUE' (as returned, French page); varieties 'a) Poil long' and 'b) Poil court'; the English standard row names it 'CHIHUAHUA'; not subject to a working trial; valid standard 04/09/2019. FCI standard (S273, Italian text hosted by ENCI): 'CLASSIFICAZIONE FCI: Gruppo 9 Cani da compagnia' (Section 6), 'ORIGINE: Messico.'

size_class.notes: PDSA (S277): 'Size | Small' — sources agree. RKC group: Toy (S275). Weight 1.8–2.7 kg (S274) = the smallest weight band (S8).

pdsa_average.notes: PDSA key facts (S277), one range for both sexes (stored per sex). No breed standard gives a height: FCI (S273) 'In questa razza non si tiene conto della taglia, ma solo del peso.' (size is not taken into account, only weight); the KC standard (S274) gives weight only. Bulldog / Boston Terrier precedent: the PDSA average range.

rkc.notes: KC breed standard (S274, hosted by KUSA, KC [01-2015]), one range for both sexes (stored per sex). PDSA (S277): 'Average weight | 1.8-2.7 kg' — agrees. The game range (adult_weight_kg).

fci.quote: Peso ideale: fra 1,5 kg. e 2,5 kg.
fci.notes: FCI standard (S273, Italian): ideal weight 1.5–2.5 kg; 'Peso: da 1 a 3 kg.' (accepted 1–3 kg); 'I cani che pesano meno di 1 kg. e più di 3 kg. saranno squalificati.' (under 1 kg or over 3 kg disqualified). Background only; the register shows the KC / PDSA range.

salt_category.notes: Category assignment by weight is ours (general_by_size.size_classes.salt_2017_bands_kg, S8): 1.8–2.7 kg = the smallest band. Salt 2017 breed list not checked.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. 1.8–2.7 kg ≈ 4–6 lb sits at the lower edge of 'Toy (5–12 pounds)' — the smallest class PetMD gives, used as the nearest (Pomeranian precedent). The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 30 min is reached at 3 months).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Chihuahua growth curve found.

rkc.notes: RKC breed page (S275). PDSA (S277): 'Average lifespan | Over 12 years' — same. The basis of the senior suggestion (verified=false — see senior_from).

vetcompass.quote: Median age at death from this young expanding population was 8.2 years (IQR 3.5–12.1).
vetcompass.notes: O'Neill et al. 2020, BMC Veterinary Research 16:42 (S279, RVC repository copy), VetCompass 2016. 'The median age of the Chihuahuas overall was 2.8 years (interquartile range [IQR] 1.6–4.9, range 0.1–18.6).' The authors (Discussion): a young population 'would have the effect of biasing the age at death results downwards.' RVC infographic (S280): 'live on average 8.2 years'. Not shown in the app or the register (a misleading median of a young population — runbook §4 export rule); background for the senior decision only.

mcmillan_2024.notes: UNSOURCED — McMillan et al. 2024: the Dogs Trust breed table (S123) URL was refused by the fetch tool (not in this session's provenance set), the Dogs Trust 'shortest and longest' PDF returned a fetch error, PMC (PMC11021557) a browser check, Science News (no breed value) — 2026-10-13. Check S123 before replacing the RKC lower bound.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × 12 y (RKC / PDSA lower bound 'Over 12 years', S275 / S277) → 0.75 × 12 = 9 y = 108 months. The strict runbook order (McMillan 2024, else a VetCompass median, else the RKC lower bound) would take the VetCompass median 8.2 y (S279) → round(0.75 × 8.2 × 12) = 74 months, but its own authors say the young population biases age at death downwards; 74 months (6 years) would also contradict both the RKC and the PDSA 'Over 12 years'. → Claude's suggestion 108, seeded verified=false (also the senior arrival age), open for David. Dogs Trust rule of thumb > 7 y = 84 months (S14).

adult.quote: Exercise: Up to 30 minutes per day
adult.notes: PDSA (S277): 'Your Chihuahua will need a minimum of half an hour exercise' / 'every day to stay happy and healthy.' (key facts 'Minimum exercise (per day) | 30 minutes'); AKC (S278): 'They require minimal exercise and are happy to curl up in their owner’s lap.' — sources agree on 30; RKC preferred (runbook rule).

after_meals.value: leave a gap after eating and before exercising
after_meals.quote: Remember to leave a gap after eating and before exercising.
after_meals.notes: PDSA (S277), feeding section; also 'it's usually recommended to split their daily allowance into two meals.' (= the game's two adult meals). → proposed_game_parameters.chihuahua.meal_exercise_gap (M5-R16, Shih Tzu precedent).

walks.quote: We'd recommend splitting this into two smaller walks so they can have a sniff and explore.
walks.notes: PDSA (S277). The game's walk counts steps over the whole day — nothing new to build.

temperament.value: gay, spirited and intelligent; bold, saucy, outgoing and confident
temperament.quote: Gay, spirited, and intelligent, neither snappy nor withdrawn.
temperament.notes: KC standard (S274) 'Temperament'. RKC breed page (S275): 'Bold and saucy in temperament, the breed comes in two varieties'; 'Outgoing and confident, the Chihuahua has a huge personality in a tiny frame.' FCI (S273): 'Svelto, sveglio, vivace e molto coraggioso.' (quick, alert, lively and very brave). PDSA (S277): personalities vary — 'some are reported to be feisty and confident,' / 'not afraid to stand up for themselves, while others can be timid, shy and fearful.'

family.value: better suited to families with slightly older children; AKC: not recommended for homes with children
family.quote: Because of this, they're better suited to families with slightly older children
family.notes: PDSA (S277): 'As Chihuahuas are small and light weight, they're very tempting for children to pick up and play with' / 'which they're unlikely to enjoy.' / 'who understand that they may not want to be picked up or fussed all the time.' AKC (S278): 'Chihuahuas can make good family pets, but aren’t recommended for homes with children.'; 'Chihuahuas are too small for roughhousing, and overly-excited children could be dangerous for them.' → consider older_children (PDSA, the Pomeranian's chip 'small dog — better with older children'); never children / small_children / family_pet (AKC advises against homes with children).

socialisation.value: socialise from a young age with lots of different people, experiences and places
socialisation.quote: This is why it's really important to socialise your Chihuahua from a young age
socialisation.notes: PDSA (S277): 'with lots of different people, experiences and places so they grow up to be a well-rounded adult.' AKC (S278): 'Early socialization and training can help make a Chihuahua more open to people and other pets.' → proposed_game_parameters.chihuahua.socialisation (DOG_SOCIALISATION row, M5-R17).

time_alone.value: love company, need someone around the home all the time; do not cope well with even very short periods alone
time_alone.quote: As companion dogs Chihuahuas love company and need someone around the home all the time.
time_alone.notes: PDSA (S277): 'They tend not to cope well with even very short periods alone' / 'so we wouldn't recommend a Chihuahua if you're away from home a lot without them' / 'as they can quickly develop separation anxiety.' → consider needs_company (Boxer precedent); never often_alone.

other_pets.value: will live happily with another pet they have grown up with, but may chase unfamiliar pets
other_pets.quote: Generally speaking, your Chihuahua will live happily with another pet they have grown up with.
other_pets.notes: PDSA (S277): 'However, this won't stop them from chasing any unfamiliar pets in their garden!' AKC (S278): 'Chihuahuas are somewhat social.' Basis of other_pets (with the grown-up-together caveat, Pomeranian / Standard Poodle precedent). Chasing unfamiliar pets is not a 'high prey drive' statement → no chases_small_pets (runbook rule).

chewing.notes: No breed-specific statement found (RKC S275, PDSA S277, AKC S278 checked) → no chews_when_bored tag.

food_motivation.notes: No breed-specific statement found → no food_motivated_weight tag. RVC infographic (S280): obesity is a common problem — health.dental_weight, not a food-motivation statement. RKC Toy group text (S275, as returned): 'some can be finicky eaters' — group, not breed.

training_notes.value: clever; positive, reward-based, consistent training
training_notes.quote: Chihuahuas are clever little dogs who respond really well to positive, reward-based training.
training_notes.notes: PDSA (S277): 'and to be treated with a firm but fair attitude.' AKC (S278): 'Chihuahuas are eager to please their owners, making them an easier breed to train.' Not a first-time-owner statement → no first_time_owner / experienced_owner tag.

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages anywhere. RKC Breed Watch Category 2 (S276) — the breed's points of concern were not returned (the page shows only the category), so no welfare chip is given (Pomeranian precedent, open for David). Main topics (PDSA S277): luxating patellas, hip dysplasia, hydrocephalus, eye problems, heart disease, tracheal collapse, Legg-Perthes disease, dental problems, dystocia, cryptorchidism, CM/SM. VetCompass (S279 / S280): dental disease and obesity particularly common.

luxating_patella.value: luxating patellas — kneecaps slipping temporarily out of place
luxating_patella.quote: Luxating patellas – where the kneecaps slip temporarily out of place.
luxating_patella.notes: PDSA (S277): 'Before breeding parents can be checked by a vet for this.' (→ breeder checklist patella_scheme, other_scheme).

hip_dysplasia.quote: Hip dysplasia – where the hip joint doesn’t fit together perfectly, which will eventually lead to arthritis.
hip_dysplasia.notes: PDSA (S277): 'Before breeding, dogs should be screened by x-rays through the BVA/Kennel Club Hip Dysplasia Scheme.' (→ breeder checklist hip_scheme, other_scheme). Not a Breed Watch point → no hips_hind_legs chip.

legg_perthes.value: Legg-Perthes disease — the hip joint dies and crumbles
legg_perthes.quote: Legg-Perthes disease (Legg-Calvé-Perthes) – a painful condition which causes the hip joint to die and crumble.

hydrocephalus.value: hydrocephalus — fluid build-up around the brain
hydrocephalus.quote: Hydrocephalus – a build-up of fluid around the brain.

eyes.value: dry eye (KCS), entropion, lens luxation; eye testing available
eyes.quote: Entropion – inward rolling of the eyelids which can often cause irritation to the eye.
eyes.notes: PDSA (S277): 'Dry eye (Keratoconjunctivitis sicca or KCS)' / 'a condition that stops your dog producing tears and causes dry, painful eyes.'; 'Lens luxation'. RKC best-practice eye testing (S275): 'Eye testing using the BVA/KC/ISDS Eye Scheme'.

heart.value: heart disease — heart scans can screen parents for heart valve problems
heart.quote: Heart disease – heart scans can screen parents for heart valve problems.
heart.notes: PDSA health list (S277) (→ breeder checklist heart_scheme, other_scheme). RVC infographic (S280) lists heart murmur among common disorders (layout unclear — background).

tracheal_collapse.value: tracheal collapse — the windpipe weakens and collapses, causing breathing problems
tracheal_collapse.quote: Tracheal collapse – a condition where the windpipe gradually gets weaker and ‘collapses’ causing breathing problems.

syringomyelia.value: Chiari-like malformation / syringomyelia (CM/SM); a BVA/KC screening scheme exists
syringomyelia.quote: CM/SM screening using the KC/ BVA Chiari-like malformation/ syringomyelia (CM/SM) screening scheme
syringomyelia.notes: RKC breed page best-practice test (S275). PDSA (S277): 'Chiari malformation and Syringomyelia (CM/SM) – a very painful condition where fluid-filled areas' / 'develop within the spinal cord near the brain.' / 'There is currently a BVA/KC scheme for this.'

dental.value: overcrowding of the teeth, retained puppy teeth and dental disease
dental.quote: Dental problems – due to the shape of their jaw, they can experience overcrowding of the teeth,
dental.notes: PDSA (S277): 'retention of puppy teeth and dental disease.'; equipment list names 'pet-safe toothpaste and toothbrushes,'. → proposed_game_parameters.chihuahua.tooth_brushing (sourced need, ROADMAP M5-R15).

dental_weight.value: dental disease and obesity particularly common; owners can help prevent them
dental_weight.quote: Dental disease and obesity are particularly common problems in Chihuahuas, which owners can take measures to help prevent.
dental_weight.notes: RVC VetCompass infographic (S280) of O'Neill et al. 2020 (S279). 'Owners should avoid purchasing these puppies on impulse or as accessories.' (S280). No frequency.

merle.value: merle not a standard colour; merle carries a higher risk of hearing and sight problems
merle.quote: the merle gene in this breed carries an increased risk of impaired hearing and sight problems.
merle.notes: RKC breed page (S276, as returned): the RKC will not register certain merle-related litters. KC standard (S274): 'Never merle (dapple).'; FCI (S273): merle disqualifying. The game never draws merle. Background only.

other_pdsa.quote: Cryptorchidism – a condition where one testicle does not descend into the scrotal sac.
other_pdsa.notes: PDSA (S277): 'Dystocia – this breed can struggle to give birth to puppies (dystocia),'. Research only — not exported.

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table of Coren's ranking (S35, read 2026-10-13): rank 67, the Chihuahua alone, tier 'Fair Working/Obedience Intelligence' (ranks 55–69; the table row itself was not returned verbatim, so no quote is stored). Coren's own top / bottom-10 article (S34) does not list the breed. Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

coren_tier.quote: Understanding of new commands: 40 to 80 repetitions.
coren_tier.notes: S35 tier definition as returned: 'Obey first command: 30% of the time or better.'

training_notes.value: clever; positive, reward-based, consistent, firm but fair
training_notes.quote: Chihuahuas are clever little dogs who respond really well to positive, reward-based training.
training_notes.notes: PDSA (S277); AKC (S278): 'It’s important to be gentle yet firm with Chihuahuas while training.', 'Like all dogs, it is crucial to begin training early.'

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value — see proposed_game_parameters.chihuahua.learning_multiplier (0.7, runbook rule: Fair tier, rank 67).

general.value: small, dainty, compact toy dog with a well-rounded 'apple dome' skull, large flaring ears and a sickle tail
general.quote: Small, dainty, compact.
general.notes: KC standard (S274): 'Alert little dog; swift moving with brisk, forceful action, and saucy expression.' FCI (S273): 'È un cane dalla costruzione compatta.' (a compact dog).

colours.quote: Any colour or mixture of colours.
colours.notes: KC (S274): 'Never merle (dapple).' FCI (S273): 'Tutti i colori, con tutte le possibili sfumature e combinazioni sono accettati, tranne il “merle”.' (all colours and combinations except merle). The list = common examples of permitted colours (the standards list none by name) — never merle.

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). Fawn first with the highest weight (portrait default), then cream, black and tan, chocolate, white, fawn and white.

coat.value: smooth coat: soft texture, close and glossy (undercoat and ruff permissible)
coat.quote: Smooth Coat: smooth, of soft texture, close and glossy, with undercoat and ruff permissible.
coat.notes: FCI (S273), short-haired variety: 'Il pelo è corto e ben adagiato su tutto il corpo.' (short, close-lying over the whole body). The game builds the Smooth Coat (RKC S275).

ears.value: large, flaring, erect, set at about 45°
ears.quote: Large, flaring, set on at an angle of approximately 45, giving breadth between ears.
ears.notes: KC (S274): 'Tipped or broken-down ears highly undesirable.' FCI (S273): 'Larghi, eretti, largamente aperti' (large, erect, wide open).

eyes.value: large, round, not protruding, set well apart, dark or ruby
eyes.quote: Large, round, but not protruding; set well apart; centre of eye is on a plane with lowest point of ear and base of stop;
eyes.notes: KC (S274): 'dark or ruby. Light eyes in light colours permissible.' FCI (S273): 'Larghi, rotondeggianti nella forma, molto espressivi, non sporgenti, perfettamente scuri.'

nose.value: well-rounded 'apple dome' skull, definite stop, muzzle moderately short and slightly pointed
nose.quote: Well-rounded 'apple dome' skull, cheeks and jaws lean, muzzle moderately short, slightly pointed. Definite stop.
nose.notes: FCI (S273): 'Testa ben arrotondata a forma di mela (una caratteristica della razza).'; nose 'Moderatamente corto, diretto leggermente verso l'alto.'; muzzle 'Corto, diritto se visto di lato, ampio all'inserzione'. Not flat-faced; the game draws a moderate dome and muzzle (no exaggerated skull, no protruding eyes).

tail.value: medium length, set high, carried up and over the back (sickle tail)
tail.quote: Medium length, set high, carried up and over back (sickle tail).
tail.notes: KC (S274): 'Furry, flattish in appearance, broadening slightly in centre and tapering to point.' FCI (S273): 'Inserita alta, piatta in apparenza, di lunghezza moderata'.

suitability._note: Source = RKC breed-page fields (S275, Smooth Coat) and PDSA (S277); AKC (S278) for children / grooming. The RKC page shows no 'Good with children' field (as returned 2026-10-13). Woodgreen not attempted.

rkc_exercise.quote: Exercise: Up to 30 minutes per day

rkc_size_of_home.notes: Basis of the apartment tag (with the garden). AKC (S278): 'make an especially ideal pet for city dwellers.'

rkc_size_of_garden.quote: Size of garden: Small/ medium garden

rkc_grooming.notes: Basis of the brushing routine (1× a week, runbook dog-grooming rule). Not frequent_grooming.

rkc_coat_length.notes: PDSA (S277): 'Coat length | Short' (longer haired Chihuahuas also exist — the Long Coat breed).

rkc_shedding.notes: PDSA (S277): 'As with any breed, you should expect your Chihuahua to shed, especially over spring and autumn.' — agrees. Basis of the sheds tag.

rkc_breed_watch.quote: This breed can be affected by conformational concerns, more information can be found here
rkc_breed_watch.notes: RKC breed page (S275 key facts 'Breed watch category' 'Category 2'; S276 Health section as returned). The points of concern were not returned → no welfare chip; open for David.

rkc_good_with_children.notes: The RKC breed page (S275) has no 'Good with children' field.

pdsa_exercise.value: a minimum of half an hour a day
pdsa_exercise.quote: Your Chihuahua will need a minimum of half an hour exercise
pdsa_exercise.notes: PDSA (S277): 'every day to stay happy and healthy.'

pdsa_grooming.value: a weekly brush for short coats; two to three times a week for longer haired Chihuahuas
pdsa_grooming.quote: A weekly brush for your short coated and two to three times per week for your longer haired Chihuahua
pdsa_grooming.notes: PDSA (S277): 'should be more than enough to keep on top of the dead hairs.' The game builds the Smooth Coat → weekly (agrees with RKC 'Once a week').

pdsa_children.value: better suited to families with slightly older children
pdsa_children.quote: Because of this, they're better suited to families with slightly older children
pdsa_children.notes: Basis of older_children.

pdsa_time_alone.value: do not cope well with even very short periods alone
pdsa_time_alone.quote: They tend not to cope well with even very short periods alone

akc_children.value: not recommended for homes with children
akc_children.quote: Chihuahuas can make good family pets, but aren’t recommended for homes with children.
akc_children.notes: AKC (S278): 'Chihuahuas are too small for roughhousing, and overly-excited children could be dangerous for them.' Stronger than PDSA; the chip stays older_children (PDSA) and never family_pet / children.

akc_grooming.value: smooth coats: occasional brushing and regular baths; ears checked and cleaned regularly
akc_grooming.quote: Chihuahuas with smooth coats require occasional brushing and regular baths to keep them looking their best.
akc_grooming.notes: AKC (S278): 'Chihuahua’s ears should be checked and cleaned regularly.' Brushing → RKC / PDSA weekly decides. Regular baths and ear cleaning = sourced needs without a game mechanic → proposed_game_parameters.chihuahua.ear_care_bathing → new ROADMAP M5-R20 (needs-david).

english_springer_spaniel._note: Added 2026-10-14 (M5-R10-34, unattended run — appended after the Chihuahua: AKC 2024 No. 28, S174 full-list table 'ranks 20–30: … Chihuahua, English Springer Spaniel, Shetland Sheepdog, Border Collie'). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-14 (the tool limits quotes to ~125 characters — long sentences are quoted in pieces; apostrophes as returned); spot-check before import (sources.md S281–S288, reused S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45, S92, S123, S174). The game builds the English Springer Spaniel as described by the UK / FCI standards (show and working lines are one breed; working types can be lighter — Wikipedia S288, background only). akc.notes: AKC standard (S283): 'a 19 inch bitch will weigh approximately 40 pounds.' Pounds converted to kg (× 0.4536) by us: 50 lb ≈ 22.7 kg, 40 lb ≈ 18.1 kg — inside the PDSA range.

adult.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S284). PDSA (S285): 'Minimum exercise (per day) | 2 hours'; 'will need an owner who’s prepared to give them over 2 hours of exercise per day.' — agrees. AKC (S286): 'require regular exercise to keep them happy and healthy.'

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages anywhere. RKC Breed Watch Category 1 (S284): 'Currently no points of concern specific to this breed have been identified for special attention by judges' → no welfare chip. PDSA (S285) health list: hip dysplasia, elbow dysplasia, progressive retinal atrophy, ear infections. Wikipedia (S288, tier C, background only) names skin conditions and chronic hepatitis — not used without an A/B source.

hip_elbow_dysplasia.value: hip and elbow dysplasia — leading to arthritis; parents' hips and elbows tested before breeding
hip_elbow_dysplasia.quote: Hip dysplasia – hip joint laxity as a result of poor development, which will eventually lead to arthritis.
hip_elbow_dysplasia.notes: PDSA (S285); also 'Elbow dysplasia – elbow joint laxity as a result of poor development, which will eventually lead to arthritis.' RKC (S284) Good Practice (minimum): 'Hip testing (for hip dysplasia) using the BVA/KC Hip Dysplasia Scheme' and 'Elbow testing (for elbow dysplasia) using the BVA/KC Elbow Dysplasia Scheme' (→ breeder checklist hip_scheme / elbow_scheme). Not a Breed Watch point → no hips_hind_legs chip.

pra.value: progressive retinal atrophy — gradual deterioration of the retina
pra.quote: Progressive retinal atrophy – gradual deterioration of the retina of the eye.
pra.notes: PDSA (S285): 'Symptoms can start with night blindness and progress to total blindness.' RKC (S284) best practice: 'DNA test for Progressive retinal atrophy (PRA(cord1))' (→ breeder checklist dna_pra_cord1); minimum: eye scheme with gonioscopy for PLA (→ eye_scheme).

ear_infections.value: ear infections (otitis externa) because of the long ears
ear_infections.quote: Ear infections can occur in Springer Spaniels due to their long ears.
ear_infections.notes: PDSA (S285): 'Bacteria can build up in the ears and cause otitis externa.' A health risk, not a care instruction (no source on the pages read tells owners to check or clean the ears) → no ear-care need recorded (Chihuahua's AKC instruction is different, ROADMAP M5-R20).

dna_tests.value: DNA tests for AMS, DAMS, fucosidosis, PFK and PRA (cord1)
dna_tests.quote: DNA test for Fucosidosis (fuco) - Find a list of tested dogs here

shetland_sheepdog._note: Added 2026-10-14 (M5-R10-35, unattended run — appended after the English Springer Spaniel: AKC 2024 No. 29, S174 full-list table 'ranks 26–32: Siberian Husky, Chihuahua, English Springer Spaniel, Shetland Sheepdog, Border Collie, Brittany, Cocker Spaniel'). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-14 (the tool limits quotes to ~125 characters; apostrophes as returned); spot-check before import (sources.md S289–S295, reused S10, S11, S14, S24, S34, S35, S45, S92, S174). Lifespan: McMillan 2024 / Dogs Trust table (S123) refused by the fetch tool (provenance) → RKC lower bound 'Over 10 years' → senior 90 months, provisional (Wikipedia S295, tier C, quotes McMillan 2024 as 13.4 y → 121, not used alone). RKC Breed Watch Category 2 with only the general line 'can be affected by conformational concerns' (S292) and no named point → no welfare chip (Pomeranian / Boston Terrier precedent, open for David); not flat-faced → in marketing.

identity.value: FCI No. 88, Group 1 Section 1 (Sheepdogs), Great Britain
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S289): Group 'n°1 - Sheepdogs and Cattledogs (except Swiss Cattledogs)', section 'Sheepdogs', country 'GREAT BRITAIN'; accepted on a definitive basis 11/9/1954; official valid standard published 9/8/2026 (FCI standard S290: 08.09.2026); 'Not subject to a working trial according to the FCI breeds nomenclature'.

size_class.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S291). PDSA (S293) key facts 'Size | Medium' — sources disagree; the RKC value is taken (runbook: RKC breed page preferred). PDSA 9 kg (S293) and AKC 15–25 lb (S294) sit in the Small class of S10. RKC group: Pastoral.

fci.notes: FCI standard (S290) 'Size and weight', as returned: ideal height 'Males 37 cm' and 'Females 35,5 cm'; deviations of more than 2.5 cm above or below 'highly undesirable'. Quoted in pieces by the tool → quote null (paraphrase of the line).

pdsa.notes: PDSA key facts (S293), one range for both sexes (stored per sex).

akc.quote: averaging between 13 and 16 inches tall and weighing 15 to 25 pounds.
akc.notes: AKC (S294). Inches converted to cm (× 2.54) by us: 13–16 in ≈ 33–40.6 cm.

akc.quote: averaging between 13 and 16 inches tall and weighing 15 to 25 pounds.
akc.notes: AKC breed article (S294), one range for both sexes (stored per sex). Pounds converted to kg (× 0.4536) by us: 15 lb ≈ 6.8 kg, 25 lb ≈ 11.3 kg. The game range (adult_weight_kg). The FCI standard (S290) gives no weight ('The standard does not specify a weight', tool summary).

pdsa.notes: PDSA key facts (S293), one average for both sexes — inside the AKC range.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. PDSA 9 kg (S293) ≈ 20 lb; AKC 15–25 lb (S294) → mostly the 'Small (12–24 pounds)' class. The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 60 min is reached at 6 months).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Shetland Sheepdog growth curve found.

rkc.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S291; older address S292 the same). PDSA (S293) 'Average lifespan | Over 10 years' — sources agree. The basis of the senior boundary (runbook: RKC lower bound when no McMillan 2024 / VetCompass value is reachable). Not shorter_lifespan.

pdsa.notes: PDSA key facts (S293).

mcmillan_2024.notes: McMillan et al. 2024: the Dogs Trust breed table (S123) was refused by the fetch tool on 2026-10-14 (provenance); the Dogs Trust research page names no Shetland Sheepdog value. Wikipedia (S295, tier C) quotes the McMillan 2024 study as 13.4 years — UNSOURCED as an A/B value; verify in S123 before replacing the RKC lower bound.

alternatives.notes: Wikipedia (tier C): 'found a life expectancy of 13.4 years for the breed' (UK study, McMillan et al. 2024 in the reference list); never shown alone. With it the senior boundary would be round(0.75 × 13.4 × 12) = round(120.6) = 121 months.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × 10 y (RKC lower bound 'Over 10 years', S291) → 0.75 × 10 = 7.5 y = 90 months. With McMillan 13.4 y (via S295, tier C): 121 months. Dogs Trust rule of thumb > 7 y = 84 months (S14). Provisional until McMillan 2024 is checked.

adult.quote: Exercise: Up to 1 hour per day
adult.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S291). PDSA (S293): 'Minimum exercise (per day) | 1 hour'; 'Shelties need around an hour of exercise daily and will enjoy playing games.' — agrees.

energy.value: athletic; needs regular mental and physical exercise
energy.quote: Shelties are quite athletic, and require regular mental and physical exercise to keep them from acting out.
energy.notes: AKC (S294): 'As long as a Sheltie has plenty of opportunities to exercise, they’ll be happy.' Basis of needs_mental_stimulation (a need, not only enjoyment).

temperament.value: alert, gentle, intelligent, strong and active; affectionate, reserved towards strangers, never nervous
temperament.quote: Alert, gentle, intelligent, strong and active.
temperament.notes: FCI standard (S290) 'Behaviour/Temperament'; affectionate and loyal to its owner, 'reserved towards strangers, never nervous.' PDSA (S293): 'Shetland Sheepdogs, or ‘Shelties’ as they’re more affectionately known, are very gentle, playful, obedient dogs.'

family.value: often fit well into family life; get along happily with children
family.quote: Shelties often fit well into family life and get along happily with children.
family.notes: PDSA (S293). RKC (S292): 'its sweet temperament has won it a firm place as one of the most popular family companions.' AKC (S294): 'They can do well with kids, but would fare best in a home with older children due to their herding instincts.' Basis of family_pet / children (explicit statement) and may_herd_children (AKC); no rating for small children → no small_children.

herding_children.value: may herd; would fare best with older children because of herding instincts
herding_children.quote: They can do well with kids, but would fare best in a home with older children due to their herding instincts.
herding_children.notes: AKC (S294): 'Herding breeds have the desire to chase or gather deeply rooted in their nature.' → may_herd_children (Australian Shepherd / Pembroke Welsh Corgi / Miniature American Shepherd precedent). Not older_children: PDSA (S293) says Shelties 'get along happily with children' (open for David).

mental_stimulation.value: needs regular mental and physical exercise
mental_stimulation.quote: Shelties are quite athletic, and require regular mental and physical exercise to keep them from acting out.

socialisation.notes: PDSA (S293). AKC (S294): 'Early socialization and training will is recommended to ensure that they don’t become fearful of new faces and situations.' (sic) → proposed_game_parameters.shetland_sheepdog.socialisation (DOG_SOCIALISATION row, M5-R17).

time_alone.notes: No statement on time alone (PDSA S293, AKC S294: only 'relax on the couch as long as their person is close by' — not a time-alone statement) → no needs_company / often_alone.

AKC (S294): 'energetic and loving with their families and other familiar animals' (tool summary) and 'Shelties will chase just about anything from squirrels to cars.' — a chasing statement, not a named high prey drive → no other_pets, no chases_small_pets (runbook rule; open for David).

barking.quote: Shelties are known to be very vocal, but they can be taught to keep excessive barking to a minimum.
barking.notes: AKC (S294). Background for parents (register text only); no vocabulary key and not a care need → no chip.

training_notes.notes: AKC (S294). PDSA (S293): intelligent and respond well to training (tool summary). Not a first-time-owner statement → no first_time_owner / experienced_owner tag.

akc_grooming.quote: Weekly brushing is key to keeping a Shetland Sheepdog looking their best, keeping the coat clean and mat- free.
akc_grooming.notes: AKC (S294): 'Matting most commonly occurs behind the ears, under the elbow on each front leg, and in the “pants” under the tail.'; 'The breed doesn’t require regular bathing.' Weekly brushing = alternative 1 (the rule takes RKC 'Every day').

akc_nails.value: nails and the hair around the foot pads trimmed regularly
akc_nails.quote: As with all dogs, you should trim Shelties’ nails and the hair around the foot pads should be trimmed regularly.
akc_nails.notes: AKC (S294). Nail trimming = sourced need without a mechanic → ROADMAP M5-R19 (needs-david).

akc_children.value: can do well with kids; best with older children because of herding instincts
akc_children.quote: They can do well with kids, but would fare best in a home with older children due to their herding instincts.

akc_mental_exercise.quote: Shelties are quite athletic, and require regular mental and physical exercise to keep them from acting out.

brittany._note: Added 2026-10-14 (M5-R10-36, unattended run — appended after the Shetland Sheepdog: AKC 2024 No. 31, S174 full-list table '28 English Springer Spaniel', '29 Shetland Sheepdog', '30 Border Collie', '31 Brittany'). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-14 (the tool limits quotes to ~125 characters; apostrophes as returned); spot-check before import (sources.md S296–S302, reused S8, S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45, S92, S123, S174, S263). The FCI standard (S297) was read in French (the English PDF was refused by the fetch tool) — French quotes, English in notes. Lifespan: McMillan 2024 / Dogs Trust table (S123) refused by the fetch tool (provenance), no VetCompass Brittany median found → RKC lower bound 'Over 10 years' → senior 90 months, provisional (PetMD S302 '12–14 years', tier B, alternative only). RKC Breed Watch Category 1 (S298) → no welfare chip; not flat-faced → in marketing.

identity.value: FCI No. 95, Group 7 Section 1.2 (Continental Pointing Dogs, Spaniel type), France
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S296): group 'n°7 - Chiens d'arrêt', section 'Chiens d'arrêt continentaux' (subsection 'Type Epagneul'), country 'FRANCE'; accepted on a definitive basis 19/11/1954; official valid standard published 25/03/2003; 'Soumise à épreuve de travail selon la Nomenclature des races de la FCI' (subject to a working trial). English FCI name 'BRITTANY SPANIEL'; the RKC (S298) and AKC (S300) call the breed 'Brittany' (RKC: 'In France the breed is called the Epagneul Breton', tool summary).

size_class.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S298). AKC 30–40 lb (S300, S301) ≈ 13.6–18.1 kg and PetMD 30–40 lb (S302) sit in the Medium class of S10. RKC group: Gundog (HPR — hunt, point, retrieve).

fci.notes: FCI standard (S297, French), 'TAILLE' as returned: males minimum 48 cm (tolerance −1 cm), maximum 51 cm (tolerance +1 cm), ideal 49–50 cm; females minimum 47 cm (−1 cm), maximum 50 cm (+1 cm), ideal 48–49 cm. Returned in pieces → quote null (paraphrase).

rkc.quote: Ideal height at withers: dogs: 48-51 cms (19-20 ins); bitches: 47-50 cms (18½-19¾ ins).
rkc.notes: RKC breed standard (S299) — agrees with the FCI standard.

akc.quote: Height - 17½ to 20½ inches, measured from the ground to the highest point of the shoulders.
akc.notes: AKC standard (S300), one range for both sexes (stored per sex). Inches converted to cm (× 2.54) by us: 17.5–20.5 in ≈ 44.5–52.1 cm.

akc.quote: Weight - Should weigh between 30 and 40 pounds.
akc.notes: AKC official standard (S300, approved 10 April 1990), one range for both sexes (stored per sex). Pounds converted to kg (× 0.4536) by us: 30 lb ≈ 13.6 kg, 40 lb ≈ 18.1 kg. The game range (adult_weight_kg). AKC article (S301) 'weighs between 30 and 40 pounds' and PetMD (S302) 'weighing 30–40 pounds' agree. The FCI standard (S297) gives no weight ('Le document ne mentionne pas de poids', tool summary); the RKC standard (S299) none either.

salt_category.notes: Category assignment by weight is ours (general_by_size.size_classes.salt_2017_bands_kg, S8): about 14–18 kg. Salt 2017 breed list not checked.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. AKC 30–40 lb (S300) → the 'Medium (24–59 pounds)' class. The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 120 min is reached at 12 months).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Brittany growth curve found.

rkc.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S298). The basis of the senior boundary (runbook: RKC lower bound when no McMillan 2024 / VetCompass value is reachable). Not shorter_lifespan.

petmd.quote: The average Brittany Spaniel lifespan is 12–14 years.
petmd.notes: PetMD (S302, tier B). Not in the runbook's lifespan order (McMillan 2024 → VetCompass median → RKC lower bound) → alternative only: with its lower bound the senior boundary would be round(0.75 × 12 × 12) = 108 months.

mcmillan_2024.notes: McMillan et al. 2024: the Dogs Trust breed table (S123) was refused by the fetch tool on 2026-10-14 (provenance); the Science News article on the study names no Brittany value. Unknown whether the Brittany is among the 155 breeds — verify in S123 before replacing the RKC lower bound.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × 10 y (RKC lower bound 'Over 10 years', S298) → 0.75 × 10 = 7.5 y = 90 months. With PetMD 12 y (S302): 108 months. Dogs Trust rule of thumb > 7 y = 84 months (S14). Provisional until McMillan 2024 is checked.

adult.quote: Exercise: More than 2 hours per day
adult.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S298). AKC (S301): 'Brittanys are high-energy dogs who were bred to hunt, and they require plenty of exercise.' (no number); PetMD (S302): 'they are athletic dogs with a lot of energy.' (no number). No PDSA Brittany page found.

energy.value: high-energy hunting dog; needs plenty of exercise and mental stimulation
energy.quote: Brittanys are high-energy dogs who were bred to hunt, and they require plenty of exercise.
energy.notes: AKC (S301). Basis of active_family (with the RKC exercise).

temperament.value: gentle and affectionate, yet full of life and exuberance; very energetic, intelligent
temperament.quote: Gentle and affectionate, yet full of life and exuberance.
temperament.notes: RKC breed standard (S299) 'Temperament'; 'Characteristics': 'Very energetic, intelligent, hunt-point-retriever.' FCI (S297, French): 'Chien s'adaptant à tout milieu, sociable, à l'expression intelligente et attentive, équilibré mentalement.' (adapts to any setting, sociable, mentally balanced).

family.value: sweet and well-behaved with children of all ages; for an active family with children
family.quote: sweet and well-behaved with children of all ages
family.notes: PetMD (S302); also 'the perfect, medium-size sporting dog for an active family with children and other pets'. AKC (S301): 'They’re gentle by nature and tend to be patient with children.' and 'They also have plenty of energy to keep up with active children.' Basis of family_pet / children (explicit statements). No rating for small children → no small_children (open for David: PetMD says 'children of all ages').

mental_stimulation.value: needs plenty of exercise and mental stimulation
mental_stimulation.quote: It’s essential that Brittanys get plenty of exercise and mental stimulation to keep them from acting out.
mental_stimulation.notes: AKC (S301); PetMD (S302): they 'require lots of mental stimulation and physical exercise'. → needs_mental_stimulation.

socialisation.value: early socialisation of puppies is a must
socialisation.quote: Early socialization in Brittany puppies is a must
socialisation.notes: PetMD (S302). AKC (S301): 'Like with all breeds, early socialization and puppy training classes are highly recommended' (truncated by the tool); 'Early socialization and puppy training courses will ensure that they’re open to new people and other pets.' → proposed_game_parameters.brittany.socialisation (DOG_SOCIALISATION row, M5-R17).

time_alone.value: does not do well when left alone for long periods
time_alone.quote: don’t do well when left alone for long periods
time_alone.notes: PetMD (S302), as returned inside the sentence 'Brittanys … don’t do well when left alone for long periods'. → consider needs_company (English Springer Spaniel / Boxer precedent); never often_alone. AKC (S301): no time-alone statement.

other_pets.value: high prey drive — will chase birds and possibly other smaller animals
other_pets.quote: The Brittany was bred to hunt birds, so they are hardwired with a high prey drive.
other_pets.notes: PetMD (S302): 'This means they will chase birds (and possibly other smaller animals) whenever they’re outside.' → chases_small_pets (a quote naming a high prey drive, runbook §3). PetMD also calls the breed a dog 'for an active family with children and other pets' and AKC (S301) says socialisation makes them 'open to new people and other pets' — conflicting with the prey drive → no other_pets tag (open for David).

barking.value: not very vocal, but lets you know when it needs activity or attention
barking.quote: The breed isn’t very vocal, but they’ll let you know when they need an activity or attention from you.
barking.notes: AKC (S301). Background only; no vocabulary key.

chewing.notes: No breed-specific statement found (RKC S298, AKC S301, PetMD S302 checked) → no chews_when_bored tag.

food_motivation.notes: No breed-specific statement found → no food_motivated_weight tag.

training_notes.value: bright, willing to work with their owners; patient, encouraging, positive training
training_notes.quote: They respond best to patient, encouraging training methods.
training_notes.notes: AKC (S301): 'Brittanys are a bright breed, and are generally ready and willing to work with their owners.' PetMD (S302): 'Smart, gentle, positive reinforcement training is the way to go with a Brittany.' Not a first-time-owner statement → no first_time_owner / experienced_owner tag.

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages anywhere. RKC Breed Watch Category 1 (S298): 'Currently no points of concern specific to this breed have been identified for special attention by judges' → no welfare chip. PetMD (S302): 'Brittany dogs are generally a very healthy breed without many notable health issues.'

hip_dysplasia.quote: Hip dysplasia is one of the few health issues some Brittany dogs may develop.
hip_dysplasia.notes: PetMD (S302). Not a Breed Watch point → no hips_hind_legs chip. The RKC Health Standard (S263) lists no test for the Brittany.

epilepsy.quote: a disorder of the brain that results in seizures, but with an unknown cause
epilepsy.notes: PetMD (S302), definition of epilepsy as returned. Background only.

hypothyroidism.quote: Hypothyroidism occurs when the thyroid is slow to produce certain hormones.

cataracts.quote: Brittany Spaniels are prone to cataracts, which causes the eye lenses to become cloudy and leads to vision loss.

ears.value: floppy ears trap debris and moisture — ears checked and cleaned
ears.quote: Brittanys have floppy ears, which means it’s easy for debris and moisture to become trapped in the canals.
ears.notes: PetMD (S302): 'clean your Brittany’s ears after you bathe them'. AKC (S301): 'Their ears should be checked regularly and cleaned as needed.' → ear care = sourced need without a mechanic → ROADMAP M5-R20 (needs-david).

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table (S35, tier C, read 2026-10-14): rank 19 under 'Excellent Working Dogs' (ranks 11–26). Coren's own article (S34) lists only the top and bottom 10 — runbook: rank from S35. Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

coren_tier.value: excellent: 5 to 15 repetitions, obeys first command ≥85%
coren_tier.quote: Understanding of new commands: 5 to 15 repetitions.; Obey first command: 85% of the time or better.;
coren_tier.notes: Tier 'Excellent Working Dogs' = ranks 11–26. Tier definitions from Wikipedia; verify in book.

training_notes.value: bright and willing; patient, encouraging training
training_notes.quote: They respond best to patient, encouraging training methods.
training_notes.notes: AKC (S301); PetMD (S302) 'can pick up cues quickly'.

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value — see proposed_game_parameters.brittany.learning_multiplier (1.5, runbook rule: Excellent tier, rank 19).

general.value: workmanlike, substance without heaviness, moderately well boned; compact, short-backed, the smallest of the pointing dogs
general.quote: Workmanlike. Substance without heaviness. Moderately well boned.
general.notes: RKC standard (S299). FCI (S297): 'Le plus petit des chiens d'arrêt.' (the smallest of the pointing dogs). AKC (S300): 'A compact, closely knit dog of medium size, a leggy dog having the appearance, as well as the agility' (truncated).

colours.quote: Any other colour or combination of colours unacceptable.
colours.notes: RKC standard (S299): 'Orange/white, liver/white, black/white, tricolour, or roan of any of these colours.' FCI (S297, French): 'blanc & orange', 'blanc & noir', 'blanc & marron', pied or roan, tricolours with tan markings; 'La robe unicolore n'est pas admise.' (no solid colour). AKC (S300): 'Color: Orange and white or liver and white in either clear or roan patterns.' and 'Black is a disqualification.' → black-based colours are standard in FCI / RKC only; they get the lowest weights and the portrait default is orange and white (standard everywhere). Never a solid colour.

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). Orange and white first with the highest weight (portrait default — the only colour all three standards list in the clear pattern with liver and white), then liver and white, orange roan, liver roan, black and white, tricolour.

coat.value: body coat dense but fairly fine, rather flat or slightly wavy; medium length
coat.quote: Body coat dense but fairly fine. Rather flat or slightly wavy.
coat.notes: RKC standard (S299); RKC key facts 'Coat length: Medium' (S298).

ears.value: triangular, slightly rounded at the tip, set and carried high, lying flat against the cheek
ears.quote: Triangular in shape, slightly rounded at tip.
ears.notes: RKC standard (S299), rest as returned (paraphrase).

eyes.value: expressive, brown to dark, in harmony with the coat colour; never light or hard
eyes.quote: Expressive, brown to dark, in harmony with coat colour.
eyes.notes: RKC standard (S299).

nose.value: skull slightly rounded; muzzle tapered but not snipy
nose.quote: Skull slightly rounded as seen from front, side or above.
nose.notes: RKC standard (S299); muzzle 'tapered but not snipy' (tool summary). Not a short-faced breed.

tail.value: naturally tailless or short (often born bob-tailed), set high, carried horizontally or slightly lower
tail.quote: Naturally tailless, short or previously customarily docked.
tail.notes: RKC standard (S299); RKC breed page (S298): 'often, but not always, naturally bob-tailed' (tool summary). FCI (S297): puppies may be born without a tail or with a short tail ('Le chiot peut naître sans queue ou avec une queue courte', tool summary). The portrait shows a natural short (bob) tail — never a docked look is implied by the prompt; docking is not shown or promoted.

suitability._note: Source = RKC breed-page key facts (S298), AKC (S301) and PetMD (S302). No PDSA Brittany page found; Woodgreen / Dogs Trust breed pages not attempted. The RKC page shows no 'Good with children' field (as returned 2026-10-14).

rkc_exercise.quote: Exercise: More than 2 hours per day
rkc_exercise.notes: Basis of 120 min, active_family and long_daily_exercise.

rkc_size_of_home.notes: Not apartment, not large_home (runbook: apartment only from 'Flat/ Apartment', large_home from 'Large house').

rkc_grooming.quote: Grooming: More than once a week
rkc_grooming.notes: No number → the runbook dog-grooming rule takes the most specific number of another A/B source: AKC (S301) 'Weekly brushing' → 1 (PetMD S302 'about once a week' agrees). Not frequent_grooming: AKC / PetMD say weekly (conflict; open for David).

rkc_shedding.notes: PetMD (S302): 'Their wavy fur does shed, especially in the spring and fall' — agrees. Basis of the sheds tag.

rkc_breed_watch.quote: Currently no points of concern specific to this breed have been identified for special attention by judges
rkc_breed_watch.notes: RKC breed page (S298): Breed Watch Category 1 → no welfare chip; in marketing.

rkc_good_with_children.notes: The RKC breed page (S298) has no 'Good with children' field.

akc_grooming.value: weekly brushing with a soft brush or hound glove
akc_grooming.quote: Weekly brushing with a soft brush or hound glove will keep a Brittany looking their best.
akc_grooming.notes: AKC (S301). Basis of the brushing value 1× a week (RKC 'More than once a week' has no number).

petmd_grooming.value: regular brushing about once a week
petmd_grooming.quote: Regular brushing (about once a week) with a soft brush is all the typical Brittany needs to stay healthy and well-groomed.
petmd_grooming.notes: PetMD (S302) — agrees with AKC (S301).

akc_nails.value: nails trimmed once a month as needed
akc_nails.quote: Their nails tend to wear down naturally, but should be trimmed once a month as needed.
akc_nails.notes: AKC (S301). Nail trimming = sourced need without a mechanic → ROADMAP M5-R19 (needs-david).

akc_ears.value: ears checked regularly and cleaned as needed
akc_ears.quote: Their ears should be checked regularly and cleaned as needed.
akc_ears.notes: AKC (S301); PetMD (S302) floppy ears trap debris and moisture. Ear care = sourced need without a mechanic → ROADMAP M5-R20 (needs-david).

akc_children.value: gentle; tend to be patient with children
akc_children.quote: They’re gentle by nature and tend to be patient with children.
akc_children.notes: AKC (S301). Supports the children tag (with PetMD S302).

petmd_family.value: for an active family with children and other pets
petmd_family.quote: the perfect, medium-size sporting dog for an active family with children and other pets
petmd_family.notes: PetMD (S302). Basis of family_pet; the 'other pets' part conflicts with the high prey drive (same source) → no other_pets tag.

petmd_children.value: sweet and well-behaved with children of all ages
petmd_children.quote: sweet and well-behaved with children of all ages
petmd_children.notes: PetMD (S302). Basis of the children tag (explicit statement, no supervision caveat).

akc_mental_exercise.value: plenty of exercise and mental stimulation
