american_cocker_spaniel._note: Added 2026-10-14 (M5-R10-37, unattended run — appended after the Brittany: AKC 2024 No. 32 'Cocker Spaniel', S174 full-list table '31 Brittany', '32 Cocker Spaniel', '36 English Cocker Spaniel'; the AKC 'Cocker Spaniel' is the American Cocker Spaniel of the FCI / RKC, not the English Cocker Spaniel). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-14 (the tool limits quotes to ~125 characters; apostrophes as returned); spot-check before import (sources.md S303–S311, reused S8, S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45, S92, S174). The FCI standard (S304) was read in French (the English PDF was refused by the fetch tool) — tool summary, French quotes only where returned. No PDSA American Cocker Spaniel page exists (the PDSA 'Cocker Spaniel' page is the English Cocker). Lifespan: McMillan 2024 / Dogs Trust table (S123) not reachable (no fetchable URL) — Wikipedia (S311, tier C) quotes McMillan 2024 at 13.3 years, background only → RKC lower bound 'Over 10 years' → senior 90 months, provisional. RKC Breed Watch Category 2 without a named point (S306) → no welfare chip; not flat-faced → in marketing. Exercise sources conflict (RKC 'More than 2 hours per day' vs AKC / PetMD 'don't require a lot / high levels of exercise') → minutes from the RKC by the rule, no exercise chip.

identity.value: FCI No. 167, Group 8 Section 2 (Flushing Dogs), USA
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S303): group 'n°8 - Retrievers - Flushing Dogs - Water Dogs', section 'Flushing Dogs', country 'UNITED STATES OF AMERICA'; definitive acceptance 1/1/1965; valid standard published 7/27/2021 (English listing 9/13/2021); 'Not subject to a working trial according to the FCI breeds nomenclature'. The AKC (S307, S308) calls the breed 'Cocker Spaniel'; the RKC (S305, S306) 'Spaniel (American Cocker)'; Wikipedia (S311): 'Cocker Spaniel (in USA), Cocker, Merry Cocker' (other names). Not the English Cocker Spaniel (FCI No. 5).

size_class.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S305). AKC 20–30 lb (S308) ≈ 9.1–13.6 kg straddles the Small / Medium bands of S10; RKC 'Small' decides. RKC group: Gundog.

fci.notes: FCI standard (S304, French, tool summary): ideal height at the withers 38.10 cm for males and 35.56 cm for females, tolerance 1.27 cm either way; males over 39.37 cm and females over 36.83 cm eliminated; smaller dogs penalised. Returned as a summary → quote null (paraphrase).

akc.quote: The ideal height at the withers for an adult dog is 15 inches and for an adult bitch, 14 inches.
akc.notes: AKC standard (S307): ideal 15 in (dogs) / 14 in (bitches); 'A dog whose height exceeds 15½ inches or a bitch whose height exceeds 14½ inches shall be disqualified.' Stored as ideal → disqualification limit; inches × 2.54 by us. AKC article (S308) 'standing between 13.5 and 15.5 inches tall'.

akc.quote: standing between 13.5 and 15.5 inches tall, and weighing about 20 to 30 pounds.
akc.notes: AKC breed article (S308), one range for both sexes (stored per sex). Pounds converted to kg (× 0.4536) by us: 20 lb ≈ 9.1 kg, 30 lb ≈ 13.6 kg. The game range (adult_weight_kg). PetMD (S309) 'The average Cocker Spaniel size is 13.5–15.5 inches tall and 20–30 pounds' agrees. The FCI (S304) and AKC (S307) standards give no weight.

vca.notes: VCA Animal Hospitals (S310) key facts '24 - 28 pounds' (≈ 10.9–12.7 kg, converted by us) — inside the AKC range; alternative only.

salt_category.notes: Category assignment by weight is ours (general_by_size.size_classes.salt_2017_bands_kg, S8): about 9–14 kg. Salt 2017 breed list not checked.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. AKC 20–30 lb (S308) straddles 'Small (12–24 pounds)' and 'Medium (24–59 pounds)' (12–15 months); RKC 'Size: Small' (S305) → Small. The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 120 min is reached at 12 months).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no American Cocker Spaniel growth curve found.

rkc.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S305). The basis of the senior boundary (runbook: RKC lower bound when no McMillan 2024 / VetCompass value is reachable). Not shorter_lifespan.

petmd.quote: The typical Cocker Spaniel lifespan is 10–14 years, so they’ll be a longtime companion.
petmd.notes: PetMD (S309, tier B). Lower bound 10 y agrees with the RKC → same senior boundary (90).

vca.notes: VCA (S310) key facts '12 - 15 years' (as returned). Not in the runbook's lifespan order → alternative only (108 months).

mcmillan_2024.quote: A 2024 study in the UK found a life expectancy of 13.3 years for the breed
mcmillan_2024.notes: McMillan et al. 2024 as quoted by Wikipedia (S311, tier C — never alone). The Dogs Trust breed table (S123) and the paper (S54) were not reachable on 2026-10-14 → not used as the basis; with it the senior boundary would be round(0.75 × 13.3 × 12) = 120 months. Verify in S123 before replacing the RKC lower bound.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × 10 y (RKC lower bound 'Over 10 years', S305) → 0.75 × 10 = 7.5 y = 90 months. With McMillan 2024 13.3 y (via S311): 120 months; with VCA 12 y (S310): 108 months; Dogs Trust rule of thumb > 7 y = 84 months (S14). Provisional until McMillan 2024 is checked.

adult.quote: Exercise: More than 2 hours per day
adult.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S305); the older RKC page (S306) agrees. Conflicting sources without a number: AKC (S308) 'They don’t require a lot of exercise to blow off energy.' and PetMD (S309) 'While Cocker Spaniels are sporting dogs, they don’t require high levels of exercise to stave off excess energy.'; VCA (S310) 'Requires daily exercise in the form of a long walk, jog, or energetic games.' Rule: RKC value preferred → 120; the others in alternatives. Because the sources conflict, no exercise chip (long_daily_exercise / active_family) — open for David.

energy.value: needs daily exercise — a long walk, jog or energetic games
energy.quote: Requires daily exercise in the form of a long walk, jog, or energetic games.
energy.notes: VCA (S310). Background only (conflicts with AKC S308 / PetMD S309).

temperament.value: equable, never timid; sweet-tempered, friendly, wants to please
temperament.quote: Equable in temperament with no suggestion of timidity.
temperament.notes: AKC standard (S307); FCI (S304, French): 'nullement craintif' (not at all fearful). PetMD (S309): 'Cocker Spaniels offer a friendly personality, both with people and with other animals.'

family.value: sweet-tempered, close to their people, great family dogs; usually very good with children
family.quote: At home, these sweet-tempered pups love being close to their people and make great family dogs.
family.notes: PetMD (S309). VCA (S310): 'Usually very good with children.' AKC (S308): 'They generally enjoy spending time with children and participating in family activities.' Basis of family_pet / children. No rating for small children → no small_children. Wikipedia (S311, tier C): 'Cockers can be easily stressed by loud noises and by rough treatment or handling.' (background, kids' copy: gentle handling).

socialisation.value: start socialisation and training classes early
socialisation.quote: Start socialization and training classes early so your Cocker Spaniel puppy learns good manners.
socialisation.notes: PetMD (S309). AKC (S308): 'early socialization and puppy training classes are recommended' (as returned). → proposed_game_parameters.american_cocker_spaniel.socialisation (DOG_SOCIALISATION row, M5-R17).

time_alone.notes: No time-alone statement (AKC S308, PetMD S309, VCA S310 checked). PetMD: 'Cockers love to be close to their people, and they are known to follow their pet parents around the house.' — closeness, not a time-alone rule → no needs_company tag.

other_pets.value: gets along well with other pets and dogs
other_pets.quote: Gets along well with other pets and dogs.
other_pets.notes: VCA (S310). PetMD (S309): 'Cocker Spaniels offer a friendly personality, both with people and with other animals.'; AKC (S308): 'Cockers usually do well in multi-dog households.' No prey-drive statement → other_pets; no chases_small_pets.

chewing.notes: No breed-specific statement found → no chews_when_bored tag.

food_motivation.value: often easily motivated by food and praise
food_motivation.quote: Cocker Spaniels want to please their pet parents, meaning they’re often easily motivated by rewards of food and praise.
food_motivation.notes: PetMD (S309). With obesity_tendency → food_motivated_weight (Labrador / Golden precedent).

obesity_tendency.value: tendency to become overweight; restrict calories if gaining
obesity_tendency.quote: Cockers have a tendency to become overweight.
obesity_tendency.notes: VCA (S310): 'Adult dogs should be fed a balanced diet, with restricted calories if the dog starts to gain too much weight.' PetMD (S309): 'Cocker Spaniels that serve exclusively as family pets can easily become overweight.' → food_motivated_weight.

training_notes.value: sensitive; no harsh corrections — food, praise and play
training_notes.quote: They’re a more sensitive breed, and don’t respond to harsh corrections or disapproving tones.
training_notes.notes: AKC (S308). Not a first-time-owner statement → no first_time_owner / experienced_owner tag.

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages anywhere (the prevalence figures on Wikipedia S311 are not copied). RKC Breed Watch Category 2 without a named point (S306) → no welfare chip (Shetland Sheepdog precedent).

ear_infections.notes: PetMD (S309) health section heading (quote = the heading) 'Ear Infections'; 'routine cleaning with a veterinary-approved ear cleanser is vital in maintaining healthy ear canals' (as returned, partial sentence). → ear care, ROADMAP M5-R20 (needs-david).

skin_infections.notes: PetMD (S309) health section heading (quote = the heading) 'Skin Infections'. AKC (S308) warns about irritation of their sensitive skin when bathing (paraphrase). Background only; no sensitive_skin chip (not a Breed Watch point).

hip_dysplasia.notes: PetMD (S309) health section heading (quote = the heading) 'Hip Dysplasia'. RKC best-practice hip scheme (S305). Background only.

prcd_pra.value: progressive retinal atrophy (prcd-PRA) — an inherited eye disease
prcd_pra.quote: DNA test for progressive retinal atrophy (prcd-PRA)
prcd_pra.notes: RKC best-practice test (S305); the RKC eye scheme with gonioscopy for PLA (glaucoma risk) is a minimum test. Background only.

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table (S35, tier C, read 2026-10-14): rank 20 'Cocker Spaniel' under 'Excellent Working Dogs' (ranks 11–26); Coren's 'Cocker Spaniel' is the American breed — the English Cocker Spaniel is listed separately at rank 18 ('also listed: English Cocker Spaniel'). Coren's own article (S34) lists only the top and bottom 10 — runbook: rank from S35. The breed article (S311) agrees: 'The breed ranks 20th in Stanley Coren's The Intelligence of Dogs'. Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

coren_tier.value: excellent: 5 to 15 repetitions, obeys first command ≥85%
coren_tier.quote: Understanding of new commands: 5 to 15 repetitions.; Obey first command: 85% of the time or better.;
coren_tier.notes: Tier 'Excellent Working Dogs' = ranks 11–26 (S35). Tier definitions from Wikipedia; verify in book.

training_notes.value: wants to please; positive reinforcement
training_notes.quote: Cocker Spaniels want to please their pet parents, meaning they’re often easily motivated by rewards of food and praise.
training_notes.notes: PetMD (S309); AKC (S308) sensitive, no harsh corrections.

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value — see proposed_game_parameters.american_cocker_spaniel.learning_multiplier (1.5, runbook rule: Excellent tier, rank 20).

general.value: the smallest of the sporting dogs; compact, sturdy, balanced
general.quote: The Cocker Spaniel is the smallest member of the Sporting Group.
general.notes: AKC standard (S307); FCI (S304): 'Le Cocker Américain est le plus petit du groupe des chiens pour amateurs de chasse et de pêche.'

colours.quote: Any solid color other than black, ranging from lightest cream to darkest red, including brown and brown with tan points.
colours.notes: AKC standard (S307) varieties: Black ('Solid color black to include black with tan points.'), ASCOB (quote; cream / buff to red, brown), Parti-color ('Two or more solid, well broken colors, one of which must be white.'); tan points ≤ 10 %. FCI (S304) the same three varieties incl. roan in parti-colours; white only on chest / throat in solid colours. Never merle (not listed), never blue eyes (FCI disqualification).

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). Buff first with the highest weight (portrait default — the lightest-cream-to-red ASCOB variety), then black, black and tan, red, chocolate, black and white, red and white, tricolour.

coat.value: silky, flat or slightly wavy; ears, chest, abdomen and legs well feathered
coat.quote: The coat is silky, flat or slightly wavy and of a texture which permits easy care.
coat.notes: AKC standard (S307); FCI (S304): moderate furnishings, heavy / curly / cottony coats severely penalised (tool summary). RKC 'Coat length: Long' (S305). The portrait shows a moderate pet-length coat, not a floor-length show skirt.

ears.value: lobular, long, fine leather, well feathered, set no higher than the lower part of the eye
ears.quote: Lobular, long, of fine leather, well feathered, and placed no higher than a line to the lower part of the eye.
ears.notes: AKC standard (S307); FCI (S304) the same.

eyes.value: round, full, looking forward; dark brown, darker preferred
eyes.quote: Eyeballs are round and full and look directly forward.
eyes.notes: AKC standard (S307); FCI (S304): dark brown, darker preferred; blue, marbled or flecked blue eyes disqualify (tool summary).

nose.value: rounded skull, pronounced stop, broad deep muzzle; black nose in blacks, black and tans, black and whites
nose.quote: The muzzle is broad and deep, with square even jaws.
nose.notes: AKC standard (S307): skull 'Rounded but not exaggerated with no tendency toward flatness.'; nose 'black in color in the blacks, black and tans, and black and whites' (others brown / liver / black, darker preferred, FCI S304). Not a short-faced breed.

tail.value: natural (undocked) tail in the game portrait; the standards describe a docked tail carried on the line of the back
tail.quote: The docked tail is set on and carried on a line with the topline of the back, or slightly higher.
tail.notes: AKC (S307) and FCI (S304) describe a docked tail. The portrait shows a natural undocked tail (German Shorthaired Pointer precedent — docking of pet dogs is banned in Slovenia and the UK); docking is never shown or promoted. Claude's proposal, open for David.

suitability._note: Source = RKC breed-page key facts (S305, older page S306), AKC (S308), PetMD (S309), VCA (S310). No PDSA American Cocker Spaniel page; Woodgreen / Dogs Trust breed pages not attempted. The RKC page shows no 'Good with children' field.

rkc_exercise.quote: Exercise: More than 2 hours per day
rkc_exercise.notes: Basis of 120 min. No exercise chip — AKC (S308) / PetMD (S309) conflict (open for David).

rkc_size_of_home.notes: Not apartment, not large_home.

rkc_grooming.notes: Runbook dog-grooming rule: 'Every day' → 7 brushing sessions a week. Basis of frequent_grooming (with VCA S310).

rkc_shedding.notes: PetMD (S309): brushing prevents 'excess shedding' — agrees. Basis of the sheds tag.

rkc_breed_watch.notes: RKC breed pages (S305, S306): 'Category 2' — 'Particular points of concern for individual breeds may include features not specifically highlighted in the breed standard' (as returned); the older page (S306) lists no specific point → no welfare chip (Shetland Sheepdog precedent, open for David); in marketing.

rkc_good_with_children.notes: The RKC breed page (S305) has no 'Good with children' field.

vca_grooming.value: brushing and combing two to three times a week
vca_grooming.quote: The coat needs brushing and combing two to three times a week to prevent mats.
vca_grooming.notes: VCA (S310) — alternative to the RKC 'Every day' (the rule takes the RKC wording 'Every day' → 7). Supports frequent_grooming.

petmd_grooming.value: frequent brushing, at least once a week
petmd_grooming.quote: Frequent brushing (at least once a week) is important to prevent infections as well as excess shedding.
petmd_grooming.notes: PetMD (S309) — a minimum, compatible with the RKC 'Every day'.

akc_grooming.value: regular brushing, combing, bathing and coat maintenance
akc_grooming.quote: Cocker Spaniels require regular brushing, combing, bathing, and coat maintenance.
akc_grooming.notes: AKC (S308), no frequency; 'Cockers require more dutiful attention when it comes to grooming, especially if kept in their full coat.'

vca_professional_grooming.value: professional grooming and clipping once a month
vca_professional_grooming.quote: Professional grooming and clipping is required once a month.
vca_professional_grooming.notes: VCA (S310); PetMD (S309): 'Cocker Spaniels also benefit from regular professional grooming.'; AKC (S308): a professional groomer for owners unsure about coat care. Groomer = sourced need without a mechanic → ROADMAP M5-R18 (needs-david).

vca_ears.quote: The ears must be checked weekly for problems.
vca_ears.notes: VCA (S310); PetMD (S309) routine cleaning with an ear cleanser, also after swimming or bathing. Ear care = sourced need without a mechanic → ROADMAP M5-R20 (needs-david).

petmd_family.quote: At home, these sweet-tempered pups love being close to their people and make great family dogs.

vca_children.notes: VCA (S310). Basis of the children tag (explicit statement); AKC (S308) agrees.

akc_children.quote: They generally enjoy spending time with children and participating in family activities.

vca_other_pets.value: gets along well with other pets and dogs
vca_other_pets.quote: Gets along well with other pets and dogs.
vca_other_pets.notes: VCA (S310). Basis of other_pets (with PetMD S309).

petmd_other_animals.value: friendly with people and other animals
petmd_other_animals.quote: Cocker Spaniels offer a friendly personality, both with people and with other animals.

belgian_malinois._note: Added 2026-10-14 (M5-R10-38, unattended run — appended after the American Cocker Spaniel: AKC 2024 No. 33 'Belgian Malinois', S174 full-list table '32 Cocker Spaniel', '33 Belgian Malinois'). The FCI recognises one breed, the Belgian Shepherd Dog (FCI No. 15), with four varieties (Groenendael, Laekenois, Malinois, Tervueren); the game breed is the short-haired Malinois variety only. Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-14 (the tool limits quotes to ~125 characters; apostrophes as returned); spot-check before import (sources.md S312–S318, reused S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45, S92, S174). No PDSA Belgian Malinois page exists (search 2026-10-14); VCA page returned no text; the new RKC address (royalkennelclub.com) returned a fetch error — the older RKC address (S314) gave the key facts verbatim. Lifespan: McMillan 2024 / Dogs Trust table (S123) not reachable — Wikipedia (S318, tier C) quotes a 2024 UK study at 12 years for the Malinois, background only → RKC lower bound 'Over 10 years' → senior 90 months, provisional. RKC Breed Watch Category 1 (S314) → no welfare chip; not flat-faced → in marketing. Grooming: RKC 'More than once a week' has no number and AKC / PetMD say 'occasional' → 2× a week, verified=false (Claude's proposal, open for David).

identity.value: FCI No. 15, Group 1 Section 1 (Sheepdogs), Belgium
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S312): group 'n°1 - Sheepdogs and Cattledogs (except Swiss Cattledogs)', section 'Sheepdogs', country 'BELGIUM'; varieties 'a) Groenendael, b) Laekenois, c) Malinois, d) Tervueren' (all CACIB); definitive acceptance 1/1/1956; valid standard 3/13/2001 (English 4/19/2002); 'Subject to a working trial according to the FCI Breeds Nomenclature'. The AKC (S315, S316) registers the Malinois as its own breed 'Belgian Malinois'; the RKC (S314) as 'Belgian Shepherd Dog (Malinois)'. Other names: 'Mal', 'Malinois', 'Belgian Shepherd Malinois' (S316 'Mals').

size_class.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S314). FCI 20–30 kg (S313) = 44–66 lb → mostly the 'Medium (24–59 pounds)' class of S10 (the top of the male range touches 'Large'); treated like the Siberian Husky (RKC 'Medium-Large'). RKC group: Pastoral.

fci.quote: The ideal height at withers is on average - 62 cm for males
fci.notes: FCI standard (S313): ideal 62 cm (males), '- 58 cm for females.'; 'Limits: 2 cm less, 4 cm more' (paraphrase as returned) → 60–66 / 56–62 cm.

akc.quote: Males are 24 to 26 inches in height; females are 22 to 24 inches; measurement to be taken at the withers.
akc.notes: AKC standard (S315); inches × 2.54 by us (rounded). Disqualification: 'Males under 23 inches or over 27 inches and females under 21 inches or over 25 inches are to be disqualified.'

fci.quote: Males about 25-30 kg.
fci.notes: FCI standard (S313) size and weight: 'Males about 25-30 kg.' and 'Females about 20-25 kg.' The game range (adult_weight_kg). The AKC standard (S315) gives no weight.

akc_article.quote: They stand between 22 and 26 inches tall, and weigh 40 to 80 pounds.
akc_article.notes: AKC article (S316), one range for both sexes; pounds × 0.4536 by us. Alternative only (wider than the FCI standard).

petmd.quote: When fully grown, male Belgian Malinois are typically 24–26 inches tall and 60–80 pounds
petmd.notes: PetMD (S317, tier B); females 'about 22–24 inches tall and weigh 40–60 pounds' (as returned). Pounds × 0.4536 by us. Alternative only (heavier than the FCI standard).

salt_category.notes: Category assignment by weight is ours (general_by_size.size_classes.salt_2017_bands_kg, S8): about 20–30 kg. Salt 2017 breed list not checked.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. FCI 20–30 kg (S313) = 44–66 lb → mostly 'Medium (24–59 pounds)'; the male maximum touches 'Large (59–99 pounds): 15–18 months' (Siberian Husky precedent). The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 120 min is reached at 12 months either way).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Belgian Malinois growth curve found.

rkc.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S314). The basis of the senior boundary (runbook: RKC lower bound when no McMillan 2024 / VetCompass value is reachable). Not shorter_lifespan.

petmd.quote: The Belgian Malinois lifespan is typically 10–14 years.
petmd.notes: PetMD (S317, tier B). Lower bound 10 y agrees with the RKC → same senior boundary (90).

mcmillan_2024.quote: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12 years for the Malinois and 13.8 years for the Tervueren
mcmillan_2024.notes: McMillan et al. 2024 as quoted by Wikipedia (S318, tier C — never alone). The Dogs Trust breed table (S123) and the paper (S54) were not reachable on 2026-10-14 → not used as the basis; with it the senior boundary would be round(0.75 × 12 × 12) = 108 months. Verify in S123 before replacing the RKC lower bound.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × 10 y (RKC lower bound 'Over 10 years', S314) → 0.75 × 10 = 7.5 y = 90 months. With McMillan 2024 12 y (via S318): 108 months; Dogs Trust rule of thumb > 7 y = 84 months (S14). Provisional until McMillan 2024 is checked.

adult.quote: Exercise: More than 2 hours per day
adult.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S314). AKC (S316): 'Mals require significant exercise on a daily basis—much more beyond just one daily walk or play session.' — agrees. PetMD (S317): 'Belgian Malinois should get more than 40 minutes of exercise per day—with you by their side.' and 'Daily walks are simply not enough for this breed.' — a minimum, in alternatives. Rule: RKC value preferred → 120.

energy.value: watchful and active, bursting with energy; happiest with plenty of mental and physical activity
energy.quote: happiest with plenty of mental and physical activity
energy.notes: AKC (S316), clause as returned. FCI (S313): 'The Belgian Shepherd is a watchful and active dog, bursting with energy, and always ready to leap into action.' PetMD (S317): 'Belgian Malinois require constant daily training to help minimize any behavioral issues and keep their mind engaged.' Basis of needs_mental_stimulation; daily training is the game's existing school (M5-R03).

temperament.value: alert, intelligent, inquisitive and confident; neither fear nor aggression
temperament.quote: He is alert, intelligent, inquisitive and confident, showing neither fear nor aggression.
temperament.notes: AKC standard (S315); FCI (S313): watchful, active, lively and confident, a devoted protector (paraphrase as returned).

family.value: best in families with older, responsible kids; supervision around children is a must
family.quote: Mals would fare best in families with older, responsible kids.
family.notes: AKC (S316); also 'supervision around children is a must'. PetMD (S317): 'They may also try to use their herding skills to round up toddlers and children.' → not_for_small_children + may_herd_children; never family_pet / children / small_children.

experienced_owner.value: not for first-time owners; needs a dedicated, experienced owner
experienced_owner.quote: don't make them a good choice for first-time dog owners
experienced_owner.notes: AKC (S316), clause as returned; 'an experienced dog owner with plenty of time to devote to a smart, hard-working breed'. PetMD (S317): 'Belgian Malinois dogs need a dedicated and experienced pet parent'. → experienced_owner.

socialisation.value: early, extensive socialisation
socialisation.quote: Early, extensive socialization will help limit aggressive tendencies towards new people.
socialisation.notes: AKC (S316). PetMD (S317): 'Consistent training and socialization should start as early as possible and continue throughout their life.' → proposed_game_parameters.belgian_malinois.socialisation (DOG_SOCIALISATION row, M5-R17).

time_alone.value: should not be left alone for extended periods
time_alone.quote: they should not be left alone for extended periods of time.
time_alone.notes: AKC (S316). PetMD (S317): 'They are not the type of dog that can just be left in the backyard to entertain themselves.' → needs_company (Boxer precedent).

other_pets.value: high prey drive; may chase other animals
other_pets.quote: Belgian Malinois also have a high prey drive, making them extremely interested in moving objects.
other_pets.notes: PetMD (S317). AKC (S316): 'inclined to chase children, cars, or other animals' and 'tend to get territorial towards other animals' (clauses as returned). → chases_small_pets (prey-drive quote); no other_pets.

chewing.notes: No breed-specific chewing statement found → no chews_when_bored tag.

food_motivation.notes: No food-motivation or weight-gain statement found → no food_motivated_weight tag. PetMD (S317): 'Belgian Malinois should be fed twice daily' — the general rule.

training_notes.value: frequent, consistent, positive-reinforcement training
training_notes.quote: Frequent, consistent training sessions rooted in positive reinforcement are the best fit for a Mal.
training_notes.notes: AKC (S316).

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages anywhere. RKC Breed Watch Category 1 (S314) → no welfare chip.

hip_elbow_dysplasia.notes: PetMD (S317) health section heading (quote = the heading). Wikipedia (S318, tier C): the Société Royale Saint-Hubert recommends hip and elbow testing for all four varieties (background). Background only.

pra.value: progressive retinal atrophy (an inherited eye disease)

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table (S35, tier C, read 2026-10-14): rank 22 'Belgian Malinois' under 'Excellent Working Dogs' (ranks 11–26); 'Belgian Shepherd Dog (Tervuren)' 14 and 'Belgian Sheepdog' 15 are other varieties. Coren's own article (S34) lists only the top and bottom 10 — runbook: rank from S35. Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

coren_tier.value: excellent: 5 to 15 repetitions, obeys first command ≥85%
coren_tier.quote: Understanding of new commands: 5 to 15 repetitions.; Obey first command: 85% of the time or better.;
coren_tier.notes: Tier 'Excellent Working Dogs' = ranks 11–26 (S35). Tier definitions from Wikipedia; verify in book.

training_notes.value: one of the smartest breeds; needs constant daily training
training_notes.quote: Belgian Malinois require constant daily training to help minimize any behavioral issues and keep their mind engaged.
training_notes.notes: PetMD (S317): 'Belgian Malinois are one of the smartest dog breeds' (as returned).

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value — see proposed_game_parameters.belgian_malinois.learning_multiplier (1.5, runbook rule: Excellent tier, rank 22).

general.value: square, well balanced, elegant and powerful; proud carriage of head and neck
general.quote: The Belgian Malinois is a well-balanced square dog, elegant in appearance
general.notes: AKC standard (S315): 'with an exceedingly proud carriage of head and neck.' FCI (S313): 'The Belgian Shepherd is a mediolineal dog, harmoniously proportioned, combining elegance and power.'

value: fawn with black overlay and black mask
mahogany with black overlay and black mask
colours.quote: Malinois: Only fawn with black overlay and with black mask.
colours.notes: FCI (S313): black overlay as flamed tips, not patches or brindle (paraphrase as returned); disqualifying 'lack of mask, including a muzzle of lighter colour than the rest of the coat in Tervueren and Malinois.' AKC (S315): 'The ideal coloring is a rich fawn to mahogany, with black tips on the hairs giving an overlay appearance.'; white only on toe tips and a small spot on the breastbone. Never black, brindle, merle, grey or white patches.

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). Fawn with black overlay and mask first with the highest weight (portrait default — the only FCI colour), then mahogany (AKC 'fawn to mahogany').

coat.value: short, straight, hard, weather-resistant, dense undercoat; very short on head, ears and lower legs
coat.quote: The coat should be comparatively short, straight, hard enough to be weather resistant, with dense undercoat.
coat.notes: AKC standard (S315). FCI (S313): 'The hair is very short on the head, the outer sides of the ears and the lower part of the legs.'; fuller at the tail and neck. RKC breed page (S314): 'Coat length: Medium' (as returned — the RKC key fact is shared wording; the standards describe a short coat). The portrait shows the short Malinois coat.

mask.value: pronounced black mask encompassing lips and eyelids
mask.quote: The mask must be pronounced and tends to encompass the top and bottom lip,
mask.notes: AKC (S315): 'the corners of the lips and the eyelids in one single black zone.' FCI (S313): the mask 'must be very pronounced and tend to encompass the top and bottom lip.' A muzzle lighter than the coat disqualifies (FCI).

ears.value: rather small, set high, distinctly triangular, stiff and erect
ears.quote: Rather small, set high, distinctly triangular appearance.
ears.notes: FCI (S313): carried 'upright and vertical when dog is alert.' AKC (S315): 'They should be stiff and carried upright and vertical when the dog is alert.'; hanging or semi-prick ears disqualify. Natural erect ears in the portrait (never cropped).

eyes.value: medium size, almond-shaped, brown, preferably dark
eyes.quote: They are brown, preferably dark brown, with black rimmed upper and lower eyelids.
eyes.notes: AKC (S315): 'Light eyes are a fault.' FCI (S313): 'Medium size, neither protruding nor sunken.'; brownish, preferably dark.

tail.value: strong at the base, reaching at least the hock, carried down at rest with the tip curved back
tail.quote: at rest carried down, with tip curved backwards at level of hock.
tail.notes: FCI (S313). AKC (S315): 'The tail is strong at the base, reaching to the hock, and carried down at rest.'; 'A cropped or stumped tail is a disqualification.' Natural full tail in the portrait.

rkc_exercise.quote: Exercise: More than 2 hours per day

rkc_grooming.quote: Grooming: More than once a week

No frequent_grooming chip (RKC vs AKC / PetMD 'occasional' — conflicting).

rkc_coat_length.notes: The standards (S313, S315) describe a short coat; background only.

rkc_shedding.notes: Basis of the sheds tag (with AKC S316 / PetMD S317 seasonal shedding).

rkc_breed_watch.quote: Currently no points of concern specific to this breed have been identified for special attention by judges
rkc_breed_watch.notes: RKC breed page (S314) 'Category 1' → no welfare chip; in marketing.

rkc_good_with_children.notes: The RKC breed page (S314) has no 'Good with children' field.

akc_exercise.value: significant daily exercise, much more than one walk
akc_exercise.quote: Mals require significant exercise on a daily basis—much more beyond just one daily walk or play session.

akc_children.quote: Mals would fare best in families with older, responsible kids.

petmd_herding_children.value: may try to round up toddlers and children
petmd_herding_children.quote: They may also try to use their herding skills to round up toddlers and children.

akc_experienced_owner.value: not a good choice for first-time owners
akc_experienced_owner.quote: don't make them a good choice for first-time dog owners
akc_experienced_owner.notes: AKC (S316). Basis of experienced_owner (with PetMD S317).

petmd_experienced_owner.value: needs a dedicated and experienced pet parent
petmd_experienced_owner.quote: Belgian Malinois dogs need a dedicated and experienced pet parent
petmd_experienced_owner.notes: PetMD (S317), clause as returned. Supports experienced_owner.

akc_mental_stimulation.value: happiest with plenty of mental and physical activity
akc_mental_stimulation.quote: happiest with plenty of mental and physical activity
akc_mental_stimulation.notes: AKC (S316). Basis of needs_mental_stimulation (with PetMD S317 'constant daily training').

akc_time_alone.value: should not be left alone for extended periods
akc_time_alone.quote: they should not be left alone for extended periods of time.

petmd_prey_drive.quote: Belgian Malinois also have a high prey drive, making them extremely interested in moving objects.

akc_shedding.value: heavier shedding twice a year; daily brushing during shedding seasons
akc_shedding.quote: During shedding seasons, daily brushing will limit the build up of hair around your home.

akc_grooming.quote: Mals only require occasional brushing to keep their coats looking healthy.

petmd_grooming.value: occasional brushing
petmd_grooming.quote: Simply brushing their coat occasionally with the right dog brushes

akc_nails.quote: regular nail trimming is a must.
akc_nails.notes: AKC (S316), clause as returned; PetMD (S317): 'As with all dogs, a Belgian Malinois’ nails should be trimmed regularly.' Nail care = sourced need without a mechanic → ROADMAP M5-R19 (needs-david).

petmd_ears.quote: For an otherwise healthy Belgian Malinois, clean their ears once a month with a vet-recommended ear cleaner or ear flush.

petmd_teeth.quote: Like all dogs, the Belgian Malinois needs daily dental care
petmd_teeth.notes: PetMD (S317), clause as returned. Tooth care = sourced need without a mechanic → ROADMAP M5-R15 (needs-david).

basset_hound._note: Added 2026-10-15 (M5-R10-39, unattended run — appended after the Belgian Malinois: AKC 2024 No. 34 'Basset Hound', S174 full-list table '33 Belgian Malinois', '34 Basset Hound', '35 Vizsla'). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-15 (the tool limits quotes to ~125 characters; apostrophes as returned); spot-check before import (sources.md S319–S325, reused S8, S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45, S92, S129, S174). The FCI standard (S320) gives no weight → PDSA (S323) weight. Lifespan: McMillan 2024 / Dogs Trust table (S123) not reachable (URL refused by the fetch tool; the 'shortest and longest' PDF returned a fetch error) — Wikipedia (S325, tier C) quotes a 2024 UK study at 12.5 years, background only → RKC lower bound 'Over 10 years' (PDSA agrees) → senior 90 months, provisional. VetCompass 2013 (S212) has no Basset Hound row. RKC Breed Watch Category 3 (S322: eyelids, ears, skin-fold dermatitis, ground clearance / excessive skin, bite, too fat) → welfare chips eyelid_problems + sensitive_skin; not flat-faced → in marketing.

identity.value: FCI No. 163, Group 6 Section 1.3 (Small-sized hounds), Great Britain
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S319): group 'n°6 - Scent hounds and related breeds', section 'Scent hounds' (subsection 'Small-sized Hounds'), country 'GREAT BRITAIN'; definitive acceptance 4/28/1955; valid standard published 9/8/2026 (English 10/6/2026, as returned); 'Subject to a working trial according to the FCI Breeds Nomenclature'. FCI standard (S320): 'Group 6 Scent hounds and related breeds' / 'Section 1.3 Small-sized hounds'. RKC (S321) and AKC (S324): 'Basset Hound'. Not the Basset Fauve de Bretagne, Basset Artésien Normand or Basset Griffon Vendéen (other FCI breeds).

size_class.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S321). PDSA (S323): 'Medium'. PDSA 18–27 kg = 40–60 lb → the 'Medium (24–59 pounds)' class of S10 (the top touches 'Large'). A short-legged, heavy dog: FCI 'Short-legged hound of considerable substance' (S320). RKC group: Hound.

fci.quote: Height at the withers: 33 - 38 cm.
fci.notes: FCI standard (S320), one range for both sexes.

akc_article.quote: Basset Hounds are low-slung dogs that stand no taller than 15 inches, and weigh between 40 and 65 pounds.
akc_article.notes: AKC article (S324): an upper bound only; 15 in × 2.54 = 38.1 cm by us. Alternative only.

pdsa.notes: PDSA breed page (S323) key fact 'Average weight', one range for both sexes. The game range (adult_weight_kg). The FCI standard (S320) gives no weight (tool: 'The document does not specify a weight.').

akc_article.quote: Basset Hounds are low-slung dogs that stand no taller than 15 inches, and weigh between 40 and 65 pounds.
akc_article.notes: AKC article (S324), one range for both sexes; pounds × 0.4536 by us. Alternative only.

salt_category.notes: Category assignment by weight is ours (general_by_size.size_classes.salt_2017_bands_kg, S8): about 18–27 kg. Salt 2017 breed list not checked.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. PDSA 18–27 kg (S323) = 40–60 lb → 'Medium (24–59 pounds)'. The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 60 min is reached at 6 months).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Basset Hound growth curve found.

rkc.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S321). PDSA (S323) 'Average lifespan' 'Over 10 years' agrees. The basis of the senior boundary (runbook: RKC lower bound when no McMillan 2024 / VetCompass value is reachable). Not shorter_lifespan.

pdsa.notes: PDSA key fact 'Average lifespan' (S323). Same lower bound as the RKC → same senior boundary (90).

mcmillan_2024.quote: A 2024 study in the UK found a life expectancy of 12.5 years compared to an average of 12.7 for purebreeds
mcmillan_2024.notes: McMillan et al. 2024 as quoted by Wikipedia (S325, tier C — never alone). The Dogs Trust breed table (S123) was refused by the fetch tool on 2026-10-15 → not used as the basis; with it the senior boundary would be round(0.75 × 12.5 × 12) = round(112.5) = 113 months. Wikipedia also: 'A 2015 French study found a life expectancy of 10.3 years.' (background). Verify in S123 before replacing the RKC lower bound.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × 10 y (RKC lower bound 'Over 10 years', S321) → 0.75 × 10 = 7.5 y = 90 months. With McMillan 2024 12.5 y (via S325): 113 months; Dogs Trust rule of thumb > 7 y = 84 months (S14). Provisional until McMillan 2024 is checked.

adult.quote: Exercise: Up to 1 hour per day
adult.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S321). PDSA (S323): 'Your Basset Hound will need a minimum of an hour of exercise a day.' — the same number (60). AKC (S324): 'Although they aren't high-energy dogs, Basset Hounds still need regular physical activity to stay healthy.' Rule: RKC value preferred → 60.

after_meals.value: leave a gap after eating before exercise (bloat / GDV)
after_meals.quote: Remember to leave a gap after eating and before exercising.
after_meals.notes: PDSA (S323), with the GDV health point 'where a dog's tummy bloats and twists around on itself, which can be fatal.' No length in the source → meal_exercise_gap 60 (David's M5-R16 decision).

scent.value: scent hound — keep on a firm lead; secure garden; scent games
scent.quote: A secure garden is a must and be careful there's no way for them to escape in case they catch the scent of something.
scent.notes: PDSA (S323): 'Remember that Basset Hounds are scent dogs, so when walking them have a firm grip on their lead…' and 'Play lots of scent games with then on top of their daily exercise' (sic, as returned). AKC (S324): 'Because their noses can easily lead them astray, secure leashes and fenced areas are important when exercising the breed.' Not secure_fencing — that chip says 'needs a secure, high fence' (Siberian Husky: digging, climbing); no source says the Basset needs a high fence (Claude's reading, open for David). Walks on the lead = the game's existing walk.

temperament.value: placid, never aggressive or timid; affectionate
temperament.quote: Placid, never aggressive or timid.
temperament.notes: FCI standard (S320): 'Affectionate.'; 'Tenacious hound of ancient lineage which hunts by scent, possesses a pack instinct and a deep melodious voice.' PDSA (S323): 'Basset Hounds are gentle, placid dogs who tend to get along with everyone and every situation if they’re well-socialised.'

family.value: does well in family environments; gets along very well with children
family.quote: They do well in family environments thanks to their sweet nature and ability to get along so well with children.
family.notes: PDSA (S323). Also 'They best suit a family home where there is always someone around and lots of opportunities to be with people.' → family_pet.

children.value: generally very tolerant; should get along with children very well
children.quote: Basset Hounds are generally very tolerant and so should get along with children very well.
children.notes: PDSA (S323). AKC (S324): 'Their patient, friendly nature often makes them good companions for children' → children (an explicit statement; no rating for small children → no small_children).

time_alone.value: generally well-behaved when left alone, but loves company; best where someone is always around
time_alone.quote: Although Basset Hounds are generally well-behaved when left alone, they love company.
time_alone.notes: PDSA (S323); 'They best suit a family home where there is always someone around and lots of opportunities to be with people.' → needs_company (Boxer precedent: 'best to have a Boxer if someone is going to be around the house with them all day').

socialisation.value: socialise from a young age with people and dogs
socialisation.quote: Be sure to socialise your Basset Hound from a young age with other people and dogs once they are fully vaccinated.
socialisation.notes: PDSA (S323). AKC (S324): 'Early socialization is important for helping puppies develop confidence and good manners.' → proposed_game_parameters.basset_hound.socialisation (DOG_SOCIALISATION row, M5-R17).

other_pets.value: usually fine with other dogs when well-socialised; never unattended with another pet
other_pets.quote: Well-socialised Basset Hounds will usually be fine around other dogs.
other_pets.notes: PDSA (S323); also 'Never leave them unattended with another pet, even if they know them well.' AKC (S324): 'The breed was developed to work alongside other dogs during hunts, so many enjoy canine company.' Conditional + supervision caveat → no other_pets; no prey-drive statement (PDSA has no 'chase' or 'prey') → no chases_small_pets.

chewing.notes: No breed-specific chewing statement found → no chews_when_bored tag.

food_motivation.value: very healthy appetite — needs plenty of exercise not to gain weight
food_motivation.quote: Beware that Basset Hounds can have very healthy appetites and so need plenty of exercise so they don't gain weight.
food_motivation.notes: PDSA (S323); also 'Being overweight can make many of the health problems Basset Hounds are prone to worse'. RKC Breed Watch (S322) point 'Too fat'. → food_motivated_weight.

drooling.value: long jowls — excess saliva is normal for the breed
drooling.quote: Their long jowls create excess saliva, which is a normal trait of the breed.

voice.quote: Tenacious hound of ancient lineage which hunts by scent, possesses a pack instinct and a deep melodious voice.
voice.notes: FCI (S320). AKC (S324): the breed uses 'their loud, ringing voices on the hunt or just to show their excitement or frustration.' Background only (no vocabulary key; the game has no barking mechanic).

training_notes.value: independent, can be stubborn when on a scent
training_notes.quote: Be aware that Basset Hounds can be very independent, especially when it comes to training.
training_notes.notes: PDSA (S323). AKC (S324): 'Though laid-back by nature, Basset Hounds can become stubborn when they catch a scent.' and 'They may be tempted to follow an interesting scent, rather than respond immediately when called.' Fits the slow learning multiplier (Coren rank 71).

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages anywhere (Wikipedia S325 glaucoma prevalence is never used). Conformation welfare topic: RKC Breed Watch Category 3 (S322) — eyelids turned inwards or outwards, very long ears, dermatitis in skin folds, inadequate ground clearance / excessive skin, incorrect bite, too fat, excessive skin → eyelid_problems (Great Dane precedent) and sensitive_skin (Westie precedent). No back_spine: PDSA names IVDD (S323, S129) but Breed Watch does not (Pembroke Welsh Corgi precedent, open for David). Not flat-faced → no brachycephalic chip, and no veterinary advice against advertising the breed type. PDSA (S323): 'Basset Hounds are prone to certain health problems, many caused by being bred for their appearance over health.'

breed_watch.value: RKC Breed Watch Category 3 — eyelids turned in or out; ears far beyond the muzzle; skin-fold dermatitis; inadequate ground clearance / excessive skin; incorrect bite; too fat; excessive skin
breed_watch.quote: Eyelids not in normal contact with the eyeball, they are turned inwards or outwards
breed_watch.notes: RKC Breed Watch page 'Basset Hound - Category 3' (S322); further points 'Ears that extend more than slightly beyond end of muzzle', 'Signs of dermatitis irritation in skin folds, and/or hair loss or scarring from previous dermatitis', 'Inadequate ground clearance - overly deep body and/ or presence of excessive skin', 'Incorrect bite', 'Too fat', 'Excessive skin on the head, body and/or legs'. RKC breed page (S321): 'Category 3' and 'This breed can be affected by conformational concerns, more information can be found here.' Basis of eyelid_problems.

skin_folds.value: skin-fold dermatitis — check the folds every day, keep them clean and dry
skin_folds.quote: Signs of dermatitis irritation in skin folds, and/or hair loss or scarring from previous dermatitis
skin_folds.notes: RKC Breed Watch (S322). PDSA (S323) health list: 'skin fold dermatitis', 'Skin infections'; care: 'However, because they have lots of excess skin, you’ll need to check the folds in their skin every day,' — 'keeping them clean and dry so they don’t get moist, sore and infected.' (one sentence, split by the tool). Basis of sensitive_skin; the daily fold check = sourced need without a mechanic → ROADMAP M5-R14.

eyes.value: eyelids turned in or out; primary open-angle glaucoma (painful, can cause blindness) — DNA-tested parents
eyes.quote: Eye problems including Primary Open Angle Glaucoma
eyes.notes: PDSA (S323): glaucoma is 'where fluid builds up inside the eye, causing pain and potentially blindness.' The RKC approved an official DNA testing scheme for POAG in the breed (K23). Breed Watch (S322) eyelids point.

gdv.notes: PDSA (S323): 'where a dog's tummy bloats and twists around on itself, which can be fatal.' and 'Remember to leave a gap after eating and before exercising.' → meal_exercise_gap (M5-R16).

ivdd.quote: Intervertebral degenerative disc disease (IVDD) – also known as a slipped disc, which can lead to back pain and paralysis.
ivdd.notes: PDSA (S323); the PDSA IVDD page (S129) lists the Basset Hound among prone breeds (background). Not a Breed Watch point → no back_spine chip (Pembroke Welsh Corgi precedent; open for David).

ears.value: long ears — keep an eye on them so they don't get dirty and infected
ears.quote: You'll also need to keep an eye on your Basset Hound's ears to make sure they don't get dirty and infected.
ears.notes: PDSA (S323); 'Remember that cleaning too often, or too forcefully, can also lead to problems.' No frequency. RKC Breed Watch (S322): 'Ears that extend more than slightly beyond end of muzzle'. Ear care = sourced need without a mechanic → ROADMAP M5-R20 (needs-david).

weight.value: becoming overweight makes many problems worse
weight.quote: Being overweight can make many of the health problems Basset Hounds are prone to worse
weight.notes: PDSA (S323); RKC Breed Watch (S322) 'Too fat'. Basis of food_motivated_weight (with behaviour.food_motivation).

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table (S35, tier C, read 2026-10-15): rank 71 'Basset Hound' under 'Lowest Degree of Working/Obedience Intelligence' (ranks 70–79). Coren's own article (S34) not re-read this run — runbook: rank from S35. Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

coren_tier.value: lowest: 80 to 100 repetitions or more, obeys first command 25% or worse
coren_tier.quote: Understanding of new commands: 80 to 100 repetitions or more.; Obey first command: 25% of the time or worse.;
coren_tier.notes: Tier 'Lowest Degree of Working/Obedience Intelligence' = ranks 70–79 (S35). Tier definitions from Wikipedia; verify in book.

training_notes.value: very independent in training; stubborn on a scent
training_notes.quote: Be aware that Basset Hounds can be very independent, especially when it comes to training.
training_notes.notes: PDSA (S323); AKC (S324) agrees (stubborn when they catch a scent).

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value — see proposed_game_parameters.basset_hound.learning_multiplier (0.5, runbook rule: Lowest tier, rank 71).

general.value: short-legged hound of considerable substance, well balanced
general.quote: Short-legged hound of considerable substance, well balanced, full of quality.
general.notes: FCI standard (S320). AKC (S324): 'Bassets are most well known for their domed heads, long ears, and somber eyes.' Welfare (RKC Breed Watch S322): adequate ground clearance, no excessive skin, ears not far beyond the muzzle, eyelids in normal contact — the portrait shows a moderate, healthy type.

colours.quote: Generally black, white and tan (tri-colour); lemon and white (bi-colour); but any recognized hound colour acceptable.
colours.notes: FCI standard (S320). 'Any recognized hound colour acceptable' — the game lists only the two named colours (runbook: colours listed by the breed standard; never merle or a non-hound colour).

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). Tricolour first with the highest weight (portrait default — 'Generally black, white and tan'), then lemon and white.

coat.value: smooth, short and close
coat.quote: Smooth, short and close without being too fine.
coat.notes: FCI standard (S320). RKC (S321): 'Coat length: Short'.

skin.value: supple and elastic without exaggeration; a small amount of wrinkle at brow and beside the eyes
skin.quote: Supple and elastic without any exaggeration.
skin.notes: FCI (S320) skin; head: 'There may be a small amount of wrinkle at brow and beside eyes.' Breed Watch (S322) 'Excessive skin on the head, body and/or legs' is a point of concern → the portrait shows moderate skin (dog trait `skin`).

ears.value: set low, just below the eye line; long, narrow, curling inwards, supple and velvety
ears.quote: Narrow throughout their length and curling well inwards; very supple, fine and velvety in texture.
ears.notes: FCI (S320): 'Set-on low, just below line of eye.' Breed Watch (S322): ears that extend more than slightly beyond the end of the muzzle are a concern → moderate ear length in the portrait.

eyes.value: lozenge-shaped, neither prominent nor deep-set, dark
eyes.quote: Lozenge-shaped, neither prominent nor deep-set, dark but may shade to mid-brown in light-coloured hounds.
eyes.notes: FCI (S320). Breed Watch (S322): eyelids turned in or out are a concern → eyelids in normal contact in the portrait (no drooping haw).

tail.value: well set-on, rather long, strong at the base, tapering
tail.quote: Well set-on, rather long, strong at base, tapering, with moderate amount of coarse hair underneath.
tail.notes: FCI (S320).

suitability._note: Source = RKC breed-page key facts (S321, older address), PDSA (S323), AKC (S324). The RKC page shows no 'Good with children' field.

PDSA (S323): 'Although Basset Hounds shed, it's not as much as some dogs and their coats are fairly low maintenance.' — sheds, less than some breeds (not 'minimal' → no conflict; never low_shedding).

akc_shedding.quote: But they shed more than you might expect.
akc_shedding.notes: AKC (S324). Supports sheds (with RKC S321 'Sheds: Yes').

rkc_breed_watch.notes: RKC breed page (S321) 'Category 3'; points on the Breed Watch page (S322) → eyelid_problems, sensitive_skin; in marketing (not flat-faced).

rkc_good_with_children.notes: The RKC breed page (S321) has no 'Good with children' field.

pdsa_family.quote: They do well in family environments thanks to their sweet nature and ability to get along so well with children.

pdsa_company.quote: They best suit a family home where there is always someone around and lots of opportunities to be with people.

akc_drooling.quote: Their long jowls create excess saliva, which is a normal trait of the breed.

pdsa_skin_folds.notes: PDSA (S323), sentence continues 'keeping them clean and dry so they don’t get moist, sore and infected.' Skin-fold care = sourced need without a mechanic → ROADMAP M5-R14 (needs-david).

hungarian_vizsla._note: Added 2026-10-15 (M5-R10-40, unattended run — appended after the Basset Hound: AKC 2024 No. 35 'Vizsla', S174 full-list table '34 Basset Hound', '35 Vizsla', '36 English Cocker Spaniel'). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-15 (the tool limits quotes to ~125 characters; '…' marks where the tool shortened a sentence); spot-check before import (sources.md S326–S334, reused S8, S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45, S174). Smooth-coated Hungarian Vizsla only (FCI 57) — not the Hungarian Wirehaired Vizsla (FCI 239). The FCI (S327) and AKC (S331) standards give no weight → PDSA (S329) weight. Lifespan: McMillan 2024 / Dogs Trust table (S123) refused by the fetch tool (provenance) — Wikipedia (S334, tier C) quotes a 2024 UK study at 13.5 years, background only → RKC lower bound 'Over 12 years' (PDSA agrees) → senior 108 months, provisional. RKC Breed Watch Category 1 → no welfare chip; in marketing.

identity.value: FCI No. 57, Group 7 Section 1.1 (Continental Pointing Dogs, Braque type), Hungary
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S326): group 'n°7 - Pointing Dogs', section 'Continental Pointing Dogs', subsection '«Braque» Type', country 'Hungary'; definitive acceptance 8/12/1954; valid standard 4/6/2000; 'Subject to a working trial'. FCI standard (S327): 'FCI-CLASSIFICATION: Group 7 Pointing Dogs.' (Section 1, Continental Pointing Dogs; Field and Water Trial). Names: RKC (S328) 'Hungarian Vizsla'; AKC (S331) 'Vizsla'; Wikipedia (S334) 'also known as Hungarian Vizsla, Magyar Vizsla or Hungarian Pointer'. Not the Hungarian Wirehaired Vizsla (FCI 239, a separate breed).

size_class.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S328); PDSA (S329) 'Large'. Dogs Trust Ireland (S333) 'Medium'; the FCI standard (S327) asks for a medium size. fci.quote: Dogs: 58 - 64 cm

pdsa.notes: PDSA key fact 'Average height' (S329), one range for both sexes. Alternative only.

petmd.notes: PetMD (S330), one range ('females are typically smaller than males'); pounds × 0.4536 by us. Alternative only.

mcmillan_2024.quote: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.5 years for the breed
