energy.value: high-energy; needs lots of exercise to stay physically and mentally healthy
energy.quote: Hungarian Vizslas are typically high-energy dogs who need lots of exercise to keep them physically and mentally healthy.
energy.notes: Dogs Trust Ireland (S333). PetMD (S330): 'They love problem-solving, and if they're not given ample amount of attention, the pups are prone to boredom' (shortened by the tool). Not needs_mental_stimulation — no explicit mental-stimulation need (German Shorthaired Pointer precedent; Claude's reading, open for David).

after_meals.value: leave a gap between eating and exercising (bloat)
after_meals.quote: Remember to leave a gap between eating and exercising.
after_meals.notes: PDSA (S329). PetMD (S330): 'One thing to keep in mind when feeding a Vizsla is that they're susceptible to bloat due to their deep-chested body.' and 'Also, avoid exercise immediately prior to and after mealtime.' No length in the sources → meal_exercise_gap 60 (David's M5-R16 decision).

temperament.value: lively, friendly, evenly tempered, easy to train; neither aggressive nor shy
temperament.quote: Lively, friendly, evenly tempered, to be trained easily.
temperament.notes: FCI standard (S327); 'His outstanding willingness to keep contact with his master while working is one of his essential qualities.' AKC standard (S331): 'A natural hunter endowed with a good nose and above-average ability to take training.'

family.value: ideal family pets for households with children (supervise; too excitable for children under 6)
family.quote: These tall, long-eared beauties are extremely loyal and friendly, making them ideal family pets for households with children.
family.notes: PetMD (S330); 'But for small children under the age of 6, [a Vizsla's] excitement can be too much.' PDSA (S329): 'Hungarian Vizslas are very people orientated dogs who love company.' → family_pet (with the small-children chip).

children.value: gets along really well with older children; not recommended with very young children
children.quote: Because of their playful nature, they get along really well with older children they can play with.
children.notes: PDSA (S329): 'We wouldn't recommend a Vizsla if you have very young children' and 'Always supervise your dog with children and vulnerable adults.' PetMD (S330): under 6 'excitement can be too much'. Older children only → no children / small_children; not_for_small_children (Belgian Malinois precedent — older_children's chip says 'small dog').

experienced_owner.value: not suitable for first-time dog owners
experienced_owner.quote: Their energy levels and strong personality means they are not suitable for first time dog owners.

socialisation.value: socialise from a young age with lots of people, dogs and experiences
socialisation.quote: as long as you socialise your Vizsla from a young age with lots of people, dogs and experiences
socialisation.notes: PDSA (S329) (fragment as returned; continues 'they will grow into happy and confident adults.'). PetMD (S330): '...though proper (and early) socialization is essential.' → proposed_game_parameters.hungarian_vizsla.socialisation (DOG_SOCIALISATION row, M5-R17).

time_alone.value: strong bonds, loves human company — often separation anxiety if left alone; ideally someone around all day
time_alone.quote: Vizslas form strong bonds with their owners and love human company so often suffer with separation anxiety if left alone.
time_alone.notes: PDSA (S329); 'Ideally, your Vizsla will need someone around all day to keep them company.' and 'If left alone they can develop negative behaviour due to stress.' → needs_company.

other_pets.value: high prey drive — not advised with smaller pets; may be OK with a cat it grew up with
other_pets.quote: Hungarian Vizslas do have a high prey drive, so we wouldn't advise keeping them with smaller pets.
other_pets.notes: PDSA (S329); 'They may get along OK with a cat they have grown up with'. PetMD (S330): 'They can be gentle and affectionate with children and live contentedly with other dogs and even cats,...' — conflicting → no other_pets; the high prey drive → chases_small_pets (runbook rule, David 2026-10-12).

chewing.notes: No breed-specific chewing statement found → no chews_when_bored tag.

food_motivation.notes: No appetite statement. PDSA (S329): 'We usually recommend splitting their daily allowance into two meals.' (the game's meals are the general rule) → no food_motivated_weight.

training_notes.value: responds well to positive, reward-based training from an early age
training_notes.quote: Hungarian Vizslas respond really well to positive, reward-based training from an early age
training_notes.notes: PDSA (S329). PetMD (S330): 'Positive reinforcement is the best training approach.'; lead training needs extra attention (paraphrase). Fits the Excellent learning tier (Coren rank 25).

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages anywhere. RKC Breed Watch Category 1 (S328: 'Currently no points of concern specific to this breed have been identified for special attention by judges,') → no welfare chip (no hips_hind_legs / eyelid_problems — hip dysplasia and entropion are PDSA list items, not Breed Watch points; Belgian Malinois precedent, open for David). RKC breed health priorities (S328): 'Unregulated over breeding', 'Autoimmune illnesses', 'Epilepsy', 'Cancers'. HUU in the PDSA list concerns the wire-haired Vizsla only (PDSA wording) — not recorded for this breed.

hip_dysplasia.value: hip dysplasia — hip and elbow screening of the parents
hip_dysplasia.notes: PDSA (S329): 'where the hip joint doesn't fit together perfectly, which will eventually lead to arthritis.' RKC (S328): 'the breed have hip and elbow screening as requirements under the Assured Breeders Scheme' and 'Estimated Breeding Values (EBVs) in place for hips.' PetMD (S330) lists hip dysplasia. Background only.

entropion.notes: PDSA (S329): 'where the eyelids turn inwards and cause irritation and pain.' Not a Breed Watch point → no eyelid_problems chip (open for David). Background only.

epilepsy.notes: PDSA (S329): 'a brain disorder causing seizures.' RKC breed health priority (S328). PetMD (S330) lists epilepsy.

autoimmune.notes: RKC breed health priority (S328); PDSA (S329) 'Autoimmune conditions' ('a condition where the body reacts against itself.').

cancers.notes: RKC breed health priority (S328); PDSA (S329) 'Certain cancers'.

pra.notes: PetMD (S330) health list (heading, no sentence returned) — background only; not in the register.

hypothyroidism.quote: If left untreated, hypothyroidism can shorten your Vizsla's lifespan.

bloat.value: bloat (deep chest) — no exercise right before or after meals
bloat.quote: One thing to keep in mind when feeding a Vizsla is that they're susceptible to bloat due to their deep-chested body.
bloat.notes: PetMD (S330); PDSA (S329) gap after eating → meal_exercise_gap (M5-R16).

ears.value: prone to ear infections — clean the ears regularly
ears.quote: Vizslas are prone to ear infections, so it's important to keep a close eye on your pet's ear hygiene...
ears.notes: PetMD (S330), shortened by the tool; no frequency. Ear care = sourced need without a mechanic → ROADMAP M5-R20 (needs-david).

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table (S35, tier C, read 2026-10-15): rank 25 'Vizsla' under 'Excellent Working Dogs' (ranks 11–26). Not in Coren's own top / bottom-10 article (S34) — runbook: rank from S35. Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

coren_tier.value: excellent: 5 to 15 repetitions, obeys first command 85% or better
coren_tier.quote: Understanding of new commands: 5 to 15 repetitions.; Obey first command: 85% of the time or better.;
coren_tier.notes: Tier 'Excellent Working Dogs' = ranks 11–26 (S35). Tier definitions from Wikipedia; verify in book.

training_notes.value: responds well to positive, reward-based training
training_notes.quote: Hungarian Vizslas respond really well to positive, reward-based training from an early age
training_notes.notes: PDSA (S329); FCI (S327) 'to be trained easily'.

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value — see proposed_game_parameters.hungarian_vizsla.learning_multiplier (1.5, runbook rule: Excellent tier, rank 25).

general.value: medium-sized, elegant gundog of noble appearance with a short russet gold coat; light, lean build
general.quote: Medium sized, elegant gun dog of noble appearance with short russet gold coat.
general.notes: FCI standard (S327). RKC (S328): 'Elegant and moderately boned, the Vizsla has a nobility in its head and carriage.'

colours.quote: Various shades of russet gold and dark sandy gold (semmelgelb).
colours.notes: FCI standard (S327): 'The leathers may be a little darker, otherwise uniform in colour.'; 'Red, brownish or lightened colour is undesirable.'; disqualifying 'Dark brown or pale yellow colour.' and parti-colour; a white chest patch up to 5 cm and white toes are allowed (paraphrase). AKC standard (S331): 'Golden rust in varying shades.' Never brown, pale yellow, white patches or parti-colour in the game.

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). Russet gold first with the highest weight (portrait default — named first by the FCI, the RKC 'russet gold gundog'), then dark sandy gold.

coat.value: short, dense, coarse and hard to the touch; no undercoat
coat.quote: Short and dense, should be coarse and hard at the touch.
coat.notes: FCI (S327); thinner and silkier on head and ears, no undercoat (paraphrase). RKC (S328): 'Coat length: Short'.

nose.value: broad, well-developed nose, dark in harmony with the coat (self-coloured)
nose.quote: Well developed and broad with nostrils as wide as possible.
nose.notes: FCI (S327): nose colour dark, in harmony with the coat (paraphrase). AKC (S331): 'Nose self-colored. Any other color is faulty.' — never a black nose.

ears.value: medium-set, hanging close to the cheeks, rounded V tip
ears.quote: Leathers set on at medium height, a little backwards.
ears.notes: FCI (S327): hang close to the cheeks, rounded V shape, about three quarters of the head length (paraphrase).

eyes.value: slightly oval, medium size, brown in harmony with the coat (darker preferred)
eyes.quote: Slightly oval, of medium size.
eyes.notes: FCI (S327) (paraphrase for the colour). AKC (S331): yellow eyes are faulty.

tail.value: set slightly low, strong at the base, tapering; natural tail reaches the hock
tail.quote: Set on slightly low, strong at the base, then tapering.
tail.notes: FCI (S327): where docking is prohibited the tail reaches the hock and is carried straight or slightly sabre-like (paraphrase); the AKC standard (S331) describes docking — the game shows the natural tail (German Shorthaired Pointer / Brittany precedent).

suitability._note: Source = RKC breed-page key facts (S328, older address), PDSA (S329), PetMD (S330), AKC article (S332), Dogs Trust Ireland (S333). The RKC page shows no 'Good with children' field.

rkc_exercise.quote: Exercise: More than 2 hours per day
rkc_exercise.notes: Basis of 120 min (PDSA S329 'a minimum of two hours' agrees) and of active_family / long_daily_exercise.

pdsa_exercise.value: a minimum of two hours every day
pdsa_exercise.quote: Your Hungarian Vizsla will need a minimum of two hours exercise every day.
pdsa_exercise.notes: PDSA (S329). Supports active_family / long_daily_exercise.

rkc_size_of_home.notes: Basis of large_home (with the garden). Not apartment.

rkc_grooming.notes: Runbook dog-grooming rule: 'Once a week' → 1 (PDSA S329 'a weekly brush', PetMD S330 'at least once a week' agree). No frequent_grooming.

pdsa_grooming.value: a weekly brush
pdsa_grooming.quote: Thanks to their short fur, a weekly brush should be enough to keep their coat looking nice and shiny.
pdsa_grooming.notes: PDSA (S329); 'Vizslas are really low maintenance when it comes to grooming.' Agrees with the RKC → 1.

petmd_grooming.value: brushing at least once a week
petmd_grooming.quote: A slicker brush and a pin brush are both good choices for brushing a Vizsla and should be used at least once a week.
petmd_grooming.notes: PetMD (S330). Agrees → 1.

rkc_shedding.notes: Basis of the sheds tag (with Dogs Trust Ireland S333 'Hungarian Vizslas shed moderately.'). Never low_shedding.

rkc_breed_watch.quote: Currently no points of concern specific to this breed have been identified for special attention by judges,
rkc_breed_watch.notes: RKC breed page (S328) 'Category 1' → no welfare chip; in marketing.

rkc_good_with_children.notes: The RKC breed page (S328) has no 'Good with children' field.

petmd_family.value: ideal family pets for households with children
petmd_family.quote: These tall, long-eared beauties are extremely loyal and friendly, making them ideal family pets for households with children.

pdsa_children.value: not recommended with very young children; great with older children
pdsa_children.quote: We wouldn't recommend a Vizsla if you have very young children
pdsa_children.notes: PDSA (S329); 'Because of their playful nature, they get along really well with older children they can play with.' Basis of not_for_small_children (with PetMD).

petmd_small_children.quote: But for small children under the age of 6, [a Vizsla's] excitement can be too much.

pdsa_experienced_owner.quote: Their energy levels and strong personality means they are not suitable for first time dog owners.

pdsa_company.quote: Ideally, your Vizsla will need someone around all day to keep them company.

pdsa_prey_drive.value: high prey drive — not with smaller pets
pdsa_prey_drive.quote: Hungarian Vizslas do have a high prey drive, so we wouldn't advise keeping them with smaller pets.

akc_nails.quote: However, their fast-growing nails need to be trimmed regularly.
akc_nails.notes: AKC article (S332); 'When it comes to grooming, an occasional bath will keep their short coat looking great.' Nail care = sourced need without a mechanic → ROADMAP M5-R19 (needs-david).

petmd_ears.value: prone to ear infections — keep a close eye on ear hygiene
petmd_ears.quote: Vizslas are prone to ear infections, so it's important to keep a close eye on your pet's ear hygiene...
petmd_ears.notes: PetMD (S330), no frequency. Ear care = sourced need without a mechanic → ROADMAP M5-R20 (needs-david).

petmd_teeth.quote: To minimize the risk of periodontal disease, brush your dog's teeth regularly using a dog-specific toothbrush and toothpaste.
petmd_teeth.notes: PetMD (S330), no frequency. Dental care = sourced need without a mechanic → ROADMAP M5-R15 (needs-david).

english_cocker_spaniel._note: Added 2026-10-15 (M5-R10-41, unattended run — appended after the Hungarian Vizsla: AKC 2024 No. 36 'English Cocker Spaniel', S174 full-list table '35 Vizsla', '36 English Cocker Spaniel', '37 Maltese'). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-15 (the tool limits quotes to ~125 characters; '…' marks where the tool shortened a sentence); spot-check before import (sources.md S335–S344, reused S8, S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45, S174). The English Cocker Spaniel (FCI 5) — not the American Cocker Spaniel (FCI 167, AKC 'Cocker Spaniel'); the RKC and PDSA call it 'Cocker Spaniel' / 'Spaniel (Cocker)'. The FCI standard (S336) was read in French (the English PDF was refused by the fetch tool) — tool summary, French quotes only where returned. Lifespan: McMillan 2024 / Dogs Trust table (S123) not reachable → VetCompass breed paper (Engdahl et al. 2023, S342): median age at death 11.44 years → senior 103 months (Beagle precedent, S116). RKC Breed Watch Category 1 → no welfare chip; in marketing.

identity.value: FCI No. 5, Group 8 Section 2 (Flushing Dogs), Great Britain
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S335): group 'n°8 - Retrievers - Flushing Dogs - Water Dogs', section 'Flushing Dogs', country 'GREAT BRITAIN'; definitive acceptance 4/10/1963; valid standard published 9/8/2026; 'Subject to a working trial according to the FCI Breeds Nomenclature'. Names: RKC (S337, S338) 'Spaniel (Cocker)'; PDSA (S339) 'Cocker Spaniel'; AKC (S343) 'English Cocker Spaniel'. Not the American Cocker Spaniel (FCI No. 167, AKC 'Cocker Spaniel').

size_class.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S337, S338). PDSA (S339) 'Medium'. PDSA 13–14.5 kg = 29–32 lb → the 'Medium (24–59 pounds)' class of S10 for growth (American Cocker Spaniel precedent: RKC 'Small' kept as the size class). RKC group: Gundog.

fci.notes: FCI standard (S336, French, tool summary — no verbatim quote returned): height at the withers about 39–41 cm for males, 38–39 cm for females (paraphrase).

akc.quote: Height at withers: males 16 to 17 inches; females 15 to 16 inches. Deviations to be penalized.
akc.notes: AKC standard (S343, as printed in the AKC study guide). Inches × 2.54 by us. Alternative only.

pdsa.notes: PDSA key fact 'Average height' (S339), one range for both sexes. Alternative only.
PDSA breed page (S339) key fact 'Average weight', one range for both sexes. The game range (adult_weight_kg). The FCI standard (S336) gives about 13–14.5 kg too (tool summary, paraphrase).

akc.quote: The most desirable weights: males, 28 to 34 pounds; females, 26 to 32 pounds.
akc.notes: AKC standard (S343). Pounds × 0.4536 by us. Alternative only.

vetcompass.quote: Males (16.14, IQR 14.25–18.35, range 6.80–34.13) were heavier than females (13.80, IQR 12.21–15.76, range 6.50–30.22)
vetcompass.notes: Engdahl et al. 2023 (S342): median adult bodyweight of UK pet English Cocker Spaniels (all 15.05 kg) — measured pets, research only; not the game range.

salt_category.notes: Category assignment by weight is ours (general_by_size.size_classes.salt_2017_bands_kg, S8): 13–14.5 kg → III (6.5–<15). Salt 2017 breed list not checked.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. PDSA 13–14.5 kg (S339) = 29–32 lb → 'Medium (24–59 pounds)'. The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 60 min is reached at 6 months).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no English Cocker Spaniel growth curve found.

median_uk.quote: The median age at death was 11.44 years (IQR 9.46–13.47)
median_uk.notes: Engdahl et al. 2023 (S342), VetCompass UK, abstract. Females 'median longevity 12.01 years, IQR 10.25–14.06' (n = 59), males '11.00 years, IQR 9.02–13.91' (n = 57), P = 0.052 (results, S342). RVC news (S344): 'The average lifespan of English Cocker Spaniels overall was 11.44 years.' McMillan 2024 (S54) and the Dogs Trust table (S123) not reachable — runbook rule: else a VetCompass median (Beagle precedent, S116). Medium until McMillan 2024 is checked.

rkc.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S337, S338). PDSA (S339) 'Over 10 years' agrees. Generic band; not the basis (a VetCompass median exists). Not shorter_lifespan.

vca.notes: VCA quick facts (S341). Alternative only (lower bound 12 y → 108 months).

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × 11.44 y (S342) → 0.75 × 11.44 = 8.58 y = 102.96 → 103 months. With the RKC lower bound 'Over 10 years' (S337): 90 months; VCA 12 y (S341): 108; Dogs Trust rule of thumb > 7 y = 84 months (S14).

adult.quote: Exercise: Up to 1 hour per day
adult.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S337, S338). PDSA (S339): 'Your Cocker Spaniel will need a minimum of an hour exercise every day.' — the same number (60). Rule: RKC value preferred, 'up to N' → N = 60. PDSA: dogs from working lines will probably need more time to run around (paraphrase of a shortened sentence).

energy.value: daily exercise for physical and mental health
energy.quote: English Cocker Spaniels need daily exercise to maintain both physical and mental health.
energy.notes: VCA (S341); PetMD (S340): 'daily exercise is important to maintain their physical and mental health.' Not needs_mental_stimulation — about exercise (German Shorthaired Pointer precedent).

working_lines.value: working-line dogs probably need more running time
working_lines.quote: You may find that if your dog comes from parents bred to work, they’ll probably need more time to run around…
working_lines.notes: PDSA (S339), shortened by the tool. Background only — the game uses the RKC value.

after_meals.value: leave a gap after eating and before exercising
after_meals.quote: Remember to leave at a gap after eating and before exercising.
after_meals.notes: PDSA (S339) (source wording 'at a' as returned). No length in the source → meal_exercise_gap 60 (David's M5-R16 decision; Dobermann / Shih Tzu precedent).

temperament.value: merry and affectionate, of equable disposition, neither sluggish nor hyperactive
temperament.quote: The English Cocker is merry and affectionate, of equable disposition, neither sluggish nor hyperactive,
temperament.notes: AKC standard (S343): '… a willing worker and a faithful and engaging companion.' RKC (S337): 'The Cocker Spaniel earns the epithet 'the merry cocker' for his ever-wagging tail denoting his happy temperament.' FCI (S336): « Naturel gai ; avec sa queue qui remue constamment ».

family.value: hugely popular family pet; a wonderful family dog for people of all ages
family.quote: It remains hugely popular as a family pet.
family.notes: RKC breed page (S337). PetMD (S340): 'a wonderful family dog that does well with people of all ages.' → family_pet.

children.value: tends to get along well with children (patient); always supervise
children.quote: Due to their patient personalities, Cocker Spaniels tend to get along well with children…
children.notes: PDSA (S339), shortened by the tool; 'Always supervise your Cocker Spaniel with children and vulnerable adults to avoid any accidents.' VCA (S341): 'Generally good with children'. → children (supervision caveat kept here); no small_children (no explicit rating without a supervision caveat).

aggression_vetcompass.value: VetCompass lists aggression among the most commonly recorded disorders of UK English Cocker Spaniels ('potentially moody')
aggression_vetcompass.quote: English Cocker Spaniels: a fairly typical, but potentially moody, dog?
aggression_vetcompass.notes: RVC VetCompass news headline (S344), summarising Engdahl et al. 2023 (S342); aggression is named among the most recorded disorders (figure not copied — no statistics in the app). No vocabulary key covers it and the standards describe the breed as 'merry and affectionate' (S343) → no chip; the `children` chip (PDSA S339 / VCA S341) keeps the PDSA supervision caveat. Claude's reading, open for David (German Shepherd precedent: a VetCompass behaviour finding recorded, not a chip).

socialisation.value: socialise from a young age with a variety of people, dogs and experiences
socialisation.quote: Socialising your Cocker Spaniel from a young age with a variety of people, dogs and experiences will help them develop
socialisation.notes: PDSA (S339) (sentence shortened by the tool; continues '… into confident adults' — paraphrase). PetMD (S340): 'Early training and socialization are very helpful in addressing any unwanted behaviors.' VCA (S341): 'Early socialization is key to ensure confidence.' → proposed_game_parameters.english_cocker_spaniel.socialisation (DOG_SOCIALISATION row, M5-R17).

time_alone.value: known for separation anxiety — never alone for more than four hours; best with someone around in the day
time_alone.quote: Cocker Spaniels are known for suffering with separation anxiety, so it’s best to have someone with them during the day.
time_alone.notes: PDSA (S339); 'It’s important that your Cocker is never left alone for more than four hours, but even this may…' (shortened by the tool). VCA (S341) time alone: 'Limited tolerance; prefers engagement'. → needs_company.

other_pets.value: easygoing and friendly with other animals; no high prey drive (cat possible under the right circumstances)
other_pets.quote: This breed tends to have an easygoing and friendly attitude with people and other animals.
other_pets.notes: PetMD (S340). PDSA (S339): 'They don’t have a high prey drive so may be able to be introduced to a cat under the right circumstances.' VCA (S341) other pets: 'Typically social with proper introduction'. → other_pets (no conflict; PDSA hedges with a cat). No chases_small_pets (no high prey drive).

chewing.value: without enough stimulation and company, entertains itself by nibbling and chewing furniture and belongings
chewing.quote: Without the right amount of stimulation and company, your Cocker Spaniel will likely try to entertain themselves –
chewing.notes: PDSA (S339); the same sentence continues '… which might involve some of your furniture and belongings falling victim to nibbling and chewing.' → chews_when_bored.

food_motivation.value: easily motivated by food; pet (non-sporting) dogs are often overweight
food_motivation.quote: often easily motivated by rewards of food and praise
food_motivation.notes: PetMD (S340) (fragment as returned); 'English Cocker Spaniels that are not used as sporting dogs are often overweight' (fragment as returned) and 'vital to maintain proper body conditioning and weight by avoiding overfeeding'. VetCompass (S344): obesity/overweight among the most common disorders (figure not copied). → food_motivated_weight.

obesity_tendency.quote: that are not used as sporting dogs are often overweight.
obesity_tendency.notes: PetMD (S340) fragment as returned. Supports food_motivated_weight.

training_notes.value: intelligent, willing to learn; positive, reward-based training from an early age
training_notes.quote: They’re intelligent dogs with a real willingness to learn, so starting positive, reward-based training…
training_notes.notes: PDSA (S339), shortened by the tool; 'Remember they pick up bad habits just as quickly as good' (fragment). PetMD (S340): 'This makes them a fun and easy breed to train'. Fits the Excellent learning tier (Coren rank 18).

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages anywhere (the prevalence figures of the VetCompass news S344 are not copied). RKC Breed Watch Category 1 (S337: 'Currently no points of concern specific to this breed have been identified for special attention by judges') → no welfare chip. RKC breed health priorities (S337): 'Immune mediated haemolytic anaemia (IMHA)', 'Pancreatitis', 'Thyroid conditions'.

hip_dysplasia.value: hip dysplasia — hip screening of the parents (BVA/KC scheme)
hip_dysplasia.notes: PDSA (S339) health list: the hip joint does not fit together properly, leading to arthritis; breeding dogs X-rayed through the BVA/Kennel Club scheme (paraphrase). RKC (S337) minimum test 'Hip testing (for hip dysplasia) using the BVA/KC Hip Dysplasia Scheme'. PetMD (S340) lists hip dysplasia.

atopy_skin.value: atopy (allergic itchy skin and ear infections); skin infections
atopy_skin.notes: PDSA (S339) health list (paraphrase); PetMD (S340) 'Skin Infections'. Not a Breed Watch point → no sensitive_skin chip (Breed Watch Category 1). Background only.

ear_infections.value: ear problems / ear infections (otitis externa) — routine ear cleaning
ear_infections.quote: Routine cleaning with a veterinary-approved ear cleaner is vital in maintaining healthy ear canals.
ear_infections.notes: PetMD (S340) 'Ear Infections (Otitis)'; PDSA (S339) 'Ear problems'; VetCompass (S344) otitis externa among the most common disorders (figure not copied). Ear care = sourced need without a mechanic → ROADMAP M5-R20 (needs-david).

prcd_pra.quote: DNA test for Progressive retinal atrophy (prcd-PRA)
prcd_pra.notes: RKC minimum test (S337); PetMD (S340) 'Progressive Retinal Atrophy'. Background only.

familial_nephropathy.value: familial nephropathy (inherited kidney disease) — DNA test
familial_nephropathy.notes: RKC best-practice test (S337); PDSA (S339) and PetMD (S340) list it. Background only.

adult_onset_neuropathy.notes: RKC best-practice test (S337); PDSA (S339), PetMD (S340) list it. Background only.

acral_mutilation.quote: DNA test for Acral mutilation syndrome (AMS)
acral_mutilation.notes: RKC minimum test (S337); PDSA (S339) lists it. Background only.

imha.notes: RKC breed health priority (S337); PDSA (S339) 'Auto-immune conditions' (paraphrase). Background only.

pancreatitis.notes: RKC breed health priority (S337). Background only.

thyroid.notes: RKC breed health priority (S337). Background only.

periodontal.notes: VetCompass news (S344) / Engdahl 2023 (S342): the most commonly recorded specific disorder (figure not copied, paraphrase). No tooth-care advice in an A/B breed source → no dental_care need recorded (Claude's reading, open for David).

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table (S35, tier C, read 2026-10-15): rank 18 'Flat-Coated Retriever', 'English Cocker Spaniel', 'Standard Schnauzer' (shared rank) under 'Excellent Working Dogs' (ranks 11–26); rank 20 'Cocker Spaniel' is the American breed. Not in Coren's own top / bottom-10 article (S34) — runbook: rank from S35. Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

coren_tier.value: excellent: 5 to 15 repetitions, obeys first command 85% or better
coren_tier.quote: Understanding of new commands: 5 to 15 repetitions.; Obey first command: 85% of the time or better.;
coren_tier.notes: Tier 'Excellent Working Dogs' = ranks 11–26 (S35). Tier definitions from Wikipedia; verify in book.

training_notes.value: intelligent, willing to learn; reward-based training
training_notes.quote: They’re intelligent dogs with a real willingness to learn, so starting positive, reward-based training…
training_notes.notes: PDSA (S339); PetMD (S340) 'a fun and easy breed to train'.

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value — see proposed_game_parameters.english_cocker_spaniel.learning_multiplier (1.5, runbook rule: Excellent tier, rank 18).

general.value: merry, sturdy, sporting dog; well balanced and compact
general.quote: Chien de chasse gai et vigoureux, harmonieux et compact.
general.notes: FCI standard (S336, French). AKC (S343): 'merry and affectionate'.

colours.quote: Solid colors are black, liver or shades of red.
colours.notes: AKC standard (S343): 'Various. Parti-colors are either clearly marked, ticked or roaned,' 'the white appearing in combination with black, liver or shades of red.' FCI (S336, tool summary): self colours black, red, golden ('fauve'), liver (chocolate), with or without tan; bicolours, tricolours and roans; « Il n’y a pas de blanc admis, à l’exception d’une petite tache sur la poitrine. » (self colours). 'golden' = the golden / red self colour; blue roan = black roan with white; orange roan = red roan with white. Never merle, never a white self colour with patches.

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). Golden first with the highest weight (portrait default — a typical self colour, distinct from the American Cocker's buff portrait), then black, liver, black and tan, blue roan, orange roan, black and white, tricolour.

coat.value: flat, silky texture, never wiry or wavy, not too profuse, never curly; well-feathered forelegs, body and hind legs above the hocks
coat.quote: Plat. Texture soyeuse, jamais « fil de fer » ni ondulé, pas trop abondant et jamais bouclé.
coat.notes: FCI (S336, French). RKC 'Coat length: Medium' (S337). The portrait shows a moderate pet-length coat.

nose.value: nose wide enough for good scenting; square muzzle, distinct stop (not short-faced)
nose.quote: Suffisamment large pour permettre la finesse du flair.
nose.notes: FCI (S336, French). Not a short-faced breed.

ears.value: lobular, set low on a level with the eyes, long silky feathering
ears.quote: Les oreilles sont en forme de lobe, attachées bas, au niveau des yeux.
ears.notes: FCI (S336, French): long silky fringes (paraphrase).

eyes.value: brown or dark brown, never light; dark hazel in livers
eyes.quote: Ils sont bruns ou brun foncé. Ils ne sont jamais clairs.
eyes.notes: FCI (S336, French); dark hazel in liver colours (paraphrase).

tail.value: natural (undocked) tail in the game portrait: slightly curved, of moderate length, carried level, never cocked up
tail.quote: Elle doit frétiller en action. Elle est portée horizontalement et jamais relevée.
tail.notes: FCI (S336): undocked it is slightly curved, of moderate length, generally not below the hock (paraphrase). The AKC standard (S343) says 'Docked.' — the game shows the natural tail (American Cocker Spaniel / German Shorthaired Pointer precedent; docking of pet dogs is banned in Slovenia and the UK). Claude's proposal, open for David.

suitability._note: Source = RKC breed page (S337, older address) and Breeds A–Z (S338), PDSA (S339), PetMD (S340), VCA (S341). The RKC page shows no 'Good with children' field.

rkc_exercise.quote: Exercise: Up to 1 hour per day
rkc_exercise.notes: Basis of 60 min (PDSA S339 'a minimum of an hour' agrees). Not long_daily_exercise / active_family.

pdsa_exercise.value: a minimum of an hour every day
pdsa_exercise.quote: Your Cocker Spaniel will need a minimum of an hour exercise every day.
pdsa_exercise.notes: PDSA (S339). Agrees with 60.

rkc_size_of_home.notes: Not apartment (needs 'Flat/ Apartment'), not large_home.

rkc_size_of_garden.quote: Size of garden: Small/ medium garden

rkc_grooming.notes: Runbook dog-grooming rule: 'Every day' → 7 (PDSA S339 'a daily brush' agrees). Basis of frequent_grooming (with PDSA).

pdsa_grooming.value: a daily brush
pdsa_grooming.quote: They need a daily brush to stay on top of dead hair and stop their fur from tangling.
pdsa_grooming.notes: PDSA (S339); a quick brush after walks (paraphrase). Agrees with the RKC → 7. Supports frequent_grooming.

petmd_grooming.value: frequent and regular brushing (fairly high-maintenance coat)
petmd_grooming.quote: Frequent and regular brushing is required to maintain an English Cocker Spaniel's fairly high-maintenance hair coat.
petmd_grooming.notes: PetMD (S340); no number. Agrees.

pdsa_professional_grooming.value: professional groomer every three months for clipping (show type; working types less often)
pdsa_professional_grooming.quote: You may need to take them to a professional groomer every three months to get them clipped
pdsa_professional_grooming.notes: PDSA (S339); the sentence continues for 'show' varieties (paraphrase); '‘Working’ varieties tend to require less coat maintenance so grooming visits will be less frequent.' Groomer / clipping = sourced need without a mechanic → ROADMAP M5-R18 (needs-david).

rkc_shedding.notes: Basis of the sheds tag (with PetMD S340 year-round shedding). Never low_shedding.

petmd_shedding.quote: manage shedding, which occurs year-round for this breed.
petmd_shedding.notes: PetMD (S340) fragment as returned. Supports sheds.

rkc_breed_watch.quote: Currently no points of concern specific to this breed have been identified for special attention by judges
rkc_breed_watch.notes: RKC breed page (S337) 'Category 1' (S338 the same) → no welfare chip; in marketing.

rkc_good_with_children.notes: The RKC breed page (S337) has no 'Good with children' field.

petmd_family.value: a wonderful family dog for people of all ages
petmd_family.quote: a wonderful family dog that does well with people of all ages.
petmd_family.notes: PetMD (S340) fragment as returned. Supports family_pet.

pdsa_children.value: tends to get along well with children; supervise
pdsa_children.quote: Due to their patient personalities, Cocker Spaniels tend to get along well with children…
pdsa_children.notes: PDSA (S339). Basis of children (with VCA).

pdsa_company.value: never alone for more than four hours; someone with them during the day
pdsa_company.quote: It’s important that your Cocker is never left alone for more than four hours, but even this may…
pdsa_company.notes: PDSA (S339), shortened by the tool. Basis of needs_company (with behaviour.time_alone).

petmd_other_animals.value: friendly with people and other animals
petmd_other_animals.quote: This breed tends to have an easygoing and friendly attitude with people and other animals.

vca_other_pets.notes: VCA quick facts 'other pets' (S341). Supports other_pets.

vca_nails.notes: VCA (S341). Nail care = sourced need without a mechanic → ROADMAP M5-R19 (needs-david).

vca_ears.value: routine bathing and ear cleaning to prevent infection
vca_ears.quote: Careful attention to skin and ear health with routine bathing and ear cleaning can help prevent infection.
vca_ears.notes: VCA (S341); PetMD (S340) routine ear cleaning. Ear care = sourced need without a mechanic → ROADMAP M5-R20 (needs-david).

petmd_ears.value: routine ear cleaning with a vet-approved cleaner
petmd_ears.quote: Routine cleaning with a veterinary-approved ear cleaner is vital in maintaining healthy ear canals.

maltese._note: Added 2026-10-18 (M5-R10-42, unattended run — appended after the English Cocker Spaniel: AKC 2024 No. 37 'Maltese', S174 full-list table '36 English Cocker Spaniel', '37 Maltese', '38 Pug'). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-18 (fragments marked as such); paraphrase only in notes. Sources S345–S352. No health percentages anywhere.

identity.value: FCI No. 65, Group 9 Section 1 (Bichons and related breeds), Italy
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S345): group 'n°9 - Chiens d'agrément et de compagnie', section 'Bichons et apparentés', country of origin 'BASSIN MEDITERRANEEN CENTRAL', country of patronage 'ITALIE' (the register shows the patronage country, Italy); no working trial; definitive acceptance '13/04/1955'. FCI standard (S346) dated 13.11.2015, valid from 01/01/2016.

size_class.notes: RKC Breeds A–Z key facts (S347) 'Size: Small'; PDSA (S348) 'Small'; RKC Toy group. 3–4 kg (FCI S346, PDSA S348) = 6.6–8.8 lb → the 'Toy (5–12 pounds)' class of S10 for growth.

fci.quote: Height at the withers: Males from 21–25 cm.
fci.notes: FCI standard (S346): 'Females from 20–23 cm.'

pdsa.notes: PDSA key fact 'Average height' (S348), one value for both sexes. Alternative only.

akc.notes: AKC standard (S349) gives no height, only weight ('Weight under 7 pounds, with from 4 to 6 pounds preferred.'). PetMD (S351): 'Maltese dogs weigh under 7 pounds and stand 7–9 inches tall.' (background).

fci.quote: Weight: 3–4 kg.
fci.notes: FCI standard (S346), one range for both sexes (stored per sex). PDSA (S348) 'Average weight' '3kg-4kg' agrees. The game range (adult_weight_kg).

pdsa.notes: PDSA key fact 'Average weight' (S348). Agrees with the FCI.

akc.quote: Weight under 7 pounds, with from 4 to 6 pounds preferred.
akc.notes: AKC standard (S349): 4–6 lb preferred = 1.8–2.7 kg (pounds × 0.4536 by us); under 7 lb = 3.2 kg. Lighter than the FCI / PDSA range; alternative only.

salt_category.notes: Category assignment by weight is ours (general_by_size.size_classes.salt_2017_bands_kg, S8): 3–4 kg = the smallest band. Salt 2017 breed list not checked.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. 3–4 kg = 6.6–8.8 lb → 'Toy (5–12 pounds)'. The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 30 min is reached at 3 months).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Maltese growth curve found.

rkc.notes: RKC Breeds A–Z key facts (S347). PDSA (S348) 'Over 12 years' agrees. The basis of the senior boundary (runbook: RKC lower bound when no McMillan 2024 / VetCompass value is reachable). Not shorter_lifespan.

pdsa.notes: PDSA key fact 'Average lifespan' (S348). Same lower bound as the RKC → same senior boundary (108).

petmd.quote: The typical Maltese lifespan is 12–15 years.
petmd.notes: PetMD (S351, tier B). Alternative only (lower bound 12 y → 108 months, the same).

mcmillan_2024.quote: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.1 years for the breed
mcmillan_2024.notes: McMillan et al. 2024 as quoted by Wikipedia (S352, tier C — never alone). The Dogs Trust breed table (S123) and the paper were not reachable on 2026-10-18 (fetch tool provenance refusal) → not used as the basis; with it the senior boundary would be round(0.75 × 13.1 × 12) = round(117.9) = 118 months. Verify in S123 before replacing the RKC lower bound. Wikipedia also quotes an Italian 2024 study (Roccaro et al.) at 11 years — background only.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × 12 y (RKC lower bound 'Over 12 years', S347) → 0.75 × 12 = 9 y = 108 months. With McMillan 2024 13.1 y (via S352): 118 months; Dogs Trust rule of thumb > 7 y = 84 months (S14). Provisional until McMillan 2024 is checked.

adult.quote: Exercise: Up to 30 minutes per day
adult.notes: RKC Breeds A–Z key facts (S347). PDSA (S348): 'Maltese don’t require much in the way of exercise, with up to half an hour a day usually sufficient.' (key facts: minimum exercise per day '30 minutes') — sources agree on 30.

energy.value: needs daily activity but no vigorous exercise
energy.notes: PetMD (S351) fragment as returned: 'they don’t require vigorous exercise' (paraphrase: daily activity needed). RKC Toy group text (S347): 'They do not need a large amount of exercise and some can be finicky eaters.'

after_meals.notes: No A/B source found on a gap between meals and exercise for this breed → no meal_exercise_gap row.

temperament.value: lively, affectionate, very calm and very intelligent
temperament.quote: BEHAVIOUR/TEMPERAMENT: Lively, affectionate, very calm and very intelligent.
temperament.notes: FCI standard (S346). AKC (S349): 'He is among the gentlest mannered of all little dogs, yet he is lively and playful as well as vigorous.' PDSA (S348): 'Maltese are very bright, friendly and affectionate.'

strangers.value: sweet-natured, can be reserved with strangers
strangers.quote: Known to be sweet-natured, they can be reserved with strangers but given the right socialisation when young,
strangers.notes: PDSA (S348) fragment as returned (the sentence continues: they can learn to be confident and sociable — paraphrase).

family.notes: No explicit family-pet statement in an A/B source (RKC S347 Toy group: friendly personalities, love attention — general). No family_pet chip.

children.value: supervise interactions with young children; rambunctious children may accidentally hurt this tiny dog
children.quote: Interactions between them and young children must be supervised.
children.notes: PetMD (S351); AKC (S350): 'it's important to supervise any interactions between a Maltese and young children' (fragment). PetMD: rambunctious children 'may accidentally hurt this tiny dog' (fragment). A supervision advice — no children chip, no new chip (open for David).

socialisation.value: given the right socialisation when young, can learn to be confident and sociable
socialisation.quote: Known to be sweet-natured, they can be reserved with strangers but given the right socialisation when young,
socialisation.notes: PDSA (S348) fragment as returned. PetMD (S351): 'Socializing and training are also commitments pet parents must make when bringing home a Maltese puppy.' Basis of the puppy socialisation row (M5-R17).

time_alone.value: can develop separation anxiety when left alone for too long
time_alone.quote: This breed can develop separation anxiety when left alone for too long.
time_alone.notes: PetMD (S351). PDSA (S348) does not cover time alone. Basis of needs_company.

other_pets.notes: Not covered by the RKC (S347), PDSA (S348) or PetMD (S351). No other_pets / chases_small_pets chip.

chewing.notes: No breed-specific chewing statement found.

food_motivation.value: some toy dogs can be finicky eaters
food_motivation.quote: They do not need a large amount of exercise and some can be finicky eaters.
food_motivation.notes: RKC Toy GROUP text (S347), not a statement about the Maltese — never promote it to a breed fact or chip. No food_motivated_weight chip; not exported.

training_notes.value: smart; picks up cues quickly with positive reinforcement
training_notes.quote: Maltese are smart dogs that can pick up training cues quickly when positive reinforcement is used.
training_notes.notes: PetMD (S351); PDSA (S348) recommends reward-based techniques (paraphrase).

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages anywhere. RKC Breed Watch Category 1 (S347: 'Currently no points of concern specific to this breed have been identified for special attention by judges') → no welfare chip. PDSA (S348) lists luxating patellas, hydrocephalus, portosystemic shunt, dental problems, heart disease, Chiari malformation with syringomyelia, cataracts and entropion (list items, paraphrase); PetMD (S351) luxating patellas, patent ductus arteriosus, liver shunts and periodontal disease.

patella.notes: PDSA (S348) health list; PetMD (S351) the same (paraphrase). Background only.

liver_shunt.notes: PDSA (S348) 'portosystemic shunt'; PetMD (S351) 'liver shunts' (paraphrase). Background only.

heart.value: heart disease, incl. patent ductus arteriosus
heart.notes: PDSA (S348) heart disease; PetMD (S351) patent ductus arteriosus (paraphrase). Background only.

cm_sm.notes: PDSA (S348) health list (paraphrase). The RKC (S347) lists no CM/SM scheme for the breed. Background only.

eyes.value: cataracts and entropion — eye testing of the parents (BVA/KC/ISDS Eye Scheme)
eyes.notes: PDSA (S348) health list: cataracts and entropion (paraphrase). Parents' eye testing: RKC best-practice 'Eye testing using the BVA/KC/ISDS Eye Scheme' (S347, breeder checklist). Not a Breed Watch point → no eyelid chip.

dental.value: heightened risk of periodontal disease — daily tooth brushing
dental.quote: Maltese dogs are at a heightened risk of periodontal disease.
dental.notes: PetMD (S351); PDSA (S348) lists dental problems. Tooth care advice: see suitability.petmd_teeth (ROADMAP M5-R15).

tear_staining.value: white coat predisposed to tear staining — routine cleaning
tear_staining.quote: Their white coat can predispose the Maltese to tear staining.
tear_staining.notes: PetMD (S351): routine cleaning with a tear stain remover 'will help keep this to a minimum' (fragment). Face / eye care need without a mechanic → ROADMAP M5-R14.

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table of Coren's ranking (S35, read 2026-10-18): rank 59 shared with the Griffon Bruxellois (table cell as returned: '59 | Griffon Bruxellois' / 'Maltese'), tier 'Fair Working/Obedience Intelligence' (ranks 55–69). Coren's own top / bottom-10 article (S34) does not list the breed. Wikipedia 'Maltese dog' (S352) agrees: 'It is ranked 59th of 79 breeds assessed for intelligence by Stanley Coren.' Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

coren_tier.quote: Understanding of new commands: 40 to 80 repetitions.
coren_tier.notes: S35 tier definition as returned: 'Obey first command: 30% of the time or better.'

training_notes.value: smart; positive reinforcement
training_notes.quote: Maltese are smart dogs that can pick up training cues quickly when positive reinforcement is used.
training_notes.notes: PetMD (S351).

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value — see proposed_game_parameters.maltese.learning_multiplier (0.7, runbook rule: Fair tier, rank 59).

general.value: small, longish body, covered from head to foot with a mantle of very long, silky, pure white hair; proud head carriage
general.quote: Of small size, longish body.
general.notes: FCI (S346); AKC (S349): 'The Maltese is a toy dog covered from head to foot with a mantle of long, silky, white hair.'

colours.quote: Colour: Pure white, a pale ivory tinge is permitted.
colours.notes: FCI (S346): 'Traces of pale orange shades are tolerated but not desirable and constitute an imperfection.'; any colour other than white (except pale ivory) and patches of colour are disqualifying (paraphrase). AKC (S349): 'Color, pure white.' 'Light tan or lemon on the ears is permissible, but not desirable.' The game uses pure white only.

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). One colour (pure white) → weight 1; it is the portrait default.

coat.value: single coat without undercoat: dense, shiny, silky, very long and straight, never curly or woolly
coat.quote: Hair: Dense, shiny, glossy - falling heavily and of a silky texture, very long on the whole of the body
coat.notes: FCI (S346) fragment as returned; 'There is no undercoat.' AKC (S349): 'The coat is single, that is, without undercoat.' 'Any suggestion of kinkiness, curliness, or woolly texture is objectionable.' The game draws a natural long coat (pet length allowed; no show wrap, no bows).

nose.value: absolutely black nose; muzzle slightly less than half the head (not short-faced)
nose.quote: The nose is black.
nose.notes: AKC (S349): 'The muzzle is of medium length, fine and tapered but not snipy.' FCI (S346): nose 'absolutely black' (fragment). Not a short-faced breed.

ears.value: almost triangular drop ears, set high, hanging close to the head, heavily feathered

eyes.value: very dark, round, black eye rims
eyes.quote: Eyes are set not too far apart; they are very dark and round, their black rims enhancing the gentle yet alert expression.
eyes.notes: FCI (S346): 'Lively and attentive expression, larger in size than would be expected, the shape tends to be rounded.'

tail.value: long-haired plume carried over the back, tip to the side
tail.quote: A long-haired plume carried gracefully over the back, its tip lying to the side over the quarter.
tail.notes: FCI (S346): a single big curve, the tip between the haunches (fragment 'Forms a single big curve'); a shortened tail is disqualifying (paraphrase).

akc.notes: AKC standard (S358, Pug Dog Club of America copy, approved April 8, 2008, effective June 3, 2008): weight 14 to 18 pounds for dogs or bitches (paraphrase — the tool summarised this section) = 6.4–8.2 kg (pounds × 0.4536 by us). PetMD (S359) 'weigh 14–18 pounds' agrees. Alternative only.

salt_category.notes: Category assignment by weight is ours (general_by_size.size_classes.salt_2017_bands_kg, S8): 6.3–8.1 kg. Salt 2017 breed list not checked.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. FCI 6.3–8.1 kg ≈ 13.9–17.9 lb → 'Small (12–24 pounds)'. The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 60 min is reached at 6 months).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Pug growth curve found.

median_uk.notes: McMillan et al. 2024 corrected Fig. 3 legend (S54, re-read 2026-10-18; the document does not define x̃ — conventionally the median, as read for the French Bulldog and the Bulldog). Wikipedia (S362, tier C) agrees: 'Another UK study found a life expectancy of 11.6 years for the breed compared to an average of 12.7 for purebreeds.' The basis of the senior boundary (runbook: McMillan 2024 first).

rkc.notes: RKC Breeds A–Z key facts (S355) 'Lifespan' / 'Over 10 years'. PDSA (S357) 'Over 10 years' agrees. Not shorter_lifespan.

pdsa.notes: PDSA key fact 'Average lifespan' (S357).

petmd.quote: The average Pug lifespan is 13–15 years.
petmd.notes: PetMD (S359, tier B, US). Alternative only — longer than the UK data (S54).

vetcompass_2016.quote: The median age of the Pugs under veterinary care during 2013 was 3.0 years (IQR: 1.3–5.2 range: 0.0–16.8) years (Fig. 5).
vetcompass_2016.notes: O'Neill et al. 2016 (S361), VetCompass England 2013: a young population (median age 3.0 y); the paper's discussion notes the 'relative excess of younger individuals' (fragment). No median longevity was returned by the tool. Wikipedia (S362) quotes a UK veterinary-records life expectancy of 7.65 years (tier C, a young population) — never used, never exported.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × 11.6 y (McMillan 2024, S54) → 0.75 × 11.6 = 8.7 y = 104.4 → 104 months. Not chosen: 90 (0.75 × RKC lower bound 'Over 10 years', S355), 84 (Dogs Trust > 7 y, S14).

adult.quote: Exercise: Up to 1 hour per day
adult.notes: RKC Breeds A–Z key facts (S355) 'Exercise' / 'Up to 1 hour per day'. PDSA (S357): 'Your Pug will need up to an hour of exercise a day.' (key facts: minimum exercise 'Less than 1 hour'). PetMD (S359): 'Several short walks (about 15–20 minutes each) is a good exercise routine for most Pugs.' — sources agree on up to 1 h.

pdsa.value: up to an hour a day, in several shorter walks
pdsa.quote: Your Pug will need up to an hour of exercise a day.
pdsa.notes: PDSA (S357): 'Several shorter walks throughout the day can help to stop them from becoming too tired or overheated' (fragment as returned).

heat_and_walk_timing.value: avoid exercise in the heat; walk early in the morning or later in the evening
heat_and_walk_timing.quote: You will also need to avoid exercising them in the heat as this can cause even more problems
heat_and_walk_timing.notes: PDSA (S357) fragment as returned; also 'opt to walk them early in the morning or later in the evening when it’s cooler' (fragment). PetMD (S359): 'Avoid strenuous exercise during hot weather.'; 'Pugs do not do very well in overly hot climates or with extreme exercise.' A sourced need without a game mechanic → ROADMAP M5-R14 (Bulldog / Boston Terrier precedent).

energy.value: even-tempered, happy and lively; not suited to high-energy activity

after_meals.notes: No A/B source found on a gap between meals and exercise for this breed → no meal_exercise_gap row. PetMD (S359): 'Pugs do best when fed two or three small meals a day.' (background).

temperament.value: great charm, dignity and intelligence; even-tempered, happy and lively
temperament.quote: Great charm, dignity and intelligence. Even-tempered, happy and lively disposition.
temperament.notes: FCI standard (S354). AKC (S358): even-tempered, stable, playful, charming, dignified, loving and outgoing (paraphrase). PetMD (S359): 'Pugs are friendly and easygoing dogs, and they make excellent dogs for kids.'

family.notes: No explicit family-pet statement in an A/B source (PetMD S359 'excellent dogs for kids' is a children statement). No family_pet chip.

time_alone.notes: PDSA (S357); 'it should never be for longer than four hours' (fragment). PetMD (S359): they 'thrive on attention from their pet parents' (fragment). Basis of needs_company.

chewing.notes: No breed-specific chewing statement found.

food_motivation.value: typically food-motivated; obesity is common for the breed
food_motivation.quote: Pugs are typically food-motivated, which makes them relatively easy to train.
food_motivation.notes: PetMD (S359); 'Diet is an important part of maintaining a Pug's health, especially because obesity is common for the breed.' PDSA (S357): 'Pugs can be prone to gaining weight that can make breathing problems worse' (fragment); 'Treats shouldn’t make up more than 10% of their daily calorie intake' (general advice, background). RKC Breed Watch (S356) 'Too fat'. Basis of food_motivated_weight.

obesity_tendency.value: prone to gaining weight, which makes breathing problems worse
obesity_tendency.quote: Pugs can be prone to gaining weight that can make breathing problems worse

training_notes.notes: PDSA (S357); they 'can also be very strong willed' (fragment). PetMD (S359): food-motivated, 'relatively easy to train' (fragment).

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages anywhere. Severely flat-faced (brachycephalic) breed; RKC Breed Watch Category 3 (S356). PDSA (S357) lists BOAS, eye problems (dry eye, eye infections, corneal ulcers, eye trauma), entropion / ectropion, skin-fold infections, luxating patellas, Pug Dog Encephalitis (PDE), hemivertebrae, elbow and hip dysplasia, Legg-Perthes disease and hypothyroidism (list items, paraphrase); PDSA: 'Our vets would strongly recommend opting for a breed with a normal snout or even a Pug cross-breed instead' and 'we always recommend thinking carefully before you buy or rescue a Pug' (fragments).

brachycephaly_boas.value: severely flat-faced (brachycephalic) breed; at risk of brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome (BOAS) — noisy, laboured breathing, overheating
brachycephaly_boas.quote: they are also a severely brachycephalic (flat-faced) breed
brachycephaly_boas.notes: PDSA (S357) fragment as returned; 'they can easily become out of breath, made worse by their flat faces, causing breathing difficulties' (fragment). RKC breed page (S355): excess soft tissue 'making it difficult for them to breathe normally (causing heavy panting or noisy breathing)' (fragment). PetMD (S359): 'Pugs' skull shape means they breathe with more effort than dogs with a normal-size muzzle.' University of Cambridge (S360): the Respiratory Function Grading Scheme 'assesses dogs for the presence and severity of a breathing problem known as BOAS.' (fragment), 'currently available for the Pug, French Bulldog and Bulldog.' BVA (S236) Figure 1 legend names the Pug among brachycephalic breeds; UK BWG (S93): 'Stop and think before buying a flat-faced dog.'

breed_watch.value: RKC Breed Watch Category 3 — points of concern: respiratory difficulty, excessive skin, protruding eyes, skin-fold dermatitis, pinched nostrils, too fat, eye irritation, unsound movement
breed_watch.quote: Signs of respiratory difficulty or distress (laboured or rapid breathing, excessive respiratory effort, respiratory noise)
breed_watch.notes: RKC Breed Watch page 'Pug - Category 3' (S356); further points as returned: 'Excessive skin on the head or body', 'Protruding eyes', 'Signs of dermatitis irritation in skin folds, and/or hair loss or scarring from previous dermatitis', 'Pinched nostrils', 'Too fat', 'Signs of visible eye irritation or discomfort (including redness, discharge and tear staining)', 'Unsound movement'. RKC breed page (S355) 'Category' / '3'.

skin_folds.value: skin-fold infections — clean and dry the facial folds daily
skin_folds.quote: It's important to clean and dry the skin folds around your Pug's face daily.
skin_folds.notes: PetMD (S359). PDSA (S357): 'Pay close attention to the folds in their skin, as these are the perfect breeding ground' (fragment), keep folds dry (paraphrase). RKC breed page (S355): folds 'can make a warm, moist environment which is perfect for bacteria and yeast to grow.' (fragment). Breed Watch (S356) skin-fold dermatitis. A sourced daily need without a game mechanic → ROADMAP M5-R14 (Bulldog precedent).

eyes.value: eye problems incl. dry eye, corneal ulcers and eye trauma due to shallow eye sockets; protruding eyes a Breed Watch point
eyes.quote: eye trauma due to shallow eye sockets
eyes.notes: PDSA (S357) fragments: 'A range of eye problems including dry eye', 'eye trauma due to shallow eye sockets'; entropion / ectropion in the list (paraphrase). Breed Watch (S356) 'Protruding eyes' and eye irritation. PetMD (S359): 'For day-to-day eye buildup, use a warm, damp washcloth to wipe the area around the eye clean.' No eyelid Breed Watch point → no eyelid_problems chip (Bulldog / French Bulldog precedent; an eye chip is open for David).

hemivertebrae.notes: PDSA (S357) health list (paraphrase). Parents: breed club x-ray checking after 12 months of age (RKC S355, breeder checklist). Paraphrase only → no back_spine chip (Boston Terrier precedent). Background only.

dental.notes: PetMD (S359). Tooth care = sourced need without a mechanic → ROADMAP M5-R15.

rough_collie._note: Added 2026-10-18/19 (M5-R10-44, unattended run — appended after the Pug: AKC 2024 No. 39 'Collie', S174 full-list table '37. Maltese', '38. Pug', '39. Collie'). The AKC 'Collie' covers the Rough and the Smooth variety (AKC standard S367 'Official Standard of the Collie Rough'); FCI (156 Rough / 296 Smooth) and RKC treat them as two breeds — this entry is the Rough Collie, the common variety. Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-18 (fragments marked as such); paraphrase only in notes. Sources S363–S369 (+ S10, S11, S14, S24, S34, S35, S45, S92, S174). No PDSA breed page found for the Rough Collie (searched pdsa.org.uk) → RKC (S365, S366) + PetMD (S368, tier B) for exercise, grooming, family and care needs. Lifespan: RKC lower bound 'Over 12 years' (S365) → senior 108 months, provisional (McMillan 2024 corrected figure S54 names only the Border Collie; the Dogs Trust table S123 was refused by the fetch tool; no VetCompass median found). RKC Breed Watch Category 2 with only the general line 'can be affected by conformational concerns' (S365) and no named point → no welfare chip (Shetland Sheepdog precedent, open for David); not flat-faced → in marketing.

identity.value: FCI No. 156, Group 1 Section 1 (Sheepdogs), Great Britain
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S363): Group 'n°1 - Sheepdogs and Cattledogs (except Swiss Cattledogs)', section 'Sheepdogs', country of origin 'GREAT BRITAIN'; definitive acceptance 4/13/1955; valid standard published 9/8/2026 (FCI standard S364: 08.09.2026); 'Not subject to a working trial according to the FCI breeds nomenclature'. The Smooth Collie is FCI 296 (not this breed).

size_class.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S365). FCI height 56–61 cm dogs / 51–56 cm bitches (S364); AKC 50–75 lb (S367) → the Large class of S10 for males, bitches straddle Medium and Large. RKC group: Pastoral.

fci.notes: FCI standard (S364) 'Size and weight': height at the withers males '56 – 61 cm', females '51 – 56 cm' (quote = the males' value as returned). RKC standard (S366): 'dogs: 56-61 cms (22-24 ins) at shoulder; bitches: 51-56 cms (20-22 ins).' — agrees.

akc.quote: Dogs are from 24 to 26 inches at the shoulder and weigh from 60 to 75 pounds.
akc.notes: AKC standard (S367), inches converted to cm (× 2.54) by us: dogs 24–26 in ≈ 61–66 cm; bitches 22–24 in ≈ 55.9–61 cm ('Bitches are from 22 to 24 inches at the shoulder, weighing from 50 to 65 pounds.'). The American type is taller; the game draws the FCI size.

akc.quote: Dogs are from 24 to 26 inches at the shoulder and weigh from 60 to 75 pounds. Bitches are from 22 to 24 inches at the shoulder, weighing from 50 to 65 pounds.
akc.notes: AKC standard (S367): the two consecutive sentences of the standard (returned separately by the tool, joined here): dogs 60–75 lb, bitches 50–65 lb. Pounds converted to kg (× 0.4536) by us: 60 lb ≈ 27.2 kg, 75 lb ≈ 34.0 kg, 50 lb ≈ 22.7 kg, 65 lb ≈ 29.5 kg. The game range (adult_weight_kg). The FCI standard (S364) and the RKC standard (S366) give no weight (tool summaries: 'The document does not specify weights'; 'The page gives no weight measurements.').

petmd.quote: The Collie is a medium to large breed dog, weighing 50-75 pounds and standing about 2 feet high at the shoulder.
petmd.notes: PetMD (S368), one range for both sexes (stored per sex); 50–75 lb ≈ 22.7–34.0 kg — agrees with the AKC standard.

salt_category.notes: Category assignment by weight is ours (general_by_size.size_classes.salt_2017_bands_kg, S8): about 23–34 kg. Salt 2017 breed list not checked.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. AKC dogs 60–75 lb are 'Large'; bitches 50–65 lb straddle 'Medium (24–59 pounds): 12–15 months' and Large (Golden Retriever precedent). The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 60 min is reached at 6 months).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Rough Collie growth curve found.

rkc.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S365). The basis of the senior boundary (runbook: RKC lower bound when no McMillan 2024 / VetCompass value is reachable). Not shorter_lifespan.

petmd.quote: They typically live 10-14 years with appropriate care.
petmd.notes: PetMD (S368). Lower bound 10 y → 90 months (alternative only; the rule prefers the RKC value).

mcmillan_2024.notes: McMillan et al. 2024: the corrected Fig. 3 legend (S54, re-read 2026-10-18) names only the 'Border Collie (dark blue, x̃=13.1)' among collies; the Dogs Trust breed table (S123) was refused by the fetch tool on 2026-10-18 (provenance). Wikipedia (S369) gives no life expectancy. UNSOURCED — verify in S123 before replacing the RKC lower bound.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × 12 y (RKC lower bound 'Over 12 years', S365) → 0.75 × 12 = 9 y = 108 months. With PetMD's lower bound 10 y (S368): 90 months. Dogs Trust rule of thumb > 7 y = 84 months (S14). Provisional until McMillan 2024 is checked.

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages anywhere. RKC Breed Watch Category 2 (S365): the breed 'can be affected by conformational concerns' — no named point → no welfare chip (open for David). The RKC does not register puppies from merle-to-merle matings born on or after 1 January 2013 (S365, tool summary) — the game never shows a double merle. PetMD (S368) main concerns: Collie eye anomaly, MDR1 mutation, progressive retinal atrophy and dermatomyositis.

eye_conditions.value: Collie eye anomaly and progressive retinal atrophy; eye-tested and DNA-tested parents
eye_conditions.quote: DNA test for Collie eye anomaly/ choroidal hypoplasia (CEA/CH)
eye_conditions.notes: RKC breed page (S365): Good Practice 'Eye testing using the BVA/KC/ISDS Eye Scheme (including litter screening)'; Best Practice DNA tests for CEA/CH and PRA-rcd2 (→ breeder checklist). PetMD (S368) names Collie eye anomaly and progressive retinal atrophy among the main concerns (paraphrase).

mdr1.value: multi-drug resistance (MDR1) — affects how some medicines are processed; DNA test
mdr1.quote: MDR1 (Multi-Drug Resistance) Mutation is a genetic condition that affects the way Collies process certain drugs.
mdr1.notes: PetMD (S368); RKC (S365) Best Practice 'DNA test for Multi-drug resistance (MDR1)'. Important for parents: tell the vet the dog is a Collie.

degenerative_myelopathy.notes: RKC (S365) Best Practice; PetMD (S368) lists it among other risks (paraphrase).

hip_dysplasia.quote: Hip testing (for hip dysplasia) using the BVA/KC Hip Dysplasia Scheme
hip_dysplasia.notes: RKC (S365) Good Practice. Not a Breed Watch point → no hips_hind_legs chip.

dermatomyositis.notes: PetMD (S368) main concerns, tool summary (paraphrase). Not a Breed Watch point → no sensitive_skin chip.

other.value: skin disorders, patent ductus arteriosus, deafness, epilepsy, blood disorders, other eye disorders
other.notes: PetMD (S368) list of other risks, tool summary (paraphrase). Background only.

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table of Coren's ranking (S35, read 2026-10-18): rank 16 'Collie', tier 'Excellent Working Dogs' (ranks 11–26) — the table row as returned by the tool. Not in Coren's own top / bottom-10 article (S34).

coren_tier.quote: Understanding of new commands: 5 to 15 repetitions.
coren_tier.notes: S35 tier definition as returned: 'Obey first command: 85% of the time or better.'

training_notes.notes: PetMD (S368).

general.value: a dog of great beauty, standing with impassive dignity, no part out of proportion to the whole
general.quote: Appears as a dog of great beauty, standing with impassive dignity, with no part out of proportion to whole.

colours.quote: Any other colour or combination of colours unacceptable.
colours.notes: FCI standard (S364): sable 'any shade of light gold to rich mahogany or shaded sable.'; tricolour 'predominantly black with rich tan markings about legs and head.'; blue merle 'predominantly clear, silvery blue, splashed and marbled with black.' RKC standard (S366): 'Sable and white, Tricolour and Blue Merle.'; 'All should carry typical white Collie markings to a greater or lesser degree.'; 'Light straw or cream coloured highly undesirable.' The AKC (S367) also lists 'White' — not an FCI / RKC colour, never drawn. Merle is standard (the RKC registers no merle-to-merle puppies, S365 — the game never draws a mostly white double merle).

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). Sable and white first with the highest weight (portrait default), then tricolour, blue merle.

coat.value: very dense, fits the outline; outer coat straight and harsh, undercoat soft, furry and very close; mane and frill very abundant; face smooth
coat.quote: Fits outline of body, very dense. Outer coat straight and harsh to touch,
coat.notes: FCI (S364); RKC standard (S366): 'undercoat soft, furry and very close almost hiding the skin;' 'mane and frill very abundant, mask and face smooth, ears smooth at tips, but carrying more hair towards base,' 'Hair on tail very profuse.'

ears.value: thrown back in repose; brought forward and semi-erect when alert
ears.quote: In repose carried thrown back, but on alert brought forward and carried semi-erect,
ears.notes: FCI (S364).

eyes.value: medium, set somewhat obliquely, almond-shaped, dark brown (blue or blue-flecked allowed in blue merles)
eyes.quote: Medium size (never very small) set somewhat obliquely, of almond-shape and dark brown colour,
eyes.notes: FCI (S364): 'except in the case of blue merles when eyes are frequently (one or both, or part of one or both) blue or blue-flecked.'

nose.value: flat skull; smooth, well-rounded, blunt muzzle, never square; nose always black
nose.quote: Always black.
nose.notes: FCI (S364): skull 'Flat.'; muzzle 'End of smooth, well rounded muzzle blunt, never square.' A long-headed breed, not short-faced.

tail.value: long, bone reaching at least to the hock; carried low with a slight upward swirl at the tip; hair very profuse
tail.quote: Long with bone reaching at least to hock joint. Carried low when quiet but with slight upward swirl at tip.
tail.notes: FCI (S364); RKC (S366) 'Hair on tail very profuse.'

No PDSA, Woodgreen or Dogs Trust breed page found for the Rough Collie. The RKC page shows no 'Good with children' field (as returned 2026-10-18).

rkc_standard_temperament.quote: A great companion dog, friendly, happy and active, good with children and other dogs.
rkc_standard_temperament.notes: RKC breed standard (S366). Basis of children and other_pets.

petmd_exercise.value: at least an hour of outdoor exercise daily
petmd_exercise.quote: at least an hour of outdoor exercise daily

petmd_grooming.quote: Collies require at least weekly brushing and monthly bathing.
