mastiff._note: Added 2026-10-19 (M5-R10-45, unattended run — appended after the Rough Collie: AKC 2024 No. 40, S174 table row '40 | Mastiff'). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-19 (the PDSA and PetMD pages only in short quotes, 125-character limit); spot-check before import (sources.md S370–S376, reused S10, S11, S14, S35, S45, S54, S174). Names: FCI 'MASTIFF' (S372), the AKC 'Mastiff' (S174, S373), PetMD 'Mastiff (English Mastiff)' (S374); Slovenian »angleški mastif« (not checked against KZS — open for David). FCI standard valid 13.10.2010 (S371); AKC standard 1991 (S373). The RKC (Breeds A–Z page, breed standard, Breed Watch) returned a fetch error on every address → no RKC key facts or health tests; exercise from PDSA (S370, runbook fallback RKC → PDSA). Lifespan: McMillan 2024 median 9.0 y (S54 corrected Fig. 3 legend; S376 results) — not provisional. Welfare: PDSA (S370) 'classed as ‘Category Three’ by The Kennel Club' (visible conformational issues); the Breed Watch points come from the breed club's copy (S375, tier C) next to PDSA. Not named flat-faced by an A/B source.

identity.value: FCI No. 264, Group 2 Section 2.1 (Molossoid breeds, Mastiff type), Great Britain
identity.quote: Section 2.1 Molossoid breeds, Mastiff Type. Without working trial.
identity.notes: FCI standard N° 264 (S371): 'FCI-CLASSIFICATION: Group 2 Pinscher and Schnauzer – Molossoid breeds - Swiss Mountain and Cattle Dogs.'; utilization 'Watch and security dog.'; 'DATE OF PUBLICATION OF THE OFFICIAL VALID STANDARD: 13.10.2010.' FCI nomenclature (S372): 'MASTIFF', '264', country of origin 'GREAT BRITAIN', 'Not subject to a working trial according to the FCI breeds nomenclature', definitive acceptance '11/5/1964'. AKC name: Mastiff (S174, S373); RKC group: Working (address of the unreachable breed page).

size_class.notes: PDSA key facts (S370), as returned. The RKC 'Size:' field (the preferred source) was not reachable on 2026-10-19 — the Great Dane's RKC value is 'Extra large'; by weight (80–85 kg, S370) the PetMD size class is 'Giant (over 100 pounds)' (S10, growth only). Kept at the source's 'Large' (open for David: 'giant' would need the RKC page).

pdsa.notes: PDSA key facts (S370), one range for both sexes (stored per sex). AKC standard (S373) gives minimums only (height.akc_minimum). FCI (S371) gives no figures: 'Size is desirable, but only if combined with quality and if absolute soundness is maintained.'

akc_minimum.quote: Dogs, minimum, 30 inches at the shoulder.
akc_minimum.notes: AKC standard (S373): 'Bitches, minimum, 27½ inches at the shoulder.' 30 in = 76.2 cm → 76; 27.5 in = 69.85 cm → 70 (our conversion). A minimum, not a range.

pdsa.notes: PDSA key facts (S370), one range for both sexes (stored per sex) — the game range. FCI (S371) and AKC (S373) give no weight. PetMD (S374): 'A Mastiff's weight is anywhere between 120 and 230 pounds' (54–104 kg), 'Female Mastiffs typically weigh 120–170 pounds' — alternatives only.

salt_category.notes: Category assignment by weight is ours (general_by_size.size_classes.salt_2017_bands_kg, S8): 80–85 kg = the band '>40 (no curve)'. Salt 2017 breed list not checked.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. PDSA 80–85 kg (S370) = 176–187 lb → 'Giant'. Same 18–24 months as the Great Dane and the Bernese Mountain Dog. The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 60 min is reached at 6 months).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Mastiff growth curve found.

puppy_exercise.value: not over-exercised as puppies while bones and joints develop
puppy_exercise.quote: but shouldn’t be over-exercised as puppies when their bones and joints are still developing.
puppy_exercise.notes: PDSA (S370), the end of the sentence that starts 'As adult dogs, Mastiffs need around an hour of exercise daily'. The game's puppy rule (10 min × age in months, capped) already limits puppy walks — no new mechanic.

median_uk.notes: McMillan et al. 2024, corrected Fig. 3 legend (S54, LJMU Author Correction — the correction changed only the Miniature Dachshund). Published version (S376), results: 'Mastiff (x̃=9.0, HR 2.3, 2.2–2.4)' among the breeds most at risk from early death (research only — never shown as a number or risk in the app). Runbook rule: McMillan 2024 first → not provisional.

pdsa.notes: PDSA key facts (S370). PetMD (S374): 'the average Mastiff lifespan is just 6–10 years.' Basis of shorter_lifespan (an A/B upper bound of 10 years or less).

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × 9.0 y (McMillan 2024, S54) → 0.75 × 9.0 = 6.75 y = 81 months. Dogs Trust rule of thumb > 7 y = 84 months (S14).

adult.quote: Minimum exercise (per day) | 1 hour
adult.notes: PDSA key facts (S370); PDSA text: 'As adult dogs, Mastiffs need around an hour of exercise daily'. RKC breed page (preferred) not reachable on 2026-10-19 → PDSA (runbook rule). PetMD (S374): 'When at home, most Mastiffs enjoy a couch potato lifestyle and tend to not have high energy needs.' — no minutes.

after_meals.value: restrict exercise for an hour before and after meals (GDV / bloat)
after_meals.quote: Restrict exercise for an hour before and after mealtimes
after_meals.notes: PetMD (S374), GDV prevention list ('Mastiffs are deep-chested dogs, which means care must be taken to prevent gastric dilatation and volvulus (GDV) or bloat.'); also 'Feed their Mastiff two to three meals per day, instead of one big meal', slow-feeder bowls, no elevated bowls. PDSA (S370): GDV 'most commonly occurs after they have eaten'. → proposed_game_parameters.mastiff.meal_exercise_gap (built, M5-R16 — the game warns after a meal; the hour before a meal is not modelled).

temperament.value: gentle giants — calm and good-natured; affectionate to owners but capable of guarding; indifferent with strangers
temperament.quote: Mastiffs are gentle giants – calm, good-natured dogs that tend to get on well with everyone.
temperament.notes: FCI (S371): 'A combination of grandeur and courage. Calm, affectionate to owners, but capable of guarding.' / 'Usually indifferent with strangers; timidity is unacceptable.' AKC (S373): 'A combination of grandeur and good nature, courage and docility.' PetMD (S374): protective by heritage, 'loyal to and watchful over their families' (as returned).

family.value: great family dogs for homes with children who know how to interact with pets; best without toddlers or babies (size)
family.quote: Yes, Mastiffs are great family dogs, and their calm nature is suitable for homes with children
family.notes: PetMD (S374), sentence continues 'who understand how to appropriately interact with pets.' and 'However, they may be best suited in homes without toddlers or babies, as their massive size can be dangerous.' → family_pet, children (with that caveat) and not_for_small_children; never small_children.

socialisation.value: early socialisation so they grow up confident and sociable
socialisation.quote: As with all breeds, early socialisation is important to ensure they grow up into confident, sociable dogs.
socialisation.notes: PDSA (S370). PetMD (S374): 'early training and socialization is essential to have a well-mannered Mastiff.' → proposed_game_parameters.mastiff.socialisation (DOG_SOCIALISATION row, M5-R17).

time_alone.notes: No statement found on the PDSA (S370) or PetMD (S374) pages → no needs_company / often_alone tag.

other_pets.value: tend to do well with other pets, especially when introduced as a puppy
other_pets.quote: But overall, Mastiffs are gentle giants and tend to do well with other pets, especially when introduced during puppyhood.
other_pets.notes: PetMD (S374). No prey-drive statement. → other_pets (with the puppyhood caveat, Pomeranian precedent).

chewing.notes: No breed-specific statement found → no chews_when_bored tag.

drooling.quote: But Mastiffs are known to be excessive droolers, and pet parents need to keep a small towel handy for quick cleanups.
drooling.notes: PetMD (S374). Basis of drools (as the Cane Corso and the Great Dane).

food_motivation.notes: No breed-specific statement found → no food_motivated_weight tag. Breed Watch (S375, tier C) 'Significantly overweight' is a judging point, not food motivation. PetMD (S374): two to three meals a day (the game's adult meals are two — no change).

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages are shown anywhere. Conformation welfare topic: PDSA (S370) 'Mastiffs are amongst a group of breeds classed as ‘Category Three’ by The Kennel Club.' — 'visible conditions or conformational issues that can cause pain, discomfort or health issues due to exaggerations'. Breed Watch points (S375, breed club copy, tier C): excessive loose facial skin with eyelid defects, excessive skin / wrinkle, dermatitis in skin folds, significantly overweight, unsound movement, weak hindquarters → eyelid_problems, sensitive_skin, hips_hind_legs (each with a PDSA quote). Not named flat-faced by an A/B source → no brachycephalic chip, and no veterinary advice against advertising the breed type.

breed_watch.value: RKC Breed Watch Category 3 — visible conformational issues (loose facial skin and eyelids, excessive skin and wrinkle, skin-fold dermatitis, weight, movement, hindquarters)
breed_watch.quote: Mastiffs are amongst a group of breeds classed as ‘Category Three’ by The Kennel Club.
breed_watch.notes: PDSA (S370): 'These are breeds of dog that have been highlighted as having visible conditions or conformational issues' / 'that can cause pain, discomfort or health issues due to exaggerations.' Points (S375, tier C): 'Excessive amounts of loose facial skin with conformational defects of the upper and/or lower eyelids', 'Excessive skin on head or body', 'Excessive wrinkle', 'Hair loss or scarring from previous dermatitis', 'Significantly overweight', 'Signs of dermatitis in skin folds', 'Unsound movement', 'Weak hindquarters'. The RKC's own page returned a fetch error.

eyelids.value: eyelids turned in or out (entropion / ectropion) because of excessive skin over the face and eyes; cherry eye
eyelids.quote: Eyelid problems – such as entropion and ectropion – occur in Mastiffs due to excessive skin over the face and eyes.
eyelids.notes: PDSA (S370): 'This skin causes the eyelids to droop either downwards, or in towards the eye,' / 'where the skin rubs and irritates the eye, causing problems.'; also cherry eye. Breed Watch (S375, tier C): 'Excessive amounts of loose facial skin with conformational defects of the upper and/or lower eyelids'. PetMD (S374): ectropion, entropion, cataracts, PRA. Basis of eyelid_problems.

skin.value: atopy (itching, skin trauma) and dermatitis in the facial skin folds — folds wiped daily
skin.quote: Atopy – hypersensitivity to certain allergens, causing itching and skin trauma.
skin.notes: PDSA (S370); grooming: 'their facial wrinkles will need daily cleaning.' Breed Watch (S375, tier C): 'Signs of dermatitis in skin folds', 'Hair loss or scarring from previous dermatitis'. PetMD (S374): seasonal allergies; wipe facial folds daily. Basis of sensitive_skin (as the Westie and the Pug).

hip_elbow_dysplasia.value: hip and elbow dysplasia — joints that don't develop correctly; screening schemes
hip_elbow_dysplasia.quote: Joint disorders – such as elbow dysplasia and hip dysplasia - occur when joints don’t develop correctly
hip_elbow_dysplasia.notes: PDSA (S370): 'and cause degenerative joint disease.' / 'Bone and joint problems can be managed but there are schemes to screen your dog'. Breed Watch (S375, tier C): 'Weak hindquarters', 'Unsound movement'. PetMD (S374): hip dysplasia. Basis of hips_hind_legs.

gdv.value: gastric dilatation volvulus ('bloat') — deep-chested; urgent vet care
gdv.quote: Gastric torsion or Gastric Dilation Volvulus (GDV) – occurs in large, deep chested breeds such as Mastiffs.
gdv.notes: PDSA (S370): 'This most commonly occurs after they have eaten.' PetMD (S374): restrict exercise for an hour before and after meals (exercise.after_meals) → meal_exercise_gap (M5-R16).

heart_dcm.quote: Dilated cardiomyopathy – is a degeneration of the muscles of the heart meaning the heart wall becomes thinner
heart_dcm.notes: PDSA (S370), truncated by the tool. Not a Breed Watch point → no heart chip (research only, Great Dane precedent).

wobbler.quote: Wobbler Syndrome – cervical spondylomyopathy is a deformity or instability of the bones in the neck
wobbler.notes: PDSA health list (S370), truncated by the tool.

back.value: back problems such as degenerative disc disease
back.quote: Back Problems – Mastiffs can suffer from back problems such as degenerative disc disease
back.notes: PDSA health list (S370), truncated by the tool. Not the Dachshund's long-back conformation point → no back_spine chip.

other_conditions.value: hypothyroidism, progressive retinal atrophy (health screen), epilepsy, cancers incl. bone tumours, panosteitis
other_conditions.quote: Cancer – Mastiffs can be more prone to some forms of cancer including bone tumours (Osteosarcoma).
other_conditions.notes: PDSA health list (S370): 'Hypothyroidism – is generally caused by an auto immune thyroiditis causing low circulating levels of thyroid hormone.'; 'Eye disease – there is a health screen for progressive retinal atrophy'; 'Epilepsy – Mastiffs can be more prone to seizures due to epilepsy'; 'Panosteitis – a painful, inflammatory bone disease.' PetMD (S374) also degenerative myelopathy. Research only.

shorter_lifespan.value: a shorter life than most breeds — usually under ten years
shorter_lifespan.notes: PDSA (S370); PetMD (S374) 'the average Mastiff lifespan is just 6–10 years.'; McMillan 2024 median 9.0 y (S54) — research only. Basis of the consider tag shorter_lifespan — a calm chip, no number.

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table of Coren's ranking (S35): rank 72 shared by the Mastiff and the Beagle (as returned '| 72 | Mastiff | Beagle'), tier 'Lowest Degree of Working/Obedience Intelligence' (ranks 70–79). Coren's own article (S34) not re-read. Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

coren_tier.quote: Understanding of new commands: 80 to 100 repetitions or more.
coren_tier.notes: S35 tier 'Lowest Degree of Working/Obedience Intelligence': 'Obey first command: 25% of the time or worse.'

training_notes.quote: Training will require patience, but can be achieved using reward-based techniques.
training_notes.notes: PetMD (S374): 'Mastiffs are eager to please, learn quickly, and respond well to positive reinforcement methods' / 'However, training sessions are best kept short to keep their attention and focus.' The game uses Coren's rank only.

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value — see proposed_game_parameters.mastiff.learning_multiplier (0.5, runbook rule: Lowest tier, rank 72, as the Beagle).

colours.quote: Apricot, fawn or brindle.
colours.notes: FCI (S371) colour as returned; 'Excessive white on body, chest or feet is unacceptable.' AKC (S373): 'Fawn, apricot, or brindle.'; 'Muzzle, ears, and nose must be dark in color, the blacker the better,' / 'with similar color tone around the eye orbits and extending upward between them.'; 'A small patch of white on the chest is permitted.' coat.value: short and close-lying, coarser over neck and shoulders; dense undercoat
coat.quote: Short and close-lying, but coarse over neck and shoulders.
coat.notes: AKC (S373): 'Outer coat straight, coarse, and of moderately short length.' / 'Undercoat dense, short, and close lying.' PDSA (S370): 'Coat length | Short'.

suitability._note: Source = PDSA (S370) and PetMD (S374). shiba_inu._note: Added 2026-10-19 (M5-R10-46, unattended run — appended after the Mastiff: AKC 2024 No. 42, S174 table row '42 | Shiba Inu'; No. 41 West Highland White Terrier is already in the app). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-19 (125-character limit — long sentences only in part); spot-check before import (sources.md S377–S383, reused S10, S11, S14, S35, S45, S174, S376). Names: FCI 'SHIBA' (S377), RKC 'Japanese Shiba Inu' (S378), AKC 'Shiba Inu' (S174, S380); Slovenian »šiba inu« (not checked against KZS — open for David). FCI standard valid 30.10.2016 (S377); AKC standard approved 7 February 1997 (S380). Lifespan: McMillan 2024 median 14.6 y (S376 results) — not provisional. No PDSA or Woodgreen Shiba Inu page found by search → RKC (S378, S379), PetMD (S381), Dogs Trust (S382), AKC (S383). Breed Watch Category 1 (S378) → not a welfare breed.

identity.value: FCI No. 257, Group 5 Section 5 (Asian Spitz and related breeds), Japan
identity.notes: FCI standard N° 257 (S377): section 5 'Asian Spitz and related breeds', without working trial (tool summary); 'ORIGIN: Japan.'; 'DATE OF PUBLICATION OF THE OFFICIAL VALID STANDARD: 30.10.2016.'; utilization 'Hunting dog for birds and small animals.' (and companion dog). RKC (S378) group: Utility; 'The name Shiba Inu translates as 'small dog' and the breed was developed to hunt small game birds.' AKC name: Shiba Inu (S174, S380).

size_class.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S378): the 'Size' field reads 'Small-Medium' (as returned, no colon). Dogs Trust (S382): 'Small'. fci.notes: FCI standard (S377): 'Height at withers: Males 39.5 cm.' / 'Females 36.5 cm.' / 'There is a tolerance of 1,5 cm smaller or taller.' → males 38–41 cm, females 35–38 cm (our arithmetic: ideal ± 1.5 cm). AKC (S380): 'Males 14½ to 16½ inches at withers.' (36.8–41.9 cm) / 'Females 13½ to 15½ inches.' (34.3–39.4 cm) — agrees, alternative only.

akc.quote: Average weight at preferred size is approximately 23 pounds for males, 17 pounds for females.
akc.notes: AKC standard (S380). Pounds converted to kg (× 0.4536) by us: 23 lb ≈ 10.4 kg, 17 lb ≈ 7.7 kg — an approximate average, not a range (register qualifier 'about'). The FCI standard (S377) gives no weight. PetMD (S381): 'Shibas are small and compact dogs, typically weighing 17–23 pounds.' — the same numbers as a range (alternative). Game range (adult_weight_kg): 7.7–10.4 kg (female → male average).

petmd.quote: Shibas are small and compact dogs, typically weighing 17–23 pounds.
petmd.notes: PetMD (S381), one range for both sexes (stored per sex); 17–23 lb ≈ 7.7–10.4 kg (our conversion). The game range.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific: 17–23 lb (S380, S381) = the Small class. The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 60 min is reached at 6 months).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Shiba Inu growth curve found.

median_uk.notes: McMillan et al. 2024, published version (S376), Results — the full list item as returned: 'Shiba Inu (x̃= 14.6, HR 0.5, 0.4–0.6)', among the breeds least at risk from early death ('Those least at risk from early death included'; neighbours Tibetan Spaniel 15.2 and Papillon 14.5). Hazard ratio research only — never shown as a number or risk in the app. Runbook rule: McMillan 2024 first → not provisional.

rkc.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S378). Consistent with the McMillan median. Not shorter_lifespan.

dogs_trust.notes: Dogs Trust breed page key facts (S382), alternative only.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × 14.6 y (McMillan 2024, S376) → 0.75 × 14.6 = 10.95 y = 131.4 → 131 months. With the RKC lower bound 10 y (S378): 90 months. Dogs Trust rule of thumb > 7 y = 84 months (S14).

adult.quote: Exercise: Up to 1 hour per day

rhodesian_ridgeback._note: Added 2026-10-19 (M5-R10-47, unattended run — appended after the Shiba Inu: AKC 2024 No. 43, S174 table row '43 | Rhodesian Ridgeback'; ranks up to 42 are already in the app). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-19 (125-character limit — long sentences only in part); spot-check before import (sources.md S384–S394, reused S8, S10, S11, S14, S35, S45, S174, S263, S376). Names: FCI 'RHODESIAN RIDGEBACK' (S384), RKC and AKC 'Rhodesian Ridgeback' (S386, S389); Slovenian »rodezijski ridgeback« (not checked against KZS — open for David). FCI standard valid 15.05.2025 (S385); RKC standard last updated 1 April 2025 (S388); AKC standard approved April 8, 2025 (S389). Lifespan: no McMillan 2024 median (S376: the name appears only as a tip label in Fig. 5, no x̃) and no VetCompass median found → RKC lower bound 'Over 10 years' (S387) — provisional. No Dogs Trust or Blue Cross page found by search → RKC (S386, S387, S388), PDSA (S390), PetMD (S391), Woodgreen (S392), AKC (S389, S393). Breed Watch Category 1 (S386, S387) → not a welfare breed.

identity.value: FCI No. 146, Group 6 Section 3 (Related breeds), South Africa
identity.notes: FCI standard N° 146 (S385): 'Section 3 Related breeds.' / 'Without working trial.'; 'ORIGIN: Southern Africa'; 'DATE OF PUBLICATION OF THE OFFICIAL VALID STANDARD: 15.05.2025.'; utilization 'The Rhodesian Ridgeback is still used to hunt game in many parts of the world,' 'but is especially prized as watch-dog and family pet.' FCI nomenclature (S384): country of origin 'SOUTH AFRICA', group 'n°6 - Scent hounds and related breeds', definitive acceptance 2/21/1955. The identity country follows the nomenclature (S384) — 'South Africa' must be in FCI_ORIGINS of the export. RKC (S386) group: Hound; 'Lion hunter from Southern Africa, athletic and courageous'. AKC name: Rhodesian Ridgeback (S174, S389).

With McMillan 2024 12 y (via S394, tier C): 108 months; Dogs Trust rule of thumb > 7 y = 84 months (S14). Provisional until McMillan 2024 is checked.

adult.quote: Exercise: More than 2 hours per day
adult.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S387; the Breeds A–Z address S386 returned 'More than 2 hours per day'). PDSA (S390): 'Your Ridgeback will need a minimum of two hours exercise every day.' Woodgreen (S392): '90-120 mins'. PetMD (S391): 'They require regular exercise—at least 45 minutes a day.' AKC article (S393): 'They're strong and athletic, requiring a moderate amount of exercise.'

pdsa.quote: Your Ridgeback will need a minimum of two hours exercise every day.
pdsa.notes: PDSA (S390); key fact 'Minimum exercise (per day)' | '2 hours'. 'This needs to be several long walks with plenty of off-lead exercise in a secure place.'

woodgreen.notes: Woodgreen pet explorer 'Exercise needs' (S392), alternative only.

petmd.quote: They require regular exercise—at least 45 minutes a day.
petmd.notes: PetMD (S391), alternative only.

energy.value: very high energy, well into adult years; needs a lot of hard exercise
energy.quote: Rhodesian Ridgebacks are very high energy dogs which lasts well into their adult years
energy.notes: PDSA (S390); 'They suit active families who are prepared to spend lots of time outdoors with them, rain or shine.' Basis of active_family / long_daily_exercise.

off_lead.value: off lead only in a secure / safely enclosed area (high prey drive)
off_lead.quote: always in a safely enclosed area when off leash
off_lead.notes: AKC article (S393), fragment as returned ('Because of their high prey drive' they need a secure area off leash). PDSA (S390): 'This needs to be several long walks with plenty of off-lead exercise in a secure place.' A sourced need without a game mechanic (the game has no off-lead walks) → open for David (needs a new ROADMAP task, Shiba Inu precedent). Not secure_fencing: no source says the breed escapes from a garden.

temperament.value: dignified, intelligent, aloof with strangers, no aggression or shyness; loyal and loving towards the family
temperament.quote: Dignified, intelligent, aloof with strangers, but showing no aggression or shyness.
temperament.notes: FCI (S385); RKC standard (S388) 'Dignified, intelligent, aloof with strangers but showing no aggression or shyness.'; AKC (S389) 'Dignified and even tempered. Reserved with strangers.'; PDSA (S390) 'Rhodesian Ridgebacks are playful and powerful dogs who are extremely loyal and loving towards their family.'

family.value: family pet (FCI); best with couples or families with older children — risks knocking over smaller children
family.quote: They best suit couples or families with older children who understand how to behave around dogs.
family.notes: PDSA (S390): 'Their large size and boisterous nature when they are younger also means they risk knocking over smaller children.'; 'Always supervise your dog with children and vulnerable adults.' FCI (S385): 'but is especially prized as watch-dog and family pet.' Woodgreen (S392): 'Ridgebacks do best with older children who understand how to interact respectfully with dogs.' AKC article (S393): 'Ridgebacks can be good with children with proper socialization, but they should always be supervised around them.' → family_pet + not_for_small_children; never children or small_children.

experienced_owner.value: powerful, intelligent, wilful dog — not for a first-time owner
experienced_owner.quote: so it’s for this reason we wouldn’t recommend them if you are a first time owner.
experienced_owner.notes: PDSA (S390): 'Rhodesian Ridgebacks are playful and powerful dogs who are extremely loyal and loving towards their family.'; 'They are perfect for experienced owners who are used to training such intelligent dogs'; 'They can be wilful at times and are known to get bored easily if they're not challenged enough'. AKC article (S393): 'Ridgebacks do best in active households with experienced dog owners with plenty of time and attention to offer.'; 'They can be strong willed and prone to independent streaks.' Basis of experienced_owner (the chip's 'powerful dog' = PDSA 'powerful dogs'; Rottweiler / Vizsla precedent).

socialisation.value: socialise from a young age with different people, dogs and experiences
socialisation.quote: It’s important to socialise them from a young age with different people, dogs and experiences
socialisation.notes: PDSA (S390); 'It's really important that Rhodesian Ridgeback puppies from a breeder get the right early socialisation'. Woodgreen (S392): 'Early socialisation and habituation are crucial for Ridegbacks.' (sic). AKC article (S393): 'Early socialization and puppy training classes are also recommended.' → proposed_game_parameters.rhodesian_ridgeback.socialisation (DOG_SOCIALISATION row, M5-R17).

time_alone.value: never alone for more than four hours; separation anxiety if left too long too soon
time_alone.quote: We would never recommend leaving your Rhodesian Ridgeback alone for more than four hours.
time_alone.notes: PDSA (S390), breed-specific sentence: 'you'll need to gradually train them that it is OK to be alone.'; 'If left for too long too soon, your Ridgeback is likely to develop separation anxiety'. Woodgreen (S392): 'They don't cope well with being left alone for long hours.' → needs_company.

other_pets.value: very high prey drive — not recommended with smaller pets; may get along with a cat it grew up with
other_pets.quote: Ridgebacks have a very high prey drive, so we wouldn’t recommend keeping them with smaller pets
other_pets.notes: PDSA (S390); 'They may get along with a cat they have grown up with, but you should always supervise your dog with other pets.' Woodgreen (S392): 'Their hunting heritage means they have a strong prey drive and they may chase cats, small dogs, rabbits,' (fragment). PetMD (S391): 'hunting history and prey drive' — 'might not be the best choice for families with smaller pets like cats' (fragments). → chases_small_pets (runbook: 'high prey drive' quote); never other_pets.

mental_stimulation.notes: No explicit 'needs mental stimulation' sentence returned verbatim: PDSA (S390) 'known to get bored easily if they're not challenged enough' is about training; Woodgreen (S392) mentions training, scent work and puzzle toys (tool summary, paraphrase). → no needs_mental_stimulation tag (Vizsla precedent; open for David).

chewing.notes: No breed-specific chewing statement; Woodgreen (S392, paraphrase): may become destructive without enough exercise and stimulation → no chews_when_bored tag.

food_motivation.notes: No breed-specific statement found → no food_motivated_weight tag. PDSA (S390): 'We usually recommend splitting their daily allowance into two meals.'; PetMD (S391): 'Most veterinarians recommend feeding adult dogs, including Rhodesian Ridgebacks, twice a day.' — the game's two adult meals.

after_meals.value: leave a gap between eating and exercising (GDV)
after_meals.quote: Remember to leave a gap between eating and exercising as this is thought to reduce the risk of GDV.
after_meals.notes: PDSA (S390), feeding section. Basis of meal_exercise_gap (M5-R16). PetMD (S391): 'Eating too fast can cause gastrointestinal upset as well as other serious medical issues such as bloat.'

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages are shown anywhere. RKC Breed Watch Category 1 (S386, S387) → no welfare chip. RKC Health Standard (S263): no Good Practice or Best Practice tests; breed club health scheme 'Dermoid sinus testing'. Breeder checklist: dermoid sinus (S263, PDSA S390), hip and elbow schemes (PDSA S390), DNA JME (PDSA S390), DNA DM (RKC K25).

breed_watch.value: RKC Breed Watch Category 1 — no points of concern
breed_watch.quote: Currently no points of concern specific to this breed have been identified for special attention by judges,
breed_watch.notes: RKC breed page (S387); continues 'other than those covered routinely by The Kennel Club's breed standard.' Breeds A–Z address (S386): Category 1 as well.

dermoid_sinus.value: dermoid sinus — a painful congenital condition where the skin on the back links to the spinal cord; puppies checked by a vet before sale
dermoid_sinus.quote: Dermoid sinus – a painful condition where the skin on the back links to the spinal cord.
dermoid_sinus.notes: PDSA (S390): 'Puppies should be assessed by a vet prior to sale for this condition.' Woodgreen (S392): 'Dermoid sinus: a tube-like opening in the skin that can become infected and requires surgery to remove.' PetMD (S391): 'Surgical removal is the treatment of choice.' RKC Health Standard (S263): breed club health scheme 'Dermoid sinus testing'. Wikipedia (S394, tier C): prevalence estimates — research only, never shown. Register health key; breeder checklist (puppy check).

hip_elbow_dysplasia.value: hip and elbow dysplasia — x-ray screening of the parents (BVA/KC schemes)
hip_elbow_dysplasia.quote: Before breeding, dogs should be screened by x-rays through the BVA/Kennel Club Hip Dysplasia Scheme.
hip_elbow_dysplasia.notes: PDSA (S390): 'Hip dysplasia – where the hip joint doesn’t fit together perfectly, which will eventually lead to arthritis.'; 'Before breeding, dogs should be screened by x-rays through the BVA/Kennel Club Elbow Dysplasia Scheme.' PetMD (S391): 'Both are thought to be inherited conditions and can cause pain and arthritis in dogs.' Not a Breed Watch point → no hips_hind_legs chip.

gdv.quote: where a dog’s stomach bloats and twists around on itself, which can be fatal.
gdv.notes: PDSA (S390) health list (after 'Gastric Dilatation Volvulus (GDV)'); Woodgreen (S392): 'Bloat: a life-threatening condition where the stomach fills with gas and twists.' → meal_exercise_gap (behaviour.after_meals).

hypothyroidism.quote: an underactive thyroid, causing problems with weight, skin and energy levels.
hypothyroidism.notes: PDSA (S390). PetMD (S391): 'Autoimmune thyroiditis is a disease of the thyroid gland resulting in low thyroid values.'

juvenile_myoclonic_epilepsy.value: juvenile myoclonic epilepsy — DNA test of the parents
juvenile_myoclonic_epilepsy.quote: Parents should be DNA tested prior to mating.
juvenile_myoclonic_epilepsy.notes: PDSA (S390): 'Juvenile Myoclonic Epilepsy – a form of epilepsy.'; 'There is testing available for this.' Breeder checklist (dna_jme).

degenerative_myelopathy.value: degenerative myelopathy — official RKC DNA testing scheme
degenerative_myelopathy.quote: The Kennel Club has approved a new official DNA testing scheme for degenerative myelopathy (DM) in the Rhodesian Ridgeback.
degenerative_myelopathy.notes: RKC media centre (breeder-checklist K25, December 2024 by its address): 'Degenerative myelopathy is a progressive neurological disease.' Breeder checklist only.

deafness_eyes.value: progressive deafness; eye problems (cataracts, entropion, distichiasis, persistent pupillary membranes)
deafness_eyes.quote: progressive deafness is not uncommon in the breed.
deafness_eyes.notes: PetMD (S391); the eye conditions are a tool summary (paraphrase). Research only.

cancer.notes: PDSA (S390) lists 'Certain cancers' without a sentence (paraphrase). Research only.

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table of Coren's ranking (S35, re-read 2026-10-19): rank 52 'Rhodesian Ridgeback' (table row; neighbours rank 51 and 53 shared by three breeds each).

coren_tier.quote: Average Working/Obedience Intelligence
coren_tier.notes: Tier heading as returned (ranks 40–54, S35).

training_notes.value: positive, reward-based training from an early age; can be wilful / independent; patience and consistency
training_notes.quote: Ridgebacks are very intelligent dogs so respond well to positive, reward-based training from an early age.
training_notes.notes: PDSA (S390): 'You'll need to be very patient and take things slowly at first'; 'consistency is key!'. PetMD (S391): 'Rhodesian Ridgeback dogs can have an independent streak, so obedience training throughout their entire life is critical.' AKC article (S393): 'must be trained with a firm but patient hand from early puppyhood.' The game uses Coren's rank only.

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value — see proposed_game_parameters.rhodesian_ridgeback.learning_multiplier (1.0, runbook rule: Average tier).

general.value: well balanced, strong, muscular, agile and active hound; elegant, never massive; the ridge on the back
general.quote: should represent a well balanced, strong, muscular, agile and active dog,
general.notes: FCI (S385): 'The emphasis is on agility, elegance and soundness' 'with no tendency towards massiveness.' RKC standard (S388): 'Handsome, strong, muscular and active dog, symmetrical in outline, capable of great endurance with fair amount of speed.'

ridge.value: ridge of hair growing in the opposite direction along the spine — clearly defined, symmetrical, two identical opposite crowns; ridgeless = disqualification
ridge.quote: A distinctive feature is the ridge on the back formed by hair growing in opposite direction to the remainder of coat.
ridge.notes: RKC standard (S388): 'Ridge clearly defined, tapering and symmetrical, starting immediately behind shoulders and continuing to haunch,'; 'and containing two identical crowns only, opposite each other,'; 'Up to 5 cm (2 ins) is a good average for width of ridge.' FCI (S385): 'The ridge is the escutcheon of the breed.'; disqualifying 'Dogs without ridge.' AKC (S389) disqualification 'Ridgelessness.' The defining trait of the portrait (dog trait `ridge`).

colours.quote: Light wheaten to red wheaten.
colours.notes: FCI (S385), RKC standard (S388) 'Light wheaten to red wheaten. Head, body, legs and tail of uniform colour.' and AKC (S389) 'Light wheaten to red wheaten.' — one colour range (the game uses its two named ends; shades in between are the same colour). RKC (S388): 'Little white on chest and toes permissible, but excessive white hairs here, on belly or above paws undesirable.'; 'Dark muzzle and ears permissible.'; 'Any other colour or combination of colours unacceptable.' FCI: 'Excessive black hairs throughout the coat are highly undesirable.' AKC disqualifications: 'Solid black.' and 'Black and tan, or brown and tan in brown/liver nosed dogs.' Never black, black and tan, brindle or a ridgeless dog.

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). Red wheaten first with the highest weight (portrait default — the warm wheaten most associated with the breed; Claude's choice, no source gives frequencies), then light wheaten.

coat.value: short and dense, sleek and glossy, neither woolly nor silky
coat.quote: Should be short and dense, sleek and glossy in appearance, but neither woolly nor silky.
coat.notes: RKC standard (S388) 'Short and dense, sleek and glossy in appearance, but neither woolly nor silky.'; RKC key facts (S387) 'Coat length: Short'.

ears.value: set rather high, medium size, wide at the base, tapering to a rounded point, carried close to the head
ears.quote: Should be set rather high, of medium size, rather wide at base, and gradually tapering to a rounded point.
ears.notes: FCI (S385): 'They should be carried close to the head.' RKC standard (S388) the same.

eyes.value: moderately well apart, round, bright and sparkling; colour harmonising with the coat (dark with a black nose, amber with a brown nose)
eyes.quote: Should be moderately well apart, round, bright and sparkling, with intelligent expression,
eyes.notes: FCI (S385): 'their colour harmonising with the colour of the coat.'

nose.value: black or brown (liver); black nose with dark eyes, brown nose with amber eyes
nose.quote: The nose should be black or brown.
nose.notes: FCI (S385): 'A black nose should be accompanied by dark eyes, a brown nose by amber eyes.' RKC standard (S388): 'Nose black or brown in keeping with colour of dog.' AKC (S389): 'Should be black, or brown, also known as liver, in keeping with the color of the dog.' Portrait: black nose with dark eyes (Claude's choice of the first-named option).

tail.value: strong at the root, tapering, moderate length, carried with a slight upward curve, never curled
tail.quote: should be carried with a slight curve upwards, never curled.
tail.notes: FCI (S385): 'Should be strong at the root and gradually tapering towards the end, free from coarseness.'; 'It should be of moderate length.' RKC standard (S388): 'Carried with a slight curve upwards, never curled.'

suitability._note: Source = RKC breed page key facts (older address S387; the Breeds A–Z address S386 returned Exercise, Size of home, Size of garden, Grooming, Lifespan only), PDSA (S390), PetMD (S391), Woodgreen (S392), AKC article (S393). No Dogs Trust or Blue Cross Rhodesian Ridgeback page found by search. The RKC page shows no 'Good with children' field.

rkc_exercise.quote: Exercise: More than 2 hours per day
rkc_exercise.notes: Also on the Breeds A–Z address (S386).

rkc_size_of_home.notes: Basis of large_home (with the garden).

rkc_size_of_garden.notes: Basis of large_home (with the home). PDSA (S390): 'a large garden is an absolute must'.

rkc_grooming.notes: Basis of the weekly brushing (1×, runbook dog-grooming rule).

rkc_shedding.notes: PDSA (S390): 'Ridgebacks shed all year round and more so in spring and autumn when you may want to brush them a little more.'; PetMD (S391): 'these dogs shed frequently'; Woodgreen (S392) 'Moderate' — all say it sheds. Basis of the sheds tag.

rkc_breed_watch.quote: Currently no points of concern specific to this breed have been identified for special attention by judges,
rkc_breed_watch.notes: No welfare chip.

pdsa_exercise.value: a minimum of two hours a day; active families
pdsa_exercise.quote: Your Ridgeback will need a minimum of two hours exercise every day.
pdsa_exercise.notes: PDSA (S390): 'They suit active families who are prepared to spend lots of time outdoors with them, rain or shine.' Basis of active_family / long_daily_exercise (with the RKC).

pdsa_active_family.quote: They suit active families who are prepared to spend lots of time outdoors with them, rain or shine.

fci_family_pet.value: especially prized as watch-dog and family pet
fci_family_pet.quote: but is especially prized as watch-dog and family pet.
fci_family_pet.notes: FCI standard utilization (S385). Basis of family_pet (with PDSA 'extremely loyal and loving towards their family').

pdsa_family.value: extremely loyal and loving towards their family
pdsa_family.quote: Rhodesian Ridgebacks are playful and powerful dogs who are extremely loyal and loving towards their family.
pdsa_family.notes: PDSA (S390), health section introduction. Basis of family_pet (with FCI) and the 'powerful dog' of experienced_owner.

pdsa_children.value: best with older children; risks knocking over smaller children
pdsa_children.quote: Their large size and boisterous nature when they are younger also means they risk knocking over smaller children.
pdsa_children.notes: PDSA (S390): 'They best suit couples or families with older children who understand how to behave around dogs.' Basis of not_for_small_children.

woodgreen_children.quote: Ridgebacks do best with older children who understand how to interact respectfully with dogs.

pdsa_experienced_owner.quote: so it’s for this reason we wouldn’t recommend them if you are a first time owner.

akc_experienced_owner.value: best with experienced dog owners in active households
akc_experienced_owner.quote: Ridgebacks do best in active households with experienced dog owners with plenty of time and attention to offer.

pdsa_company.value: never alone for more than four hours
pdsa_company.quote: We would never recommend leaving your Rhodesian Ridgeback alone for more than four hours.
pdsa_company.notes: PDSA (S390), breed-specific; 'If left for too long too soon, your Ridgeback is likely to develop separation anxiety'. Basis of needs_company.

woodgreen_time_alone.value: does not cope well alone for long hours
woodgreen_time_alone.quote: They don't cope well with being left alone for long hours.

pdsa_prey_drive.value: very high prey drive — not with smaller pets
pdsa_prey_drive.quote: Ridgebacks have a very high prey drive, so we wouldn’t recommend keeping them with smaller pets

pdsa_grooming.value: a weekly brush; more in spring and autumn
pdsa_grooming.quote: A weekly brush should be more than enough to keep on top of dead hairs.
pdsa_grooming.notes: PDSA (S390). Agrees with the RKC 'Once a week'. The heavier spring / autumn moult is not modelled.

woodgreen_grooming.value: weekly brush; check and clean the ears weekly; brush teeth regularly or dental chews
woodgreen_grooming.quote: A weekly brush with a rubber curry brush or hound glove will remove loose hair and keep their coat looking healthy and shiny.
woodgreen_grooming.notes: Woodgreen (S392); 'Grooming needs' 'Moderate'. Nails (tool summary, paraphrase): usually kept short by exercise — no need recorded.

woodgreen_ears_teeth.value: check and clean the ears weekly; brush the teeth regularly or give dental chews
woodgreen_ears_teeth.quote: Check and clean their ears weekly to prevent infections, and brush their teeth regularly or provide them with dental chews.
woodgreen_ears_teeth.notes: Woodgreen (S392). → ear care ROADMAP M5-R20, tooth care ROADMAP M5-R15 (needs-david).

petmd_grooming.value: weekly brushing; a bath at least once a month
petmd_grooming.quote: Because these dogs shed frequently, weekly brushing can help keep the coat free of excess hair.
petmd_grooming.notes: PetMD (S391): 'Baths, at least once a month, will keep the hair glossy and healthy.' → bathing ROADMAP M5-R20 (needs-david).

petmd_ears.value: floppy ears — prone to ear infections; clean routinely
petmd_ears.quote: Their ears need to be cleaned routinely.
petmd_ears.notes: PetMD (S391): 'Rhodesian Ridgebacks have floppy ears, making them more susceptible to ear infections.' → ROADMAP M5-R20.

akc_grooming.quote: Weekly brushings are fine to remove loose hair.
akc_grooming.notes: AKC article (S393): 'The Rhodesian Ridgeback doesn't require any specific kind of grooming.' Agrees with weekly brushing.

pdsa_home.value: a large garden is a must; space and open areas
pdsa_home.quote: a large garden is an absolute must
pdsa_home.notes: PDSA (S390), fragment as returned; better suited to 'an environment where they'll get lots of access to open spaces'. → no apartment tag.

papillon._note: Added 2026-10-20 (M5-R10-48, unattended run — appended after the Rhodesian Ridgeback: AKC 2024 No. 44 'Papillon', S174 full-list table '43 Rhodesian Ridgeback', '44 Papillon', '45 Portuguese Water Dog'). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-20 (fragments marked as such); paraphrase only in notes. Sources S395–S401. No health percentages anywhere. The FCI breed is the Continental Toy Spaniel with two varieties (Papillon — erect ears; Phalène — drooping ears); the game builds the Papillon (erect-eared) variety under the AKC / RKC name.

identity.value: FCI No. 77, Group 9 Section 9 (Continental Toy Spaniels), Belgium / France
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S395): group 'n°9 - Companion and Toy Dogs', section 'Continental Toy Spaniel and others', country of origin 'BELGIUM, FRANCE', 'Not subject to a working trial according to the FCI breeds nomenclature', definitive acceptance '1/1/1954'; varieties 'a) Papillon - with erect ears' and 'b) Phalène - with drooping ears'. FCI standard N° 77 (S396): 'Group 9 Companion and Toy Dogs.' / 'Section 9 Continental Toy Spaniels.'; origin 'France, Belgium.'; date of publication '17.09.1990'. The identity country follows the nomenclature order (Belgium / France) — both must be in FCI_ORIGINS of the export. RKC (S397) group: Toy. AKC name: Papillon (S174, S399).

size_class.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S397) 'Size: Small' (value as returned); PDSA (S398) 'Small'. FCI (S396) weight 1.5–5 kg = 3.3–11 lb → the 'Toy (5–12 pounds)' class of S10 for growth.

fci.quote: Height at the withers: About 28 cm.
fci.notes: FCI standard (S396), one approximate value for both sexes (stored per sex).

akc.quote: Height at withers, 8 to 11 inches.
akc.notes: AKC-approved standard of the Papillon Club of America (S399): 8–11 in = 20.3–27.9 cm (inches × 2.54 by us, rounded); disqualification 'Over 12 inches.' Alternative only.

pdsa.notes: PDSA key fact 'Average height' (S398), one range for both sexes. Agrees with the AKC range.

fci.quote: From 2,5 kg to 4,5 kg for dogs,
fci.notes: FCI standard (S396) has two weight categories: 'Less than 2,5 kg for dogs and bitches.' with 'Minimum weight 1,5 kg.', and 'From 2,5 kg to 4,5 kg for dogs,' / 'from 2,5 kg to 5 kg for bitches.' Stored as the span of both categories (males 1.5–4.5, females 1.5–5). The game range (adult_weight_kg).

pdsa.notes: PDSA key fact 'Average weight' (S398), one range for both sexes. Inside the FCI span; alternative only.

akc.quote: Weight is in proportion to height.
akc.notes: AKC-approved standard (S399) gives no weight number. PetMD (S400): 'At 8–11 inches tall and 5–10 pounds, Papillons are compact and adaptable.' (5–10 lb = 2.3–4.5 kg, background).

salt_category.notes: Category assignment by weight is ours (general_by_size.size_classes.salt_2017_bands_kg, S8): 1.5–5 kg = the smallest band. Salt 2017 breed list not checked.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. 1.5–5 kg = 3.3–11 lb → 'Toy (5–12 pounds)'. The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 30 min is reached at 3 months).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Papillon growth curve found.

rkc.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S397) 'Lifespan: Over 12 years' (value as returned). PDSA (S398) 'Over 12 years' agrees. The basis of the senior boundary (runbook: RKC lower bound when no McMillan 2024 / VetCompass value is reachable). Not shorter_lifespan.

pdsa.notes: PDSA key fact 'Average lifespan' (S398). Same lower bound as the RKC → same senior boundary (108).

petmd.quote: The average Papillon lifespan is 14–16 years, and they're one of the dog breeds with the longest life expectancies.
petmd.notes: PetMD (S400, tier B). Alternative only (lower bound 14 y → 126 months).

mcmillan_2024.quote: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 14.5 years for the breed
mcmillan_2024.notes: McMillan et al. 2024 as quoted by Wikipedia (S401, tier C — never alone). The Dogs Trust breed table (S123) was not reachable on 2026-10-20 (fetch tool provenance refusal) → not used as the basis; with it the senior boundary would be round(0.75 × 14.5 × 12) = round(130.5) = 131 months. Verify in S123 before replacing the RKC lower bound.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × 12 y (RKC lower bound 'Over 12 years', S397) → 0.75 × 12 = 9 y = 108 months. With McMillan 2024 14.5 y (via S401): 131 months; PetMD 14 y lower bound: 126; Dogs Trust rule of thumb > 7 y = 84 months (S14). Provisional until McMillan 2024 is checked.

adult.quote: Exercise: Up to 30 minutes per day
adult.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S397) 'Exercise: Up to 30 minutes per day' (value as returned). PDSA (S398): 'Around 30 minutes exercise daily is usually sufficient to keep them happy.' (key facts: minimum exercise per day '30 minutes') — sources agree on 30.

energy.value: active and playful; needs daily exercise and mental stimulation
energy.quote: They are active, playful, and need daily exercise and mental stimulation.
energy.notes: PetMD (S400); also 'they need more exercise than you might think' (fragment). PDSA (S398): 'Papillons are lively little dogs, but will just as happily jump at a chance of a cuddle and they will play or a walk.'

after_meals.notes: No A/B source found on a gap between meals and exercise for this breed → no meal_exercise_gap row.

temperament.value: gentle, playful, gets along well with everyone; happy, alert and friendly
temperament.quote: Papillons are gentle, playful dogs that generally get along well with everyone.
temperament.notes: PDSA (S398). AKC-approved standard (S399): 'Happy, alert and friendly. Neither shy nor aggressive.' FCI (S396): 'lively personality, graceful yet robust, proud carriage with an easy and elegant gait.'

family.value: great family dogs because they are affectionate
family.quote: Papillons are great family dogs because they are affectionate
family.notes: PetMD (S400) fragment as returned. Basis of family_pet.

children.value: live well with kids; very young or rambunctious children can accidentally injure small dogs — supervise
children.quote: Papillons live well with other dogs, cats, kids, adults, and seniors alike.
children.notes: PetMD (S400). Caveat (fragment as returned): 'very young or very rambunctious children can easily (though accidentally!) injure small dog breeds' — kept here as a supervision caveat (runbook: children chip with an explicit statement, caveat in notes). No small_children chip.

socialisation.value: training and socialisation very important at a young age
socialisation.quote: Training, along with socialisation, is very important at a young age
socialisation.notes: PDSA (S398) fragment as returned (the sentence continues: so they become confident, sociable adults — paraphrase). PetMD (S400): 'Begin socializing your Papillon puppy from the moment they come home'. Basis of the puppy socialisation row (M5-R17).

time_alone.value: some may develop separation anxiety
time_alone.quote: However, some Papillons may develop separation anxiety.

portuguese_water_dog._note: Added 2026-10-20 (M5-R10-49, unattended run — appended after the Papillon: AKC 2024 No. 45 'Portuguese Water Dog', S174 full-list table '44 Papillon', '45 Portuguese Water Dog'). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-20 (the tool limits quotes to about 125 characters; fragments marked as such); paraphrase only in notes. Sources S402–S408. No health percentages anywhere. The FCI standard PDF (fci.be 037g08-en.pdf) was refused by the fetch tool (provenance) → appearance, height and weight from the RKC breed standard (S403, last updated 1 April 2025), which follows the FCI standard. Never 'hypoallergenic' (Wikipedia S408 itself says there is no scientific evidence for hypoallergenic breeds).

identity.value: FCI No. 37, Group 8 Section 3 (Water Dogs), Portugal
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S402): English name 'PORTUGUESE WATER DOG', group 'n°8 - Retrievers - Flushing Dogs - Water Dogs', section 'Water Dogs', country of origin 'PORTUGAL', 'Not subject to a working trial according to the FCI breeds nomenclature', definitive acceptance '2/1/1955'; valid standard dated 11/4/2008. RKC (S403 / S404) group: Working. AKC name: Portuguese Water Dog (S174). Section number 3 = the FCI group 8 section of the Water Dogs (the nomenclature page names the section without its number — our reading).

vca_nails.value: nail trimming, taking care of the webbing between the toes (no frequency)
vca_nails.quote: When trimming her nails, pay attention to the webbing between her toes and take care not to injure that delicate skin.

bichon_frise._note: Added 2026-10-20 (M5-R10-50, unattended run — appended after the Portuguese Water Dog: AKC 2024 No. 46 'Bichon Frise', S174 full-list table '45 Portuguese Water Dog', '46 Bichon Frise'). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-20 (fragments marked as such); paraphrase only in notes. Sources S409–S418 (reused S8, S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45). No health percentages anywhere. Appearance from the FCI standard (S410, 04.04.2016) and the RKC breed standard (S412, January 2025). The FCI standard gives one approximate weight ('Approximately 5 kg') → the game weight range from PDSA (S413, '4-7 kg', which brackets it). Lifespan: no McMillan 2024 / VetCompass value reachable (Dogs Trust table S123 and nature.com refused by the fetch tool; McMillan 2024 12.5 y only via Wikipedia S417, tier C) → runbook rule: RKC lower bound 'Over 12 years' (S411; PDSA S413 the same). Never 'hypoallergenic' (PetMD and VCA use the word; VCA itself says no breed is non-allergenic) — low_shedding only (RKC 'Sheds: No').

identity.value: FCI No. 215, Group 9 Section 1 (Bichons and related breeds), Belgium / France
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S409): group 'n°9 - Companion and Toy Dogs', section 'Bichons and related breeds', country of origin 'BELGIUM, FRANCE', 'Not subject to a working trial according to the FCI breeds nomenclature', definitive acceptance '10/28/1959', valid standard 4/4/2016; English name 'BICHON FRISE'. FCI standard N° 215 (S410): 'ORIGIN: Franco-Belgian.' / 'PATRONAGE: France and Belgium.' / 'F.C.I. CLASSIFICATION: Group 9 Companion and toy dogs.' Section number 1 = the FCI group 9 section of the Bichons (the nomenclature page names the section without its number — our reading). The identity country follows the nomenclature order (Belgium / France, as the Papillon). RKC group: Toy (S411). AKC name: Bichon Frise (S174). Wikipedia (S417, tier C) names the Canary Islands as the older origin — background only.

size_class.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S411) 'Size: Small' (value as returned); PDSA (S413) 'Small'. FCI (S410) approximately 5 kg ≈ 11 lb → the 'Toy (5–12 pounds)' class of S10 for growth.

fci.quote: Height at the withers: 25 to 29 cm.
fci.notes: FCI standard (S410): 'A tolerance of 1 cm taller is accepted for males,' / 'A tolerance of 2 cm lower is accepted for females,' → males 25–30 cm, females 23–29 cm (the tolerances applied by us; Wikipedia S417 gives the same per-sex ranges).

rkc_standard.quote: Ideal height 23-28 cms (9-11 ins) at withers.
rkc_standard.notes: RKC breed standard (S412), one range for both sexes. Alternative only.

pdsa.notes: PDSA key fact 'Average height' (S413), one range for both sexes. Agrees with the RKC standard.

fci.quote: Weight: Approximately 5 kg, in proportion with the size.
fci.notes: FCI standard (S410): one approximate value for both sexes (stored per sex). Inside the PDSA range used by the game.

pdsa.notes: PDSA key fact 'Average weight' (S413), one range for both sexes (value as returned). The game range (adult_weight_kg 4–7): the FCI gives one approximate number only, and 5 kg lies inside this range. The RKC standard (S412) gives no weight. VCA (S414) 'Weight: 12 to 18 pounds' ≈ 5.4–8.2 kg; VCA older page (S415) '10 - 16 pounds' ≈ 4.5–7.3 kg; PetMD (S416) 12–18 lb — alternatives only (our conversions).

salt_category.notes: Category assignment by weight is ours (general_by_size.size_classes.salt_2017_bands_kg, S8): FCI approximately 5 kg = the smallest band. Salt 2017 breed list not checked.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. FCI approximately 5 kg (S410) ≈ 11 lb → 'Toy (5–12 pounds)'; the PDSA upper end 7 kg (≈ 15 lb) would fall in 'Small (12–24 pounds): 9–12 months' — the game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 30 min is reached at 3 months).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Bichon Frise growth curve found.

rkc.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S411) 'Lifespan: Over 12 years' (value as returned). PDSA (S413) 'Over 12 years' agrees. The basis of the senior boundary (runbook: RKC lower bound when no McMillan 2024 / VetCompass value is reachable). Not shorter_lifespan.

pdsa.notes: PDSA key fact 'Average lifespan' (S413). Same lower bound as the RKC → same senior boundary (108).

vca.notes: VCA breed overview (S414). The older VCA page (S415) gives '12 - 15 years'; PetMD (S416): 'The average Bichon Frise lifespan is 14–15 years.' Alternatives only.

mcmillan_2024.quote: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12.5 years for the breed
mcmillan_2024.notes: McMillan et al. 2024 as quoted by Wikipedia (S417, tier C — never alone). The main article (LJMU copy) names the breed only in a Fig. 5 label; the per-breed table (Supplementary Table 3) and the Dogs Trust breed table (S123) were not reachable on 2026-10-20 → not used as the basis; with it the senior boundary would be round(0.75 × 12.5 × 12) = round(112.5) = 113 months. Verify in S123 before replacing the RKC lower bound.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × 12 y (RKC lower bound 'Over 12 years', S411) → 0.75 × 12 = 9 y = 108 months. With McMillan 2024 12.5 y (via S417): 113 months; VCA / PetMD 14 y lower bound: 126; Dogs Trust rule of thumb > 7 y = 84 months (S14). Provisional until McMillan 2024 is checked.

adult.quote: Exercise: Up to 30 minutes per day

energy.value: moderate daily activity; content to lounge once the energy needs are met
energy.quote: Bichon Frises need moderate daily activity to stay healthy and engaged.
energy.notes: VCA (S414). Older VCA page (S415): 'A walk around the block once or twice daily, plus a vigorous game' (fragment). PetMD (S416): 'Once their energy needs are met, Bichons are content to lounge with their family on the couch.'

after_meals.notes: No A/B source found on a gap between meals and exercise for this breed → no meal_exercise_gap row.

temperament.value: cheerful, happy, lively; friendly and outgoing; neither nervous nor a frequent barker
temperament.quote: Friendly and outgoing.
temperament.notes: RKC standard 'Temperament' (S412); 'Gay, happy, lively little dog.' FCI (S410): 'It is a true companion dog which can be taken anywhere without trouble.' / 'It is neither nervous nor does it often bark.' PDSA (S413): 'Bichons have a happy, playful nature, but will just as quickly jump at the chance of a cuddle and fuss as they will play.'

family.value: a great family pet
family.quote: The Bichon Frise dog breed is a great family pet and highly suitable for families with younger children.

children.value: excellent with children; PetMD: highly suitable for families with younger children
children.quote: Bichons are very affectionate, loving dogs that are excellent with children and other pets alike.
children.notes: PDSA (S413). PetMD (S416): 'The Bichon Frise dog breed is a great family pet and highly suitable for families with younger children.' VCA (S414): 'Children: Generally good with children'; older VCA (S415): 'Playful, gentle and very good with children.' Basis of children. No small_children chip: no rating (the runbook requires an explicit rating) — open for David.

time_alone.value: limited tolerance of being alone; prefers companionship
time_alone.quote: Time Alone: Limited tolerance; prefers companionship
time_alone.notes: VCA (S414); 'They may develop attention-seeking behaviors if left alone too often.' PetMD (S416): 'If they're bored or lonely, Bichons may turn to undesirable behaviors like excessive barking.' Basis of needs_company.

other_pets.value: excellent with other pets
other_pets.quote: Bichons are very affectionate, loving dogs that are excellent with children and other pets alike.
other_pets.notes: PDSA (S413). PetMD (S416): 'They are good with kids and other animals, and they're very playful.' VCA (S414): 'Other Pets: Typically social and adaptable'. No prey-drive statement → no chases_small_pets. Basis of other_pets.

chewing.notes: No breed-specific chewing statement found.

food_motivation.notes: No breed-specific food-motivation statement found. Older VCA (S415): 'Does best with reward-based training involving food or games.' — training advice, not food motivation. No food_motivated_weight chip.

training_notes.value: highly trainable, learns quickly; relatively easy to train
training_notes.quote: The Bichon Frise is highly trainable, smart, and learns quickly.
training_notes.notes: PetMD (S416). VCA (S414): 'This breed is social and responsive, making them relatively easy to train.' PDSA (S413) rating label 'Easy to train' (no text).

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages anywhere (Wikipedia S417 gives study ratios — never exported). RKC Breed Watch Category 1 (S411: 'Currently no points of concern specific to this breed have been identified') → no welfare chip. PDSA (S413) lists luxating patellas, allergies, cataracts, bladder stones, portosystemic shunt and diabetes mellitus; VCA (S414) patellar luxation, congenital deafness, allergic dermatitis, dental disease, bladder stones, degenerative joint disease, cataracts, diabetes mellitus; PetMD (S416) diabetes, corneal dystrophy, cataracts, bladder stones and dental disease.

patella.quote: Luxating patellas – the kneecaps slipping temporarily out of place.
patella.notes: PDSA (S413) health list; VCA (S414) 'Patellar luxation'. AKC parent club recommends a patella evaluation (breeder checklist K28). Background only.

allergies.quote: Skin allergies are a common issue in Bichon Frises and may require ongoing management.
allergies.notes: VCA (S414); PDSA (S413) 'Allergies'. Background only — not a Breed Watch point → no sensitive_skin chip.

cataracts.quote: Cataracts – opacity of the lens of the eye – giving a 'cloudy' appearance.
cataracts.notes: PDSA (S413); VCA (S414), PetMD (S416) agree. RKC minimum: BVA/KC/ISDS eye scheme (breeder checklist). Background only.

bladder_stones.quote: Bladder stones – a collection of minerals that form in the bladder.
bladder_stones.notes: PDSA (S413); VCA (S414), PetMD (S416) agree. Background only.

liver_shunt.quote: Portosystemic shunt – abnormal blood circulation, with the blood effectively bypassing the liver
liver_shunt.notes: PDSA (S413) fragment as returned. Background only.

diabetes.quote: Diabetes Mellitus – a complex disorder of carbohydrate, fat and protein metabolism
diabetes.notes: PDSA (S413) fragment as returned; VCA (S414) senior list; PetMD (S416): 'Diabetes in dogs is a disease of the pancreas that results in a failure to regulate blood sugar.' Background only.

dental.value: dental disease — tooth brushing at home
dental.quote: As with all small dogs, the Bichon Frise is highly susceptible to dental disease.
dental.notes: PetMD (S416): 'Brushing your dog's teeth at home with a dog-friendly toothbrush and toothpaste will help, too.' VCA (S414): 'Dental disease' (adult list). Tooth care advice: see suitability.petmd_teeth (ROADMAP M5-R15).

Coren's own top / bottom-10 article (S34) does not list the breed. Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

newfoundland._note: Added 2026-10-20 (M5-R10-51, unattended run — appended after the Bichon Frise: AKC 2024 No. 47 'Newfoundland', S174 full-list table '46 Bichon Frise', '47 Newfoundland'). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-20 (PDSA and PetMD only in short quotes, 125-character limit; fragments marked as such); paraphrase only in notes. Sources S419–S426 (reused S8, S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45, S123, S174). No health percentages anywhere. The RKC (Breeds A–Z page on royalkennelclub.com, Breed Watch page and DNA testing page) returned a fetch error on 2026-10-20 → no RKC key facts; exercise from PDSA (S423, runbook fallback RKC → PDSA). The English FCI PDF redirects to itself → the Spanish FCI standard (S420, 29.10.1996) and the FCI nomenclature (S419). Lifespan: McMillan 2024 median 11.0 y via the Dogs Trust table (S123) — not provisional. Welfare: PDSA (S423) 'Category Two'; the Breed Watch point (loose eyelids) from the Kennel Club Breed Health and Conservation Plan 2018 (S425). Names: FCI 'NEWFOUNDLAND' (S419), AKC 'Newfoundland' (S174, S421); Slovenian »novofundlandec« (not checked against KZS — open for David).

FCI standard N° 50 (S420, Spanish original, the only language version the tool could read): 'CLASIFICACIÓN FCI: Grupo 2 Perros tipo Pinscher y Schnauzer, Molosoides Perros tipo montaña y boyeros suizos.'; 'ORIGEN: Canadá.'; 'FECHA DE PUBLICACIÓN DEL ESTÁNDAR OFICIAL VÁLIDO: 29.10.1996.'; 'UTILIZACIÓN: Perro de trineo para cargas pesadas, perro de agua.'
