Runbook first choice (McMillan 2024) → not provisional. The breed is not in the Fig. 3 legend of the Author Correction (S54, checked 2026-10-20). Wikipedia (S426, tier C): 'A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 11 years for the breed' — agrees.

pdsa.notes: PDSA key facts (S423). PetMD (S424): 'The average Newfoundland dog lifespan is 9–10 years.' Basis of shorter_lifespan (runbook: an A/B source gives an upper bound ≤ 10 years) although the McMillan median is 11.0 y — noted for David.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × 11.0 y (McMillan 2024 via S123) → 0.75 × 11.0 = 8.25 y = 99 months. Dogs Trust rule of thumb > 7 y = 84 months (S14). Not chosen: 0.75 × 9 y (PetMD lower bound, S424) = 81.

adult.quote: Minimum exercise (per day): 1 hour
adult.notes: PDSA key facts (S423); PDSA text: 'As adult dogs, Newfoundlands need around an hour of exercise daily' (opening clause), they particularly love to swim and pull. RKC breed page (preferred) not reachable on 2026-10-20 → PDSA (runbook rule). PetMD (S424): 'Newfoundlands are calm dogs that don't need an excessive amount of exercise—but this doesn't mean no exercise.' — no minutes.

after_meals.value: avoid exercise an hour before or after a meal (GDV / bloat)
after_meals.quote: Avoiding exercising their dog an hour before or after a meal
after_meals.notes: PetMD (S424), bloat / GDV prevention list; also 'Feeding their dog at least twice a day instead of one big meal' and 'Adult Newfies do best if fed about every 12 hours.' PDSA (S423) lists GDV: 'often known as ‘bloat’, this is a condition where the stomach twists, trapping the contents and gases.' (fragment). → proposed_game_parameters.newfoundland.meal_exercise_gap (built, M5-R16 — the game warns after a meal; the hour before a meal is not modelled).

swimming.value: natural swimmers; love to swim and pull
swimming.quote: Because of this history, Newfoundlands are natural swimmers
swimming.notes: PetMD (S424); PDSA (S423): 'they particularly love to swim and pull' (fragment). Background only — the game counts steps.

temperament.value: gentle giants — calm, good-natured; sweetness of temperament is the hallmark
temperament.quote: Sweetness of temperament is the hallmark of the Newfoundland;
temperament.notes: AKC (S421): 'this is the most important single characteristic of the breed.' PDSA (S423): 'Newfoundlands, or ‘Newfies’ as they’re more affectionately known, are gentle giants.' (the rest: calm, good-natured dogs that tend to get on well with everyone — paraphrase). CKC (S422): gentle, intelligent, dignified yet playful (paraphrase).

family.value: an outstanding family pet; gets along well with children; supervise small kids
family.quote: A Newfoundland dog's personality makes the breed an outstanding family pet.
family.notes: PetMD (S424): 'They have a sweet disposition and gentle nature, so Newfies get along well with children, small pets, and other dogs.' and 'But just like with all dogs, supervise all interactions between small kids and Newfoundlands.' → family_pet, children (supervision caveat kept); never small_children.

socialisation.value: consistent socialisation as puppies
socialisation.quote: All dogs, even the friendly Newfoundland, need consistent socialization as puppies
socialisation.notes: PetMD (S424); 'Early and consistent obedience training is a must.' → proposed_game_parameters.newfoundland.socialisation (DOG_SOCIALISATION row, M5-R17).

time_alone.value: loving; some may develop separation anxiety when left alone
time_alone.quote: Because Newfoundland dogs are so loving, some may develop separation anxiety when left alone.
time_alone.notes: PetMD (S424). Basis of needs_company (Boxer precedent: a separation-anxiety statement).

other_pets.value: gets along with small pets, other dogs and cats
other_pets.quote: good roommates to other dogs and cats
other_pets.notes: PetMD (S424), fragment; also 'Newfies get along well with children, small pets, and other dogs.' No prey-drive statement. → other_pets.

chewing.notes: No breed-specific statement found → no chews_when_bored tag.

drooling.quote: Newfies also tend to drool and can be quite messy drinkers.
drooling.notes: PDSA (S423). PetMD (S424): 'Pet parents will also need to regularly wipe their Newfie's drool, which can get caught in their fur.' Basis of drools (as the Mastiff, Great Dane, Cane Corso).

food_motivation.notes: No breed-specific statement found → no food_motivated_weight tag. PetMD (S424): walks 'to provide mental stimulation and prevent obesity' (general) and two meals a day (the game's two adult meals — no change).

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages are shown anywhere. Conformation welfare topic: PDSA (S423) 'Newfoundlands are amongst a group of breeds classed as ‘Category Two’ by The Kennel Club.'; the Kennel Club's Breed Health and Conservation Plan (S425, 2018) names the one Breed Watch point: loose eyelids → eyelid_problems. PDSA's 'Eyelid problems' entry reads 'occur in Bulldogs due to excessive skin over the face and eyes' (copied from another breed page) — not used as a quote. Not named flat-faced by any source → no brachycephalic chip, in marketing.

breed_watch.value: Kennel Club Breed Watch Category 2 — one point of concern: loose eyelids
breed_watch.quote: Conformational defects of the upper and lower eyelids (loose eyelids)
breed_watch.notes: Kennel Club Newfoundland Breed Health and Conservation Plan, version 1, August 2018 (S425): 'The Newfoundland is currently a category two breed which indicates that it has one or more Breed Watch points of concern.' PDSA (S423): 'Newfoundlands are amongst a group of breeds classed as ‘Category Two’ by The Kennel Club.' and 'These are breeds of dog that have been highlighted as having ‘points of concern’.' (fragment). The RKC Breed Watch page itself returned a fetch error on 2026-10-20.

eyelids.value: loose eyelids (Breed Watch point of concern)
eyelids.quote: Conformational defects of the upper and lower eyelids (loose eyelids)
eyelids.notes: S425 (Breed Watch point). Basis of eyelid_problems (welfare rule §3, as the Great Dane and the Mastiff). PDSA's own eyelid sentence names Bulldogs (copy error on the page) — not quoted.

gdv.value: gastric dilatation volvulus ('bloat') — urgent vet care
gdv.quote: Take your Newfoundland to the nearest emergency vet immediately if you notice any symptoms of bloat and GDV.
gdv.notes: PetMD (S424); PDSA (S423) GDV; BHCP (S425) priority. → meal_exercise_gap (M5-R16).

hip_elbow_dysplasia.value: hip and elbow dysplasia — joint laxity leading to arthritis; BVA/KC schemes
hip_elbow_dysplasia.quote: hip joint laxity as a result of poor development, which will eventually lead to arthritis.
hip_elbow_dysplasia.notes: PDSA (S423) hip dysplasia; elbow dysplasia: 'elbow joint laxity as a result of poor development, which will eventually lead to arthritis.' BHCP (S425): elbow dysplasia and cruciate ligament disease among the priorities; hip and elbow scoring required of Assured Breeders (breeder checklist). Not a Breed Watch point → no hips_hind_legs chip.

heart.value: heart conditions, especially dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and subaortic stenosis (SAS)
heart.quote: Heart conditions, especially DCM and SAS
heart.notes: BHCP (S425) priority list as returned; PDSA (S423) lists heart problems; PetMD (S424) DCM. Research only (no heart chip — not a Breed Watch point).

other_conditions.value: osteosarcoma (bone cancer), atopy, hypothyroidism, panosteitis, cystinuria (DNA test), cruciate ligament disease
other_conditions.notes: PDSA (S423) health list: osteosarcoma 'malignant bone cancer.'; atopy 'hypersensitivity to certain allergens, causing itching and skin trauma.'; hypothyroidism 'a condition in which there's a decrease in thyroid hormone production.'; panosteitis 'a painful, inflammatory bone disease.' BHCP (S425): osteosarcoma, cruciate ligament disease; cystinuria DNA test required of Assured Breeders. Research only.

shorter_lifespan.value: a shorter life than many breeds — usually around ten years
shorter_lifespan.notes: PDSA (S423); PetMD (S424) 'The average Newfoundland dog lifespan is 9–10 years.'; McMillan 2024 median 11.0 y (S123) — research only. Basis of the consider tag shorter_lifespan — a calm chip, no number.

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table of Coren's ranking (S35): rank 34 shared by the Field Spaniel, Newfoundland, Australian Terrier, American Staffordshire Terrier, Gordon Setter and Bearded Collie (row as returned), tier 'Above Average Working Dogs' (ranks 27–39). Coren's own article (S34) not re-read. Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

coren_tier.quote: Understanding of new commands: 15 to 25 repetitions.
coren_tier.notes: S35 tier 'Above Average Working Dogs': 'Obey first command: 70% of the time or better.'

training_notes.value: early, consistent obedience training; reward-based, patient
training_notes.quote: Early and consistent obedience training is a must.
training_notes.notes: PetMD (S424); PDSA (S423): 'Training will require patience, but can be achieved using reward-based techniques.' The game uses Coren's rank only.

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value — see proposed_game_parameters.newfoundland.learning_multiplier (1.2, runbook rule: Above average tier, rank 34).

general.value: large, deep-bodied, heavily boned, muscular; sweet-dispositioned; dignified
general.quote: The Newfoundland is a sweet-dispositioned dog that acts neither dull nor ill-tempered.
general.notes: AKC (S421). CKC (S422): large, deep-bodied and muscular with a dignified bearing; 'Large size is desirable but never at the expense of gait, symmetry and balance.'

colours.quote: Color: Negro, blanco y negro y castaño.
colours.notes: FCI (S420, Spanish): black ('Este es el color tradicional.'; a slight bronze tinge and white markings on chest, toes and tail tip permitted), white and black (Landseer — 'Esta variedad tiene un significado histórico para la raza.'; black head preferably with a white blaze, black saddle, black rump and upper tail), brown ('Este color va desde el chocolate hasta el bronce.'). FCI nomenclature (S419): Black, White and black, Brown. AKC (S421): 'Recognized Newfoundland colors are black, brown, gray, and white and black.' — gray is AKC only (S426); CKC (S422): black and Landseer only. The game lists the colours shared by the FCI and AKC: black, brown, white and black. Never gray (not FCI), never markings of another colour.

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). Black first with the highest weight ('the traditional colour', S420; the portrait default), then white and black (Landseer), brown.

coat.value: water-resistant double coat; moderately long, straight outer coat; soft dense undercoat
coat.quote: The adult Newfoundland has a flat, water-resistant, double coat that tends to fall back into place
coat.notes: AKC (S421), fragment. CKC (S422): outer coat moderately long and straight, a slight wave permitted, no curl; undercoat soft and dense (paraphrase). PDSA (S423): 'Coat length: Medium'.

ears.value: relatively small, triangular with rounded tips, lying close to the head
ears.quote: Ears are relatively small and triangular with rounded tips.
ears.notes: AKC (S421): 'They are set on the skull level with, or slightly above, the brow and lie close to the head.'

eyes.value: dark brown, relatively small, deep-set, wide apart; eyelids fitting closely (welfare)
eyes.quote: They are relatively small, deep-set, and spaced wide apart.
eyes.notes: AKC (S421): 'Eyes are dark brown.' Breed Watch (S425): loose eyelids → eyelids in normal contact in the portrait (welfare).

nose.value: clean-cut, broad, deep muzzle; moderately short; well-developed nostrils
nose.quote: The muzzle is clean-cut, broad throughout its length, and deep.
nose.notes: AKC (S421): 'The top of the muzzle is rounded, and the bridge, in profile, is straight or only slightly arched.' CKC (S422): moderately short, nostrils well developed (paraphrase). Moderate muzzle in the portrait.

tail.value: broad at the base and strong, reaching the hock, hanging straight or with a slight curve
tail.quote: The tail is broad at the base and strong.
tail.notes: AKC (S421): 'It has no kinks, and the distal bone reaches to the hock.'; 'When the dog is standing relaxed, its tail hangs straight or with a slight curve at the end.'

suitability._note: Source = PDSA (S423) and PetMD (S424). The RKC breed page (preferred: size of home / garden, grooming, sheds, lifespan band, town or country) returned a fetch error on 2026-10-20 → no rkc_* fields; large_home and apartment need the RKC page (runbook) → neither. Woodgreen and VCA not attempted.

pdsa_exercise.value: 1 hour per day (minimum)
pdsa_exercise.quote: Minimum exercise (per day): 1 hour
pdsa_exercise.notes: PDSA text: 'As adult dogs, Newfoundlands need around an hour of exercise daily'.

pdsa_grooming.value: daily, particularly when shedding
pdsa_grooming.quote: Grooming is a daily task, particularly when shedding.
pdsa_grooming.notes: PDSA (S423) → grooming 7× a week (M5-R13 rule 'daily' → 7, built); frequent_grooming. PetMD (S424) 'at least once a week' — a lower minimum, alternative.

petmd_grooming.value: thorough brushing at least once a week; coat blown twice a year
petmd_grooming.quote: The Newfie's long, coarse coat requires thorough brushing at least once a week to prevent matting and remove dead hair.
petmd_grooming.notes: PetMD (S424); 'Newfies shed year-round but usually "blow their coat" twice a year' (as returned).

pdsa_lifespan.notes: Basis of shorter_lifespan (runbook criterion: an A/B upper bound ≤ 10 years).

petmd_family.quote: A Newfoundland dog's personality makes the breed an outstanding family pet.

petmd_children.value: gets along well with children; supervise interactions with small kids
petmd_children.quote: They have a sweet disposition and gentle nature, so Newfies get along well with children, small pets, and other dogs.
petmd_children.notes: Basis of children and other_pets; caveat 'But just like with all dogs, supervise all interactions between small kids and Newfoundlands.' → never small_children.

petmd_other_pets.value: good roommates to other dogs and cats
petmd_other_pets.quote: good roommates to other dogs and cats

petmd_time_alone.value: some may develop separation anxiety when left alone
petmd_time_alone.quote: Because Newfoundland dogs are so loving, some may develop separation anxiety when left alone.

petmd_shedding.value: sheds year-round, blows the coat twice a year
petmd_shedding.quote: Newfies shed year-round but usually "blow their coat" twice a year
petmd_shedding.notes: PetMD (S424), as returned; PDSA (S423) 'particularly when shedding' agrees. Basis of sheds (no conflicting source).

petmd_bathing.value: bath roughly once a month, never more than once every two weeks
petmd_bathing.quote: Newfoundland dogs do best if bathed roughly once a month, but never more than once every two weeks.

petmd_ears.value: floppy ears trap debris and moisture; clean at the vet's recommendation
petmd_ears.quote: The Newfoundland's floppy ears can easily trap debris and moisture, leading to ear infections.
petmd_ears.notes: PetMD (S424): 'To prevent infections, clean your dog's ears at your vet's recommendation with a pet-specific ear cleaner.' → ear care ROADMAP M5-R20 (needs-david).

petmd_drooling.quote: Pet parents will also need to regularly wipe their Newfie's drool, which can get caught in their fur.
petmd_drooling.notes: Basis of drools (with PDSA S423); the wiping itself has no game mechanic (needs a new ROADMAP task — David).

dalmatian._note: Added 2026-10-21 (M5-R10-52, unattended run — appended after the Newfoundland: AKC 2024 No. 48 'Dalmatian', S174 full-list table '47 Newfoundland', '48 Dalmatian'). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-21 (PDSA and PetMD only in short quotes, 125-character limit; fragments marked as such); paraphrase only in notes. Sources S427–S434 (reused S8, S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45, S123, S174). No health percentages anywhere. RKC breed page reachable at the older address (S429): exercise 'More than 2 hours per day', grooming 'Once a week', Breed Watch Category 1. Lifespan: McMillan 2024 median 13.2 y via the Dogs Trust table (S123) — not provisional. Names: FCI 'DALMATIAN' (S427), AKC 'Dalmatian' (S174); Slovenian »dalmatinec« (Siol.net S434, tier C — not checked against KZS, open for David).

identity.value: FCI No. 153, Group 6 Section 3 (Related breeds), Croatia
identity.notes: FCI standard N° 153 (S428): 'Group 6 Scenthounds and related breeds.'; 'ORIGIN : Croatia.'; 'DATE OF PUBLICATION OF THE OFFICIAL VALID STANDARD: 13.10.2010.'; 'Hunting dog. Companion dog, family dog, suitable to be trained for various purposes.' FCI nomenclature (S427): 'DALMATINSKI PAS (153)', English name 'DALMATIAN', country of origin 'CROATIE', not subject to a working trial, definitive acceptance 01/01/1955, valid standard 13/10/2010. 'Croatia' must be in FCI_ORIGINS of the export (new origin HR). AKC name: Dalmatian (S174). Other names 'Carriage Dog; Spotted Coach Dog; Leopard Carriage Dog; Firehouse Dog; Plum Pudding Dog; Leopard-Spotted Dog' (S433, tier C).

size_class.notes: RKC breed page key facts (older address, S429), as returned ('Size: "Large"'). PDSA (S430) 'Size: Large' agrees.

fci.quote: Height at the withers: Males 56 – 62 cms. Females 54 – 60 cms.
fci.notes: FCI standard (S428). PDSA (S430) 'Average height: 56-61 cm' (one range); PetMD (S431) 'stand 19-24 inches tall' (48–61 cm); Wikipedia (S433, tier C) males 58–61 / females 56–58 cm — alternatives.

pdsa.notes: PDSA key facts (S430), one range for both sexes (stored per sex). Alternative to the FCI ranges.

PDSA key fact 'Average weight' (S430), one range for both sexes (stored per sex) — the game range. The FCI standard (S428) gives no weight. PetMD (S431) 'weigh 45-70 pounds' (20–32 kg) — alternatives.

alternatives.quote: stand 19-24 inches tall and weigh 45-70 pounds.
alternatives.notes: PetMD (S431); 45–70 lb = 20.4–31.8 kg (our conversion, rounded).

salt_category.notes: Category assignment by weight is ours (general_by_size.size_classes.salt_2017_bands_kg, S8): 18–27 kg spans the bands 15–25 and 25–40. Salt 2017 breed list not checked.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. PDSA 18–27 kg (S430) = 40–60 lb → 'Medium (24–59 pounds)'; the top touches 'Large (59–99 pounds): 15–18 months' (Hungarian Vizsla precedent). The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 120 min is reached at 12 months either way).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Dalmatian growth curve found.

median_uk.notes: McMillan et al. 2024 (Sci Rep) data as tabled by Dogs Trust (S123, columns Breed | Median Life Expectancy (Years) | Lower and Upper 95% CI | Total Number Individuals (Alive and Deceased) | Number Deceased Individuals), re-read 2026-10-21. Runbook first choice (McMillan 2024) → not provisional. Not in the Fig. 3 legend of the Author Correction (S54, checked 2026-10-21). Wikipedia (S433, tier C): 'A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.2 years for the Dalmatian.' — agrees.

rkc.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S429), as returned ('Lifespan: "Over 12 years"'). PDSA (S430) 'Average lifespan: Over 12 years' — the same. Not shorter_lifespan.

petmd.quote: Dalmatian dogs generally live 11–13 years.
petmd.notes: PetMD (S431), US alternative only.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × 13.2 y (McMillan 2024 via S123) → 0.75 × 13.2 = 9.9 y = 118.8 → 119 months (half up). Dogs Trust rule of thumb > 7 y = 84 months (S14). Not chosen: 0.75 × 12 y (RKC lower bound, S429) = 108.

adult.quote: Exercise: More than 2 hours per day
adult.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S429). PDSA (S430): 'Minimum exercise per day: 2 hours' (key fact) and 'Dalmatians are so high energy they need a minimum of two hours of exercise every day.' — agrees. PetMD (S431): 'a lot of daily exercise' — no minutes.

walks.value: at least two walks a day, ideally with a chance to run in a secure area
walks.quote: This needs to be done in at least two walks, ideally with a chance to run in a secure area.
walks.notes: PDSA (S430). The game counts the daily step total, not the number of walks, and has no off-lead runs → proposed_game_parameters.dalmatian.walk_pattern (needs-david: no mechanic, needs a new ROADMAP task — as the Shiba Inu / Rhodesian Ridgeback off-lead need).

temperament.value: pleasant, friendly, not shy, free from nervousness and aggression; high energy
temperament.quote: Pleasant temperament, friendly, not shy or hesitant, free from nervousness and aggression.
temperament.notes: FCI standard (S428). PDSA (S430): 'Dalmatians are so high energy …'; 'Dalmatians can be strong willed'; can be excitable when young (paraphrase).

family.value: great pets for active households; better suited to households with older children; always supervise with children
family.quote: They tend to be better suited to households with older children
family.notes: PDSA (S430): 'Dalmatians can be great pets for active households'; 'shouldn't be left unsupervised with children, vulnerable adults or older people'; 'It's important to always supervise your Dalmatian with children and vulnerable adults.' PetMD (S431): 'These playful pups can be good with kids and other pets, but small children must be taught how to treat dogs nicely.' → not_for_small_children (Vizsla / Ridgeback precedent); never children / small_children.

socialisation.value: socialise puppies early with other dogs, people and experiences
socialisation.quote: This is why socializing Dalmatian puppies early in life is so important.
socialisation.notes: PetMD (S431; adults can be aloof with new people and dogs — paraphrase). PDSA (S430): 'Socialising your Dalmatian as a puppy with lots of other dogs, different people and types of experiences' (fragment). → proposed_game_parameters.dalmatian.socialisation (DOG_SOCIALISATION row, M5-R17).

time_alone.value: needs company; never alone for more than four hours; can develop separation anxiety
time_alone.quote: Dalmatians need company so we would recommend a household where there is always someone at home with them
time_alone.notes: PDSA (S430): 'you should never leave your dog alone for more than four hours' (fragment); separation anxiety (paraphrase). PetMD (S431): 'Dalmatians shouldn’t be left alone for long periods of time—not only because they crave activity, but also because they can' (fragment). Basis of needs_company.

other_pets.value: may get the urge to chase; supervise with smaller pets
other_pets.quote: always supervise your Dalmatian with smaller pets and introductions should be done very carefully
other_pets.notes: PDSA (S430): 'As Dalmatians were not bred for hunting or herding' … 'even the most placid Dalmatian may get the urge to chase!' (fragments). Not a 'high prey drive' statement → no chases_small_pets (runbook: supervision advice alone is not enough). PetMD (S431) 'can be good with kids and other pets' — conflicting with PDSA → no other_pets.

chewing.notes: No breed-specific statement found → no chews_when_bored tag.

food_motivation.notes: No breed-specific statement found → no food_motivated_weight tag. PDSA (S430): two meals a day, treats under 10 % of the daily calories (general advice; the game's two adult meals stay).

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages are shown anywhere (PetMD's deafness figures from UFAW stay out). RKC Breed Watch Category 1 (S429) → no welfare chip. Breeder checklist: BAER hearing test and hip evaluation (AKC national breed club recommendation, K28; PDSA S430 'There is BAER testing for this.'; Kennel Club news S432).

breed_watch.value: RKC Breed Watch Category 1 — no points of concern
breed_watch.quote: Currently no points of concern specific to this breed have been identified for special attention by judges
breed_watch.notes: RKC breed page (S429). No welfare chip.

deafness.value: deafness (one or both ears) occurs; puppies can be hearing-tested (BAER)
deafness.quote: There is BAER testing for this.
deafness.notes: PDSA (S430) lists 'Deafness.' and 'There is BAER testing for this.' Kennel Club (S432): 'dogs can have their hearing checked using a BAER (Brainstem Auditory Evoked Response) test' (fragment) and 'Breeders can use the results of these tests to help them select unaffected breeding dogs' (fragment). FCI (S428) lists 'Deafness' as a disqualifying fault. PetMD (S431): deaf dogs may need hand signals (paraphrase). Register health key deafness (new) + breeder checklist hearing_baer.

urinary_stones.notes: PDSA (S430), as returned (spelling 'urolithisis' as on the page). PetMD (S431): 'Speak with your veterinarian before putting your Dalmatian on a low-purine diet.' — background (a vet's decision, no game mechanic). Wikipedia (S433, tier C): hyperuricemia with kidney and bladder stones. Register health key bladder_stones.

atopy.quote: Dalmatians are known to suffer from skin allergies
atopy.notes: PDSA (S430): atopy listed; check with a vet before using a dog shampoo (paraphrase). Not a Breed Watch point → no sensitive_skin chip (that chip follows the welfare rule). Register health key itchy_skin_allergy.

epilepsy.notes: PDSA (S430) health list: Epilepsy (name only as returned). Register health key epilepsy.

hip_dysplasia.notes: PDSA (S430) health list: Hip dysplasia (name only). AKC national breed club recommends 'Hip Evaluation' (K28). Not a Breed Watch point → no hips_hind_legs chip (breeder checklist instead). Register health key hip_dysplasia.

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table of Coren's ranking (S35, re-read 2026-10-21): rank 39 'Dalmatian' (the only breed at that rank), tier 'Above Average Working Dogs' (ranks 27–39). Coren's own article (S34) not re-read. Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

coren_tier.quote: Understanding of new commands: 15 to 25 repetitions.
coren_tier.notes: S35 tier 'Above Average Working Dogs': 'Obey first command: 70% of the time or better.'

training_notes.value: strong willed; positive, reward-based training; patience
training_notes.quote: Dalmatians can be strong willed
training_notes.notes: PDSA (S430): 'positive, reward-based training' (fragment); an accredited trainer for first-time owners (paraphrase). PetMD (S431): smart but independent and headstrong (paraphrase). The game uses Coren's rank only.

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value — see proposed_game_parameters.dalmatian.learning_multiplier (1.2, runbook rule: Above average tier, rank 39).

general.value: mesocephalic; rectangular, strong, muscled and distinctively spotted body; elegant movement
general.quote: The body is rectangular, strong, muscled and distinctively spotted.
general.notes: FCI (S428): 'Mesocephalic. Head prismatic form with hanging ears.'; 'The movement must be elegant.'

colours.quote: Black spotted variety with black spots, liver spotted variety with brown spots.
colours.notes: FCI (S428): 'The ground colour is pure white.'; spots symmetrical, clearly defined, 2–3 cm (liver around 2 cm), smaller on head and legs, preferably on the ears and tail; 'Patches and coloured areas are not desirable.' Disqualifying (S428): monocle / patching, tricolour, brindle, lemon, orange or blue spots, pure white without spots, blue eyes. Wikipedia (S433, tier C) names blue, brindle, mosaic, lemon / orange and tricolour as occasional non-standard colours — never in the game.

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). Black-spotted first with the highest weight (the portrait default), then liver-spotted.

coat.value: short, shiny, hard and dense
coat.quote: Short, shiny, hard and dense all over the body.
coat.notes: FCI (S428). RKC (S429) 'Coat length: Short'; disqualifying: 'Wirehaired or longhaired' (S428).

ears.value: hanging ears, spotted (never solid black or brown)
ears.quote: It is very important that the ears are spotted
ears.notes: FCI (S428): 'the ears must not be completely black or brown but black or brown spotted etc.' (fragment).

australian_cattle_dog._note: Added 2026-10-21 (M5-R10-53, unattended run — appended after the Dalmatian: AKC 2024 No. 49 'Australian Cattle Dog', S174 full-list table '48 Dalmatian', '49 Australian Cattle Dog'). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-21 (short quotes, 125-character limit; paraphrase only in notes). Sources S435–S441 (reused S8, S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45, S123, S174). No health percentages anywhere. FCI English standard PDF not in provenance → identity from the FCI nomenclature (S435); appearance and heights from the Kennel Club breed standard as reprinted by KUSA (S436). RKC breed page (older address, S437): exercise 'More than 2 hours per day', grooming 'Once a week', Breed Watch Category 1, health tests. Lifespan: McMillan 2024 median 14.0 y via the Dogs Trust table (S123) — not provisional (small sample: 117 dogs, 50 deceased). Names: FCI / AKC 'Australian Cattle Dog' (S435, S174); Slovenian »avstralski govedar« (Siol.net S441, tier C — not checked against KZS, open for David).

identity.value: FCI No. 287, Group 1 Section 2 (Cattledogs (except Swiss Cattledogs)), Australia
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S435, French page as returned): English name 'AUSTRALIAN CATTLE DOG', French 'BOUVIER AUSTRALIEN', group 'n°1 - Chiens de berger et de bouvier (sauf chiens de bouvier suisses)', section 'Chiens de bouvier (sauf chiens de bouvier suisses)', country of origin 'AUSTRALIE', not subject to a working trial, definitive acceptance 20/03/1972, valid standard 08/10/2012. 'Australia' must be in FCI_ORIGINS of the export (new origin AU). AKC name: Australian Cattle Dog (S174). Other names 'ACD, Cattle Dog, Blue/Red Heeler, Queensland Heeler' (S440, tier C).

size_class.notes: RKC breed page key facts (older address, S437), Size 'Medium' as returned. PDSA (S438) 'Size: Medium' agrees (its page sits under 'medium-dogs').

The FCI standard has the same heights (Italian ENCI copy, read only as a check — not a source). PDSA (S438) 'Average height: 43-51 cm' (one range); PetMD (S439) '17-20 inches tall' (43–51 cm) — alternatives.

pdsa.notes: PDSA key facts (S438), one range for both sexes (stored per sex). Alternative to the KC ranges.

alternatives.quote: Australian Cattle Dogs are medium-sized dogs weighing in at 35-50 pounds and 17-20 inches tall.

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Australian Cattle Dog growth curve found.

median_uk.notes: McMillan et al. 2024 (Sci Rep) data as tabled by Dogs Trust (S123, columns Breed | Median Life Expectancy (Years) | Lower and Upper 95% CI | Total Number Individuals (Alive and Deceased) | Number Deceased Individuals), read 2026-10-21. Runbook first choice (McMillan 2024) → not provisional; small sample (117 dogs, 50 deceased) noted. rkc.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S437), Lifespan 'Over 10 years' as returned. PDSA (S438) 'Average lifespan: Over 10 years' — the same. Not shorter_lifespan.

adult.quote: More than 2 hours per day
adult.notes: RKC breed page key facts (S437), Exercise. PDSA (S438): 'Minimum exercise: 2 hours per day' (key fact) and 'Australian Cattle Dogs have high energy levels and will need over 2 hours exercise per day.' — agrees. PetMD (S439): 'Running/jogging daily for at least 45 minutes' among suggested activities — not a daily total (alternative only).

energy.quote: Australian Cattle Dogs have high energy levels and will need over 2 hours exercise per day.
energy.notes: PDSA (S438). Basis of active_family (with the RKC exercise).

temperament.quote: Alert, intelligent, watchful, courageous, trustworthy, devoted to its work.

family.quote: Australian Cattle Dogs can be good family dogs, and can be raised with children.
family.notes: PetMD (S439): '… should be supervised when around young children' (fragment); 'They will try to herd small children, and some adults, so supervision is needed.' PDSA (S438): 'Due to their strong herding instinct, they may nip at the heels of running children' → may_herd_children; family_pet from PetMD; never small_children; not children (herding caveat — Australian Shepherd precedent).

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages are shown anywhere. RKC Breed Watch Category 1 (S437) → no welfare chip. Breeder checklist: DNA prcd-PRA, BVA/KC/ISDS eye scheme, BVA/KC hip and elbow schemes, BAER, inbreeding calculators (RKC S437).

breed_watch.quote: Currently no points of concern specific to this breed have been identified for special attention by judges
breed_watch.notes: RKC breed page (S437). No welfare chip.

pra.notes: PetMD (S439): progressive retinal atrophy (PRA), an inherited eye disease that leads to blindness (paraphrase as returned). RKC (S437) 'DNA test - prcd-PRA' (priority). Register health key pra_eye_disease.

other_pets.value: really high prey drive — not recommended with smaller pets; may get along with a cat it grew up with (supervise)
other_pets.quote: Whippets have a really high prey drive, so we wouldn’t recommend keeping them with smaller pets.
other_pets.notes: PDSA (S444); 'Your Whippet may get along with a cat they have grown up with, but you should always supervise them together.' PetMD (S445): 'Whippets have been bred for centuries to chase after prey.' Basis of chases_small_pets; never other_pets.

socialisation.value: socialise with other dogs from a young age; otherwise can be shy with new people
socialisation.quote: As long as you socialise your Whippet with other dogs from a young age they should be fine meeting them out and about.
socialisation.notes: PDSA (S444): socialise from a young age with lots of different experiences, people and dogs (paraphrase). PetMD (S445): 'Training and socialization must start young for Whippet puppies.' → proposed_game_parameters.whippet.socialisation (DOG_SOCIALISATION row, M5-R17).

chewing.notes: PDSA (S444): when left alone all day they may start destroying things (paraphrase) — not chewing → no chews_when_bored tag.

food_motivation.notes: No breed-specific statement found → no food_motivated_weight tag.

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages are shown anywhere. RKC Breed Watch category not fetched (RKC page unreachable) → no welfare chip; the PDSA page names no Kennel Club category. WSAVA / IPFD (Bonnett 2022, read only as a check, not numbered): 'Whippets are a relatively healthy breed'. Breeder checklist: breed club cardiac exam, ophthalmologist evaluation and BAER (AKC K30); Kennel Club advice to auscultate breeding stock (K31).

pra.value: progressive retinal atrophy — gradual loss of sight; parents should be screened
pra.quote: Progressive Retinal atrophy – gradual loss of sight over several months or years. Parents should be screened for this.
pra.notes: PDSA (S444) health list. Register health key pra_eye_disease.

mitral_valve.quote: Mitral valve disease – a heart condition where the valve is weakened allowing blood to flow back into the heart.
mitral_valve.notes: PDSA (S444) health list; PetMD (S445) names mitral valve disease. Kennel Club statement on Whippet heart health (via The Whippet Club, 2023, breeder-checklist K31): 'There is currently no official heart testing scheme for Whippets in the UK.' Not a fetched Breed Watch point → no heart_and_spine chip. Register health key mitral_valve_disease (new).

immune_mediated.notes: PDSA (S444) health list: immune-mediated problems, where the body reacts against its own cells, such as immune-mediated haemolytic anaemia (paraphrase as returned). Register health key autoimmune_conditions.

gdv.notes: PetMD (S445) names gastric dilatation and volvulus (GDV) among the breed's conditions (as returned, no full sentence). PDSA (S444) advises a gap between eating and exercising (exercise.after_meals). Register health key bloat_gdv.

von_willebrand.notes: PetMD (S445) names von Willebrand disease (as returned, no full sentence). Register health key bleeding_disorder_vwd.

deafness.notes: PetMD (S445) names deafness (as returned, no full sentence); the AKC national breed club recommends BAER testing (K30). Register health key deafness.

skin_injuries.value: thin skin prone to cuts; bones can be damaged on uneven ground
skin_injuries.quote: Whippets can be prone to cutting their skin on thorns, twigs or any other sharp objects.
skin_injuries.notes: PDSA (S444); PetMD (S445) names lacerations. Background for parents (not a register health key).

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table of Coren's ranking (S35, re-read 2026-10-21): rank 51 'Whippet' (tied with Shar Pei and Wire Fox Terrier), tier 'Average Working/Obedience Intelligence' (ranks 40–54). Coren's own article (S34) not re-read. Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

coren_tier.quote: Understanding of new commands: 25 to 40 repetitions.
coren_tier.notes: S35 tier 'Average Working/Obedience Intelligence': 'Obey first command: 50% of the time or better.'

training_notes.value: can be a little slow to learn; start positive, reward-based training early; be patient and consistent
training_notes.quote: Whippets have a reputation to be a little slow learning new things, even though they are thought to be fairly clever dogs.
training_notes.notes: PDSA (S444): 'Their medium size makes them popular with first-time owners although training a Whippet can take some time!' — popularity, not a suitability statement → no first_time_owner tag. The game uses Coren's rank only.

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value — see proposed_game_parameters.whippet.learning_multiplier (1.0, runbook rule: Average tier, rank 51).

general.value: balanced combination of muscular power and strength with elegance and grace of outline; built for maximum speed
general.quote: Balanced combination of muscular power and strength with elegance and grace of outline.
general.notes: Kennel Club breed standard (S443), General appearance. A lean sighthound with a deep chest and an arched loin (standard, paraphrase) — never emaciated in the game.

colours.quote: Any colour or mixture of colours, except merle.
colours.notes: Kennel Club standard (S443): every colour or mixture except merle (the Kennel Club stopped registering merle Whippets in 2019 — Wikipedia S446, tier C). The listed colours are common examples within the standard (Wikipedia S446: 'ranging from solid black to solid white, with red, fawn, brindle, blue, or cream'); never merle in the game.

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). Fawn first with the highest weight (the portrait default), then brindle, black, blue and the white particolours.

coat.value: fine, short, close in texture
coat.quote: Fine, short, close in texture.
coat.notes: Kennel Club standard (S443). PDSA (S444) 'Coat length: Short'; sensitive skin → soft brush (S444).

head.value: long and lean, flat on top, tapering to the muzzle with a slight stop
head.quote: Long and lean, flat on top, tapering to muzzle with slight stop, rather wide between the eyes,

ears.value: rose-shaped, small, fine in texture
ears.quote: Rose-shaped, small, fine in texture.
ears.notes: Kennel Club standard (S443).

eyes.value: oval, bright, very alert expression
eyes.quote: Oval, bright, expression very alert.
eyes.notes: Kennel Club standard (S443).

tail.value: long, tapering, reaching at least to the hock; no feathering
tail.quote: No feathering. Long, tapering, reaching at least to the hock.
tail.notes: Kennel Club standard (S443).

suitability._note: Source = PDSA (S444) and PetMD (S445). The RKC breed page (preferred: size of home / garden, grooming, sheds, lifespan band, town or country) could not be fetched on 2026-10-21 → no rkc_* fields; large_home and apartment need the RKC page (runbook) → neither. Woodgreen and VCA not attempted.

pdsa_exercise.value: 1 hour per day (minimum)
pdsa_exercise.quote: Minimum exercise (per day): 1 hour
pdsa_exercise.notes: PDSA text: 'Your Whippet will need a minimum of an hour exercise every day.'

pdsa_grooming.value: a weekly brush; soft brush (sensitive skin)
pdsa_grooming.quote: Whippets have short fur, so a weekly brush is usually more than enough to keep it in good condition.
pdsa_grooming.notes: PDSA (S444): 'They do have quite sensitive skin, though, so it's better to look for a soft brush for them.' → brushing 1× a week (M5-R13 rule 'Once a week' → 1, built).

pdsa_shedding.value: sheds, but fairly minimal compared to other breeds
pdsa_shedding.quote: Your Whippet will shed, but this is fairly minimal compared to other breeds.
pdsa_shedding.notes: PDSA (S444), more in spring and autumn (paraphrase). PetMD (S445) 'This dog doesn't shed very much.' low_shedding only from RKC 'Sheds: No' (precedent) and the dog sheds → neither sheds nor low_shedding.

pdsa_family.value: a popular choice for families
pdsa_family.quote: Whippets are a popular choice for families as they are so calm and gentle around children.
pdsa_family.notes: Basis of family_pet and children (explicit statement; supervision caveat in behaviour.family).

pdsa_children.value: a home with slightly older children recommended
pdsa_children.quote: we'd recommend a home with slightly older children
pdsa_children.notes: PDSA (S444), fragment (the full sentence is longer than the quote limit; it continues: children who can recognise when the dog needs space — paraphrase). Basis of sensitive_older_children (new chip).

pdsa_company.value: can get very stressed when left alone
pdsa_company.quote: They form strong bonds with their owners and can get very stressed when left alone for any length of time.
pdsa_company.notes: PDSA (S444): only get one if someone will be at home with them all day (paraphrase). Basis of needs_company (with behaviour.time_alone).

pdsa_cold_coat.value: may need a coat in winter; thick, soft, snug bedding
pdsa_cold_coat.quote: your Whippet might need a coat over the winter months
pdsa_cold_coat.notes: PDSA (S444), fragment (lean, little body fat); 'Whippets have prominent bones, such as their elbows, shoulders and hips so prefer thick, soft snug bedding to avoid sores.' PetMD (S445): they 'generally don't do well in cold or wet weather'. The game has no weather / coat / bedding mechanic → open for David (needs a new ROADMAP task).

petmd_children.value: loud, rambunctious little kids might be too much
petmd_children.quote: A home with loud, rambunctious little kids might be too much for these sensitive pups.
petmd_children.notes: PetMD (S445); good with kids when 'the child and dog are introduced slowly' (fragment). Supports sensitive_older_children.

petmd_grooming.value: weekly grooming check; won't need to be brushed often
petmd_grooming.quote: Grooming your Whippet on a weekly basis
petmd_grooming.notes: PetMD (S445), fragment; agrees with PDSA's weekly brush.

wirehaired_pointing_griffon._note: Added 2026-10-22 (M5-R10-55, unattended run — appended after the Whippet: AKC 2024 No. 51 'Wirehaired Pointing Griffon', S174 full-list table '50 Whippet', '51 Wirehaired Pointing Griffon', '52 Chesapeake Bay Retriever'). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-22 (short quotes, 125-character limit; fragments marked as such); paraphrase only in notes. Sources S448–S456 (reused S8, S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45, S123, S174). No health percentages anywhere. RKC Breeds A–Z page 'Korthals Griffon (Imp)' (S450) reached: key facts and health-testing list; no breed-specific temperament text and no Breed Watch category on the page. Identity from the FCI nomenclature (S448); appearance, heights and temperament from the FCI standard (S449), AKC standard (S451) and UKC standard (S452) — none gives a weight → weight from PetMD (S453, DVM author). Lifespan: the Dogs Trust McMillan 2024 table (S123) has no Korthals / Wirehaired Pointing Griffon row and no VetCompass median was found → RKC lower bound 'Over 10 years' (runbook order; Siberian Husky precedent). Names: FCI 'WIRE-HAIRED POINTING GRIFFON KORTHALS' (S448), AKC 'Wirehaired Pointing Griffon' (S174, S451), RKC 'Korthals Griffon' (S450); Slovenian »francoski ostrodlaki ptičar« (smrcek.si S456, tier C — not checked against KZS, open for David).

identity.value: FCI No. 107, Group 7 Section 1 (Continental Pointing Dogs), France
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S448): number '107', group 'n°7 - Pointing Dogs', section 'Continental Pointing Dogs' (section 1 of group 7 in the FCI nomenclature; the page gives no section number), country of origin 'FRANCE'; French name 'GRIFFON A POIL DUR KORTHALS', German 'FRANZÖSISCHER RAUHHAARIGER VORSTEHHUND (KORTHALS)'; standard dated '9/5/2023'. 'France' is already in FCI_ORIGINS (FR). AKC name 'Wirehaired Pointing Griffon' (S174, S451); RKC 'Korthals Griffon (Imp)' (S450). Wikipedia (S455, tier C): other names 'Korthals Griffon', 'Griffon d'arrêt à poil dur Korthals'.

size_class.notes: RKC breed page key fact (S450). The FCI standard (S449) says 'rustic of medium size'; PetMD (S453) 'As a medium-size dog' — the RKC field is the runbook's preferred source.

fci.quote: About 55 to 60 cm for males and 50 to 55 cm for females.
fci.notes: FCI standard (S449), Size (as returned). AKC standard (S451) 'Size-22 to 24 inches for males, 20 to 22 inches for females.' (56–61 / 51–56 cm); UKC (S452) males 21½–23½ in, females 19½–21½ in; PetMD (S453) 20–24 inches; VCA (S454) '20 to 24 inches' — alternatives.

petmd.quote: As a medium-size dog, Wirehaired Pointing Griffons stand 20–24 inches tall and weigh 35–70 pounds.
petmd.notes: PetMD (S453, V. LaMon, DVM), one range for both sexes (stored per sex); 35–70 lb = 15.9–31.8 kg → 16–32 kg (our conversion, rounded) — the game range. The FCI (S449), AKC (S451) and UKC (S452) standards give no weight. VCA (S454) '50 to 60 pounds' (23–27 kg) — alternative inside this range. Wikipedia (S455, tier C) '35-50 pounds for females and 50-70 pounds for males' agrees.

alternatives.quote: 50 to 60 pounds
alternatives.notes: VCA quick facts (S454); 50–60 lb = 22.7–27.2 kg (our conversion, rounded).

salt_category.notes: Category assignment by weight is ours (general_by_size.size_classes.salt_2017_bands_kg, S8): 16–32 kg spans the 15–25 and 25–40 bands. Salt 2017 breed list not checked.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. VCA 50–60 lb (S454) lies in 'Medium (24–59 pounds)'; PetMD's upper 70 lb (S453) would be the Large class (15–18 months) — alternative. The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 120 min is reached at 12 months).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Wirehaired Pointing Griffon growth curve found.

rkc.notes: RKC breed page key fact (S450). PetMD (S453): 'They have a typical lifespan of 12–15 years.'; VCA (S454) '10 to 12 years' — alternatives (US pages, no median).

mcmillan_2024.notes: Dogs Trust table of McMillan et al. 2024 data (S123, read 2026-10-22): no Korthals Griffon / Wirehaired Pointing Griffon row (the only Griffon row is 'Petite Basset Griffon Vendeen'). No VetCompass median found (search 2026-10-22). UNSOURCED value.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × RKC lower bound 10 y (S450) → 0.75 × 10 = 7.5 y = 90 months. Runbook order: McMillan 2024 (no row in S123) → VetCompass median (none found) → RKC lower bound. Alternative: 84 (Dogs Trust > 7 y, S14). Not chosen: 0.75 × 12 y (PetMD lower bound, S453) = 108.

adult.quote: Exercise: More than 2 hours per day
adult.notes: RKC breed page key fact (S450) — the runbook's preferred source. PetMD (S453): 'At a minimum, Wirehaired Pointing Griffons need 20 minutes of activity twice a day.' (40 min, a minimum) — alternative; VCA (S454) 'High - needs to walk every day, plus some running and play' (no minutes).

daily_text.value: high — walk every day, plus some running and play
daily_text.quote: High - needs to walk every day, plus some running and play
daily_text.notes: VCA quick facts (S454). A versatile hunting dog (FCI S449 'Essentially a versatile pointing dog.').

temperament.value: gentle and proud, very attached to his master; outgoing, eager to please, trustworthy
temperament.quote: Gentle and proud, excellent hunter, very attached to his master and his territory which he guards with vigilance.
temperament.notes: FCI standard (S449), Behaviour / temperament. AKC standard (S451): 'He is outgoing, shows a tremendous willingness to please and is trustworthy.' UKC (S452): a biddable, affectionate nature (paraphrase).

family.value: very gentle with children; suitable as a family pet; patient and gentle with children when socialised as puppies
family.quote: Very gentle with children.
family.notes: FCI standard (S449). UKC standard (S452): 'which makes it suitable as a family pet and guardian' (fragment). PetMD (S453): 'Wirehaired Pointing Griffons are generally patient and gentle with children when socialized as puppies.' (condition kept here). VCA (S454) 'With Kids: Excellent'. → family_pet, children; not small_children (PetMD's socialisation condition).

time_alone.value: do not like being left alone for long; VCA: fine with lots of exercise first
time_alone.quote: They love spending time with their humans and do not appreciate being left alone for extended periods.
time_alone.notes: PetMD (S453); leaving a Griff alone too often without stimulation can lead to separation-related anxiety (paraphrase). VCA (S454) 'Home Alone: Fine with lots of exercise first' — the sources differ → neither needs_company nor often_alone.

other_pets.value: strong prey drive — may chase cats and rabbits; usually fine with other friendly dogs
other_pets.quote: Their hunting history also means these pups can have a strong prey drive.
other_pets.notes: PetMD (S453): 'A Griff might see smaller animals, such as cats and rabbits, as something to chase.' VCA (S454): 'Cats may prove too great a temptation, as this dog can't resist a boisterous romp around the house.' and 'Most Wirehaired Pointing Griffons are social enough to fit well into a household with other friendly dogs,' (fragment). Basis of chases_small_pets; never other_pets.

socialisation.value: socialise as a puppy
socialisation.quote: Wirehaired Pointing Griffons are generally patient and gentle with children when socialized as puppies.
socialisation.notes: PetMD (S453), a condition ('when socialized as puppies'). VCA (S454): 'Some members of the breed can be aloof with strangers.' → proposed_game_parameters.wirehaired_pointing_griffon.socialisation (DOG_SOCIALISATION row, M5-R17).

chewing.notes: PetMD (S453): too little stimulation can lead to destructive behaviour (paraphrase) — not chewing → no chews_when_bored tag.

food_motivation.notes: No breed-specific statement found → no food_motivated_weight tag.

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages are shown anywhere. The RKC page (S450) shows no Breed Watch category and no welfare statement → no welfare chip. PetMD (S453): the breed is 'generally a healthy breed' (fragment). Breeder checklist: RKC best practice BVA/KC hip and elbow schemes, minimum 'Prioritising genetic diversity' (S450).

hip_dysplasia.notes: PetMD (S453) names hip dysplasia (an inherited loose hip joint that can lead to arthritis — paraphrase, sentence longer than the quote limit); RKC best practice: hip and elbow scoring of the parents (S450). Register health key hip_dysplasia.

pra.value: progressive retinal atrophy — inherited retinal disorders leading to blindness
pra.notes: PetMD (S453) names progressive retinal atrophy (paraphrase — sentence longer than the quote limit). Register health key pra_eye_disease.

cataracts.quote: Cataracts occur more frequently in Wirehaired Pointing Griffons than in many other dog breeds.
cataracts.notes: PetMD (S453). A comparison without a number — never shown as a statistic. Register health key cataracts.

gdv.quote: Using a slow feeder bowl can help to pace your Griff when they eat, which can help prevent bloat and GDV.
gdv.notes: PetMD (S453); also 'Do not feed your Wirehaired Pointing Griffon from a raised food bowl, as this can increase the risk of bloat and GDV.' and smaller, more frequent meals for older deep-chested dogs. No gap between eating and exercise is given → no meal_exercise_gap row (runbook: quote required). Register health key bloat_gdv.

eyelids.value: entropion or ectropion (eyelids turned in or out)
eyelids.quote: Occasionally, entropion or ectropion occurs – don't buy a pup that will suffer from painful eyes.

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table of Coren's ranking (S35, re-read 2026-10-22): rank 46 'Wirehaired Pointing Griffon' (tied with Tibetan Spaniel, English Foxhound, Otterhound, Jack Russell Terrier, American Foxhound and Greyhound), tier 'Average Working/Obedience Intelligence' (ranks 40–54). Coren's own article (S34) not re-read. Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

coren_tier.quote: Understanding of new commands: 25 to 40 repetitions.
coren_tier.notes: S35 tier 'Average Working/Obedience Intelligence': 'Obey first command: 50% of the time or better.'

training_notes.value: eager to please, trustworthy
training_notes.quote: He is outgoing, shows a tremendous willingness to please and is trustworthy.
training_notes.notes: AKC standard (S451). The game uses Coren's rank only.

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value — see proposed_game_parameters.wirehaired_pointing_griffon.learning_multiplier (1.0, runbook rule: Average tier, rank 46).

general.value: vigorous, rustic dog of medium size, longer than tall; long, square muzzle
general.quote: Vigorous dog, rustic of medium size. Longer than tall. The skull is not too broad. The muzzle is long and square.
general.notes: FCI standard (S449), General appearance. AKC standard (S451): 'Medium sized, with a noble, square-shaped head, strong of limb.'

colours.quote: Preferably steel grey shade with brown (liver) patches or self-coloured brown (liver) coat.
colours.notes: FCI standard (S449): also 'Frequently liver-roan or a close mixture of brown (liver) and white hairs.' and 'Equally permissible white and brown and white and orange coats.' AKC standard (S451): 'A black coat disqualifies.'; UKC (S452) disqualifies 'Black coat or nose color.' → never black in the game; nose always brown.

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). Steel grey with liver patches first with the highest weight (the standard's preferred colour, the portrait default), then liver roan, solid liver, white and liver, white and orange.

coat.value: harsh, coarse, wiry outer coat of medium length, never curly or woolly; soft dense undercoat
coat.quote: Harsh and coarse, reminding of the touch of a wild boar's bristles. Never curly or woolly.
coat.notes: FCI standard (S449). AKC standard (S451): 'The outer coat is medium length, straight and wiry, never curly or woolly.' with a soft, dense undercoat (paraphrase). RKC (S450) 'Coat length: Medium'.

head.value: long, square muzzle of the same length as the skull; nose always brown; moustache and eyebrows
head.quote: Long and square, of the same length as the skull, bridge of the nose slightly convex.

ears.value: medium-sized, flat, set level with the eyes
ears.quote: Of medium size, not curled inwards, flat, set on level line with the eyes,
ears.notes: FCI standard (S449, fragment as returned).

eyes.value: large, rounded, dark yellow or brown, very intelligent expression
eyes.quote: Dark yellow or brown, large, rounded surmounted but not covered by the eyebrows, very intelligent expression.
eyes.notes: FCI standard (S449).

tail.value: carried horizontally or with the tip slightly raised, thick harsh hair, no fringing
tail.quote: Carried horizontally or with the tip slightly raised, covered with thick hair but without fringing,
tail.notes: FCI standard (S449, fragment). The standards say the tail is generally docked (FCI 'generally should be docked by a third or a quarter'; AKC 'docked by one-third to one-half length'); the game and the portrait show a natural tail (Claude 2026-10-22, moderate depiction; docking is not shown).

suitability._note: Source = RKC breed page (S450), PetMD (S453), VCA (S454), UKC standard (S452). RKC key facts reached on 2026-10-22.

rkc_exercise.quote: Exercise: More than 2 hours per day
rkc_exercise.notes: RKC key fact (S450). Basis of active_family and long_daily_exercise.

rkc_size_of_home.notes: RKC key fact (S450). Basis of large_home.

rkc_grooming.quote: Grooming: More than once a week
rkc_grooming.notes: RKC key fact (S450) — no number → the grooming rule takes the most specific number of another A/B source: VCA (S454) 'weekly brushing' → 1 (Brittany precedent).

rkc_shedding.notes: RKC key fact (S450). PetMD (S453): 'The Wirehaired Pointing Griffon is a low-shedding breed.'; VCA (S454) 'minimal shedding' — the sources differ → neither sheds nor low_shedding.

rkc_lifespan.notes: RKC key fact (S450). Not shorter_lifespan (that needs 'Under 10 years').

ukc_family.value: suitable as a family pet and guardian
ukc_family.quote: which makes it suitable as a family pet and guardian
ukc_family.notes: UKC standard (S452), Characteristics (fragment): a biddable, affectionate nature (paraphrase). Basis of family_pet.

vca_grooming.quote: The Wirehaired Pointing Griffon is an easy-care pet, demanding only weekly brushing, with a bonus of minimal shedding.
vca_grooming.notes: VCA (S454). Its quick-facts table says 'Brush a few times a week' (no number). PetMD (S453): weekly brushing, some dogs need hand stripping (paraphrase — sentence longer than the quote limit). → brushing 1× a week (M5-R13 rule).

vca_children.notes: VCA quick facts (S454) 'With Kids'; the Ideal Owner table adds 'Any age is fine.' Supports children; small_children not proposed (PetMD's socialisation condition, S453).

chesapeake_bay_retriever._note: Added 2026-10-22 (M5-R10-56, unattended run — appended after the Wirehaired Pointing Griffon: AKC 2024 No. 52 'Chesapeake Bay Retriever', S174 full-list table as recorded on 2026-10-21 / 2026-10-22 ('51 Wirehaired Pointing Griffon', '52 Chesapeake Bay Retriever'; the AKC page was not re-fetched — refused by the fetch tool as not in provenance). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-22 (short quotes, 125-character limit; fragments marked as such); paraphrase only in notes. Sources S457–S462 (reused S8, S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45, S123, S174). No health percentages anywhere. RKC Breeds A–Z page 'Retriever (Chesapeake Bay)' (S459) reached: key facts, Breed Watch Category 1 and the health-testing list; no breed-specific temperament text. identity.value: FCI No. 263, Group 8 Section 1 (Retrievers), USA
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S457): number '263', group 'n°8 - Retrievers - Flushing Dogs - Water Dogs', section 'Retrievers' (section 1 of group 8; the page gives no section number), country of origin 'UNITED STATES OF AMERICA'; French 'RETRIEVER DE LA BAIE DE CHESAPEAKE'; English standard published 3/12/1999 (official valid standard 2/14/1995).
