size_class.notes: RKC breed page key fact (S459). FCI standard (S458): 'Size and substance should not be excessive as this is a working retriever of an active nature.'

fci.quote: Males should measure 23 to 26 inches; (58 - 66cm).
fci.notes: FCI standard No. 263 (S458, KUSA copy), Size; females 'Females should measure 21 to 24 inches; (53 - 61cm).' VCA (S460) '21 - 26 inches' and PetMD (S461) 21–26 inches — alternatives.

fci.quote: Males should weigh 65 to 80 pounds (29,5-36,5kg).
fci.notes: FCI standard No. 263 (S458, KUSA copy); females 'Females should weigh 55 to 70 pounds (25-32kg).' The game range 25–36.5 kg spans both sexes. VCA (S460) '55 - 80 pounds' and PetMD (S461) 55–80 pounds agree.

salt_category.notes: Category assignment by weight is ours (general_by_size.size_classes.salt_2017_bands_kg, S8): 25–36.5 kg spans the bands. Salt 2017 breed list not checked.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific: FCI males 65–80 lb (S458) are 'Large (59–99 pounds)'; females 55–70 lb straddle Medium (24–59 lb: 12–15 months) and Large (Labrador Retriever precedent). The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 120 min is reached at 12 months).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Chesapeake Bay Retriever growth curve found.

rkc.notes: RKC breed page key fact (S459). VCA (S460): '10 - 13 years' — alternative (US page, no median). Wikipedia (S462, tier C): a UK Kennel Club survey median of 10.75 years (KC Purebred Dog Health Survey, not fetched) — background only.

mcmillan_2024.notes: Dogs Trust table of McMillan et al. 2024 data (S123): not fetchable on 2026-10-22 (refused by the fetch tool as not in provenance); the paper on PMC (S54 / PMC10834484) returned a captcha page. Whether the table has a Chesapeake row is unknown → open for David. Teng et al. 2022 (PMC9050668) has no breed row (gundog group only). UNSOURCED value.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × RKC lower bound 10 y (S459) → 0.75 × 10 = 7.5 y = 90 months. Runbook order: McMillan 2024 (table not reachable) → VetCompass median (none found) → RKC lower bound. Alternative: 84 (Dogs Trust > 7 y, S14). Not chosen: 0.75 × 10.75 y (KC survey via Wikipedia, tier C) = 97.

adult.quote: Exercise: More than 2 hours per day
adult.notes: RKC breed page key fact (S459) — the runbook's preferred source. VCA (S460): 'Needs daily walks, jogs, hikes or play sessions.' (no minutes); PetMD (S461): 'pet parents should be dedicated to providing constant exercise and stimulation.' (fragment, no minutes).

daily_text.value: daily walks, jogs, hikes or play sessions
daily_text.quote: Needs daily walks, jogs, hikes or play sessions.
daily_text.notes: VCA (S460). A working water retriever (FCI S458 'Equally proficient on land and in the water').

temperament.value: bright, cheerful and extremely affectionate; adventurous and loyal; may be aloof towards strangers
temperament.quote: Chesapeake Bay Retrievers have a bright and cheerful disposition.
temperament.notes: PetMD (S461); also 'extremely affectionate' (fragment). VCA (S460): 'Makes an adventurous and loyal companion.' and 'Aloof toward strangers.' FCI standard (S458): 'Extreme shyness or extreme aggressive tendencies are not desirable in the breed' (fragment). AKC (S174 is the ranking only — the AKC breed page, not numbered, calls the breed 'loyal, upbeat, affectionate, and tireless').

family.value: playful and generally good with children; a great family addition with proper introductions and socialisation
family.quote: Playful and generally good with children.
family.notes: VCA (S460). PetMD (S461): 'With proper introductions and socialization, Chessies would be a great addition to a family.' (condition kept here) and 'Interactions between kids and all dogs, Chessie or not, should be supervised.' → family_pet, children (supervision caveat); not small_children.

time_alone.value: becomes destructive and mischievous if left alone for too long
time_alone.quote: will become destructive and mischievous if they're not stimulated properly or if they're left alone for too long.
time_alone.notes: PetMD (S461, fragment). VCA (S460) has no home-alone statement. Basis of needs_company.

other_pets.value: gets along fairly well with other pets and dogs
other_pets.quote: Gets along fairly well with other pets and dogs.
other_pets.notes: VCA (S460). 'Fairly well' is a qualified statement → no other_pets chip. No source names a high prey drive (PetMD S461: bred to help hunt ducks and other birds — paraphrase) → no chases_small_pets.

socialisation.value: socialise properly as a puppy
socialisation.quote: With proper introductions and socialization, Chessies would be a great addition to a family.
socialisation.notes: PetMD (S461), a condition. VCA (S460): 'Aloof toward strangers.' Wikipedia (S462, tier C): 'Chesapeake Bay Retrievers can make excellent family dogs when socialized properly.' → proposed_game_parameters.chesapeake_bay_retriever.socialisation (DOG_SOCIALISATION row, M5-R17).

chewing.notes: PetMD (S461): 'If they're bored, they can become destructive.' (fragment) — not chewing → no chews_when_bored tag.

food_motivation.notes: No breed-specific statement found → no food_motivated_weight tag. VCA (S460): fed so they do not become overweight (paraphrase, general advice).

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages are shown anywhere. RKC Breed Watch Category 1 (S459: no breed-specific points of concern) → no welfare chip. Breeder checklist: RKC minimum genetic diversity, BVA/RKC elbow and hip schemes, DNA test DM; best practice DNA prcd-PRA, BVA/RKC/ISDS eye scheme (S459).

hip_elbow.quote: Hip dysplasia stems from the loosening of the hip joints.
hip_elbow.notes: PetMD (S461). RKC minimum tests: 'Hip testing (for hip dysplasia) using the BVA/RKC Hip Dysplasia Scheme' and 'Elbow testing (for elbow dysplasia) using the BVA/RKC Elbow Dysplasia Scheme' (S459). Register health key hip_elbow_dysplasia.

degenerative_myelopathy.value: degenerative myelopathy (DM) — a spinal cord disease that slowly weakens the hind legs
degenerative_myelopathy.quote: Due to the high prevalence of degenerative myelopathy in the Retriever (Chesapeake Bay), it’s important that breeders
degenerative_myelopathy.notes: RKC breed page (S459, fragment — the first 120 characters of a longer sentence); RKC minimum test 'DNA test for Degenerative myelopathy (DM).' Wikipedia (S462, tier C): one of the breeds more commonly affected. A prevalence statement without a number — never shown as a statistic. Register health key degenerative_myelopathy.

pra.value: progressive retinal atrophy (prcd-PRA) — an inherited eye disease that can lead to blindness
pra.quote: PRA causes cells in the eyes to eventually disintegrate.
pra.notes: PetMD (S461). RKC best practice: 'DNA test for Progressive retinal atrophy (prcd-PRA)' and 'Eye testing using the BVA/RKC/ISDS Eye Scheme' (S459). Register health key pra_eye_disease.

cataracts.notes: PetMD (S461) names cataracts (no short sentence returned — paraphrase). Wikipedia (S462, tier C) also lists cataract. Register health key cataracts.

eic.quote: This neuromuscular condition can cause Chessies to collapse.
eic.notes: PetMD (S461): an inherited neuromuscular condition; collapse after intense exercise (paraphrase). Wikipedia (S462, tier C) lists it too. New register health key exercise_induced_collapse (calm sentence, no numbers). No game mechanic (the game never pushes a dog to intense exercise).

gdv.quote: GDV is a medical emergency and can kill a pet in as little as 30 minutes if left untreated.
gdv.notes: PetMD (S461); feeding advice 'Do not let your dog exercise directly before or after eating.', 'Introduce a slow feeder bowl if your dog is eating too quickly.' and 'Avoid using raised food bowls.' → meal_exercise_gap row (M5-R16); slow feeder / no raised bowl open for David. The '30 minutes' is a clinical urgency, not a breed statistic — not exported. Register health key bloat_gdv.

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table of Coren's ranking (S35, re-read 2026-10-22): rank 27 'Chesapeake Bay Retriever' (tied with the Puli and the Yorkshire Terrier), tier 'Above Average Working Dogs' (ranks 27–39). Coren's own article (S34) not re-read. Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

coren_tier.quote: 15 to 25 repetitions.
coren_tier.notes: S35 tier 'Above Average Working Dogs': understanding of new commands '15 to 25 repetitions.'

training_notes.value: may be assertive and wilful
training_notes.quote: Some Chesapeakes are assertive and willful and may be reserved with strangers
training_notes.notes: Wikipedia (S462, tier C) — background only. The game uses Coren's rank only.

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value — see proposed_game_parameters.chesapeake_bay_retriever.learning_multiplier (1.2, runbook rule: Above average tier, rank 27).

general.value: powerful working retriever, equally at home on land and in water; size and substance not excessive
general.quote: Size and substance should not be excessive as this is a working retriever of an active nature.
general.notes: FCI standard No. 263 (S458): 'Equally proficient on land and in the water'.

colours.quote: Any colour of brown, sedge or deadgrass is acceptable, self-coloured Chesapeakes being preferred.
colours.notes: FCI standard (S458): 'One colour is not to be preferred over another.'; disqualifying 'Black coloured.' and 'White on any part of the body except breast, belly, toes, or back of feet.' → never black, at most a small white spot on the chest or toes. Wikipedia (S462, tier C) infobox: reddish gold, dead-grass and liver.

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). The standard prefers no colour; brown first with the highest weight (the portrait default — the most familiar Chessie colour, Claude 2026-10-22), then deadgrass, sedge.

coat.value: thick, short, wavy outer coat (never over 4 cm) with a dense, fine, woolly undercoat — waterproof
coat.quote: Coat should be thick and short, nowhere over 1 1/2 inches (4 cm) long, with a dense, fine, woolly undercoat.
coat.notes: FCI standard (S458); 'Moderate feathering on rear of hindquarters and tail is permissible.'; disqualifying 'Coat curly or with a tendency to curl all over the body.' RKC (S459) 'Coat length: Short'. AKC breed page: 'famous for his waterproof coat' (fragment).

head.value: muzzle about as long as the skull, tapering, pointed but not sharp
head.quote: Approximately the same length as the skull, tapering pointed but not sharp.

ears.value: small, set well up on the head, hanging loosely
ears.quote: Are to be small, set well up on the head, hanging loosely, and of medium leather.
ears.notes: FCI standard (S458).

eyes.value: medium large, very clear, yellowish or amber, wide apart
eyes.quote: Are to be medium large, very clear of yellowish or amber color and wide apart.
eyes.notes: FCI standard (S458).

tail.value: medium length, medium heavy at the base, straight or slightly curved
tail.quote: The tail should be straight or slightly curved and should not curl over back or side kink.
tail.notes: FCI standard (S458); 'Of medium length; medium heavy at the base.'

suitability._note: Source = RKC breed page (S459), VCA (S460), PetMD (S461). RKC key facts reached on 2026-10-22.

rkc_exercise.quote: Exercise: More than 2 hours per day
rkc_exercise.notes: RKC key fact (S459). Basis of active_family and long_daily_exercise.

rkc_size_of_home.notes: RKC key fact (S459). Basis of large_home.

rkc_grooming.notes: RKC key fact (S459) → brushing 1× a week (M5-R13 rule 'Once a week' → 1). VCA (S460) 'Brushing once a week is adequate; more during shedding seasons.' and PetMD (S461) 'They need to be brushed weekly.' agree.

rkc_shedding.notes: RKC key fact (S459). VCA (S460) 'Shedding is average.'; PetMD (S461) sheds more in spring — consistent → sheds.

rkc_lifespan.notes: RKC key fact (S459). Not shorter_lifespan (that needs 'Under 10 years').

rkc_breed_watch.notes: RKC Breed Watch (S459): Category 1 — no points of concern specific to the breed identified for special attention by judges (paraphrase). → no welfare chip.

petmd_family.value: a great addition to a family with proper introductions and socialisation
petmd_family.quote: With proper introductions and socialization, Chessies would be a great addition to a family.
petmd_family.notes: PetMD (S461), a family statement with a socialisation condition (kept in notes; Brittany precedent for a PetMD family statement). Basis of family_pet.

vca_children.value: playful and generally good with children
vca_children.quote: Playful and generally good with children.
vca_children.notes: VCA (S460). PetMD (S461): 'Interactions between kids and all dogs, Chessie or not, should be supervised.' → children (supervision caveat), not small_children.

vca_grooming.value: brushing once a week; more during shedding seasons
vca_grooming.quote: Brushing once a week is adequate; more during shedding seasons.
vca_grooming.notes: VCA (S460). The out-of-season number 1 is the game value (shedding seasons are not modelled).

samoyed._note: Added 2026-10-22 (M5-R10-57, unattended run — appended after the Chesapeake Bay Retriever: AKC 2024 No. 53 'Samoyed', S174 full-list table as recorded on 2026-10-22 ('52 Chesapeake Bay Retriever', '53 Samoyed'; the AKC page was not re-fetched in this run). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-22 (short quotes, 125-character limit; fragments marked as such); paraphrase only in notes. Sources S463–S471 (reused S10, S11, S14, S35, S45, S54, S123, S174). No health percentages anywhere. The RKC Breeds A–Z page (royalkennelclub.com/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/pastoral/samoyed; the older thekennelclub.org.uk display.aspx?id=5139 address redirects there) was refused by the fetch tool as not in provenance → no RKC key facts, no Breed Watch category, no RKC health-testing list; exercise, lifespan band, size and suitability from PDSA (S467) and Woodgreen (S468). Identity from the FCI nomenclature (S463); appearance and heights from the FCI standard No. 212 (S464, the French version — the English PDF was refused by the fetch tool), checked against the AKC (S465) and UKC (S466) standards. No standard gives a weight (FCI, AKC, UKC) → PDSA (S467). Lifespan: the Dogs Trust McMillan 2024 table (S123) was refused by the fetch tool; the McMillan 2024 paper (S54 repository copy) names the Samoyed only as a tip label of Fig. 5 (the breed table is Supplementary Table 3, not reached); no VetCompass median found; RKC page not reachable → closest row: the PDSA band 'Over 10 years' (S467), seeded verified=false (Miniature American Shepherd precedent). Not hypoallergenic (PetMD S469 says so explicitly; Wikipedia S470 notes the breed is 'touted as' hypoallergenic) — never tagged. Names: FCI 'SAMOIEDSKAÏA SABAKA' (English 'SAMOYED'), AKC / RKC 'Samoyed'; nickname 'Sammy' (Woodgreen S468 'Sammy smile'); Slovenian »samojed« (siol.net S471, tier C; KZS not checked).

identity.value: FCI No. 212, Group 5 Section 1 (Nordic Sledge Dogs), Russia
identity.quote: Group: n°5 - Spitz and primitive types; Section: Nordic Sledge Dogs; Country of origin: NORTHERN RUSSIA, SIBERIA
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S463): number '212', breed name 'SAMOIEDSKAÏA SABAKA', English 'SAMOYED', French 'SAMOYEDE', German 'SAMOJEDE', Spanish 'SAMOYEDO'; official valid standard '9/4/2019'. FCI standard (S464, French): 'CLASSIFICATION FCI : Groupe 5 Chiens de type Spitz et de type primitif.' 'Section 1 Chiens nordiques de traîneau.' 'ORIGINE : Russie septentrionale et Sibérie.' Quote assembled from the nomenclature fields as returned (Siberian Husky precedent). 'Russia' is NOT yet in FCI_ORIGINS of scripts/export-breed-registry.mjs → add Russia: 'RU' (+ EN/SL words on the website: Russia / Rusija).

size_class.notes: PDSA table 'Size' (S467); Woodgreen at-a-glance 'Size: Medium' (S468); FCI standard (S464): 'Spitz de l'Arctique blanc, élégant, de taille moyenne.' PetMD (S469): 'They are medium- to large-sized dogs; …' (fragment). The RKC page (the usual size source) was not reachable.

fci.quote: La taille idéale chez le mâle est de 57cm, avec une tolérance de +/- 3cm.
fci.notes: FCI standard No. 212 (S464, French): males ideal 57 cm ± 3 cm → 54–60; females 'Chez la femelle, elle est de 53cm, avec une tolérance de +/- 3cm.' → 50–56. AKC (S465) 'Males: 21 to 23½ inches; females: 19 to 21 inches at the withers.' (53–60 / 48–53 cm) and UKC (S466) agree; PDSA (S467) '46-56 cm' — alternatives.

pdsa.notes: PDSA table 'Average weight' (S467), one range for both sexes (stored per sex) — the game range. No standard gives a weight: FCI (S464) none; AKC (S465) 'The weight should be in proportion to the height.'; UKC (S466) heights only. Woodgreen (S468) '16-30 kg' and PetMD (S469) 'Samoyeds weigh 35–65 pounds' (16–29 kg, our conversion) agree. Wikipedia (S470, tier C) infobox: males 20–30 kg, females 16–20 kg — background only.

alternatives.notes: Woodgreen at-a-glance (S468).

alternatives.quote: They are medium- to large-sized dogs; Samoyeds weigh 35–65 pounds and confidently stand 19–23.5 inches tall.
alternatives.notes: PetMD (S469); 35–65 lb = 15.9–29.5 kg (our conversion, rounded).

salt_category.notes: Category assignment by weight is ours (general_by_size.size_classes.salt_2017_bands_kg, S8): 16–29 kg spans the 15–25 and 25–40 bands. Salt 2017 breed list not checked.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. PDSA 16–29 kg (S467) = 35–64 lb → mostly 'Medium (24–59 pounds)'; the heaviest dogs reach 'Large (59–99 pounds): 15–18 months'. The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 120 min is reached at 12 months).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Samoyed growth curve found.

pdsa.notes: PDSA table 'Average lifespan' (S467). The RKC band (the runbook's third option) could not be read (page not reachable). PetMD (S469): 'they can live for 12–14 years' (fragment); Woodgreen (S468) '12-14 years' — alternatives (no median). Wikipedia (S470, tier C): 'a life expectancy of 13.1 years for the breed' from a 2024 UK study (= McMillan 2024, not verified in S123) — background only.

mcmillan_2024.notes: McMillan et al. 2024 (S54; full paper at researchonline.ljmu.ac.uk eprint 22506, re-read 2026-10-22): the Samoyed appears only as a tip label of the Fig. 5 phylogeny ('Samoyed Alaskan Malamute Siberian Husky'), colour-coded without a number; the breed estimates are in Supplementary Table 3 (not reached). The Dogs Trust table of the same data (S123) was refused by the fetch tool as not in provenance. Wikipedia (S470, tier C) quotes 13.1 y. UNSOURCED value → open for David (check the S123 row).

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × PDSA lower bound 10 y (S467) → 0.75 × 10 = 7.5 y = 90 months. The runbook rule (McMillan 2024, else a VetCompass median, else the RKC lower bound) yields no value in this run: S123 not reachable, no VetCompass median, RKC page not reachable → closest row (Miniature American Shepherd precedent): the PDSA band of the same form as the RKC band, seeded verified=false (Claude's suggestion, open for David). Alternatives: PetMD / Woodgreen lower bound 12 y (S469, S468) → 108; McMillan 2024 13.1 y via Wikipedia (S470, tier C) → round(117.9) = 118; Dogs Trust > 7 y (S14) = 84.

adult.quote: We recommend a minimum of two hours exercise every day for your Samoyed.
adult.notes: PDSA (S467) — the RKC page (preferred) was not reachable. PetMD (S469): 'They need regular exercise (at least two hours a day!)' (fragment) agrees; Woodgreen (S468) at-a-glance '90-120 minutes' and 'Samoyeds are active dogs who need at least one to two hours of good exercise every day.' — alternatives.

mental_stimulation.value: puzzle feeders, scent work and short training sessions
mental_stimulation.quote: Puzzle feeders, scent work, and short training sessions help to keep a Sammy's curious mind productively occupied.
mental_stimulation.notes: Woodgreen (S468). PetMD (S469): 'need lots of exercise and mental stimulation to prevent boredom' (fragment). Basis of needs_mental_stimulation.

heat.value: struggles in hot weather; can develop heatstroke; needs shaded outdoor space
heat.quote: Samoyed dogs require daily brushing and do not do well in hot temperatures.
heat.notes: PetMD (S469); also 'a Samoyed can develop heatstroke in hot weather' (fragment). Woodgreen (S468): 'Their thick coats mean they can struggle in the heat, so shaded outdoor space' (fragment) and 'Never shave a Samoyed's coat, even in warm weather, as their double coat is essential for regulating their temperature.' The game has no weather / heat mechanic → open for David.

temperament.value: friendly, open, alert and lively; never fearful or aggressive; loving and loyal
temperament.quote: Amical, ouvert, éveillé et vif.
temperament.notes: FCI standard (S464, French — 'friendly, open, alert and lively'); also 'Jamais craintif ni agressif, il ne convient pas comme chien de garde.' PDSA (S467): 'Samoyeds are a loving and loyal breed with big personalities to match their fluffy coats.' AKC (S465): 'Intelligent, gentle, loyal, adaptable, alert, full of action, eager to serve,' (fragment). UKC (S466): 'The Samoyed is affectionate, gentle, intelligent and adaptable.' Woodgreen (S468): vocal (paraphrase).

family.value: usually great with children and loyal to the whole family; supervise children
family.quote: they are usually great with children and will be very loyal to the whole family
family.notes: PDSA (S467, fragment of a longer sentence); also 'Always supervise children and vulnerable people with your Samoyed' (fragment) — size and boisterous nature (paraphrase). Woodgreen (S468): 'They usually get on well with children' (fragment) and 'interactions with young children should always be supervised to ensure both parties are behaving safely and respectfully.' PetMD (S469): 'Yes, Samoyeds can make excellent family companions as long as their needs are met.' UKC (S466): 'They are extremely sociable and live very easily with children and other dogs.' → family_pet, children (supervision caveat); not small_children.

herding_children.value: may try to round up younger children by nudging or circling them
herding_children.quote: Samoyeds’ herding history means they may try to "round up" younger children by nudging or circling them.
herding_children.notes: Woodgreen (S468); not aggression (paraphrase). PetMD (S469): 'they may try to herd these critters and even small children' (fragment). Basis of may_herd_children.

time_alone.value: should not be left alone for more than four hours; becomes stressed and anxious
time_alone.quote: never leave them alone for more than four hours as they can become stressed and anxious.
time_alone.notes: PDSA (S467, fragment). Woodgreen (S468): 'they really don't like being left alone for long periods.' and 'Samoyeds do best in active homes where someone is around for most of the day.' Basis of needs_company.

other_pets.value: strong prey drive — care on walks; supervise around smaller animals
other_pets.quote: Be careful on walks though as they have a strong prey drive
other_pets.notes: PDSA (S467, fragment). Woodgreen (S468): 'Samoyeds also have a strong prey drive and a love of exploring.'; at-a-glance 'Sociable with pets: Moderate'. PetMD (S469): 'Supervise your Samoyed when they’re around smaller animals like cats, rabbits, or neighborhood squirrels' (fragment). Basis of chases_small_pets (strong = high prey drive).

escaping.value: accomplished escape artists — need a very secure garden
escaping.quote: Make sure your garden is very secure as Samoyeds are very accomplished escape artists.
escaping.notes: PDSA (S467). Woodgreen (S468): 'A fully secure garden is essential as they're natural explorers' (fragment). Basis of secure_fencing.

socialisation.value: socialise and train early in life
socialisation.quote: As with all dog breeds, Samoyed puppies respond best to training and socialization early in life.
socialisation.notes: PetMD (S469). Woodgreen (S468): 'Early socialisation is key, and training should continue well beyond puppyhood' (fragment). PDSA (S467): 'As long as they have been properly socialised they should love trips to the local dog park' (fragment, a condition). → proposed_game_parameters.samoyed.socialisation (DOG_SOCIALISATION row, M5-R17).

experienced_owner.quote: We would recommend an experienced owner for this breed,
experienced_owner.notes: PDSA (S467, fragment). Woodgreen (S468): 'Getting support from a professional trainer early on is a really good idea for this breed.'; training 'Moderately hard'. No chip: the experienced_owner chip names a powerful dog (open for David).

chewing.notes: Woodgreen (S468): 'Separation-related issues can include excessive barking, digging, or destructive chewing.' — a separation-anxiety statement, not chewing from boredom → covered by needs_company; no chews_when_bored tag.

food_motivation.notes: No breed-specific appetite statement found → no food_motivated_weight tag. PDSA (S467): split the daily allowance into two meals (paraphrase).

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages are shown anywhere. RKC Breed Watch category unknown (RKC page not reachable); no veterinary association names the breed for conformation-related welfare problems → no welfare chip. Breeder checklist: PDSA (S467) BVA/KC hip scheme for all breeding Samoyeds and BVA/KC eye screening; AKC national breed club list (K32): hip evaluation, cardiac exam, ophthalmologist evaluation, DNA RD/OSD2, DNA XLPRA1.

hip_dysplasia.value: hip dysplasia — hip screening of breeding dogs
hip_dysplasia.quote: All breeding Samoyeds should have their hips x-rayed through the BVA/Kennel Club Hip Dysplasia Scheme.
hip_dysplasia.notes: PDSA (S467): hip dysplasia 'a condition where the hip joints don’t fit together properly, which causes pain, swelling and eventually, arthritis.' Woodgreen (S468): 'Reputable breeders should have their dogs scored under the BVA/KC hip scheme before breeding.' PetMD (S469) lists hip dysplasia. Register health key hip_dysplasia.

diabetes.quote: Samoyeds are considered a higher-risk breed for diabetes.
diabetes.notes: Woodgreen (S468) — a risk statement without a number, never shown as a statistic. PDSA (S467): 'not being able to produce or use insulin, causing a high blood sugar level.' Register health key diabetes_mellitus.

cancer.notes: PDSA (S467) health list. Register health key certain_cancers.

eye_problems.value: eye problems including cataracts, eye ulcers and progressive retinal atrophy
eye_problems.quote: Eye problems, including cataracts and eye ulcers.
eye_problems.notes: PDSA (S467); 'There is BVA/KC screening available for eye problems.' PetMD (S469): retinal dysplasia, progressive retinal atrophy, uveodermatologic syndrome (paraphrase). Woodgreen (S468): 'DNA testing is available and responsible breeders should test for these before breeding.' AKC breed club (K32): DNA XLPRA1, RD/OSD2. Register health keys cataracts and pra_eye_disease.

kidney.value: Samoyed hereditary glomerulopathy (X-linked hereditary nephritis) — an inherited kidney disease
kidney.quote: SHG is a genetic kidney disorder often seen in Samoyeds.
kidney.notes: PetMD (S469); a DNA test exists (paraphrase). Woodgreen (S468): X-linked hereditary nephritis 'a serious inherited kidney condition that can affect Samoyeds.' (fragment). NEW register health key hereditary_nephritis (calm sentence, no numbers).

heart.quote: Potential genetic predisposition to eye problems, heart problems, hip dysplasia, and kidney disease.
heart.notes: PetMD (S469); several heart defects (paraphrase). Wikipedia (S470, tier C): pulmonary stenosis. AKC breed club (K32): 'Cardiac Exam'. Not a register health key (breeder checklist heart_scheme only).

skin.notes: Woodgreen (S468) names sebaceous adenitis, a skin condition (paraphrase — no quote returned); Wikipedia (S470, tier C) too. Not a register key.

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table of Coren's ranking (S35, re-read 2026-10-22): rank 33 'Samoyed' (table row '| 33 | Samoyed |'), tier 'Above Average Working Dogs' (ranks 27–39). Coren's own article (S34) not re-read. Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

coren_tier.quote: Understanding of new commands: 15 to 25 repetitions.
coren_tier.notes: S35 tier 'Above Average Working Dogs'.

training_notes.value: intelligent but independent and sometimes mischievous; reward-based training; a professional trainer early on
training_notes.quote: Getting support from a professional trainer early on is a really good idea for this breed.
training_notes.notes: Woodgreen (S468); training 'Moderately hard' (at-a-glance). PetMD (S469): 'Samoyeds are clever, quick-witted, and even mischievous,' (fragment, citing the breed club). The game uses Coren's rank only.

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value — see proposed_game_parameters.samoyed.learning_multiplier (1.2, runbook rule: Above average tier, rank 33).

general.value: white, elegant Arctic spitz of medium size
general.quote: Spitz de l'Arctique blanc, élégant, de taille moyenne.
general.notes: FCI standard No. 212 (S464, French — 'white, elegant Arctic spitz of medium size'). AKC (S465): 'The Samoyed should never be so heavy as to appear clumsy nor so light as to appear racy.'

colours.quote: Blanc pur, crème ou blanc et biscuit
colours.notes: FCI standard (S464, French — 'pure white, cream or white and biscuit'); fault 'Ne doit jamais donner l'impression d'être beige.' (never beige); disqualifying 'Autre couleur de robe que celles décrites dans le standard.' (any other colour) and 'Yeux bleus ou de couleurs différentes.' (blue or odd eyes). AKC (S465) also allows 'all biscuit' ('Samoyeds should be pure white, white and biscuit, cream, or all biscuit.') — not in the FCI standard → not used. Wikipedia (S470) infobox: 'White, Cream, White and Biscuit'.

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). Pure white first with the highest weight (the most typical Samoyed — the portrait default; PetMD / Wikipedia note pure white dogs are common, S470 'pure white and all biscuit dogs are common' — tier C), then cream, white and biscuit. Suggested 70 / 15 / 15.

coat.value: abundant, thick, soft and dense polar coat (double coat) with a silver sheen
coat.quote: Fourrure polaire, abondante, épaisse, souple et dense.
coat.notes: FCI standard (S464, French — 'polar fur, abundant, thick, pliable and dense'). AKC (S465): 'The Samoyed is a doublecoated dog.' and 'The coat should glisten with a silver sheen.' Woodgreen (S468): 'Their thick double coat needs brushing several times a week' (fragment).

head.value: strong, deep muzzle about as long as the skull; black lips slightly upturned at the corners — the 'Samoyed smile'
head.quote: Les commissures des lèvres sont légèrement retroussées pour former le « sourire du Samoyède » caractéristique.
head.notes: FCI standard (S464, French — the corners of the lips are slightly upturned to form the characteristic 'Samoyed smile'); muzzle 'Fort et haut, à peu près de la même longueur que le crâne' (fragment). AKC (S465): lips 'Should be black for preference and slightly curved up at the corners of the mouth, giving the "Samoyed smile."'

ears.value: erect, rather small, thick, triangular, slightly rounded at the tips
ears.quote: Droites, plutôt petites, épaisses, triangulaires et légèrement arrondies à l'extrémité.
ears.notes: FCI standard (S464, French). AKC (S465): 'Strong and thick, erect, triangular and slightly rounded at the tips;'

eyes.value: dark brown, almond-shaped, well set; never blue
eyes.quote: De couleur brun foncé, bien enchâssés dans les orbites.
eyes.notes: FCI standard (S464, French — 'dark brown, well set in the sockets'); disqualifying 'Yeux bleus ou de couleurs différentes.' AKC (S465): 'Should be dark for preference;' and 'Blue eyes disqualifying.'

tail.value: carried curved forward over the back or side; moderately long
tail.quote: la queue est portée courbée vers l'avant à partir de la base
tail.notes: FCI standard (S464, French, fragment — the tail is carried curved forward from the root). AKC (S465): 'The tail should be moderately long with the tail bone terminating approximately at the hock when down.'

nose.value: black preferred
nose.notes: AKC standard (S465): nose black preferred (paraphrase — not returned verbatim). FCI (S464): depigmented eyelid rims or lips are a serious fault ('Zones nettement dépigmentées sur le bord des paupières ou sur les lèvres.').

suitability._note: Source = PDSA (S467), Woodgreen (S468), PetMD (S469). The RKC breed page (the usual suitability source) was not reachable on 2026-10-22 → no rkc_* rows.

pdsa_exercise.value: a minimum of two hours exercise every day
pdsa_exercise.quote: We recommend a minimum of two hours exercise every day for your Samoyed.
pdsa_exercise.notes: PDSA (S467). Basis of active_family and long_daily_exercise.

pdsa_grooming.value: grooming on a daily basis, even when not shedding
pdsa_grooming.quote: They shed very often, but even when they’re not shedding they’ll need grooming on daily basis.
pdsa_grooming.notes: PDSA (S467) → brushing 7× a week (M5-R13 rule 'daily' → 7). PetMD (S469) 'Samoyed dogs require daily brushing and do not do well in hot temperatures.' agrees; Woodgreen (S468) 'Their thick double coat needs brushing several times a week' (fragment; daily during the spring and autumn moults) — alternative without a number. Also 'Samoyeds are very high maintenance when it comes to grooming because of their thick, fluffy coats.' (PDSA).

pdsa_shedding.quote: They shed very often, but even when they’re not shedding they’ll need grooming on daily basis.
pdsa_shedding.notes: PDSA (S467). Woodgreen (S468) at-a-glance 'Shedding: High'; PetMD (S469) 'These dogs shed regularly year-round and require consistent brushing.' — consistent → sheds; never low_shedding, never hypoallergenic (PetMD: 'No, Samoyeds are not considered to be a hypoallergenic dog breed.').

pdsa_lifespan.notes: PDSA table 'Average lifespan' (S467). Not shorter_lifespan (that needs 'Under 10 years').

pdsa_children.value: usually great with children; always supervise
pdsa_children.quote: they are usually great with children and will be very loyal to the whole family
pdsa_children.notes: PDSA (S467, fragment); 'Always supervise children and vulnerable people with your Samoyed' (fragment) → children (supervision caveat), not small_children.

pdsa_family.value: loyal to the whole family
pdsa_family.quote: they are usually great with children and will be very loyal to the whole family
pdsa_family.notes: PDSA (S467, fragment). Basis of family_pet with petmd_family.

pdsa_secure_garden.value: very secure garden — accomplished escape artists
pdsa_secure_garden.quote: Make sure your garden is very secure as Samoyeds are very accomplished escape artists.

pdsa_experienced_owner.quote: We would recommend an experienced owner for this breed,
pdsa_experienced_owner.notes: PDSA (S467, fragment). No chip: the experienced_owner chip names a powerful dog (open for David).

pdsa_meal_gap.value: leave a gap after eating and before exercising
pdsa_meal_gap.quote: Remember to leave a gap after eating and before exercising.
pdsa_meal_gap.notes: PDSA (S467); the page gives no length of the gap and does not name bloat. → proposed_game_parameters.samoyed.meal_exercise_gap (M5-R16).

petmd_family.value: excellent family companions when their needs are met
petmd_family.quote: Yes, Samoyeds can make excellent family companions as long as their needs are met.

woodgreen_grooming.value: brushing several times a week; daily during the spring and autumn moults; professional grooming every six to eight weeks
woodgreen_grooming.quote: Their thick double coat needs brushing several times a week
woodgreen_grooming.notes: Woodgreen (S468, fragment); 'daily brushing during their heavy seasonal moults in spring and autumn' (fragment); 'Professional grooming every six to eight weeks is recommended.'; at-a-glance 'Grooming needs: High'. 'Several times a week' has no number → the PDSA daily value is used (M5-R13 rule).

woodgreen_professional_grooming.value: professional grooming every six to eight weeks
woodgreen_professional_grooming.quote: Professional grooming every six to eight weeks is recommended.
woodgreen_professional_grooming.notes: Woodgreen (S468). No groomer mechanic → open for David (ROADMAP M5-R18).

woodgreen_care.value: regular nail trims, ear checks and dental care
woodgreen_care.quote: Regular nail trims, ear checks, and dental care are also important.
woodgreen_care.notes: Woodgreen (S468). PetMD (S469): 'Samoyeds should have their ears cleaned with a dog-specific ear cleaner' (fragment). No nail / ear / tooth mechanic → open for David (ROADMAP M5-R19, M5-R20, M5-R15).

woodgreen_sociable_with_pets.notes: Woodgreen at-a-glance 'Sociable with pets' (S468) — no other_pets tag.

scottish_terrier._note: Added 2026-10-23 (M5-R10-58, unattended run — appended after the Samoyed: AKC 2024 No. 54 'Scottish Terrier', S174 full-list table as recorded on 2026-10-22 '54 Scottish Terrier'). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-23 (short quotes, 125-character limit; fragments marked as such); paraphrase only in notes. Sources S472–S476 (reused S8, S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45, S54, S123, S174). No health percentages anywhere. The RKC Breeds A–Z page (display.aspx?id=3076 redirects to royalkennelclub.com …/terrier/scottish-terrier, refused by the fetch tool) and the RKC breed-standard page (redirect refused) could not be read → no RKC key facts and no Breed Watch category; exercise from PDSA (S474, runbook fallback RKC → PDSA). Identity from the FCI nomenclature (S472); appearance, height and weight from the Kennel Club breed standard as reprinted by KUSA (S473, 01-2026). Lifespan: the McMillan 2024 table (S123) was refused by the fetch tool and the paper (S54) has the breed only in Supplementary Table 3 → the senior boundary is Claude's suggestion (verified=false, Samoyed precedent). Names: FCI / AKC / KC 'Scottish Terrier' (S472, S174, S473); Slovenian »škotski terier« (no Slovenian source found — not checked against KZS, open for David).

identity.value: FCI No. 73, Group 3 Section 2 (Small-sized Terriers), Great Britain
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S472, as returned): 'Scottish Terrier (FCI No. 73)', Group 3 Terriers, section 'Small-sized terriers' (section 2 of group 3), country of origin Great Britain, no working trial, definitive acceptance 18/10/1954, valid standard 08/09/2026. 'Great Britain' is already in FCI_ORIGINS (GB). Other names: Terrier Écossais (FR), Schottischer Terrier (DE). AKC name: Scottish Terrier (S174). Wikipedia (S476, tier C): 'Scottie', 'Aberdeen Terrier' (paraphrase as returned).

size_class.notes: PDSA key facts table (S474; the page sits under 'medium-dogs'). The RKC 'Size:' field (preferred) could not be fetched. Note: by weight (8.5–10.5 kg, S473) the breed is in PetMD's 'Small' growth class (growth.adult_weight_reached) — the size chip follows PDSA.

kc_standard.notes: Kennel Club breed standard as reprinted by KUSA (S473, 01-2026), Size — height at withers, one range for both sexes (stored per sex). PDSA (S474) 'Average height | 25-28 cm' agrees; PetMD (S475) 'Standing just 10 inches tall' (US) — alternative.

Kennel Club breed standard (S473), Size — weight, one range for both sexes (stored per sex) — the game range. PDSA (S474) 'Average weight | 8.5-10.5 kg' agrees. PetMD (S475) 'weighing 18–22 pounds' (8.2–10.0 kg, our conversion) — alternative. Wikipedia (S476, tier C) infobox males 8.5–10 kg, females 8–9.5 kg — background only.

alternatives.quote: Average weight | 8.5-10.5 kg
alternatives.notes: PDSA key facts table (S474).

alternatives.quote: Standing just 10 inches tall and weighing 18–22 pounds
alternatives.notes: PetMD (S475, fragment); 18–22 lb = 8.2–10.0 kg (our conversion, rounded).

salt_category.notes: Category assignment by weight is ours (general_by_size.size_classes.salt_2017_bands_kg, S8): 8.5–10.5 kg spans the 5–10 and 10–15 bands. Salt 2017 breed list not checked.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. KC 8.5–10.5 kg (S473) = 18.7–23.1 lb → the 'Small (12–24 pounds)' class. The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 60 min is reached at 6 months).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Scottish Terrier growth curve found.

pdsa.notes: PDSA key facts table (S474). The RKC band (the runbook's third option) could not be read (page not reachable). PetMD (S475): 'Scottish Terriers are generally a healthy breed that usually live to be around 12 years old, on average.' — alternative (no median). Wikipedia (S476, tier C): a 2024 UK study gives 12.7 years for the breed (paraphrase as returned; = McMillan 2024, not verified in S123) — background only.

mcmillan_2024.notes: McMillan et al. 2024 (S54; full paper at researchonline.ljmu.ac.uk eprint 22506, re-read 2026-10-23): the Scottish Terrier appears only as a label of the Fig. 5 phylogeny, without a number; the breed estimates are in Supplementary Table 3 (not reached). The Dogs Trust table of the same data (S123) was refused by the fetch tool as not in provenance. Wikipedia (S476, tier C) gives 12.7 y. UNSOURCED value → open for David (check the S123 row).

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × PDSA lower bound 10 y (S474) → 0.75 × 10 = 7.5 y = 90 months. The runbook rule (McMillan 2024, else a VetCompass median, else the RKC lower bound) yields no value in this run: S123 not reachable, no VetCompass median, RKC page not reachable → closest row (Miniature American Shepherd / Samoyed precedent): the PDSA band of the same form as the RKC band, seeded verified=false (Claude's suggestion, open for David). Alternatives: PetMD 'around 12 years' (S475) → 108; McMillan 2024 12.7 y via Wikipedia (S476, tier C) → round(114.3) = 114; Dogs Trust > 7 y (S14) = 84.

adult.quote: Minimum exercise (per day) | 1 hour
adult.notes: PDSA key facts table (S474); PDSA text: 'Scotties need around an hour of exercise daily.' The RKC breed page (preferred) was not reachable → PDSA (runbook rule). PetMD (S475): 'They need regular, but not constant, exercise and stimulation to live a happy life.' — no minutes.

daily_text.value: around an hour of exercise daily
daily_text.quote: Scotties need around an hour of exercise daily.

digging.notes: PetMD (S475). Not an escape statement (no fence / tunnelling quote) → no secure_fencing chip; the game has no digging mechanic and digging is not a care need.

temperament.value: loyal and faithful; dignified, independent and reserved, but courageous and highly intelligent; bold, never aggressive
temperament.quote: Loyal and faithful. Dignified, independent, and reserved, but courageous and highly intelligent.
temperament.notes: Kennel Club breed standard (S473), Characteristics; Temperament: 'Bold, but never aggressive.' PDSA (S474): bred as hardy, brave hunting dogs; 'quite bold, determined dogs' (paraphrase / fragment as returned).

family.value: can be good dogs for families with the right training and socialisation; loyal and devoted to their family
family.quote: With the right training and socialization, Scottish Terriers can be good dogs for families.
family.notes: PetMD (S475) — a condition, not a child rating. PDSA (S474): 'Although they can be independent, they're loyal and devoted to their family and get on well with other pets.' No A/B statement about children → family_pet only, never children / small_children.

time_alone.value: should not be left alone for extended periods
time_alone.quote: you shouldn’t leave your dog alone for extended periods
time_alone.notes: PetMD (S475, fragment); the article puts 'extended' at more than four hours at once, citing the Scottish Terrier Club of America (paraphrase). PDSA (S474) has no sentence about time alone. Basis of needs_company.

other_pets.value: conflicting: PDSA says they get on well with other pets; PetMD names a strong prey drive and slow introductions to cats and smaller animals
other_pets.quote: Although they can be independent, they're loyal and devoted to their family and get on well with other pets.
other_pets.notes: PDSA (S474). PetMD (S475): Scotties are 'natural-born hunters with a strong prey drive.' and introductions to smaller animals, including cats, 'should be done properly and slowly' (fragments). Conflicting sources → neither other_pets nor chases_small_pets (runbook: conflicting sources → neither tag); open for David.

alternatives.value: strong prey drive; introduce to smaller animals properly and slowly
alternatives.quote: natural-born hunters with a strong prey drive
alternatives.notes: PetMD (S475, fragment).

socialisation.value: puppy socialisation is important for a well-mannered, confident dog
socialisation.quote: Socializing your Scottish Terrier puppy is important for having a well-mannered, confident dog.
socialisation.notes: PetMD (S475). → proposed_game_parameters.scottish_terrier.socialisation (DOG_SOCIALISATION row, M5-R17).

training.value: can be stubborn; needs patience and commitment; reward-based training
training.quote: Scotties can be stubborn so will need patience and commitment when training
training.notes: PDSA (S474, fragment); PDSA recommends reward-based techniques (paraphrase). PetMD (S475): 'Though Scottish Terriers are smart, training can take time and patience due to their independent nature.' No 'better for an experienced owner' statement → no independent_experienced_owner chip.

chewing.notes: No breed-specific chewing statement found → no chews_when_bored tag.

food_motivation.notes: No breed-specific statement found → no food_motivated_weight tag. PetMD (S475): 'Scotties do well with at least two meals each day, instead of eating one large meal.' (feeding, not food motivation).

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages are shown anywhere. RKC Breed Watch category unknown (RKC page not reachable); no veterinary association named by the runbook (BVA, UK BWG, UFAW, RVC/VetCompass, RKC) was found naming the breed for conformation-related welfare problems → no welfare chip (PDSA's note on difficult births, health.whelping, is recorded but is not one of those bodies). Bladder cancer: Wikipedia only (S476, tier C, with a risk multiple) → not recorded as a fact, never shown. Breeder checklist: PDSA (S474) Canine Health Schemes advice; AKC national breed club list (K33) and the STCA CHIC requirements (K34): DNA vWD III, patella evaluation, craniomandibular osteopathy (CMO).

von_willebrand.value: von Willebrand's disease — a bleeding disorder
von_willebrand.quote: Von Willebrand's disease – deficiency in blood platelet function resulting in excessive bleeding.
von_willebrand.notes: PDSA (S474) health list. PetMD (S475): 'Von Willebrand Disease is a genetic condition that makes it difficult for blood to clot properly.' A DNA test exists (breeder checklist dna_vwd3, K33 / K34). Register health key bleeding_disorder_vwd.

scottie_cramp.value: Scottie cramp — periodic cramping of the muscles, usually brought on by excitement
scottie_cramp.quote: Scottie cramp – periodic cramping of the muscles, usually brought on by excitement
scottie_cramp.notes: PDSA (S474) health list. PetMD (S475): the condition 'isn’t painful and won’t affect a dog’s quality of life.' (fragment). NEW register health key scottie_cramp (calm sentence, no numbers).

patella.value: luxating patellas — kneecaps slipping out of place
patella.quote: Luxating patellas – the kneecaps slipping temporarily out of place.
patella.notes: PDSA (S474) health list; breed club patella evaluation (K33 / K34). Register health key kneecap_luxation.

deafness.notes: PDSA (S474) health list (single word). Register health key deafness.

atopy.quote: Atopy – hypersensitivity to certain allergens, causing itching and skin trauma.
atopy.notes: PDSA (S474) health list. Not a fetched Breed Watch point → no sensitive_skin chip (Westie precedent needs RKC Breed Watch). Register health key itchy_skin_allergy.

cardiomyopathy.quote: Cardiomyopathy – enlarged heart due to degeneration of the heart muscle.
cardiomyopathy.notes: PDSA (S474) health list. Register health key heart_muscle_disease.

cushings.notes: PDSA (S474) health list: 'Cushing's syndrome (Hyperadrenocorticism) - hormonal disorder which results in the production off too much cortisol.' (as returned, 118 characters — kept in notes; no register key: background only).

eyes.value: cataracts and lens luxation
eyes.quote: Lens luxation – dislocation of the lens of the eye.
eyes.notes: PDSA (S474) health list: also 'Cataracts – opacity of the lens of the eye – giving a ‘cloudy’ appearance.' Register health key cataracts_lens_luxation.

whelping.value: difficulty giving birth naturally (large shoulders relative to the hindquarters and pelvis)
whelping.quote: Scotties have quite large shoulders relative to their smaller hind quarters and pelvic bones.
whelping.notes: PDSA (S474) health list (first sentence of the item). Breeding background only — not shown in the app or the register.

Coren's own article (S34) not re-read. Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

training_notes.notes: PetMD (S475); PDSA (S474) 'Scotties can be stubborn so will need patience and commitment when training' (fragment). The game uses Coren's rank only.

general.value: thick-set, short-legged terrier, alert in carriage; great power and activity in small compass
general.quote: Short-legged, alert in carriage, and suggestive of great power and activity in small compass.

Names: FCI / RKC / AKC 'Weimaraner'; nickname 'Weim' / 'grey ghost' not sourced; Slovenian »weimarski ptičar« (common name, not checked against KZS — open for David).

identity.value: FCI No. 99, Group 7 Section 1.1 (Continental Pointing Dogs, Braque type), Germany
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S477): heading 'WEIMARANER (99)', group 'n°7 - Pointing Dogs', section 'Continental Pointing Dogs', country of origin 'GERMANY', varieties 'a) Short-haired' and 'b) Long-haired'; English standard 5/26/2015, official valid standard 3/19/2015. FCI standard (S478): 'Section 1.1 Continental Pointing Dogs,' 'Type "Braque".' 'With working trial.' 'Germany' is already in FCI_ORIGINS (DE). RKC 'Weimaraner' (S479).

size_class.notes: RKC breed page key fact (S479). PDSA (S480) 'Large'; FCI standard (S478): 'Medium to large size hunting dog.'

fci.notes: FCI standard No. 99 (S478), Height at withers: males '59 – 70 cm.', females '57 – 65 cm.' (as returned, fragments). PDSA (S480) '56-69 cm'; PetMD (S481) males 25–27 in, females 23–25 in — alternatives.

fci.quote: about 30 – 40 kg.
fci.notes: FCI standard No. 99 (S478): males 'about 30 – 40 kg.', females 'about 25 – 35 kg.' (as returned, fragments). The game range 25–40 kg spans both sexes. PDSA (S480) '25-40 kg' agrees; PetMD (S481) males 70–90 lb, females 55–75 lb — alternative.

salt_category.notes: Category assignment by weight is ours (general_by_size.size_classes.salt_2017_bands_kg, S8): 25–40 kg spans the bands. Salt 2017 breed list not checked.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific: FCI males about 30–40 kg (≈ 66–88 lb, S478) are 'Large (59–99 pounds)'; females about 25–35 kg straddle Medium and Large (Chesapeake Bay Retriever precedent). The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 120 min is reached at 12 months).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Weimaraner growth curve found.

rkc.notes: RKC breed page key fact (S479). PDSA (S480) 'Over 10 years' agrees; Dogs Trust (S482) 'typically 10+ years'; PetMD (S481): 'the lifespan of Weimaraner dogs is 10–13 years' (fragment) — alternatives without a median. Wikipedia (S483, tier C): McMillan et al. 2024 'a median lifespan of 12.8 years for the breed' — background only (not the paper itself).

mcmillan_2024.notes: Dogs Trust table of McMillan et al. 2024 data (S123): refused by the fetch tool on 2026-10-23 (not in provenance). Wikipedia (S483, tier C) cites McMillan 2024 with a Weimaraner median of 12.8 years — not verified in the paper or the table → open for David (0.75 × 12.8 × 12 = 115.2 → senior 115 if confirmed). UNSOURCED value.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × RKC lower bound 10 y (S479) → 0.75 × 10 = 7.5 y = 90 months. Runbook order: McMillan 2024 (table not reachable, value only via Wikipedia tier C) → VetCompass median (none found) → RKC lower bound. Alternatives: 84 (Dogs Trust > 7 y, S14); 115 (0.75 × 12.8 y McMillan 2024 via Wikipedia S483, tier C — not chosen).

adult.quote: Exercise: More than 2 hours per day
adult.notes: RKC breed page key fact (S479) — the runbook's preferred source. PDSA (S480): 'Your Weimaraner will need a minimum of two hours exercise every day.' and 'Weimaraners don’t tire out easily, so it’s important to remember that two hours is the minimum they need!'; PetMD (S481): 'at least two hours every day' (fragment) — all agree on 120.

daily_text.value: long walks and off-lead running and play in a secure area, plus playtime and training
daily_text.quote: This will need to include some long walks and plenty of opportunity to run and play off-lead in a secure area.
daily_text.notes: PDSA (S480). Also 'On top of this, your Weimaraner will need lots of playtime with you and training sessions.'

temperament.value: loving and loyal, thrives in active families; active and very intelligent; can be a little wilful; takes time to warm to new people
temperament.quote: Weimaraners are known for their beautifully striking looks and loyalty to their owners.
temperament.notes: PDSA (S480); also 'They’re active and very intelligent dogs so can be easy to train with experienced owners.' and 'Because they can be a little wilful at times, Weimaraners do best with owners familiar with the breed and their needs.' PetMD (S481): 'The Weimaraner is a friendly, fearless, and obedient dog.' FCI standard (S478): 'Versatile, easily trained steady and passionate hunting dog.' (fragment).

experienced_owner.value: does best with owners familiar with the breed and its needs
experienced_owner.quote: Because they can be a little wilful at times, Weimaraners do best with owners familiar with the breed and their needs.

family.value: fairly good around children, but not recommended with smaller children (a large dog can knock them over); always supervise
family.quote: we wouldn’t recommend getting a Weimaraner if you have smaller children as they could accidentally knock them over.
family.notes: PDSA (S480, fragment of a longer sentence that starts 'Weimaraners are fairly good around children as they enjoy playtime, although due to their larger size…'); also 'Always supervise your dog with children and vulnerable adults.' PetMD (S481): 'When well socialized, they do great with people of all ages but should be supervised around babies and toddlers.' → family_pet, not_for_small_children; never children / small_children (Hungarian Vizsla precedent).

time_alone.value: can develop separation anxiety; best to have someone with them all day
time_alone.quote: Weimaraners can develop separation anxiety.
time_alone.notes: PetMD (S481). PDSA (S480): 'For this reason and due to their exercise needs, it’s best to have someone with them all day.' and 'If left alone, Weimaraners can develop separation anxiety and may bark or chew anything they can get their paws on…' (fragment). Basis of needs_company.

other_pets.value: very strong prey drive — not recommended with smaller pets
other_pets.quote: They have a very strong prey drive and are likely to chase anything that moves!
other_pets.notes: PDSA (S480); also 'For this reason, we wouldn’t recommend having them with smaller pets.' PetMD (S481): 'Their prey drive might make it difficult for Weimaraners to live in the same home as smaller animals,' (fragment). Basis of chases_small_pets (a high prey drive named in this breed's own entry); never other_pets.

socialisation.value: socialise from a young age with a variety of people, dogs and experiences
socialisation.quote: Weimaraners tend to be a little cautious of unfamiliar dogs, so socialisation from a young age is really important.
socialisation.notes: PDSA (S480), a need; also 'Weimaraners can take a while to warm to new people (and dogs) so it’s really important to socialise them…' / '…with a variety of people, dogs and experiences from a young age.' (fragments). PetMD (S481): 'If properly socialized, they get along well with other dogs.' → proposed_game_parameters.weimaraner.socialisation (DOG_SOCIALISATION row, M5-R17).

chewing.notes: PDSA (S480): when left alone they 'may bark or chew anything they can get their paws on…' (fragment — a separation-anxiety statement, covered by needs_company) → no chews_when_bored tag (open for David).

food_motivation.notes: No breed-specific statement found → no food_motivated_weight tag.

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages are shown anywhere. RKC Breed Watch Category 1 (S479: no breed-specific points of concern) → no welfare chip. Breeder checklist: RKC Best Practice elbow, eye and hip schemes (S479).

hip_dysplasia.quote: where the hip joint doesn’t fit together perfectly, which will eventually lead to arthritis.
hip_dysplasia.notes: PDSA (S480, fragment after 'Hip dysplasia'). PetMD (S481): 'Hip dysplasia in dogs is a degenerative joint disease that affects the hind limbs.' RKC Best Practice hip and elbow schemes (S479). Register health key hip_dysplasia.

gdv.quote: Remember to leave a gap between eating and exercising as this is thought to reduce the risk of GDV.
gdv.notes: PDSA (S480): 'Remember to leave a gap between eating and exercising as this is thought to reduce the risk of GDV.'; GDV 'where a dog’s stomach bloats and twists around on itself, which can be fatal.' (fragment). PetMD (S481): 'To limit the risk of GDV, do not feed your Weimaraner dog immediately before or after exercise; allow one to two hours.' → meal_exercise_gap row (M5-R16; PetMD's 'one to two hours' recorded as an alternative — the game uses David's 60 min). Register health key bloat_gdv.

cancer.notes: PDSA (S480) lists 'Certain cancers.' without detail. Register health key certain_cancers (Samoyed precedent).

distichiasis.value: distichiasis — extra small eyelashes on the inner surface or the edge of the eyelid
distichiasis.quote: a condition in which small eyelashes grow on the inner surface or the very edge of the eye…
distichiasis.notes: PDSA (S480, fragment). RKC Best Practice eye scheme (S479). New register health key extra_eyelashes (calm sentence, no numbers).

entropion.quote: Entropion is the most common eyelid abnormality in dogs.
entropion.notes: PetMD (S481) names entropion for the breed (the eyelid rolling inwards — paraphrase). Register health key entropion.

hypothyroidism.quote: Hypothyroidism is a common endocrine disease where the dog's body functions, including metabolism,
hypothyroidism.notes: PetMD (S481, fragment). Register health key hypothyroidism.

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table of Coren's ranking (S35, re-read 2026-10-23): rank 21 'Weimaraner' (no other breed shares the rank), tier 'Excellent Working Dogs' (ranks 11–26). Coren's own article (S34) not re-read. Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

coren_tier.quote: Understanding of new commands: 5 to 15 repetitions.
coren_tier.notes: S35 tier 'Excellent Working Dogs': 'Obey first command: 85% of the time or better.'

training_notes.value: easy to train with experienced owners; can be a little wilful
training_notes.quote: They’re active and very intelligent dogs so can be easy to train with experienced owners.
training_notes.notes: PDSA (S480). The game uses Coren's rank only.

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value — see proposed_game_parameters.weimaraner.learning_multiplier (1.5, runbook rule: Excellent tier, rank 21).

general.value: medium to large, functional working hunting dog; sinewy and very muscular
general.quote: Medium to large size hunting dog. Functional working type, pleasing in shape, sinewy and very muscular.
general.notes: FCI standard No. 99 (S478).

colours.quote: Silver, roe or mouse grey, as well as shades of these colours. Head and leathers generally slightly paler.
colours.notes: FCI standard (S478): 'Only small white markings on chest and toes permitted.'; disqualifying 'Deviations from grey tones, such as yellow or brownish, tan brand.' and 'Colour other than grey. Blue colouring.' → grey only, never blue, brown or tan markings.

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). Silver grey first with the highest weight (the portrait default — the colour most associated with the breed, Claude 2026-10-23), then roe grey, mouse grey.

coat.value: short-haired variety: short, strong, very dense, smooth-lying topcoat (a long-haired variety also exists)
coat.quote: Short (but longer and thicker than with most comparable breeds), strong, very dense, smooth lying topcoat.
coat.notes: FCI standard (S478), short-haired variety; long-haired 'Soft, long topcoat with or without undercoat. Smooth or slightly wavy.' The game shows the short-haired variety (open for David). RKC (S479) 'Coat length: Short & long'.

head.value: long muzzle, powerful especially in the male, almost angular in profile
head.quote: Long and, especially in the male, powerful, seen from profile appearing almost angular.

nose.value: large nose leather, dark flesh colour merging into grey
nose.quote: Dark flesh colour, merging gradually into gray towards the rear.
nose.notes: FCI standard (S478); 'Nose leather large, protruding over the under jaw.'

ears.value: broad, fairly long, set on high, reaching the corner of the mouth
ears.quote: EARS: Broad and fairly long, just reaching to corner of mouth.
ears.notes: FCI standard (S478); 'Set on high and narrow, forming a rounded off point at tip.'

eyes.value: amber, dark to pale (sky blue in puppies)
eyes.quote: EYES: Amber colour, dark to pale, with intelligent expression.
eyes.notes: FCI standard (S478); 'Skyblue in puppies.'

tail.value: natural tail, hanging down in repose, carried level or higher when alert
tail.quote: Carried hanging down in repose.
tail.notes: FCI standard (S478); 'When alert or working, carried level or higher.' The standard permits docking for hunting dogs where legal ('appropriate tail docking is permissible for shorthaired Weimaraner used for hunting.') — the game shows the natural tail (runbook: never a docked tail as a goal).

suitability._note: Source = RKC breed page (S479), PDSA (S480), PetMD (S481). RKC key facts reached on 2026-10-23.

rkc_exercise.quote: Exercise: More than 2 hours per day
rkc_exercise.notes: RKC key fact (S479). Basis of active_family and long_daily_exercise.

rkc_size_of_home.notes: RKC key fact (S479). Basis of large_home.

rkc_grooming.notes: RKC key fact (S479) → brushing 1× a week (M5-R13 rule 'Once a week' → 1). PDSA (S480) 'A weekly brush should be plenty to keep on top of any dead hairs.' and PetMD (S481) 'once a week' agree.

rkc_coat_length.notes: RKC key fact (S479) — both varieties; the game shows the short-haired one.

rkc_shedding.notes: RKC key fact (S479). PDSA (S480): 'They do shed all year round, but as long as you keep on top of the hoovering you won’t really notice it much.' — consistent → sheds.

rkc_lifespan.notes: RKC key fact (S479). Not shorter_lifespan (that needs 'Under 10 years').

rkc_breed_watch.quote: Currently no points of concern specific to this breed have been identified for special attention by judges
rkc_breed_watch.notes: RKC Breed Watch (S479): 'Category 1'. → no welfare chip.

pdsa_family.value: wonderful family pets in the right hands
pdsa_family.quote: In the right hands, Weimaraners make wonderful family pets and can be very good natured dogs.
pdsa_family.notes: PDSA (S480), a family statement with a condition ('in the right hands'; also 'thrive in active families'). Basis of family_pet.

pdsa_children.value: not recommended with smaller children
pdsa_children.quote: we wouldn’t recommend getting a Weimaraner if you have smaller children as they could accidentally knock them over.
pdsa_children.notes: PDSA (S480, fragment). Basis of not_for_small_children.

petmd_grooming.value: brushing once a week; a bath once a month; ears cleaned once a month
petmd_grooming.quote: Bathing your dog once a month is sufficient to keep their coat and skin healthy and hydrated.
petmd_grooming.notes: PetMD (S481); also 'brushing with a rubber curry comb once a week helps decrease shedding and keeps their coat shiny.' and 'Use a vet-approved ear cleanser to clean your dog's ears once a month.' Bath and ear cleaning → proposed_game_parameters.weimaraner.ear_care_bathing (no mechanic yet — ROADMAP M5-R20).

italian_greyhound._note: Added 2026-10-23 (M5-R10-60, unattended run — appended after the Weimaraner: AKC 2024 No. 56 'Italian Greyhound', S174 full-list table fetched 2026-10-23 '56 | Italian Greyhound'). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-23 (short quotes, 125-character limit; fragments marked as such); paraphrase only in notes. Sources S484–S490 (reused S8, S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45, S123, S174). No health percentages anywhere. Identity from the FCI nomenclature (S484, FCI name 'PICCOLO LEVRIERO ITALIANO', English 'ITALIAN SIGHTHOUND'); appearance, heights and weights from the Kennel Club breed standard as reprinted by KUSA (S485, effective 01/07/2025). RKC Breeds A–Z page (S486) reached: key facts, Breed Watch Category 1 and the Best Practice eye test. Lifespan: the Dogs Trust McMillan 2024 table (S123) was refused by the fetch tool (not in provenance); McMillan 2024's 'about 14 years' only via Wikipedia (S489, tier C) → RKC lower bound 'Over 12 years' (runbook order; Papillon / Weimaraner precedent). Names: AKC / KC 'Italian Greyhound' (S174, S485); Slovenian »mali italijanski hrt« (MrPet.si S490, tier C — common name, not checked against KZS, open for David).

identity.value: FCI No. 200, Group 10 Section 3 (Short-haired Sighthounds), Italy
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S484, as returned): name 'PICCOLO LEVRIERO ITALIANO', English name 'ITALIAN SIGHTHOUND', group 'n°10 - Lévriers', section 'Lévriers à poil court' (section 3 of group 10, Short-haired Sighthounds — the page gives no section number), country of origin 'ITALIE', no working trial, definitive acceptance '22/10/1956', valid standard '13/11/2015'. Italy is already in FCI_ORIGINS (IT, Cane Corso). AKC / KC name: Italian Greyhound (S174, S485). Wikipedia (S489, tier C): other names 'Italian Sighthound; Piccolo Levriero Italiano'.

size_class.notes: RKC breed page key fact (S486); PDSA (S487) 'Small' (its page sits under 'small-dogs'). KC weight 3.6–4.5 kg (S485) = 7.9–9.9 lb → the 'Toy (5–12 pounds)' class of S10 for growth. RKC places the breed in the Toy group.

kc_standard.notes: Kennel Club breed standard as reprinted by KUSA (S485, effective 01/07/2025), Size — height at withers, one range for both sexes (stored per sex). PDSA (S487) 'Average height 32-38 cm' agrees; PetMD (S488) 'Italian Greyhounds stand only 13-15 inches tall.' (33–38 cm) — alternative. Wikipedia (S489, tier C) '32 to 38 cm' agrees.

pdsa.notes: PDSA key fact 'Average height' (S487), one range for both sexes. Same as the KC standard.

kc_standard.notes: Kennel Club breed standard (S485), Size — weight, one range for both sexes (stored per sex) — the game range (adult_weight_kg). PDSA (S487) 'Average weight 3-4.5kg'; PetMD (S488) 'weighing between 7-14 pounds' (3.2–6.4 kg, US dogs); Wikipedia (S489, tier C) 'not over 5 kg' (FCI) — alternatives.

alternatives.notes: PDSA key fact 'Average weight' (S487), one range for both sexes.

salt_category.notes: Category assignment by weight is ours (general_by_size.size_classes.salt_2017_bands_kg, S8): 3.6–4.5 kg = the smallest band. Salt 2017 breed list not checked.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. KC 3.6–4.5 kg (S485) = 7.9–9.9 lb → 'Toy (5–12 pounds)'. The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 60 min is reached at 6 months). PDSA (S487) warns of bone fragility during growth (behaviour.family).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Italian Greyhound growth curve found.

rkc.notes: RKC breed page key fact (S486). PDSA (S487) 'Average lifespan Over 12 years' agrees. The basis of the senior boundary (runbook: RKC lower bound when no McMillan 2024 / VetCompass value is reachable). Not shorter_lifespan.

pdsa.notes: PDSA key fact 'Average lifespan' (S487). Same lower bound as the RKC.

petmd.notes: PetMD (S488): the breed is said to 'live to be 14-15 years old' (fragment as returned). Alternative only (lower bound 14 y → 126 months).

mcmillan_2024.notes: Dogs Trust table of McMillan et al. 2024 data (S123): refused by the fetch tool on 2026-10-23 (not in provenance). Wikipedia (S489, tier C) cites McMillan 2024: 'Median longevity is about 14 years, compared to an average of 12.5 for all dogs.' — not verified in the paper or the table → open for David (0.75 × 14 × 12 = 126 → senior 126 if confirmed). UNSOURCED value.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × RKC lower bound 12 y (S486) → 0.75 × 12 = 9 y = 108 months. Runbook order: McMillan 2024 (table not reachable, value only via Wikipedia tier C) → VetCompass median (none found) → RKC lower bound. Alternatives: 126 (McMillan 2024 about 14 y via Wikipedia S489, and the PetMD 14 y lower bound S488); 84 (Dogs Trust > 7 y, S14).

adult.quote: Exercise: Up to 1 hour per day
adult.notes: RKC breed page key fact (S486), runbook first choice → 60 min. PDSA (S487) 'Minimum exercise (per day) 1 hour' and 'Italian Greyhounds are full of energy, requiring around an hour of exercise per day.' agree. PetMD (S488): energy needs 'can be easily met with a daily walk or outdoor playtime' (fragment) — no minutes.

daily_text.value: around an hour of exercise per day
daily_text.quote: Italian Greyhounds are full of energy, requiring around an hour of exercise per day.

off_lead.value: exercise in a confined area — hard to call back once they see prey
off_lead.quote: exercise in a confined area is recommended.
off_lead.notes: PDSA (S487, fragment): 'if they catch sight of potential prey you may find it hard to get them back' (fragment). The game counts steps; off-lead running only in a confined area is not modelled → open for David (needs a new ROADMAP task; Whippet precedent).

after_meals.notes: No advice to leave a gap between eating and exercising found (PDSA S487, PetMD S488: two meals a day for adults, paraphrase) → no meal_exercise_gap row.

temperament.value: intelligent, affectionate and vivacious; may appear aloof; elegant, graceful and quick-moving
temperament.quote: Intelligent, affectionate, and vivacious; may appear aloof.
temperament.notes: Kennel Club breed standard (S485), Temperament; Characteristics: 'Elegant, graceful, and quick-moving.'

family.value: do well with children who know how to treat a dog, but avoid small, rambunctious children; bones fragile during growth — not ideal with young children
family.quote: Though Italian Greyhounds do well with children who understand how to appropriately interact with dogs, they will often…
family.notes: PetMD (S488, fragment as returned): the breed tends to avoid smaller, rambunctious children and interactions with kids should be supervised (paraphrase). PDSA (S487): 'Due to their bone fragility during growth, they may not be the ideal breed to live with other pets or young children.' → children (explicit statement, caveat kept here) + fragile_older_children; never small_children.

fragile_bones.value: bones fragile during growth — not ideal with young children or other pets
fragile_bones.quote: Due to their bone fragility during growth, they may not be the ideal breed to live with other pets or young children.
fragile_bones.notes: PDSA (S487), children and other pets. Basis of fragile_older_children (Yorkshire Terrier precedent); never other_pets.

time_alone.notes: No time-alone statement found (PDSA S487, PetMD S488: without enough attention the dog may become shy or hyper, paraphrase) → no needs_company tag.

other_pets.value: has a prey drive (small, fast-moving animals); not ideal with other pets while growing
other_pets.quote: It’s also important to note that Italian Greyhounds have a prey drive, thanks to their history as hunters.
other_pets.notes: PetMD (S488): small, fast-moving animals such as cats, rabbits or squirrels can trigger it; owners with smaller pets should teach the dog not to chase them (paraphrase). Not a 'high prey drive' statement → no chases_small_pets (runbook rule); PDSA (S487) bone fragility → never other_pets.

socialisation.value: can be quite timid — early socialisation is essential
socialisation.quote: They can also be quite timid, so early socialisation is essential.
socialisation.notes: PDSA (S487). → proposed_game_parameters.italian_greyhound.socialisation (DOG_SOCIALISATION row, M5-R17).

bonding.value: slow to form a bond, then a fantastic companion
bonding.quote: They can be slow to form a bond but make a fantastic companion once the bond is established.

chewing.notes: No chewing statement found → no chews_when_bored tag.

food_motivation.notes: No breed-specific statement found → no food_motivated_weight tag.

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages are shown anywhere. RKC Breed Watch Category 1 (S486) → no welfare chip. Breeder checklist: RKC Best Practice eye testing (BVA/KC/ISDS Eye Scheme, S486).

periodontal_disease.notes: PDSA (S487) health list: 'infection and inflammation of the periodontium (tissues that surround and support the teeth).' (fragment). Register health key periodontal_disease (new). No tooth-brushing advice with a frequency in the sources fetched (PetMD S488 does not mention teeth).

epilepsy.quote: a brain disorder which can lead to seizures.
epilepsy.notes: PDSA (S487) health list (fragment). Register health key epilepsy.

patella.value: luxating patellas (kneecaps slipping out of place)
patella.quote: the kneecaps slipping temporarily out of place.
patella.notes: PDSA (S487) health list (fragment). Register health key kneecap_luxation.

pra.value: progressive retinal atrophy — gradual loss of sight
pra.quote: gradual deterioration of the retina of the eye. Symptoms can start with night blindness and progress to total blindness.
pra.notes: PDSA (S487) health list (fragment); PetMD (S488) names it too. RKC Best Practice eye testing (S486). Register health key pra_eye_disease.

autoimmune.notes: PetMD (S488): the breed is 'susceptible to different conditions in which the immune system confuses vital tissues' (fragment). Register health key autoimmune_conditions.

legg_calve_perthes.notes: PetMD (S488): the femoral head degenerates, causing 'joint failure' over time (fragment). Register health key legg_perthes.

hypothyroidism.notes: PetMD (S488): 'a fairly common condition in which the thyroid gland is underactive' (fragment). Register health key hypothyroidism.

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table of Coren's ranking (S35, re-read 2026-10-23): rank 60 'Italian Greyhound', tier 'Fair Working/Obedience Intelligence' (ranks 55–69). Coren's own article (S34) not re-read. Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

coren_tier.notes: S35 tier 'Fair Working/Obedience Intelligence' (ranks 55–69).

training_notes.value: often prefer to do their own thing and can be difficult to train; positive reinforcement
training_notes.quote: they often prefer to do their own thing and can be difficult to train.

coat.notes: Kennel Club standard (S485). RKC 'Coat length: Short' (S486); PetMD (S488): 'their coat does not insulate them well' (cold).

head.quote: Skull long, flat, and narrow, slight stop. Muzzle fine and long. Nose dark in colour.

ears.quote: Rose-shaped, placed well back, soft and fine, not pricked.

eyes.value: rather large, bright, full of expression
eyes.quote: Rather large, bright; full of expression.
eyes.notes: Kennel Club standard (S485).

temperament.value: gentle, placid, kind and sociable with people; particularly attached to its owner
temperament.quote: Gentle, placid, kind and sociable with people. Particularly attached to its owner.
temperament.notes: FCI standard (S501), behaviour / temperament. PDSA (S503): 'Bloodhounds are gentle and placid dogs known for their amazing sense of smell.'; 'They’re affectionate dogs and very easy-going in the home environment.'

experienced_owner.value: high maintenance because of the exercise needs — better suited to experienced owners; not for first-time owners
experienced_owner.quote: Bloodhounds are a high maintenance breed due their exercise needs, so are better suited to experienced owners

family.value: gentle and placid; likely to get along with children of all ages, but not recommended with smaller children because of their size
family.quote: This means that they are likely to get along with children of all ages, however due to their size
