No explicit family-pet statement by an A/B source (Wikipedia S504 'excellent family pets' is tier C) → no family_pet / children chip.

small_children.value: not recommended with smaller children — could knock them over
small_children.quote: we wouldn’t recommend having a Bloodhound if you have smaller children.
small_children.notes: PDSA (S503, fragment). Basis of not_for_small_children; never small_children or children.

time_alone.value: not known to suffer with separation anxiety; never alone for more than four hours (general PDSA advice)
time_alone.quote: Bloodhounds aren’t a breed known to suffer with separation anxiety.
time_alone.notes: PDSA (S503); 'you should never leave your dog alone for more than four hours' (fragment, general advice for all dogs). No breed-specific need → no needs_company / often_alone.

other_pets.value: very high prey drive — not with smaller pets; fine with other dogs if socialised well
other_pets.quote: Bloodhounds do have a very high prey drive, so we wouldn’t advise keeping them with smaller pets.
other_pets.notes: PDSA (S503): high prey drive → chases_small_pets (runbook rule, appended at the end of the consider list); 'As long as your Bloodhound has been socialised well from a young age, they should get along fine with other dogs.' (fragment). Never other_pets.

socialisation.value: socialise from a young age with lots of people, dogs and experiences (can sometimes be nervous)
socialisation.quote: Generally speaking, Bloodhounds aren’t aggressive dogs but can sometimes be nervous so it’s important to socialise your Bloodhound from a young age with lots of people, dogs and experiences.
socialisation.notes: PDSA (S503; returned in two consecutive fragments, joined here without change). A need (runbook M5-R17) → proposed_game_parameters.bloodhound.socialisation (DOG_SOCIALISATION row).

drooling.quote: You’ll find that your Bloodhound is a drooler
drooling.notes: PDSA (S503); 'If you don’t mind mopping up the drool then you should be fine!' Basis of drools (as the Mastiff and the Newfoundland).

chewing.notes: No chewing statement found → no chews_when_bored tag.

food_motivation.notes: No breed-specific statement found → no food_motivated_weight tag. PDSA (S503): split the daily allowance into two meals (general advice).

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages are shown anywhere. RKC Breed Watch Category 2 (S502: 'This breed can be affected by conformational concerns' — paraphrase as returned; the PDSA page S503 says 'Category Three'); welfare rule §3 → eyelid_problems. Breeder checklist: RKC minimum tests (genetic diversity, BVA/KC elbow and hip schemes) and Best Practice (BVA/KC/ISDS eye scheme) (S502).

hip_elbow_dysplasia.quote: Hip dysplasia – where the hip joint doesn’t fit together perfectly, which will eventually lead to arthritis.
hip_elbow_dysplasia.notes: PDSA (S503); also 'Elbow dysplasia – where the elbow joint doesn’t fit together perfectly, which will eventually lead to arthritis.' RKC minimum hip and elbow schemes (S502). Register health key hip_elbow_dysplasia.

gdv.quote: Gastric Dilatation Volvulus (GDV) – where a dog’s stomach bloats and twists around on itself, which can be fatal.
gdv.notes: PDSA (S503). The Kennel Club BHCP (S505) names it the leading specific cause of death in the 2004 survey (percentages research only). → meal_exercise_gap (M5-R16). Register health key bloat_gdv.

eyes.value: eyelid problems (ectropion, entropion) and corneal ulcers
eyes.quote: Eye problems – such as ectropion, entropion and corneal ulcers.
eyes.notes: PDSA (S503). RKC Best Practice eye scheme (S502). Basis of eyelid_problems (welfare rule). Register health key eyelids_turned.

skin.value: atopy (itchy skin); skin folds to be kept clean and dry
skin.quote: Atopy – itchy skin caused by sensitivity to things in the environment (such as pollen, grass and dust mites).
skin.notes: PDSA (S503); care: 'It’s important to make sure their skin folds are kept clean and dry and regularly check their ears for signs of infection.' Register health key itchy_skin_allergy.

ears.value: ear infections
ears.quote: Ear infections.
ears.notes: PDSA (S503) health list; care: regularly check the ears for signs of infection (suitability.pdsa_care). Register health key ear_infections_prone.

breed_watch.value: RKC Breed Watch Category 2 (conformational concerns); PDSA: Kennel Club Category Three
breed_watch.notes: RKC Breeds A–Z page (S502): 'Category 2'; 'This breed can be affected by conformational concerns' (as returned, paraphrase); points of concern not returned. PDSA (S503): 'Bloodhounds are amongst a group of breeds classed as ‘Category Three’ by The Kennel Club.' / 'This means that they have been bred to look a certain way, which can cause them problems and discomfort.' The two sources differ in the category; both name conformational concerns → welfare rule §3 (eyelid_problems, the eye problems PDSA lists). Open for David: the current RKC category is 2.

shorter_lifespan.value: a shorter life than most breeds — under ten years
shorter_lifespan.notes: RKC (S502) and PDSA (S503) 'Under 10 years'; Kennel Club survey median 6 y 9 m (S505) — research only. Basis of the consider tag shorter_lifespan — a calm chip, no number.

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table of Coren's ranking (S35, re-read 2026-10-24): rank 74 'Bloodhound', tier 'Lowest Degree of Working/Obedience Intelligence' (ranks 70–79: 'Understanding of new commands: 80 to 100 repetitions or more.; Obey first command: 25% of the time or worse.;'). Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

coren_tier.notes: S35 tier 'Lowest Degree of Working/Obedience Intelligence' (ranks 70–79).

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value — see proposed_game_parameters.bloodhound.learning_multiplier (0.5, runbook rule: Lowest tier, rank 74).

general.value: large, massive scent hound, the most powerful of all scent hounds; supple, loose, elastic skin
general.quote: Large-sized hound and massive leash hound, the most powerful of all the scent hounds.
general.notes: FCI standard (S501), general appearance; skin 'Supple over all the body, loose and elastic.'

colours.quote: There are three distinct coat colours: the bicolours black and tan and liver and tan and the unicolour red.
colours.notes: FCI standard (S501), colour; disqualifying 'Coat colours not matching the standard; excessive white markings' (paraphrase as returned). Wikipedia (S504) 'Black and tan, liver and tan or red'. Never merle, brindle, white or patches.

colour_weights.notes: UNSOURCED — game draft (verified=false in breed_appearance.php). Black and tan first with the highest weight (the portrait default), then liver and tan, then red.

coat.value: short, dense, quite harsh and weatherproof close-lying hair
coat.quote: On the body, the close-lying hair is short, dense, quite harsh and weatherproof.
coat.notes: FCI standard (S501). RKC 'Coat length: Short' (S502).

nose.value: black or brown, always black on black and tan dogs
nose.quote: Black or brown, always black on black and tan dogs.
nose.notes: FCI standard (S501).

eyes.value: dark brown or hazel (amber in dogs without a black saddle)
eyes.quote: Dark brown or hazel, of a lighter hue (amber) in dogs without black saddle or mantle.
eyes.notes: FCI standard (S501). The game shows healthy eyelids (welfare rule — never drooping or turned).

ears.value: long, thin, supple, low-set folding ears covered in short, velvety hair
ears.quote: Thin and supple, covered in short hair, delicate and velvety to the touch
ears.notes: FCI standard (S501, fragment).

tail.value: long, strong, thick, set high
tail.quote: Long, strong, thick, set high, in continuation of the dorsal line
tail.notes: FCI standard (S501, fragment).

suitability._note: Source = RKC breed page (S502) and PDSA (S503). RKC key facts reached on 2026-10-24. Woodgreen and PetMD not attempted.

rkc_exercise.quote: Exercise: More than 2 hours per day
rkc_exercise.notes: RKC key fact (S502). Basis of active_family and long_daily_exercise.

rkc_size_of_home.notes: RKC key fact (S502) → large_home; never apartment.

rkc_grooming.notes: RKC key fact (S502) → brushing 1× a week (M5-R13 rule 'Once a week' → 1). PDSA (S503) weekly brush agrees. Not frequent_grooming.

rkc_coat_length.notes: RKC key fact (S502); PDSA (S503) 'Coat length: Short'.

rkc_shedding.notes: RKC key fact (S502). Basis of sheds.

pdsa_grooming.value: a weekly brush; a drooler
pdsa_grooming.quote: Their short fur means your Bloodhound will only need a weekly brush to keep on top of any dead hairs.
pdsa_grooming.notes: PDSA (S503) → agrees with the RKC 'Once a week' (S502); 'You’ll find that your Bloodhound is a drooler' (behaviour.drooling).

pdsa_care.value: skin folds kept clean and dry; ears checked regularly for signs of infection
pdsa_care.quote: It’s important to make sure their skin folds are kept clean and dry and regularly check their ears for signs of infection.
pdsa_care.notes: PDSA (S503). → proposed_game_parameters.bloodhound.skin_fold_care (no mechanic — ROADMAP M5-R14) and ear_checks (no mechanic — ROADMAP M5-R20).

akita._note: Added 2026-10-24 (M5-R10-63, unattended run — appended after the Bloodhound: AKC 2024 No. 59 'Akita', S174 full-list table fetched 2026-10-24 '59 | Akita'). The AKC 'Akita' is the American type: AKC, The Kennel Club and the FCI treat the American Akita and the Japanese Akita Inu as separate breeds (Wikipedia S512, tier C, background only); FCI No. 344 'AMERICAN AKITA' (S506). Quotes as returned by the web-fetch tool on 2026-10-24 (short quotes; fragments marked as such); paraphrase only in notes. Sources S506–S511 (+ S512 tier C; reused S8, S10, S11, S14, S24, S35, S45, S174). No health percentages anywhere. Identity, height, colours and appearance from the FCI nomenclature (S506) and the FCI standard in English (S507, published 11.02.2026; no weight in the standard). The RKC Breeds A–Z page (royalkennelclub.com …/utility/akita) was refused by the fetch tool (provenance; both old thekennelclub.org.uk addresses redirect there) → PDSA (S508) for key facts, exercise, grooming and chips; PetMD (S510) for the second view; AKC standard (S509) for height and colours. Lifespan: PDSA 'Under 10 years' has no lower bound, the Dogs Trust McMillan 2024 table (S123) was refused by the fetch tool (11.4 years only via Wikipedia, S512, tier C) → the Kennel Club / BSAVA 2004 survey median 9 y 11 m (S511, 28 deaths) as the closest row; the senior boundary is Claude's suggestion (verified=false, open for David). Names: AKC / RKC 'Akita', FCI 'American Akita'; Slovenian »ameriška akita« (FCI name) — no KZS page checked, open for David.

identity.value: FCI No. 344, Group 5 Section 5 (Asian Spitz and related breeds), Japan
identity.notes: FCI nomenclature (S506, as returned): breed 'AMERICAN AKITA' (No. 344), group 'n°5 - Spitz and primitive types', section 'Asian Spitz and related breeds', country of origin 'JAPAN.' with the country of development 'UNITED STATES OF AMERICA.'; date of publication of the official valid standard '2/11/2026'; 'Recognized on a definitive basis', no working trial. Japan is already in FCI_ORIGINS (JP, Shiba Inu). The section number 5 is the FCI's 'Asian Spitz and related breeds' section (as for the Shiba Inu, S377). AKC and RKC name: 'Akita' (S174, S509).

size_class.notes: PDSA key fact 'Size: Large' (S508; its page sits under 'large-dogs'). PDSA 31–59 kg (S508) = 68–130 lb → mostly the 'Large' class of S10 for growth (heavy males 'Giant').

fci.quote: Height at withers: For males: 66 to 71 cm
fci.notes: FCI standard No. 344 (S507, English, published 11.02.2026): 'Height at withers: For males: 66 to 71 cm' and 'for females: 61 to 66 cm' (as returned); disqualifying 'Males under 63,5 cm; females under 58,5 cm.' AKC standard (S509): 'Males 26 to 28 inches at the withers; bitches 24 to 26 inches.' (66–71 / 61–66 cm) — agrees. PDSA (S508) 'Average height: 61-71 cm'.

pdsa.notes: PDSA key fact (S508), one range for both sexes — the game range (adult_weight_kg). The FCI standard (S507) and the AKC standard (S509) give no weight. PetMD (S510): 'they weigh 70–130 pounds and stand 24–28 inches tall.' (32–59 kg) — agrees.

alternatives.quote: they weigh 70–130 pounds and stand 24–28 inches tall.
alternatives.notes: PetMD (S510), 70–130 lb = 31.8–59.0 kg, no sex split.

salt_category.notes: Category assignment by weight is ours (general_by_size.size_classes.salt_2017_bands_kg, S8): 31–59 kg spans the bands 30–40 and '>40 (no curve)'. Salt 2017 breed list not checked.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size-class value (PetMD S10), not breed-specific. PDSA 31–59 kg (S508) = 68–130 lb → mostly 'Large'; heavy males 'Giant (over 100 pounds) | 18–24 months' — alternative. The game is unaffected (the puppy cap of 120 min is reached at 12 months).

alternatives.quote: Giant (over 100 pounds) | 18–24 months
alternatives.notes: Heavy males over 100 lb (45 kg).

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — no Akita growth curve found.

pdsa.notes: PDSA key fact (S508). No lower bound → not usable for the senior boundary. Conflicts with PetMD 10–14 years (S510) and McMillan 2024 11.4 y (only via Wikipedia, S512) → no shorter_lifespan chip (conflicting sources), open for David.

petmd.quote: The Akita lifespan is typically 10–14 years.
petmd.notes: PetMD (S510) — tier B; its page treats the American and the Japanese type together ('considered the same breed', FAQ, paraphrase). Not in the runbook's lifespan order (McMillan → VetCompass → RKC lower bound); alternative for the senior boundary (0.75 × 10 × 12 = 90).

median_kc_survey.quote: The median age at death for the Akita breed was 9 years and 11 months (min = 4 months, max = 13 years and 8 months)
median_kc_survey.notes: Kennel Club / BSAVA Scientific Committee, Purebred Dog Health Survey 2004, Akita section (S511): 'A total of 28 deaths were reported …' (fragment). An older, owner-reported UK survey of 28 deaths — the closest breed median reachable in this run (Bloodhound precedent, S505); never shown as a statistic in the app. Causes of death (research only): cancer, cardiac and gastrointestinal (incl. GDV) the leading groups.

mcmillan_2024.notes: Dogs Trust table of McMillan et al. 2024 data (S123): not reachable this run (provenance refusal). Wikipedia (S512, tier C): 'A UK study found a life expectancy of 11.4 years for the breed' — not verified in the paper or the table → open for David (0.75 × 11.4 × 12 = 102.6 → senior 103 if confirmed). UNSOURCED value.

senior_from.notes: Derived: AAHA senior = last 25 % of lifespan (S11) × Kennel Club 2004 survey median 9 y 11 m (S511) → 0.75 × 9.9167 = 7.44 y = 89.25 → 89 months. The runbook rule yields no value: McMillan 2024 not reachable (S123), no VetCompass Akita median found, no RKC page (PDSA 'Under 10 years' has no lower bound) → closest row (Bernese Mountain Dog / Bloodhound precedent): a published breed median, seeded verified=false (Claude's suggestion, open for David). Alternatives: PetMD lower bound 10 y (S510) → 90; McMillan 2024 11.4 y via Wikipedia (S512, tier C) → 103; Dogs Trust > 7 y (S14) = 84.

adult.quote: Minimum exercise (per day): 2 hours
adult.notes: PDSA key fact (S508); PDSA text: 'Your Akita will need a minimum of two hours of exercise every day – this can be spent running and walking.' The RKC breed page (preferred) was refused by the fetch tool → PDSA (runbook rule). PetMD (S510) gives no minutes.

daily_text.value: a minimum of two hours every day, running and walking; many enjoy a swim
daily_text.quote: Your Akita will need a minimum of two hours of exercise every day – this can be spent running and walking.
daily_text.notes: PDSA (S508); 'Akitas tend to love water so many enjoy a swim every now and again.'; 'It’s best to keep them on a lead when walking just in case they smell or spot something to chase!'

after_meals.value: leave a gap after eating and before exercising (GDV / bloat)
after_meals.quote: Remember to leave a gap after eating and before exercising.
after_meals.notes: PDSA (S508), feeding section; the same page lists GDV ('bloat', an emergency, health.gdv). PetMD (S510): 'Large dogs with deep chests, including the Akita, are at an increased risk of gastric dilatation-volvulus.' The source gives no length of the gap → proposed_game_parameters.akita.meal_exercise_gap (built, M5-R16).

heat.value: prone to overheating in very hot weather
heat.quote: they are prone to overheating in very hot weather.
heat.notes: PDSA (S508, fragment). Not a flat-faced breed → no DOG_NO_WALK_IN_HEAT row (runbook §3: that row is for flat-faced breeds); a fact for the breed text only.

temperament.value: loyal, independent and intelligent; alert, dignified and courageous; can be reserved with new people
temperament.quote: Originating from Japan, Akitas are known for being incredibly loyal family pets.
temperament.notes: PDSA (S508); 'Akitas are independent and due to their intelligence this is often mistaken for stubbornness.' FCI standard (S507): 'Alert and responsive, dignified and courageous.' PetMD (S510): 'Akitas are strong-willed dogs bred to work independently.'; they 'can be reserved or even uncomfortable around new people at first.' (fragment).

experienced_owner.value: very large — best with experienced owners; not for inexperienced owners
experienced_owner.quote: While Akitas adapt well to family life, they are also very large and therefore would do best with experienced owners.
experienced_owner.notes: PDSA (S508); also 'they’re not suitable for inexperienced owners' (fragment). PetMD (S510): 'An experienced pet parent is best for raising an Akita puppy.' Basis of experienced_owner.

family.value: loyal family pets that adapt well to family life, but best with experienced owners and not with young children
family.quote: Originating from Japan, Akitas are known for being incredibly loyal family pets.
family.notes: PDSA (S508). The family statement comes with the advice against young children and for experienced owners → no family_pet chip (Bloodhound / Giant Schnauzer precedent: an A/B family statement with a strong caveat is not used as a 'suits' chip; open for David).

small_children.value: not recommended with young children — could knock them over; protective of toys and food
small_children.quote: we wouldn’t recommend an Akita if you have young children
small_children.notes: PDSA (S508, fragment; continues 'as they could accidentally knock them over…'); 'Akitas can also be protective and possessive with toys and food, which younger children may not understand.'; 'Always supervise children and vulnerable adults with your Akita' (fragment). PetMD (S510): 'Akitas may also not have much patience for young children.' Basis of not_for_small_children; never small_children or children.

time_alone.value: strongly attached to the family; many don’t cope well alone — never more than four hours
time_alone.quote: we wouldn’t recommend leaving them alone as many don’t cope well with this
time_alone.notes: PDSA (S508, fragment); 'this should never be for more than four hours' (fragment). Basis of needs_company.

other_pets.value: high prey drive — not with smaller pets; wary of unfamiliar dogs (ongoing socialisation)
other_pets.quote: Akitas were often used for hunting in the past and so have a high prey drive.
other_pets.notes: PDSA (S508, fragment as returned); 'we wouldn’t recommend keeping an Akita with smaller pets.' (fragment); 'Akitas tend to be naturally wary of unfamiliar dogs so socialisation will need to be ongoing throughout their lives.' FCI (S507): 'American Akitas may be highly responsive of other dogs, particularly of the same sex.' PetMD (S510): 'Akita dogs may do best as the only pet at home.' High prey drive → chases_small_pets (runbook rule, appended at the end of the consider list). Never other_pets.

socialisation.value: well socialised from a young age, and ongoing throughout life
socialisation.quote: your dog will need to be well socialised from a young age
socialisation.notes: PDSA (S508, fragment as returned). A need (runbook M5-R17) → proposed_game_parameters.akita.socialisation (DOG_SOCIALISATION row). PetMD (S510): 'Begin training and socializing your Akita puppy as soon as you bring them home.'

drooling.notes: No drooling statement on the pages read → no drools tag.

chewing.notes: No chewing statement found → no chews_when_bored tag. PDSA (S508): puzzles and rotating toys help prevent boredom (paraphrase) — no explicit need statement → no needs_mental_stimulation tag.

food_motivation.notes: No breed-specific statement found → no food_motivated_weight tag. PDSA (S508): feed at the same time every day; treats no more than 10 % of the daily calories (general advice).

health._note: Parent-facing background only, recorded factually with sources; no percentages are shown anywhere. The RKC Breeds A–Z page (Breed Watch category, health tests) was not reachable → no welfare chip and no breeder-checklist tests (open for David). PDSA (S508) and PetMD (S510) health lists.

hip_dysplasia.notes: PDSA (S508) health list item (as returned; paraphrase in the second fetch: 'which can lead to arthritis'). PetMD (S510): 'Akitas can be prone to hip dysplasia, an orthopedic condition that affects the hip joints.' Register health key hip_dysplasia_arthritis.

gdv.quote: Large dogs with deep chests, including the Akita, are at an increased risk of gastric dilatation-volvulus.
gdv.notes: PetMD (S510); PDSA (S508): GDV, often known as bloat, 'This is an emergency and requires urgent veterinary attention.' → meal_exercise_gap (M5-R16). Register health key bloat_gdv.

eyes.value: eye problems — cataracts, multifocal retinal dysplasia, progressive retinal atrophy, glaucoma, entropion, ectropion
eyes.quote: Eye problems, including cataracts and multifocal retinal dysplasia
eyes.notes: PDSA (S508) health list (as returned; also 'Progressive retinal atrophy', 'Glaucoma', 'Entropion', 'Ectropion' as items). PetMD (S510): microphthalmia, 'a congenital (present at birth) disorder in which one or both eyes are smaller than usual.' (fragment). Register health key eye_problems_pra_cataracts_entropion. No eyelid chip: the welfare rule needs a Breed Watch / BVA conformation point (RKC page not reachable).

autoimmune.value: autoimmune diseases, including sebaceous adenitis (skin glands) and VKH-type syndrome
autoimmune.quote: Autoimmune diseases, including sebaceous adenitis and hypothyroidism
autoimmune.notes: PDSA (S508) health list (as returned); also 'VKH-type syndrome' (Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada). PetMD (S510): 'Sebaceous adenitis … is a disease that affects a dog's skin glands.' (paraphrase of the returned fragment). Register health key autoimmune_conditions.

hypothyroidism.quote: Hypothyroidism is common in the Akita dog breed.
hypothyroidism.notes: PetMD (S510, as returned: '… is common in the Akita dog breed.'); PDSA (S508) lists it under autoimmune diseases. Register health key hypothyroidism (no number).

skin.notes: PDSA (S508) health list item. Not a separate register key (covered by autoimmune_conditions / hypothyroidism sentences).

breed_watch.notes: UNSOURCED — the RKC Breeds A–Z page (Breed Watch category and points of concern) was refused by the fetch tool on 2026-10-24. No welfare chip without it (runbook §3); open for David.

coren_rank.notes: Wikipedia table of Coren's ranking (S35, read 2026-10-13 for the Boston Terrier): rank 54, shared with the Boston Terrier, under 'Average Working/Obedience Intelligence' (ranks 40–54). Coren's own top / bottom-10 article (S34) does not list the breed (runbook: rank from S35). Coren ranked the 'Akita' before the FCI split — applied to the AKC Akita. Verify in The Intelligence of Dogs.

coren_tier.quote: Understanding of new commands: 25 to 40 repetitions.; Obey first command: 50% of the time or better.;
coren_tier.notes: Tier 'Average Working/Obedience Intelligence' = ranks 40–54 (S35, as returned for the Boston Terrier). Tier definitions from Wikipedia; verify in book.

training_notes.value: learns quickly, also bad habits — consistent, positive, reward-based training with clear boundaries
training_notes.quote: Akitas are independent and due to their intelligence this is often mistaken for stubbornness.
training_notes.notes: PDSA (S508); training advice paraphrased (reward-based, firm but fair, an accredited trainer for inexperienced owners).

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value — see proposed_game_parameters.akita.learning_multiplier (1.0, runbook rule: Average tier, rank 54).

general.value: large-sized, sturdily built, well balanced dog with much substance and heavy bone; broad head, small eyes, erect ears, large curled tail
general.quote: Large-sized dog, sturdily built, well balanced, with much substance and heavy bone.
general.notes: FCI standard (S507), general appearance. AKC standard (S509): 'Large, powerful, alert, with much substance and heavy bone.'; 'The broad head, forming a blunt triangle, with deep muzzle, small eyes and erect ears carried forward' (fragment).

colours.quote: Any colour like red, fawn, white, etc; or even pinto and brindle.
colours.notes: FCI standard (S507), colour: 'Colours are brilliant and clear, and markings are well balanced, with or without mask or blaze.'; 'White dogs (solid in colour) have no mask.'; 'Pinto have a white ground colour with large, evenly placed patches covering head and more than one-third of body.' coat.quote: Outer coat straight, harsh/stiff and standing somewhat off body.
coat.notes: FCI standard (S507); 'Undercoat thick, soft, dense and shorter than outer coat.' AKC (S509): 'Double-coated.' PDSA (S508) 'Coat length: Short'.

nose.value: broad and black
nose.quote: Broad and black.
nose.notes: FCI standard (S507); slight lack of pigment acceptable in white dogs only (paraphrase).

eyes.value: dark brown, relatively small, not prominent, almost triangular
eyes.quote: Dark brown, relatively small, not prominent, almost triangular in shape.
eyes.notes: FCI standard (S507).

ears.value: strongly erect, small in relation to the head
ears.quote: Strongly erect and small in relation to the rest of the head.

tail.value: large, well furnished, set high, carried over the back in a three-quarter, full or double curl
tail.quote: Large and well furnished with hair, set high and carried over back or against flank
tail.notes: FCI standard (S507, fragment); 'in a three-quarter, full, or double curl, always dipping to or below level of back.'; disqualifying 'Sickle or uncurled tail.'

suitability._note: Source = PDSA (S508) and PetMD (S510): the RKC Breeds A–Z page was refused by the fetch tool on 2026-10-24, so there are no rkc_* fields (no 'Size of home', no 'Grooming' key fact). Woodgreen not attempted.

pdsa_exercise.value: a minimum of two hours every day
pdsa_exercise.quote: Minimum exercise (per day): 2 hours
pdsa_exercise.notes: PDSA key fact (S508). Basis of active_family and long_daily_exercise.

pdsa_grooming.value: Once a week
pdsa_grooming.quote: at minimum a weekly brush to help get rid of dead hairs.
pdsa_grooming.notes: PDSA (S508, fragment as returned) — 'a weekly brush' read as the category 'Once a week' (our wording; quote verbatim); 'You may want to brush your Akita more regularly during the warmer months when they shed more.' (seasonal, not modelled). PetMD (S510) 'Daily brushing is best to reduce shedding and prevent matting.' conflicts → no frequent_grooming chip; brushing 1× a week by the source order (PDSA before PetMD), PetMD daily listed for David.

pdsa_professional_grooming.value: a professional groomer every three months or so (optional)
pdsa_professional_grooming.quote: You might like to get your Akita professionally groomed every three months or so.
pdsa_professional_grooming.notes: PDSA (S508). A stated frequency → groomer reminder every 12 program weeks (runbook §3 'Breed care tasks', M5-R18; '3 months' → 84 days).

pdsa_shedding.quote: Although their fur is short, it's dense, so Akitas shed a lot!
pdsa_shedding.notes: Read as 'sheds: yes' (our wording; quote verbatim). PetMD (S510): 'Akitas have a thick double coat that sheds year-round, with heavy shedding in the spring and fall.' Basis of sheds.

pdsa_lifespan.notes: PDSA key fact. shorter_lifespan criterion (A/B upper bound ≤ 10 years) met, but PetMD 10–14 years (S510) conflicts → no chip (open for David).

petmd_ears.value: occasional ear cleanings; ask the vet how often
petmd_ears.quote: Akitas can also benefit from occasional ear cleanings.
petmd_ears.notes: PetMD (S510); 'Talk to your vet about how and how often you should clean your dog's ears.' No frequency → no task (runbook §3 'Breed care tasks').

medium_mixed_breed._note: No breed standard exists. All values below are SIZE-CLASS data (general_by_size) applied to an assumed medium size; the size assumption itself is a proposal.

assumed_adult_weight.notes: UNSOURCED — proposal. Proposal: use Salt category IV (S8) as the 'medium' band. Alternative: PetMD medium 10.9–26.8 kg (S10). David to choose.

adult_weight_reached.notes: Size class.

weight_by_month_kg.notes: UNSOURCED — proposal. = assumed adult band × logistic %.

median_uk_crossbreeds.quote: This was slightly shorter for crossbred dogs at 12.0 years.
median_uk_crossbreeds.notes: CONFLICT: O'Neill 2013 (S17) found crossbreds lived 1.2 years LONGER than purebreds.

senior_from.notes: Derived: 0.75 × 12.0 y (S11, S15). Dogs Trust rule of thumb > 7 y (S14).
senior_from.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-05: senior from 108 months (0.75 × 12.0 y)

adult.quote: all adult dogs should receive between 30 minutes and two hours
adult.notes: General adult range; no mixed-breed-specific source.

adult_game_target.notes: UNSOURCED in the literature — game value inside the sourced 30–120 range (S24).

coren.quote: Non-AKC/CKC recognized breeds like Jack Russell Terriers were excluded from rankings
coren.notes: Coren ranked breeds recognised by AKC/CKC only (judges ranked breeds); mixed breeds therefore have NO rank.

breed_effect_on_behaviour.value: breed explains ~9% of individual behaviour variation
breed_effect_on_behaviour.quote: Breed explains just 9% of behavioral variation in individuals
breed_effect_on_behaviour.notes: Supports modelling a mixed breed as 'average with individual randomness'; the size of the random spread is a proposal.

game_model.value: average learning speed + individual random factor
game_model.notes: UNSOURCED — proposal. REALISM_SPEC §4 idea; the numeric spread is not sourced.

learning_multiplier.notes: UNSOURCED as a number — game baseline. Mixed breeds have no Coren rank (S35); breed explains only ~9 % of individual behaviour (S42), so the mixed breed is the average dog.
learning_multiplier.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-06: the mixed breed is the baseline (1.0) (M5-R03)

individual_variation.unit: ± share of the learning speed, drawn once per dog
individual_variation.notes: UNSOURCED as a number — game value for 'average + individual randomness' (game_model). S42: breed explains ~9 % of behavioural variation, individuals vary. Uniform draw in [0.8, 1.2], seeded per pet and stored (pets.training_learning_factor).
individual_variation.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-06: mixed breed = baseline with a per-pet random factor ±20 % (M5-R03)

standard.notes: No standard exists for mixed breeds — nothing to cite for colour/ear/coat frequencies.

distribution.notes: UNSOURCED — proposal. No shelter-intake statistics on mixed-breed appearance were found. Current breed_appearance.php 'mutt' options remain unsourced.

three_three_three_rule.quote: the first three days should be used for adjusting to their new surroundings, the next three weeks for training and bonding, and the first three months for continued socialization and training
three_three_three_rule.notes: Stated by a local US shelter (Longmont Humane Society) as 'a guideline'. ORIGIN UNKNOWN — no national body or study found that defines it.

adjustment_literature_range.quote: adoption literature has varyingly indicated that this process can range from four to six weeks or up to three months

adjustment_observed.quote: Over half of participants perceived the adjustment period to last longer than four months.

post_adoption_issues.notes: n=27; percentages via Faunalytics summary + paper.

c_barq_6_months.quote: Separation-related behaviors: Decrease reported at 180 days
c_barq_6_months.notes: n=99, Ohio. Prevalence = any non-zero C-BARQ score, so numbers look high; not severity.

shelter_age_distribution.quote: Puppies (≤6 months): 26% of admissions; Adults (>6 months): 74%
shelter_age_distribution.notes: Queensland RSPCA, 2014, n=11,967. Admissions, not adoptions; Australia only.

bought_puppy_age.notes: UNSOURCED — proposal. REALISM_SPEC draft; consistent with training start ~8 weeks (S36) but no source on purchase age was collected.

proposed_game_parameters._note: Everything here is a PROPOSAL derived from the values above; see README for the derivation. Not facts.

feed_windows.notes: UNSOURCED — proposal. From feeding_meals_per_day (S18, S21, S19, S14). Window clock times are UNSOURCED.
feed_windows.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-05: meal counts as listed; senior = 2

walk_minutes_puppy.notes: UNSOURCED — proposal. 5 min × months × 2 (S24) — contested rule (S25).
walk_minutes_puppy.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-05: 10 min × age in months

step_goal_border_collie_adult.notes: UNSOURCED — proposal. 120 min (S5) × 100 steps/min (S45, adult heuristic).

accident_window_hours.unit: hours a puppy can hold, by age in months
accident_window_hours.notes: UNSOURCED — proposal. 1 h per month of age (S30, S31).
accident_window_hours.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-06: 1 h of hold per month of age (game rule accident_hold_hours_per_age_month = 1), puppy stage only; the clock counts only outside quiet hours and restarts at take-out, accident, birth and family-local midnight

chewing_risk.notes: UNSOURCED — proposal. From S32, S33, S7.
chewing_risk.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-06: teething puppies (teething_months) chew occasionally, at most once per local day; any dog whose previous day's walk goal was missed chews once the next day

chewing_teething_chance_per_day.notes: UNSOURCED — proposal (Claude, M5-R02, waiting for David). S32 / S33 say teething puppies chew a lot but give no frequency; 0.5 = about every other day during teething_months. Stored verified = false.

training_minigame_minutes.unit: minutes of mini-game per dog and family-local day (budget)
training_minigame_minutes.notes: UNSOURCED — proposal (Claude, M5-R03, waiting for David). S36/S37: 5–10 min sessions, ≤15 min/day for puppies. Used as the dog's daily training budget (one mini-game session ≈ 50 s, so ≤ 6 sessions a day); same for every stage (no source for adults).
training_minigame_minutes.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-06: 5 minutes of mini-game per dog and day, shared equally by the children who care for the dog (M5-R03b)

feed_window_times.notes: UNSOURCED in the literature (clock times; the meal COUNT is sourced, S18). Derivation: first window 07:00, last 19:00, equal spacing, 2 h each. A window entirely inside quiet hours is done by the parent.
feed_window_times.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-05: 2-hour windows (was a 1-hour proposal), start times kept

arrival_age_months.notes: UNSOURCED in the literature except the puppy (~8 weeks, S36): representative age = first month of the stage, so the dog stays in that stage for the 12-week challenge.
arrival_age_months.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-05: puppy 2 months, other stages the first month of the stage

senior_exercise_minutes.notes: UNSOURCED in the literature: 75 % of the adult minutes. Sources only say "frequent short walks instead of one long one" (S14) and that energy needs fall with age (S13).
senior_exercise_minutes.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-05: senior = 75 % of the adult minutes

training_progress_per_success.unit: percentage points of command progress per correctly timed praise (mixed-breed baseline, before the breed / individual factors)
training_progress_per_success.notes: UNSOURCED — proposal (Claude, M5-R03, waiting for David). Game balance: a session has 8 cues; about 16 good daily sessions teach one command to a mixed breed (≈ 8 for a Border Collie), so all four commands take about the 12-week challenge with one session a day.
training_progress_per_success.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-06: +1 point per correctly timed praise (× breed × individual factor)

training_decay_per_missed_day.unit: percentage points lost by every command per family-local day whose training routine was missed
training_decay_per_missed_day.notes: UNSOURCED — proposal (Claude, M5-R03, waiting for David). REALISM_SPEC §4 / David 2026-10-06: without practice progress slowly decays; no source gives a rate. A day excused like the walk (hard stop / vet ≥ 50 % of the day) or the birth day never decays.
training_decay_per_missed_day.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-06: −2 points per missed training day, every command

potty_training_accident_reduction.unit: share of due puppy accidents avoided at 100 % potty training (linear in progress)
potty_training_accident_reduction.notes: UNSOURCED — proposal (Claude, M5-R03, waiting for David). A house-trained puppy learns to 'ask' to go out (S47); full house training takes 4–6 months (S31). The bladder physics (1 h per month of age, S30 / S31) stay unchanged: when the hold runs out, a trained puppy signals instead of having an accident with this probability, and its clock restarts.
potty_training_accident_reduction.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-07: a puppy at 100 % potty training avoids 3 of 4 due accidents (linear in progress); the size of the effect is PetPrep's

place_training_chewing_reduction.unit: share of the teething chewing chance removed at 100 % 'place' training (linear in progress)
place_training_chewing_reduction.notes: UNSOURCED — proposal (Claude, M5-R03, waiting for David). ASPCA: guidance teaches a puppy to restrict chewing to its toys (S33). Applies to the teething chance only — the chewing after a missed walk stays certain (David 2026-10-06).
place_training_chewing_reduction.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-07: 100 % place training halves the teething chewing chance (linear in progress); chewing after a missed walk stays certain; the size of the effect is PetPrep's

training_starting_progress.unit: training progress % per command when the dog arrives in that life stage (bought or adopted)
training_starting_progress.notes: UNSOURCED — Claude proposal (M5-R03b): a dog that arrives grown has usually learnt some basics in its previous home or shelter; no source gives numbers. Applied once at pet creation, only for pets with training; not a session.
training_starting_progress.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-06: young, adult and senior arrivals start with sit 50 %, potty 70 %, come 30 %, place 0 %; a puppy (also bought) starts at 0 %

puppy_socialisation.unit: new-experience tasks per program week while a puppy (game stage puppy, under 9 months; one tap, never scored)
puppy_socialisation.applies_to: every dog breed without its own proposed_game_parameters.<breed>.socialisation entry (the mutt, Border Collie, Golden Retriever, French Bulldog, Cavalier King Charles Spaniel, Dachshund, West Highland White Terrier, Bernese Mountain Dog, German Shorthaired Pointer, Yorkshire Terrier and every future dog breed); never cats
puppy_socialisation.notes: No breed-specific A/B quote and no general_by_size socialisation entry in this file — the basis is David's decision alone (no quote is invented). The 12 breeds with a verbatim PDSA quote keep their own entry. Built in M5-R17: one "new experience" (a new person, another dog, a new sound, a new place) per program week while a puppy; shown to the parent, no penalty.
puppy_socialisation.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-12: socializacija za vse mladičke (1 nova izkušnja na teden, dokler je mladiček; brez kazni, M5-R17)

step_goal_adult.notes: Game value (no literature step count). 90 min (Guide Dogs UK 'at least 90 minutes of exercise daily', S59) × 100 steps/min (S45, adult heuristic) — same method as the Border Collie. Alternatives recorded, not chosen: RKC 'More than 2 hours per day' (S50) → 12,000 (= Border Collie); Woodgreen 60–90 min (S60) → 6,000–9,000.
step_goal_adult.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-09: 90 min (Guide Dogs UK ≥ 90 min, S59) × 100 steps/min → 9,000 steps; keeps the Labrador apart from the Border Collie (12,000)

exercise_minutes_adult.notes: Game value = Guide Dogs UK lower bound (S59; see labrador_retriever.exercise for the exact quote). RKC (S50) says more than 2 hours, Woodgreen (S60) 60–90 min.
exercise_minutes_adult.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-09: 90 min/day (RKC '>2 h' S50 and Woodgreen 60–90 min S60 recorded as alternatives)

exercise_minutes_senior.notes: Game value (no literature number). 75 % of the adult 90 min (senior rule David confirmed for other breeds 2026-10-05) = 67.5 min; minutes are whole numbers (StageParamKey::validate, API exercise_minutes int) → 68 min = 6,800 steps.
exercise_minutes_senior.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-09: 68 min → 6,800 steps (75 % of 90 = 67.5, rounded to whole minutes)

stage_boundaries_months.notes: Game boundaries (no exact month in the literature). young 9: AAHA 'cessation of rapid growth (~6–9 months, varying with breed and size)' (S11) — same as the other dogs. Large-breed evidence: growth ends 15–18 months (S10 'Large (59–99 pounds): 15–18 months'), up to 24 months (S8); AAHA's young-adult boundary is cessation of RAPID growth, not end of growth, so 9 months still fits (alternative 12 not chosen). adult 36: AAHA 3–4 years (S11), same as other breeds. senior 118 = 0.75 × 13.1 y (S11 + S54); 108 if the VetCompass median 12.0 y (S55) were used (not chosen).
stage_boundaries_months.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-09: young 9, adult 36, senior 118 (0.75 × McMillan 2024 median 13.1 y, S54)

arrival_age_months.notes: Game value (no literature number). First month of each stage (rule David confirmed 2026-10-05), so the dog stays in its stage for the 12-week challenge.
arrival_age_months.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-09: first month of each stage (2 / 9 / 36 / 118)

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value (no literature factor). Coren rank 7 is in the same 'brightest' tier as the Border Collie (<5 repetitions, ≥95 % first-command obedience; S35, tier C); the tier is Coren's only quantitative statement, so the evidence alone would give 2.0 — David chose 1.8 so the Border Collie stays visibly fastest. No individual variation (like the Border Collie; S42 says breed explains only ~9 % of individual behaviour — not used). Food motivation (S59, S57) could later justify a treat-training bonus.
learning_multiplier.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-09: 1.8 — same Coren 'brightest' tier as the Border Collie (2.0), BC stays visibly fastest

obesity_mechanic.notes: UNSOURCED idea, not built (post-MVP backlog; no decision asked). Labradors are prone to obesity (S53; 8.8 % overweight/obese, S55) and highly food motivated (S59, S57). Idea: extra treats/overfeeding raise a weight score faster than for other breeds; no number sourced.

care_rates.unit: % per hour / count per day / minutes
care_rates.notes: Game values (no breed-specific number in the sources) — identical to the Border Collie breed_configs row (BreedConfigsSeeder).
care_rates.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-09: same as the Border Collie — hunger −12 %/h, thirst −15 %/h, 2 poops/day, water 3×/day ≥ 180 min apart

grooming.notes: RKC (S50) 'Once a week'; PDSA (S53) 'a weekly brush usually enough' (labrador_retriever.suitability.rkc_grooming.notes). Matted coat when the week's brushing is missed (ceil(1 / 2) = 1).
grooming.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-12 (pravilo runbooka (David 2026-10-11/12: »enkrat na teden« → 1, »vsak dan« → 7, razpon A–B → B)): 1× na teden; mehanika česanja psa zgrajena v ROADMAP M5-R13 (David 2026-10-12, »kot pri mački«)

socialisation.unit: new-experience tasks per program week while a puppy (game stage puppy, under 9 months; one tap, never scored)
socialisation.quote: Labradors make perfect family pets, given the right socialisation, as with all breeds.
socialisation.notes: PDSA (S53), verbatim in labrador_retriever.suitability.pdsa_family.quote. The source gives socialisation advice without an amount; the weekly "new experience" (a new person, another dog, a new sound, a new place) while a puppy is David's mechanic (M5-R17, 2026-10-12) — never scored.
socialisation.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-12: 1 nova izkušnja na teden, dokler je mladiček; brez kazni (ROADMAP M5-R17, »tedenska naloga«)

step_goal_adult.notes: Game value (no literature step count). 120 min (RKC 'More than 2 hours per day', S65; PDSA 'a minimum of two hours of good exercise per day', S68) × 100 steps/min (S45, adult heuristic) — same method as the Border Collie / Labrador. Unlike the Labrador (PDSA gave no minutes, Guide Dogs gave ≥ 90), two tier-B sources agree on ≥ 2 h and Guide Dogs (S70) gives no number. Alternatives recorded, not chosen: 90 min → 9,000 (= Labrador; Woodgreen upper bound S69); Woodgreen 60–90 min → 6,000–9,000.
step_goal_adult.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-09: 120 min (RKC S65 '> 2 h' + PDSA S68 'minimum of two hours') × 100 steps/min → 12,000 steps (= Border Collie)

exercise_minutes_adult.notes: Game value = PDSA 'minimum of two hours' (S68) = RKC '> 2 h' (S65) lower bound. Woodgreen 60–90 min (S69) recorded as alternative (90), not chosen.
exercise_minutes_adult.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-09: 120 min/day (Woodgreen 60–90 min S69 recorded as alternative)

exercise_minutes_senior.notes: Game value (no literature number). 75 % of the adult 120 min (senior rule David confirmed 2026-10-05) = 90 min exactly → 9,000 steps (= Border Collie senior).
exercise_minutes_senior.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-09: 90 min → 9,000 steps (75 % of 120)

stage_boundaries_months.notes: Game boundaries (no exact month in the literature). young 9 / adult 36: AAHA (S11), same reasoning as the Labrador (large-breed growth ends 15–18 months, S10, but AAHA's young-adult boundary is cessation of RAPID growth; alternative young 12 not chosen). senior 119 = 0.75 × 13.2 y × 12 = 118.8 → 119 (S11 + S15, Dogs Trust summary of McMillan 2024). Alternatives not chosen: 112 = 0.75 × 12.48 y (VetCompass poster, S71); 118 (= Labrador / Border Collie). 119 is 1 month later than the Labrador / Border Collie (118).
stage_boundaries_months.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-09: young 9, adult 36, senior 119 (0.75 × 13.2 y, S15 Dogs Trust summary of McMillan 2024)

arrival_age_months.notes: Game value (no literature number). First month of each stage (rule David confirmed 2026-10-05), so the dog stays in its stage for the 12-week challenge.
arrival_age_months.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-09: first month of each stage (2 / 9 / 36 / 119)

learning_multiplier.notes: Game value (no literature factor). Coren rank 4 (S34, S35) — same 'brightest' tier as the Border Collie (rank 1 → 2.0) and the Labrador (rank 7 → 1.8). Linear between them by rank: 2.0 − (4−1)/(7−1) × 0.2 = 1.9 → keeps the Border Collie fastest and the order of Coren's list. PDSA 'Easy to train' (S68), Guide Dogs 'motivated by food and play, making them easy to train' (S70); Woodgreen 'Moderately easy' (S69, same as the Labrador). No individual variation (like the Border Collie and the Labrador). Alternatives not chosen: 1.8 (= Labrador), 2.0 (= tier only).
learning_multiplier.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-09: 1.9 (Coren rank 4, S34) — between the Border Collie (2.0) and the Labrador (1.8)

care_rates.notes: Game values (no breed-specific number in the sources) — identical to the Border Collie / Labrador breed_configs row (BreedConfigsSeeder).

grooming_mechanic.notes: Superseded by proposed_game_parameters.golden_retriever.grooming (built in M5-R13, David 2026-10-12: 3 brushings per program week, PDSA S68 'three times a week at a minimum'). learning_multiplier.notes: Game value (no literature factor). Coren rank 58 (S35, tier C), tier 'Fair' (ranks 55–69: 40–80 repetitions, obeys first command ≥ 30 %) — one tier BELOW 'Average' (40–54). The mixed-breed baseline (1.0) is unranked and treated as 'Average'. The existing scale spends ~0.3 per Coren tier step (Average 1.0 → Above average → Excellent → Brightest ≈ 1.8–2.0, i.e. 3 steps for +0.8–1.0), so one step down = 0.7. Linear-by-rank extrapolation from BC (1 → 2.0) and Labrador (7 → 1.8) would give ≈ 0.1 at rank 58 — rejected, the scale is per tier, not per rank. Counterweight: PDSA 'eager to please … easy to train … strong-willed at times' (S81) and Woodgreen 'Moderately easy' (S82, same as Labrador/Golden) → alternative 0.8. No individual variation (like the other pedigree breeds). Mixed breed with ±20 % can be as slow as 0.8 — overlaps with the alternative.
learning_multiplier.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-10: 0.7 (Coren rank 58, S35 — 'Fair' tier, one tier below Average)

Small dogs drink and eat less in absolute terms (water is per kg: 60–80 ml/kg/day, S22), but the game bars are % of the dog's own need, and no source gives a breed- or size-specific hunger/thirst rate or meal count for small adults → no change proposed. Heat makes water more important (S81/S82), but that is handled by the heat idea below, not by the base rate.

heat_breathing_mechanic.notes: UNSOURCED idea, not built (post-MVP backlog). Must NOT use a weather API (CLAUDE.md scope guard). Sourced facts it rests on: overheat and struggle to breathe quickly in warm weather, walk in cooler morning/evening, know the heatstroke signs (PDSA S81); 'two good walks a day' (Woodgreen S82); OR 2.10 for heat illness in flat-faced dogs (S86); noisy breathing at rest is not normal (RKC standard S79 'excessive respiratory noise unacceptable'). Idea: (1) the daily step goal counts only in ≥ 2 walks — one walk above ~30 min (half the goal; our number) makes the dog 'pant' and pause (child learns: short walks, rests); (2) in the game's summer months (calendar, family timezone — no weather data) midday walks (e.g. 11–16 h, our number) trigger a 'too hot — walk in the morning or evening' hint and a water reminder; (3) a calm 'Did you know?' card: flat faces can make breathing harder, so Frenchies need cool shade, water and gentle walks. No illness, collapse or death shown to the child; no percentages.

not_proposed.family_pet: PDSA 'incredibly loyal family pets' (S508) comes with 'not with young children' and 'experienced owners' (S508); PetMD: best as the only pet, patience for young children limited (S510) → no suits chip (open for David).
not_proposed.children: PDSA advises against young children (S508) → not_for_small_children; PetMD: may live well with older children (S510) — no explicit children rating.
not_proposed.small_children: PDSA: not recommended with young children (S508).
not_proposed.first_time_owner: PDSA: not suitable for inexperienced owners (S508).
not_proposed.apartment: No RKC 'Size of home' key fact (page not reachable); a very large dog (S508).
not_proposed.large_home: Only from the RKC key fact 'Large house' (runbook) — not reachable.
not_proposed.other_pets: PDSA: high prey drive, not with smaller pets (S508); PetMD best as the only pet (S510) → chases_small_pets.
not_proposed.frequent_grooming: PDSA weekly (S508) vs PetMD daily (S510) — conflicting sources → no chip.
not_proposed.shorter_lifespan: PDSA 'Under 10 years' (S508) vs PetMD 10–14 years (S510) and McMillan 2024 11.4 y (only via Wikipedia, S512) — conflicting sources → no chip (open for David).
not_proposed.needs_mental_stimulation: PDSA mentions puzzles and rotating toys against boredom (paraphrase only) — no explicit need statement returned verbatim.
not_proposed.heat: PDSA: prone to overheating in very hot weather (S508) — not a flat-faced breed, no chip in the vocabulary for it (breed text only).
not_proposed.welfare: No RKC Breed Watch category reachable; not flat-faced → no welfare chip (open for David).

marketing.notes: Not flat-faced; the only veterinary advice against advertising a breed type is for flat-faced breeds (BVA S92). Marketing never promises health; never with small children (S508), never next to small pets (S508), never as a guard dog or as a beginner's dog (S508), never confused with the Japanese Akita Inu.
marketing.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-10 (pravilo runbooka): in the app yes, in marketing yes (not flat-faced, no veterinary advice against advertising)

ai_appearance.value: adult Akita (American type), red fawn with a black mask (default); large, sturdy, well balanced dog with heavy bone; broad head forming a blunt triangle, deep muzzle, small dark brown eyes; strongly erect small ears; thick double coat; large tail curled over the back; never merle or liver
ai_appearance.quote: Any colour like red, fawn, white, etc; or even pinto and brindle.
ai_appearance.notes: Colours of the FCI standard (S507) / AKC standard (S509): any colour incl. white, pinto and brindle, with or without mask; disqualifying merle and liver. The game offers four typical standard colours (red fawn with a black mask, pinto, brindle, white). Weights unsourced in prompts. Red fawn with a black mask as the portrait default — Claude's choice.
ai_appearance.decision: potrdil David 2026-10-10 (pravilo runbooka): red fawn with a black mask is the portrait default; standard colours only (never merle or liver); natural erect ears and curled tail
